workers.title: ArcGIS REST Feature Services
workers.tagline: Query ArcGIS REST feature services (FeatureServer/MapServer) from DuckDB as SQL tables, via VGI
workers.subtitle: Live ArcGIS feature queries, server summaries and raster sampling from service URLs worldwide.
workers.summary: Live ArcGIS FeatureServer, MapServer and ImageServer data from any service URL as SQL: layers as views with GEOMETRY, server-side counts and statistics, and raster pixel sampling. Public services need no key; secured ones take ArcGIS tokens or OAuth app credentials.
workers.doc_md:
# ArcGIS REST services in DuckDB

Government agencies, utilities and organizations worldwide publish their GIS data as ArcGIS REST services. This worker reads them live, from whatever service URL you give it: there is no built-in list of agencies, and no data is copied or cached apart from layer metadata.

## Two ways in

Call a function with a layer URL when you already know the layer. The functions read features, count or summarize them on the server (so a ten-million-parcel layer is never downloaded to answer a count), or sample ImageServer pixel values such as elevation at a batch of points.

Attach with a `url` option when you want to browse. A services directory (`.../arcgis/rest/services`) becomes one schema per service with one view per layer; a single service (`.../FeatureServer`) becomes one view per layer in `main`; a layer (`.../FeatureServer/0`) becomes one view. An ArcGIS Hub or Open Data site (such as `https://gis.data.ca.gov`) works like a services directory, and a Hub dataset page (`.../datasets/<itemId>_0`) resolves to the REST layer behind it.

```sql
ATTACH 'arcgis' AS va (TYPE vgi, LOCATION 'github-auto://Query-farm/vgi-arcgis@v0.6.1',
  url 'https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Admin_Boundaries/FeatureServer');
SHOW ALL TABLES;
```

## Geometry and filters

Attribute fields arrive as typed columns and feature geometry as a WGS84 `GEOMETRY` column, rounded to `precision` decimals (default 7, about 1 cm). Simple filters (numeric comparisons, string equality and `IN`, `IS NULL`, prefix matches) and spatial filters against a constant (`geometry && <box>`, `ST_Intersects`, `ST_Within`, ...) are sent to the ArcGIS server, and every filter is also applied exactly in the worker, so results never depend on how much the server understood. Pages are fetched automatically.

## Secured services

Public services need no credentials. For token-secured ones, either ATTACH with the secret options `token`, `username` + `password`, or `client_id` + `client_secret` (redacted from `duckdb_databases()` and sent only to the ATTACH `url`'s server), or create an `arcgis` secret scoped to a URL prefix for the functions. Generated tokens are renewed automatically; `getenv()` keeps a credential out of the SQL text:

```sql
CREATE SECRET gis_token (TYPE arcgis, TOKEN getenv('ARCGIS_TOKEN'),
  SCOPE 'https://gis.example.gov/arcgis/rest/services/');
```

## Sources

Every query goes live to the ArcGIS server named by the URL you supply, through the public ArcGIS REST API:

- Feature scans, counts and statistics use [Query (Feature Service/Layer)](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/query-feature-service-layer/) and [Query (Map Service/Layer)](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/query-map-service-layer/).
- Services directories are walked through the [Services Directory root](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/catalog/).
- Imagery sampling uses [Get Samples](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/get-samples/) on an ImageServer.
- ArcGIS Hub sites and dataset pages are resolved through the [Hub API](https://hub.arcgis.com/api/v3/).
- Secured services: [Generate Token](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/generate-token/), the portal [/token](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/users-groups-and-items/token/) OAuth endpoint, and Esri's [security and authentication guide](https://developers.arcgis.com/documentation/security-and-authentication/).
workers.readme_sql:
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;   -- for the ST_ functions; reading the views needs no extension
ATTACH 'arcgis' AS va (TYPE vgi, LOCATION '/abs/path/to/vgi-arcgis-worker',
                       url 'https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services');

SELECT LOCALITY, count(*)
FROM va.va_base_layers_va_parcels.virginia_parcels
WHERE FIPS = '51580'          -- runs on the ArcGIS server
GROUP BY ALL;

attach_options.name: url
attach_options.description: ArcGIS REST URL to expose as tables: a services directory (.../arcgis/rest/services or a folder), a service (.../FeatureServer or .../MapServer) or a single layer (.../FeatureServer/0); or an ArcGIS Hub / Open Data site (https://<site>, one schema per service in its catalog) or one of its dataset pages (https://<site>/datasets/<id>, resolved to the REST layer or service). Omit it to use the ArcGIS query, summary and imagery functions without catalog views.

attach_options.name: precision
attach_options.description: Decimal places kept in returned coordinates (ArcGIS geometryPrecision), 0-15. 7 is about 1 cm in longitude/latitude.

attach_options.name: token
attach_options.description: A pre-generated ArcGIS token for token-secured services, sent as the token parameter on requests to the ATTACH url's server only (credentials require url). Not renewed: when it expires, attach again. Pass it as token getenv('ARCGIS_TOKEN') to keep it out of the SQL text.

attach_options.name: username
attach_options.description: ArcGIS Server, ArcGIS Enterprise or ArcGIS Online user name. With password, the worker generates tokens at the server's token service (from <server>/rest/info) and renews them before they expire.

attach_options.name: password
attach_options.description: Password for username, sent only to the server's token service over HTTPS. Pass it as password getenv('ARCGIS_PASSWORD').

attach_options.name: client_id
attach_options.description: Client ID of an ArcGIS OAuth application (ArcGIS Online or an ArcGIS Enterprise portal). With client_secret, the worker gets app tokens with the OAuth client-credentials flow and renews them.

attach_options.name: client_secret
attach_options.description: Client secret of the OAuth application named by client_id, sent only to the portal's oauth2/token endpoint over HTTPS. Pass it as client_secret getenv('ARCGIS_CLIENT_SECRET').

example_queries.description: Empty point input returns no samples without contacting a service
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS sample_count FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_sample('https://example.org/arcgis/rest/services/Elevation/ImageServer', '[]') ORDER BY sample_count;

example_queries.description: Count the parcels in Covington, Virginia (FIPS 51580); the filter runs on the ArcGIS server
example_queries.sql: SELECT LOCALITY, count(*) AS parcels FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Parcels/FeatureServer/0') WHERE FIPS = '51580' GROUP BY ALL

example_queries.description: Areas of two Virginia cities with DuckDB spatial
example_queries.sql: SELECT NAMELSAD, ST_Area_Spheroid(geometry) / 1e6 AS km2 FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Admin_Boundaries/FeatureServer/1') WHERE NAME IN ('Covington', 'Buena Vista') ORDER BY NAMELSAD

example_queries.description: Hospitals in Virginia cities whose names start with 'Rich', from the statewide landmarks layer
example_queries.sql: SELECT LandmkName, City FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Landmarks/FeatureServer/1') WHERE PlaceType = 'Hospital Points' AND City LIKE 'Rich%' ORDER BY LandmkName

example_queries.description: Parcels touching a small box in downtown Covington; the server returns only features near the box, not the state's millions of parcels
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS parcels FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Parcels/FeatureServer/0') WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, ST_MakeEnvelope(-80.005, 37.785, -79.99, 37.795))

example_queries.description: The five states with the most counties and county equivalents (Virginia's count includes its independent cities), by name: arcgis_statistics counts them per state FIPS on the Census server, and arcgis_query on the states layer turns each code into its abbreviation and name
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.STUSAB, s.NAME, c.statistic_value::INTEGER AS counties FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/0') s JOIN arcgis.main.arcgis_statistics('https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1', 'OBJECTID', statistic := 'count', group_by := 'STATE') c ON c.group_value = s.STATE ORDER BY counties DESC, s.STUSAB LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Count New York counties on Census TIGERweb
example_queries.sql: SELECT feature_count FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_count('https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1', where_clause := 'STATE = ''36''')

example_queries.description: Sum county land area by state on the Census server
example_queries.sql: SELECT group_value AS state, statistic_value AS land_area FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_statistics('https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1', 'AREALAND', group_by := 'STATE', where_clause := 'STATE = ''36''') ORDER BY state

example_queries.description: Parcels per square mile in four small Virginia cities: arcgis_statistics counts parcels per FIPS on the server, and arcgis_query supplies each city's name and area from the boundaries layer
example_queries.sql: SELECT b.NAMELSAD, p.statistic_value::BIGINT AS parcels, round(b.AREASQMI, 2) AS sq_mi, round(p.statistic_value / b.AREASQMI) AS parcels_per_sq_mi FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_statistics('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Parcels/FeatureServer/0', 'OBJECTID', statistic := 'count', group_by := 'FIPS', where_clause := 'FIPS IN (''51530'', ''51580'', ''51678'', ''51720'')') p JOIN arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Admin_Boundaries/FeatureServer/1') b ON b.STCOFIPS = p.group_value ORDER BY parcels_per_sq_mi DESC

example_queries.description: Sample USGS bare-earth elevation in meters near the White House
example_queries.sql: SELECT point_index, TRY_CAST(value AS DOUBLE) AS elevation_m FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_sample('https://elevation.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/3DEPElevation/ImageServer', '[[-77.0365,38.8977],[-77.04,38.90]]') ORDER BY point_index

example_queries.description: USGS elevation at four points, labelled with the Virginia city each falls in: arcgis_sample reads the pixels and arcgis_query supplies city boundaries for a point-in-polygon join
example_queries.sql: SELECT b.NAMELSAD, round(TRY_CAST(s.value AS DOUBLE)) AS elevation_m FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_sample('https://elevation.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/3DEPElevation/ImageServer', '[[-79.9937,37.7935],[-79.3540,37.7343],[-79.4428,37.7840],[-82.6290,36.9334]]') s JOIN arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Admin_Boundaries/FeatureServer/1') b ON ST_Contains(b.geometry, ST_Point(s.sample_x, s.sample_y)) WHERE b.JURISTYPE = 'CI' ORDER BY elevation_m DESC

agent_tasks: Count New York counties at https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1 using a server-side count without downloading features. New York's STATE FIPS is 36.

Using https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1, count non-null OBJECTID values grouped by STATE for New York (36), computing the statistic on the server. Return exactly the columns group_value and statistic_value, ordered by group_value.

Sample elevation in meters at longitude -77.0365, latitude 38.8977 from https://elevation.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/3DEPElevation/ImageServer using the imagery function. Save the answer as a temporary table white_house_elevation with one DOUBLE column elevation_m.

Using the arcgis worker, how many parcels does the Virginia statewide parcel layer (https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Parcels/FeatureServer/0) have in Covington City (FIPS 51580)? Save the answer as a temporary table covington_parcels with one BIGINT column parcels.

Which Virginia independent city has the most land parcels per square mile? Count parcels per FIPS code on the server from the statewide parcel layer (https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Parcels/FeatureServer/0, field FIPS) and divide by each city's AREASQMI from the cities and counties layer (https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Admin_Boundaries/FeatureServer/1, where cities have JURISTYPE 'CI' and STCOFIPS is the FIPS code). Save the answer as a temporary table densest_city with one row and one VARCHAR column name holding the city's NAME.

Using the cities and counties layer at https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Admin_Boundaries/FeatureServer/1, which is larger by area: Covington or Buena Vista? Return only the winning city's NAME column.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The `main` schema holds the URL-driven functions (reading features, server-side counts and grouped statistics, ImageServer pixel sampling) and, when the catalog was attached with a service or layer `url`, one view per layer. A services directory or Hub site `url` adds one schema per service instead. For a token-secured URL the functions use the catalog's ATTACH credentials when they cover the URL's server, else the `arcgis` secret whose SCOPE is the longest prefix of the URL. tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

The entry point of the ArcGIS worker. Its functions take an ArcGIS layer or ImageServer URL directly, so nothing needs to be attached first; when the catalog was attached with a service or layer `url`, `main` also lists one view per layer of it. Attaching a services directory or ArcGIS Hub site instead adds one schema per service alongside `main`.

For a token-secured URL, the functions use the catalog's ATTACH credentials when they cover the URL's server, and otherwise the `arcgis` secret whose `SCOPE` is the longest prefix of the URL. Catalog views see only ATTACH credentials.

vgi.example_queries.description: Count the parcels in Covington, Virginia (FIPS 51580); the filter runs on the ArcGIS server
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT LOCALITY, count(*) AS parcels FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Parcels/FeatureServer/0') WHERE FIPS = '51580' GROUP BY ALL

functions.name: arcgis_sample
functions.comment: Sample elevation or multiband pixel values from an ArcGIS ImageServer at WGS84 points

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Read pixel values from an ArcGIS ImageServer using getSamples. Required url and points_json, a JSON array of WGS84 [longitude,latitude] pairs (maximum 10000; empty gives no rows; NULL/invalid coordinates rejected). Makes batched requests of 100 points, not one RPC per row. Returns point_index (zero-based input index when locationId is supplied, else NULL), sample_x, sample_y, spatial_reference JSON text, value text, raster_id `BIGINT`, resolution `DOUBLE`. Raw value text preserves multiband and NoData values; TRY_CAST to `DOUBLE` for elevation. Uses the service's default mosaic/pixel size and first non-NoData value. Points outside coverage may produce no row. No raster downloads, image export or catalog views. Scoped arcgis credentials work as for arcgis_query.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Image sampling

Sample raster pixels at WGS84 points using `arcgis_sample(url, points_json)`. Requests contain up to 100 points each, with a maximum input of 10000. Empty input gives no rows; NULL/invalid input fails. Returns sample coordinates and spatial-reference JSON, raw pixel `value`, source raster ID and resolution. `point_index` refers to the input array when the service returns `locationId`, otherwise NULL. Multiband and NoData values remain text; use `TRY_CAST(value AS DOUBLE)` for elevation. Uncovered points may have no row. Uses the default mosaic and first non-NoData value. This samples pixels; it does not download raster files.

functions.name: arcgis_query
functions.comment: Read the features of one ArcGIS FeatureServer/MapServer layer or table, with filter pushdown

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Read every feature of one ArcGIS REST layer or table at `url` (ending in /FeatureServer/<id> or /MapServer/<id>). An ArcGIS Hub / Open Data dataset page URL for one layer also works (`https://<site>/datasets/<itemId>_<id>` or `.../datasets/<orgKey>::<slug>`); it is resolved to the layer's REST URL first. The result columns depend on the layer: one column per attribute field, typed from the layer metadata (object ids and integers as `INTEGER`, small integers as `SMALLINT`, doubles as `DOUBLE`, dates as `TIMESTAMP_MS`, strings and GUIDs as `VARCHAR`). Layers with geometry add `geometry` (`GEOMETRY`), WGS84 longitude/latitude rounded to the ATTACH `precision` (default 7 decimals). Simple WHERE predicates are sent to the server (numeric comparisons, string equality and IN, IS NULL, prefix/contains matches), and so are spatial filters against a constant: `geometry && <box>` and ST_Intersects / ST_Within / ST_Contains / ST_Covers / ST_Touches / ST_Overlaps / ST_Crosses / ST_Equals(geometry, <constant geometry>) make the server return only features whose envelope meets the constant's. Every predicate is also applied exactly to the returned rows. Results are paged automatically. Filter large layers on an attribute (e.g. a FIPS code) or an area: an unfiltered scan downloads the whole layer.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## arcgis_query(url)

Every feature of one ArcGIS FeatureServer/MapServer layer or table, paged automatically.

- `url` is a layer URL (`.../FeatureServer/0`) or an ArcGIS Hub dataset page for one layer (`https://<site>/datasets/<itemId>_0`).
- Attribute fields become typed columns; the set of columns depends on the layer.
- Layers with geometry add `geometry` (`GEOMETRY`, WGS84 longitude/latitude).
- Simple attribute filters and spatial filters against a constant (`&&`, `ST_Intersects`, `ST_Within`, ...) run on the ArcGIS server, so filter large layers on an attribute or an area.

The columns follow the layer at `url`: one column per attribute field, in server order, typed from its ArcGIS field type (object ids and integers `INTEGER`, small integers `SMALLINT`, big integers `BIGINT`, doubles `DOUBLE`, singles `FLOAT`, dates `TIMESTAMP_MS`, strings and GUIDs `VARCHAR`), with the field alias as the column comment. functions.name: arcgis_count
functions.comment: Count matching ArcGIS features on the server without downloading them

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Count one ArcGIS layer via returnCountOnly=true, without transferring features. Required url; optional where_clause (ArcGIS SQL, default 1=1) and bbox (WGS84 xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax, default empty). Uses scoped arcgis credentials. Returns one feature_count `BIGINT`, including zero. NULL url is rejected; NULL optional arguments use their defaults. Remote comparison/collation and spatial semantics apply; this is not automatic pushdown of DuckDB COUNT(*) or its WHERE clauses. Apply restrictions using the named arguments. Unsafe or missing counts raise an error.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## ArcGIS count

Returns one `feature_count BIGINT` using the server's `returnCountOnly` operation. Restrict rows with `where_clause` (ArcGIS SQL) and `bbox` (WGS84 xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax). Uses the same credentials as `arcgis_query`. No feature download. Zero matches return 0; NULL url is rejected; NULL optional arguments use their defaults. Outer SQL filters apply to the summary, so use the named arguments to filter source records.

functions.name: arcgis_statistics
functions.comment: Compute a numeric statistic, optionally grouped by one field, on an ArcGIS server

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Aggregate a layer using ArcGIS outStatistics. Required url and statistic_field; optional statistic (sum by default; count/min/max/avg/stddev/var also supported), group_by (one field, default empty), where_clause (ArcGIS SQL, default 1=1) and bbox (WGS84 bounds, default empty). Scoped arcgis credentials apply. Returns group_value `VARCHAR` and statistic_value `DOUBLE`; null groups and null aggregate values remain NULL. Without group_by, group_value is NULL. Empty grouped results have no rows. NULL required inputs are rejected; NULL optional arguments use their defaults. Numeric statistics need a numeric field; count counts non-null field values. Large integer aggregates may lose `DOUBLE` precision. A truncated server result raises an error; narrow the source filters. This is an explicit server operation, not automatic DuckDB GROUP BY pushdown.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## ArcGIS statistics

Compute `statistic` over `statistic_field`, optionally grouped by `group_by`. Filter source rows using ArcGIS SQL `where_clause` or WGS84 `bbox`. Returns `group_value VARCHAR` and `statistic_value DOUBLE`, retaining NULL values. Defaults: sum, no grouping, all rows. NULL required inputs are rejected; NULL optional arguments use their defaults. Count counts non-null field values. Truncated responses fail rather than return partial groups; narrow the source filter. `DOUBLE` can round large integer aggregates; `arcgis_count` provides exact total feature counts.

examples: SELECT group_value AS state, statistic_value AS land_area FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_statistics('https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1', 'AREALAND', group_by := 'STATE', where_clause := 'STATE = ''36''') ORDER BY state

SELECT b.NAMELSAD, p.statistic_value::BIGINT AS parcels, round(b.AREASQMI, 2) AS sq_mi, round(p.statistic_value / b.AREASQMI) AS parcels_per_sq_mi FROM arcgis.main.arcgis_statistics('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Parcels/FeatureServer/0', 'OBJECTID', statistic := 'count', group_by := 'FIPS', where_clause := 'FIPS IN (''51530'', ''51580'', ''51678'', ''51720'')') p JOIN arcgis.main.arcgis_query('https://vginmaps.vdem.virginia.gov/arcgis/rest/services/VA_Base_Layers/VA_Admin_Boundaries/FeatureServer/1') b ON b.STCOFIPS = p.group_value ORDER BY parcels_per_sq_mi DESC

result_columns.name: group_value
result_columns.description: Group field value as text; NULL for an ungrouped aggregate or a null-valued group.

result_columns.name: statistic_value
result_columns.description: Server aggregate as `DOUBLE`, possibly NULL for no non-null values. Large integers may lose precision; use arcgis_count for exact total counts.

secret_type_details.name: arcgis
secret_type_details.description: Credentials for token-secured ArcGIS REST services (ArcGIS Server, ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online) read by arcgis_query: a pre-generated ArcGIS token, an ArcGIS username and password, or an ArcGIS OAuth app's client_id and client_secret. Give it a SCOPE (a URL prefix such as 'https://host/arcgis/rest/services/') so it is only sent to that server; the longest matching scope wins.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: A pre-generated ArcGIS token (from the server's generateToken page, or an ArcGIS Online API key), sent as the token parameter as is. Generate it with client=requestip, or with referer https://github.com/Query-farm/vgi-arcgis. It is not renewed when it expires.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: ArcGIS Server, ArcGIS Enterprise or ArcGIS Online user name; exchanged with password for a token at the server's token service (authInfo.tokenServicesUrl of <server>/rest/info).

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password of username. Sent only to the server's token service, over HTTPS.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Client ID of an ArcGIS OAuth application (ArcGIS Online or an ArcGIS Enterprise portal: Content > the app item > Settings), used with client_secret for the client-credentials flow.

parameters.name: client_secret
parameters.description: Client secret of the OAuth application named by client_id. Sent only to the portal's oauth2/token endpoint, over HTTPS.

workers.subtitle: Decode ASN.1 BER/DER blobs and SNMP, Kerberos, LDAP, CMS, PKCS and OCSP messages into SQL rows.

workers.doc_md:
# asn1 — ASN.1 BER/DER Decoding & Security-Payload Shredding in SQL

**Decode generic ASN.1 (BER/CER/DER) and the security/telecom modules that ride on it — SNMP, Kerberos, LDAP, CMS/PKCS#7, PKCS#8/#12, OCSP — directly in DuckDB SQL.** Walk any DER blob into a typed JSON tree, dump it `openssl asn1parse`-style, inventory every OBJECT IDENTIFIER, and shred the named modules into joinable rows — signers, SNMP varbinds, LDAP messages, PKCS#12 bags. The flagship pairing is **vgi-x509**: the CMS and PKCS#12 decoders surface embedded-certificate SHA-256 hashes so you can join them straight to cert metadata and revocation.

The worker is **structural-decode only** — signatures, MACs, and encrypted parts are surfaced (algorithm OID + bytes) but never verified or decrypted, and PKCS#8/#12 never expose plaintext key material. Decoding is robust against hostile input: bounded recursion and allocation, and per-row error capture (the validator classifies the failure kind) so a malformed blob never aborts a scan.

## Sources and references

- [ITU-T X.690](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.690) — ASN.1 BER, CER and DER encoding rules
- [RFC 5652](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652) — Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS / PKCS#7)
- [RFC 6960](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6960) — OCSP
- [RFC 5958](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5958) — PKCS#8 asymmetric key packages; [RFC 7292](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7292) — PKCS#12
- [RFC 3416](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3416) — SNMP PDUs; [RFC 4120](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4120) — Kerberos V5; [RFC 4511](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4511) — LDAP

example_queries.description: Decode a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }` into its nested typed JSON projection.
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.decode(from_hex('3003020105'));

example_queries.description: Project the same blob into self-describing JSON, one object per TLV node.
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.to_json(from_hex('3003020105'));

example_queries.description: Render an `openssl asn1parse`-style indented text dump of the blob.
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.dump(from_hex('3003020105'));

example_queries.description: Resolve a dotted OID to its friendly algorithm name ('sha256WithRSAEncryption').
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.oid_name('1.2.840.113549.1.1.11');

example_queries.description: Triage a truncated blob — `well_formed(...).ok` is false.
example_queries.sql: SELECT (asn1.main.well_formed(from_hex('300502'))).ok;

example_queries.description: Validate a bare INTEGER 5 under strict DER encoding rules.
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.is_valid(from_hex('020105'), 'der');

example_queries.description: Split a three-block PEM bundle (PRIVATE KEY, PKCS7, CERTIFICATE) and triage each block's DER: well-formedness, the classified failure kind, and how many OIDs it carries. The PRIVATE KEY (1 OID) and PKCS7 (3 OIDs) blocks are well-formed; the CERTIFICATE body is truncated and flagged ok=false with kind 'length-overflow'.
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.idx, p.label, (asn1.main.well_formed(p.der)).ok AS ok, (asn1.main.well_formed(p.der)).kind AS kind, len(asn1.main.oids(p.der)) AS n_oids FROM asn1.main.pem_decode('-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----' || chr(10) || 'MBYCAQAwDQYJKoZIhvcNAQEBBQAEAmhp' || chr(10) || '-----END PRIVATE KEY-----' || chr(10) || '-----BEGIN PKCS7-----' || chr(10) || 'ME0CAQExADARBgkqhkiG9w0BBwGgBAQCaGmgBTADAgEFMSwwKgIBAYAEAQIDBDALBglghkgBZQMEAgEwDQYJKoZIhvcNAQEBBQAEA6q7zA==' || chr(10) || '-----END PKCS7-----' || chr(10) || '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' || chr(10) || 'MAUC' || chr(10) || '-----END CERTIFICATE-----') AS p ORDER BY p.idx;

example_queries.description: Find the certificates a PKCS#12 keystore shares with a CMS SignedData: join the keystore's cert bags (cert_sha256) to the SHA-256 of each certificate embedded in the signed message (cms_certs). The keystore holds two certBags; only the one whose certificate is also embedded in the message (417c…d729) is returned.

Shred a CMS SignedData's signers and join the oid_registry table to recover the dotted OIDs behind the named digest and signature algorithms (sha256 → 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1, rsaEncryption → 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1).
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.digest_alg, d.oid AS digest_oid, s.sig_alg, g.oid AS sig_oid FROM asn1.main.cms_signers(from_hex('304d0201013100301106092a864886f70d010701a00404026869a0053003020105312c302a020101800401020304300b0609608648016503040201300d06092a864886f70d01010105000403aabbcc')) AS s LEFT JOIN asn1.main.oid_registry AS d ON d.name = s.digest_alg LEFT JOIN asn1.main.oid_registry AS g ON g.name = s.sig_alg ORDER BY s.signer_sid;

example_queries.description: Canonicalize an indefinite-length BER blob with to_der, then prove the result: is_valid under strict DER is false before and true after, and decode yields the same value for both encodings. The canonical bytes are 300404024869.
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.is_valid(b, 'der') AS der_before, hex(asn1.main.to_der(b)) AS der_hex, asn1.main.is_valid(asn1.main.to_der(b), 'der') AS der_after, asn1.main.decode(b) = asn1.main.decode(asn1.main.to_der(b)) AS same_value FROM (SELECT from_hex('3080040248690000') AS b) AS t;

example_queries.description: Decode a real SNMP GetResponse (community 'public') into JSON with its resolved varbinds.

example_queries.sql: SELECT name FROM asn1.main.oid_registry WHERE oid = '1.2.840.113549.1.1.11'

example_queries.description: Count the digest/signature algorithm OIDs the worker knows whose name mentions 'RSA'.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS rsa_oids FROM asn1.main.oid_registry WHERE name ILIKE '%rsa%'

example_queries.description: Walk a minimal PKCS#12 PFX and list each SafeBag's type, encryption flag, and (for cert bags) the vgi-x509 join hash.

example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.dump(from_hex('3003020105'), 'dumpasn1') AS text;

example_queries.description: Inventory every OID in an AlgorithmIdentifier blob — here 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 (sha256WithRSAEncryption), with its resolved name and node path.
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.oids(from_hex('300d06092a864886f70d01010b0500')) AS oids;

example_queries.description: Project the outer [APPLICATION 1] Ticket envelope to a STRUCT (here tkt_vno = 5; realm/sname/enc-part NULL on this minimal ticket).
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.krb_ticket(from_hex('61073005a003020105')) AS ticket;

example_queries.description: Extract the encapsulated eContent BLOB from a CMS SignedData (NULL for this minimal id-data ContentInfo, which wraps no SignedData).
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.cms_content(from_hex('301106092a864886f70d010701a00404026869')) AS econtent;

example_queries.description: Pull the node at path '$.0' (the first child — the INTEGER) of a DER `SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5 }`.
example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.at_path(from_hex('3003020105'), '$.0') AS node;

example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.well_formed(from_hex('3003020105')) AS w;

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## The `main` schema

Everything the `asn1` worker exposes lives here — one place to decode raw BER/CER/DER bytes and the security and telecom protocols layered on top of ASN.1.

**Key concepts**

- *Generic decode* — walk any DER/BER blob into a typed JSON tree, render it `openssl asn1parse`-style, flatten it to TLV nodes, or inventory every OBJECT IDENTIFIER.
- *Structural decoders* — shred the named modules (SNMP, Kerberos, LDAP, CMS/PKCS#7, PKCS#8/#12, OCSP) into joinable rows and JSON projections.
- *Validation & canonicalization* — classify malformed input and re-encode to minimal-length DER, all robust per row: a hostile blob yields an error value, never a crash.

**When to use it**

Reach for this schema to triage, inventory, and join PKI and security binary payloads at scale — for example lifting embedded certificate hashes so signed CMS or PKCS#12 material joins straight to [vgi-x509](https://query.farm). No cryptography is verified or decrypted; this is structural decode only.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.idx, p.label, (asn1.main.well_formed(p.der)).ok AS ok, (asn1.main.well_formed(p.der)).kind AS kind, len(asn1.main.oids(p.der)) AS n_oids FROM asn1.main.pem_decode('-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----' || chr(10) || 'MBYCAQAwDQYJKoZIhvcNAQEBBQAEAmhp' || chr(10) || '-----END PRIVATE KEY-----' || chr(10) || '-----BEGIN PKCS7-----' || chr(10) || 'ME0CAQExADARBgkqhkiG9w0BBwGgBAQCaGmgBTADAgEFMSwwKgIBAYAEAQIDBDALBglghkgBZQMEAgEwDQYJKoZIhvcNAQEBBQAEA6q7zA==' || chr(10) || '-----END PKCS7-----' || chr(10) || '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' || chr(10) || 'MAUC' || chr(10) || '-----END CERTIFICATE-----') AS p ORDER BY p.idx;

vgi.example_queries.description: Find the certificates a PKCS#12 keystore shares with a CMS SignedData: join the keystore's cert bags (cert_sha256) to the SHA-256 of each certificate embedded in the signed message (cms_certs). The keystore holds two certBags; only the one whose certificate is also embedded in the message (417c…d729) is returned.

Shred a CMS SignedData's signers and join the oid_registry table to recover the dotted OIDs behind the named digest and signature algorithms (sha256 → 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1, rsaEncryption → 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT s.digest_alg, d.oid AS digest_oid, s.sig_alg, g.oid AS sig_oid FROM asn1.main.cms_signers(from_hex('304d0201013100301106092a864886f70d010701a00404026869a0053003020105312c302a020101800401020304300b0609608648016503040201300d06092a864886f70d01010105000403aabbcc')) AS s LEFT JOIN asn1.main.oid_registry AS d ON d.name = s.digest_alg LEFT JOIN asn1.main.oid_registry AS g ON g.name = s.sig_alg ORDER BY s.signer_sid;

vgi.example_queries.description: Canonicalize an indefinite-length BER blob with to_der, then prove the result: is_valid under strict DER is false before and true after, and decode yields the same value for both encodings. The canonical bytes are 300404024869.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT asn1.main.is_valid(b, 'der') AS der_before, hex(asn1.main.to_der(b)) AS der_hex, asn1.main.is_valid(asn1.main.to_der(b), 'der') AS der_after, asn1.main.decode(b) = asn1.main.decode(asn1.main.to_der(b)) AS same_value FROM (SELECT from_hex('3080040248690000') AS b) AS t;

functions.name: tlv
functions.comment: Flatten a blob into a LIST of TLV nodes in document order: STRUCT(path, class, tag, tag_name, constructed, header_len, len, value JSON). The raw-structure escape hatch.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Flatten a BER/CER/DER blob into a `LIST` of every TLV node in document order — `STRUCT(path, class, tag, tag_name, constructed, header_len, len, value)` where `path` is a JSONPath-ish locator (e.g. `$.0.2`) and `value` is the node's JSON value. workers.doc_md:
# Audio Feature Extraction in SQL

![librosa logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/librosa/librosa/main/docs/img/librosa_logo_text.png)

Extract tempo, timbre, loudness, key, and rhythm descriptors from audio files and raw audio bytes directly in DuckDB SQL — no separate media pipeline required. The audio catalog turns music information retrieval (MIR) and digital signal processing primitives into ordinary SQL, so you can query, filter, and cluster large audio collections by their acoustic properties using nothing but SELECT.

This VGI worker is built for data engineers, music-tech developers, and ML practitioners who need audio descriptors without leaving the database. Every feature is computed by [librosa](https://librosa.org/), the de-facto standard Python library for audio and music analysis ([documentation](https://librosa.org/doc/latest/index.html), [source on GitHub](https://github.com/librosa/librosa)). Audio is decoded with libsndfile via [soundfile](https://python-soundfile.readthedocs.io/); WAV, FLAC, and OGG decode natively, while compressed formats such as MP3 and M4A use ffmpeg/audioread when available. DuckDB attaches the worker over Apache Arrow, streaming feature vectors back with zero-copy efficiency.

Every feature takes the audio two ways — a filesystem path the worker opens, or a blob of raw audio bytes — and undecodable or hostile input yields NULL (or no rows) rather than crashing. The features span a handful of families, from cheap per-file metadata and loudness levels through spectral-timbre descriptors and compact cepstral feature vectors to rhythm/beat tracking and a heuristic musical-key estimate; list the schema to browse them. Typical uses include building feature tables for audio search and recommendation, detecting tempo or key across a music library, filtering recordings by loudness or brightness, and generating embeddings for downstream clustering or classification — all in plain SQL.
workers.readme_sql:
INSTALL vgi FROM community; LOAD vgi;
ATTACH 'audio' (TYPE vgi, LOCATION 'uvx --from git+https://github.com/Query-farm/vgi-audio@v0.4.3 vgi-audio-worker');

SELECT audio.duration('/tmp/tone.wav');            -- 2.0   (seconds)
SELECT audio.sample_rate('/tmp/tone.wav');          -- 22050 (Hz)
SELECT audio.channels('/tmp/tone.wav');             -- 1
SELECT audio.tempo('/tmp/click.wav');               -- ~120.0 (estimated BPM)
SELECT audio.rms_energy('/tmp/tone.wav');           -- mean RMS energy
SELECT audio.zero_crossing_rate('/tmp/tone.wav');   -- mean ZCR
SELECT audio.spectral_centroid('/tmp/tone.wav');    -- Hz (spectrum centre of mass)
SELECT audio.spectral_bandwidth('/tmp/tone.wav');   -- Hz
SELECT audio.mfcc('/tmp/tone.wav');                 -- DOUBLE[13]
SELECT audio.mfcc('/tmp/tone.wav', 20);             -- DOUBLE[20]
SELECT audio.estimated_key('/tmp/tone.wav');        -- 'C major' (heuristic!)

SELECT * FROM audio.beats('/tmp/click.wav');        -- (seq, time) beat onsets
SELECT * FROM audio.audio_info('/tmp/tone.wav');    -- (duration, sample_rate, channels)

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Audio features (`main`)

The `main` schema is where the audio catalog's librosa-powered feature functions live. It groups them into a few navigable families so you can go from a raw recording to a queryable descriptor in a single SQL call.

### Feature families

- **Container metadata** — cheap per-file facts (length, native sampling frequency, channel count), read from the header when possible.
- **Loudness & energy** — level proxies for ranking recordings or gating near-silent clips.
- **Spectral timbre** — brightness, spread, noisiness, and compact cepstral feature vectors for similarity search and ML.
- **Rhythm** — an estimated tempo and per-beat onset times.
- **Tonality** — a heuristic musical-key estimate.

### Inputs & robustness

Every function takes the audio two ways: a filesystem path the worker opens, or a blob of raw audio bytes. WAV, FLAC, and OGG decode natively; compressed formats such as MP3 and M4A need ffmpeg. Undecodable or hostile input returns NULL (scalars) or no rows (table functions) rather than raising, so a bad row never poisons a batch.

Reach for this schema to index, filter, or cluster audio collections by their acoustic properties without leaving SQL.

A **browsable table** (no arguments) listing the worker's built-in example audio clips, one row each: `name`, a one-line `description`, the decoded `duration`/`sample_rate`/`channels`, the detected `beat_count`, and the raw `audio` `BLOB`.

## audio.beats

A **table function** that returns the **detected beat onset times** of a recording, one row per beat: `(seq BIGINT, time DOUBLE)`. Accepts a `VARCHAR` path or a `BLOB` of audio bytes.

**When to use.** Build a beat grid for visualisation or editing, segment a track on its beats, count beats, or align events to the rhythm.

**Output.** `seq` is the 0-based, ascending beat index; `time` is the onset in seconds. Beats are found by librosa's beat tracker on a bounded mono signal -- a **heuristic**, strongest on material with a clear pulse. Returns **no rows** for `NULL`/undecodable input or audio with no detectable beat; it never raises.

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## audio.spectral_centroid

Return the **mean spectral centroid in Hz** as a `DOUBLE` -- the amplitude-weighted center of mass of the magnitude spectrum, the standard measure of timbral brightness. Accepts a `VARCHAR` path or a `BLOB` of bytes.

**When to use.** Quantify brightness to rank or cluster sounds (bright/sharp vs dark/dull), gate on tone colour, or feed a similarity model.

**Behavior.** Computed per analysis frame and averaged over a bounded mono signal resampled to 22.05 kHz, so the value ranges from `0` up to the Nyquist limit of ~11 kHz; brighter sounds sit higher. It is energy-weighted, so near-silent frames contribute little. `NULL` on `NULL` or undecodable input.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# spectral_centroid

Mean **spectral centroid in Hz** (`DOUBLE`) -- spectral brightness.


Higher = brighter/sharper timbre. Analysis runs at 22.05 kHz, so values top out near the ~11 kHz Nyquist limit. Also accepts a `BLOB` of raw bytes. `NULL` for undecodable input.

## audio.estimated_key

Estimate the **musical key** of a recording, e.g. `'C major'` or `'A minor'`, as a `VARCHAR`. Accepts a `VARCHAR` path or a `BLOB` of bytes.

functions.name: mfcc
functions.comment: Mean of each of 13 MFCC coefficients, from a file path

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## audio.mfcc

Return the **mean of each Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC)** over the whole clip as a `DOUBLE[]` -- a compact timbral fingerprint.

**Signature.** `mfcc(audio)` or `mfcc(audio, n)`. `audio` is a `VARCHAR` path or a `BLOB` of raw bytes; the optional `n` sets how many coefficients to keep (default `13`, clamped to `[1, 128]`), and the result is a length-`n` list of per-coefficient means.

**When to use.** A ready-made feature vector for audio similarity search, clustering, or classification -- store the list per recording and compare with a distance metric.

**Caveats for ML.** The first coefficient (`MFCC-0`) tracks overall log-energy/loudness rather than timbre and can dominate a raw Euclidean distance -- drop it or weight it down for timbral similarity. The means are unnormalized and the coefficients live on different scales, so standardize (z-score) them across your corpus before computing distances. Averaging over the whole clip also discards how timbre evolves over time. Returns `NULL` on `NULL` or undecodable input.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# mfcc

Per-coefficient **MFCC means** over the clip as a `DOUBLE[]` (a timbral fingerprint).

```sql
SELECT audio.main.mfcc('/music/track.wav');       -- 13 coefficient means
SELECT audio.main.mfcc('/music/track.wav', 20);   -- keep 20 instead
```

Call it as `mfcc(audio)` or `mfcc(audio, n)`: the optional `n` (default 13, clamped to 1..128) sets the vector length, and `audio` is a path or a `BLOB`.

**Using it as an ML feature.** `MFCC-0` (the first entry) mostly reflects overall loudness, not timbre -- drop or down-weight it for similarity. The means are unnormalized and per-coefficient scales differ, so z-score them across your data before Euclidean distance. `NULL` for undecodable input.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT audio.main.mfcc(from_base64(''))

vgi.example_queries.description: Keep 20 MFCC coefficients instead of the default 13.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT audio.main.mfcc(from_base64(''), 20)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## audio.mfcc

Return the **mean of each Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC)** over the whole clip as a `DOUBLE[]` -- a compact timbral fingerprint.

**Signature.** `mfcc(audio)` or `mfcc(audio, n)`. `audio` is a `VARCHAR` path or a `BLOB` of raw bytes; the optional `n` sets how many coefficients to keep (default `13`, clamped to `[1, 128]`), and the result is a length-`n` list of per-coefficient means.

**When to use.** A ready-made feature vector for audio similarity search, clustering, or classification -- store the list per recording and compare with a distance metric.

**Caveats for ML.** The first coefficient (`MFCC-0`) tracks overall log-energy/loudness rather than timbre and can dominate a raw Euclidean distance -- drop it or weight it down for timbral similarity. The means are unnormalized and the coefficients live on different scales, so standardize (z-score) them across your corpus before computing distances. Averaging over the whole clip also discards how timbre evolves over time. Returns `NULL` on `NULL` or undecodable input.

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## audio.tempo

Estimate the **tempo of a recording in beats per minute** as a `DOUBLE`, using librosa's onset/beat analysis. Accepts a `VARCHAR` path or a `BLOB` of bytes.

**When to use.** Sort a music library by speed, find tracks within a BPM range for a playlist or DJ set, or cluster rhythmically similar audio.

**Behavior.** This is a **heuristic estimate** -- it can land on a half/double-time multiple of the perceived tempo, and is unreliable on material with no steady pulse. Computed on a bounded mono signal at a fixed analysis rate. `NULL` on `NULL` or undecodable input.

functions.name: channels
functions.comment: Number of audio channels (1=mono, 2=stereo), from a file path

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## audio.channels

Return the **number of audio channels** in a recording as an `INTEGER` (`1` = mono, `2` = stereo, higher for surround). Accepts either a `VARCHAR` filesystem path or a `BLOB` of raw audio bytes.

**When to use.** Separate mono from stereo material, flag unexpected channel layouts before mixing, or pick a down-mix strategy.

**Behavior.** The count is read from the container header, which is exact for WAV/FLAC/OGG. Only when the header cannot be read does the worker fall back to a decode, and because that analysis path is mono it then reports `1` -- so a `1` from a header-less source means 'decodable as mono', not a guaranteed true channel count. Returns `NULL` for `NULL` input and for anything undecodable; it never raises.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# channels

Number of **audio channels** (`INTEGER`): `1` = mono, `2` = stereo, more for surround.

```sql
-- Path input:
SELECT audio.main.channels('/music/track.wav');
-- Bytes input (a BLOB column or literal):
SELECT audio.main.channels(audio_bytes);
```

Read from the file header (exact for WAV/FLAC/OGG). If only a decode is possible the worker's mono analysis path reports `1`. `NULL` for `NULL` or undecodable input.

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## audio.zero_crossing_rate

Return the **mean zero-crossing rate** of the signal as a `DOUBLE` -- the average fraction of adjacent samples where the waveform changes sign. Accepts a `VARCHAR` path or a `BLOB` of bytes.

**When to use.** A cheap timbre/noisiness cue: percussive, noisy, or unvoiced content has a high ZCR; smooth tonal content a low one. Useful for rough speech-vs-music or voiced-vs-unvoiced splits.

**Behavior.** Computed per analysis frame over a bounded mono signal and averaged; the value is a fraction in `0`..`1` (the share of sample pairs that cross zero). It tracks high-frequency/noise content but is not a pitch or frequency estimate. `NULL` on `NULL` or undecodable input.

workers.title: Azure Cost Management
workers.subtitle: Daily Azure actual and amortized cost as typed SQL rows, with restatement-aware incremental loading.
workers.summary: Azure Cost Management (actual/amortized cost) as typed DuckDB rows over a restatement-aware date watermark — apply by OVERWRITE keyed on (scope,date,dims) — vgi-azure-cost
workers.doc_md:
## Azure Cost Management

Azure Cost Management actual/amortized cost as typed DuckDB rows over a restatement-aware date watermark, exposed as one DuckDB table function.

- **`cost_query`** — Actual or amortized cost for an ARM scope over a trailing restatement window, as (date, grouping dims, Float64 cost, currency) rows plus a marker row carrying the next watermark.

Read data rows with `WHERE _row_kind IS NULL`. Take the next `from` watermark from the single marker row's `_watermark_next`, and OVERWRITE the window `[_restated_from, _watermark_next]` keyed on (scope, date, grouping dims) — never a blind INSERT (that double-counts on every restatement). An app-only `azure_graph` secret (Microsoft Entra client credentials with Cost Management reader access) is required; tokens are minted for the ARM audience.

### Sources and references

- [Azure Cost Management overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/overview-cost-management) — what the actual/amortized cost data is
- [Cost Management Query - Usage REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/cost-management/query/usage) — the `Microsoft.CostManagement/query` endpoint `cost_query` calls
- [Assign access to Cost Management data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/assign-access-acm-data) — which role the service principal needs on each scope
- [Register an app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app) — create the app-only client credentials for the `azure_graph` secret

example_queries.title: cost_bind_probe
example_queries.description: Bind cost_query and expose its result columns (credential-free; drop LIMIT 0 and attach an azure_graph secret to pull real daily cost)
example_queries.sql: SELECT date, cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-31') LIMIT 0;

example_queries.title: cost_grouped_bind_probe
example_queries.description: Bind cost_query grouped by resource group and expose its result columns, including the ResourceGroup dimension column (credential-free)
example_queries.sql: SELECT date, "ResourceGroup", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-31', group_by := 'Dimension:ResourceGroup') LIMIT 0;

example_queries.title: list_group_by_dimensions
example_queries.description: Browse the credential-free dimensions manifest to discover the group_by tokens cost_query accepts (runs with no secret)
example_queries.sql: SELECT token, kind FROM azure.main.dimensions ORDER BY kind, token;

example_queries.description: Daily actual cost by resource group for June (data rows only; the date filter drops the 7-day restatement lookback the scan also re-pulls)
example_queries.sql: SELECT date, "ResourceGroup", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ResourceGroup') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ResourceGroup"

example_queries.description: Monthly amortized cost totals for January–June (the date filter drops the open prior month the amortized lookback also re-pulls)
example_queries.sql: SELECT date, cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-01-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Monthly', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-01-01' ORDER BY date

example_queries.description: Read the restatement watermark to persist for the next incremental scan
example_queries.sql: SELECT _watermark_next, _restated_from, _key_columns FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30') WHERE _row_kind = 'marker'

example_queries.description: Daily cost by service and cost-center tag for June (multi-axis grouping; restatement-lookback days filtered out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT date, "ServiceName", "costcenter", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName,TagKey:costcenter') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ServiceName", "costcenter"

example_queries.description: Actual vs amortized June cost per service, from two cost_query scans joined on ServiceName; amortization_shift (amortized − actual) shows where reservation/savings-plan purchases are spread out (largest absolute shift first; the date filter drops the restatement-lookback days each scan re-pulls)
example_queries.sql: WITH actual AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS actual_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL), amortized AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS amortized_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL) SELECT "ServiceName", currency, round(coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS actual_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0), 2) AS amortized_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0) - coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS amortization_shift FROM actual FULL JOIN amortized USING ("ServiceName", currency) ORDER BY abs(amortization_shift) DESC, "ServiceName"

example_queries.description: List the Dimension group_by tokens cost_query accepts
example_queries.sql: SELECT token, description FROM azure.main.dimensions WHERE kind = 'Dimension' ORDER BY token

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The Azure Cost Management query function. cost_query returns actual or amortized cost for an ARM scope (subscription, resource group, billing account, management group) over a trailing restatement window as typed rows — an ISO date, one column per requested grouping dimension, a Float64 cost, and a currency — followed by one marker row whose _watermark_next is the high-water `to` to persist as the next `from`. Because past-day costs are restated for days-to-weeks, each scan re-pulls [from−lookback, to] and the caller overwrites that window keyed on (scope, date, grouping dims). Requires an app-only azure_graph secret with Cost Management reader access.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Azure Cost Management query

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `cost_query` | actual/amortized cost rows + restatement watermark marker |

Read data rows with `WHERE _row_kind IS NULL`; take the next `from` watermark from the single marker row's `_watermark_next` and OVERWRITE `[_restated_from, _watermark_next]` keyed on (scope, date, grouping dims). Requires an app-only `azure_graph` secret (ARM audience).

vgi.example_queries.description: Daily actual cost by resource group for June (data rows only; the date filter drops the 7-day restatement lookback the scan also re-pulls)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, "ResourceGroup", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ResourceGroup') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ResourceGroup"

vgi.example_queries.description: Monthly amortized cost totals for January–June (the date filter drops the open prior month the amortized lookback also re-pulls)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-01-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Monthly', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-01-01' ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the restatement watermark to persist for the next incremental scan
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT _watermark_next, _restated_from, _key_columns FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30') WHERE _row_kind = 'marker'

vgi.example_queries.description: Daily cost by service and cost-center tag for June (multi-axis grouping; restatement-lookback days filtered out)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, "ServiceName", "costcenter", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName,TagKey:costcenter') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ServiceName", "costcenter"

vgi.example_queries.description: Actual vs amortized June cost per service, from two cost_query scans joined on ServiceName; amortization_shift (amortized − actual) shows where reservation/savings-plan purchases are spread out (largest absolute shift first; the date filter drops the restatement-lookback days each scan re-pulls)
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH actual AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS actual_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL), amortized AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS amortized_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL) SELECT "ServiceName", currency, round(coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS actual_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0), 2) AS amortized_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0) - coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS amortization_shift FROM actual FULL JOIN amortized USING ("ServiceName", currency) ORDER BY abs(amortization_shift) DESC, "ServiceName"

tags.vgi.doc_llm: A static, credential-free manifest of the grouping tokens the cost_query `group_by` argument accepts. One row per token with its kind (Dimension or TagKey) and a one-line description. Browse this view to learn which `group_by` values are valid before supplying credentials — each `token` value drops straight into group_by (comma-join several to break cost down along multiple axes). TagKey:<name> is a template: replace <name> with one of your own resource tag keys such as costcenter or env.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## dimensions

A credential-free manifest of the `group_by` tokens `cost_query` accepts — a browsable entry point for discovery. Each row is one `token` (e.g. `Dimension:ResourceGroup`), its `kind` (`Dimension` or `TagKey`), and a short `description`. Drop a `token` value straight into `cost_query(..., group_by := <token>)`; comma-join several to group along multiple axes. `TagKey:<name>` is a template — replace `<name>` with one of your resource tag keys.

vgi.example_queries.description: List the Dimension group_by tokens cost_query accepts
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT token, description FROM azure.main.dimensions WHERE kind = 'Dimension' ORDER BY token

functions.name: cost_query
functions.comment: Azure Cost Management actual/amortized cost over a trailing RESTATEMENT window, as typed DuckDB rows (date, grouping dims, Float64 cost, currency). Costs are restated retroactively, so each scan re-pulls [from−lookback, to] and the caller MUST apply by OVERWRITE keyed on (scope, date, grouping dims) — never a blind INSERT (that double-counts, SPEC §2 #2). The new high-water `to` rides back on a marker row as _watermark_next (persist only after the rows are durable); _restated_from is the low edge to overwrite; _key_columns guards the group_by key shape — a change is a full reload, not an incremental resume (§2 #3). Continuation pages re-POST the ORIGINAL query body (the $skiptoken is in the nextLink URL). AUDIENCE: arm.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Query Azure Cost Management for actual or amortized cost of an ARM scope over a trailing restatement window, returned as typed rows: an ISO `date`, one Utf8 column per grouping dimension named in `group_by`, a Float64 `cost`, and a `currency`. Because Azure restates past-day costs for days-to-weeks, each scan re-pulls [from−lookback, to] and the caller MUST apply by OVERWRITE keyed on (scope, date, grouping dims) — never a blind INSERT. Read data rows with `WHERE _row_kind IS NULL`; the single marker row carries `_watermark_next` (persist as the next `from`), `_restated_from` (low edge to overwrite), and `_key_columns` (the group_by key shape). Requires an app-only azure_graph secret (ARM audience).
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## cost_query

Azure Cost Management actual/amortized cost for an ARM scope over a trailing restatement window. The output schema is DEFERRED — it is derived at bind time from the `group_by` argument (one extra column per grouping dimension), so it varies by call.

Read data rows with `WHERE _row_kind IS NULL`. Persist the marker row's `_watermark_next` as the next `from`, and apply each scan by OVERWRITE over `[_restated_from, _watermark_next]` keyed on (scope, date, grouping dims) — never a blind INSERT (that double-counts on every restatement). Grouping tokens (`Dimension:…` / `TagKey:…`) each add a result column and join the overwrite key; `cost_type := 'AmortizedCost'` spreads reservation/savings-plan purchases across their benefit period.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, "ResourceGroup", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ResourceGroup') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ResourceGroup"

vgi.example_queries.description: Monthly amortized cost totals for January–June (the date filter drops the open prior month the amortized lookback also re-pulls)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-01-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Monthly', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-01-01' ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the restatement watermark to persist for the next incremental scan
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT _watermark_next, _restated_from, _key_columns FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30') WHERE _row_kind = 'marker'

vgi.example_queries.description: Daily cost by service and cost-center tag for June (multi-axis grouping; restatement-lookback days filtered out)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, "ServiceName", "costcenter", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName,TagKey:costcenter') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ServiceName", "costcenter"

vgi.example_queries.description: Actual vs amortized June cost per service, from two cost_query scans joined on ServiceName; amortization_shift (amortized − actual) shows where reservation/savings-plan purchases are spread out (largest absolute shift first; the date filter drops the restatement-lookback days each scan re-pulls)
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH actual AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS actual_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL), amortized AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS amortized_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL) SELECT "ServiceName", currency, round(coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS actual_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0), 2) AS amortized_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0) - coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS amortization_shift FROM actual FULL JOIN amortized USING ("ServiceName", currency) ORDER BY abs(amortization_shift) DESC, "ServiceName"

tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
The result schema is DEFERRED — decided at bind time from the `group_by` argument. **One extra `VARCHAR` column is injected per grouping token**, named exactly as the dimension/tag key (e.g. `group_by := 'Dimension:ResourceGroup,TagKey:costcenter'` adds a `ResourceGroup` and a `costcenter` column), positioned between `date` and `cost`. The two variant tables below show the default ungrouped shape and a representative grouped shape.

### Default (empty `group_by`) — no dimension columns

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| date | VARCHAR | ISO date of the cost bucket (per `granularity`). NULL on the marker row. |
| cost | DOUBLE | Cost for the bucket (Float64). NULL on the marker row. |
| currency | VARCHAR | Billing currency code (e.g. USD). NULL on the marker row. |
| _row_kind | VARCHAR | NULL for data rows; `marker` for the single trailing cursor row. |
| _watermark_next | VARCHAR | On the marker row, the new high-water `to` to persist and pass back as the next `from`; NULL on data rows. |
| _restated_from | VARCHAR | On the marker row, the low edge of the overwritten (restated) window; NULL on data rows. |
| _key_columns | VARCHAR | On the marker row, the ordered grouping-key column set (comma-joined) guarding the group_by key shape; NULL on data rows. |

### Grouped (e.g. `group_by := 'Dimension:ResourceGroup'`) — one extra dimension column

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| date | VARCHAR | ISO date of the cost bucket (per `granularity`). NULL on the marker row. |
| ResourceGroup | VARCHAR | The grouping-dimension value (one such column per `group_by` token); part of the overwrite key. NULL on the marker row. |
| cost | DOUBLE | Cost for the bucket (Float64). NULL on the marker row. |
| currency | VARCHAR | Billing currency code (e.g. USD). NULL on the marker row. |
| _row_kind | VARCHAR | NULL for data rows; `marker` for the single trailing cursor row. |
| _watermark_next | VARCHAR | On the marker row, the new high-water `to` to persist and pass back as the next `from`; NULL on data rows. |
| _restated_from | VARCHAR | On the marker row, the low edge of the overwritten (restated) window; NULL on data rows. |
| _key_columns | VARCHAR | On the marker row, the ordered grouping-key column set (comma-joined) guarding the group_by key shape; NULL on data rows. |

arguments.name: scope
arguments.description: The ARM scope to query, e.g. `subscriptions/{id}`, `providers/Microsoft.Billing/billingAccounts/{id}`, `managementGroups/{id}`, or `subscriptions/{id}/resourceGroups/{name}`. Required (positional). The service principal in the azure_graph secret must have Cost Management reader access on this scope.

arguments.name: from
arguments.description: Low edge of the requested window (ISO date or instant, e.g. `2026-06-01`). This IS the caller-held watermark: on an incremental scan pass back the prior scan's `_watermark_next`. The function re-pulls a trailing restatement window starting `from − restatement_lookback_days` (open-period-clamped for AmortizedCost). Required (positional).

arguments.name: to
arguments.description: High edge of the requested window (ISO date or instant), typically today (UTC). Rides back on the marker row as `_watermark_next`, the new high-water watermark to persist. Required (positional).

arguments.name: cost_type
arguments.description: `ActualCost` (billed cost as incurred) or `AmortizedCost` (reservation/savings-plan purchases spread across the benefit period). AmortizedCost auto-widens the trailing lookback toward the open, still-restating billing period (capped). Named (name:=value). Defaults to `ActualCost`.

arguments.name: granularity
arguments.description: Time bucketing of the returned rows: `Daily`, `Monthly`, or `None` (a single total over the window). Named (name:=value). Defaults to `Daily`.

arguments.name: group_by
arguments.description: Comma-separated grouping list, each token `Dimension:Name` or `TagKey:Name` (e.g. `Dimension:ResourceGroup,TagKey:costcenter`; a bare token defaults to a Dimension). Each becomes an extra result column and part of the overwrite key. Empty (the default) returns an ungrouped total. CHANGING this between scans changes the overwrite-key shape → full reload, not incremental. Named (name:=value).

arguments.name: restatement_lookback_days
arguments.description: Size in days of the trailing ActualCost restatement window re-pulled on each scan (effFrom = from − this). Guards against retroactive restatement of recently-reported costs. Named (name:=value). Defaults to 7. (AmortizedCost instead uses an open-period clamp.)

examples: SELECT date, "ResourceGroup", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ResourceGroup') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ResourceGroup"

SELECT date, cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-01-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Monthly', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-01-01' ORDER BY date
SELECT _watermark_next, _restated_from, _key_columns FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30') WHERE _row_kind = 'marker'

SELECT date, "ServiceName", "costcenter", cost, currency FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', granularity := 'Daily', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName,TagKey:costcenter') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date >= '2026-06-01' ORDER BY date, "ServiceName", "costcenter"

WITH actual AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS actual_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL), amortized AS (SELECT "ServiceName", currency, sum(cost) AS amortized_cost FROM azure.main.cost_query('subscriptions/<guid>', '2026-06-01', '2026-06-30', cost_type := 'AmortizedCost', group_by := 'Dimension:ServiceName') WHERE _row_kind IS NULL AND date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY ALL) SELECT "ServiceName", currency, round(coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS actual_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0), 2) AS amortized_cost, round(coalesce(amortized_cost, 0) - coalesce(actual_cost, 0), 2) AS amortization_shift FROM actual FULL JOIN amortized USING ("ServiceName", currency) ORDER BY abs(amortization_shift) DESC, "ServiceName"

workers.subtitle: Incremental SQL feeds of Microsoft 365 Defender / Sentinel security incidents and alerts for security teams.
workers.summary: Microsoft 365 Defender / Sentinel incidents & alerts via Microsoft Graph security API — lastUpdateDateTime watermark cursor (safety-lag, ge boundary, dedup-by-id). vgi-azure-defender
workers.doc_md:
## Microsoft Defender Security

Incremental (watermark) access to Microsoft 365 Defender / Microsoft Sentinel security data via the Microsoft Graph security API: an incidents feed (each incident with its correlated alerts, `$expand=alerts`) and the authoritative alerts (`alerts_v2`) feed.

Each feed returns changed rows plus a single marker row (`_row_kind = 'marker'`) whose `_watermark_next` column holds the ISO-8601 cursor to persist and replay as the next scan's `since`. Call with no arguments for a bounded cold start; pass `since := '<_watermark_next>'` for an incremental sync. The incident watermark does NOT guarantee alert-level freshness — use the alerts feed for authoritative alert completeness. An app-only `azure_graph` secret (Microsoft Entra client credentials) is required.

### Sources and references

- [Microsoft Graph security API overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/security-api-overview) — the incidents/alerts data model
- [List incidents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-list-incidents) — the `/security/incidents` endpoint behind `security_incidents`
- [List alerts_v2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/security-list-alerts_v2) — the `/security/alerts_v2` endpoint behind `security_alerts`
- [Microsoft Graph permissions reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/permissions-reference) — `SecurityIncident.Read.All` / `SecurityAlert.Read.All` application permissions
- [Register an app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app) — create the app-only client credentials for the `azure_graph` secret

example_queries.title: incidents_bind_probe
example_queries.description: Bind security_incidents and expose its result columns (credential-free; drop LIMIT 0 and attach an azure_graph secret to sync real incidents)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, incident_id, display_name, status, severity, _row_kind, _watermark_next FROM azure.main.security_incidents() LIMIT 0;

example_queries.title: alerts_bind_probe
example_queries.description: Bind security_alerts and expose its result columns (credential-free; attach an azure_graph secret to sync real alerts)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, incident_id, title, status, severity, category, _row_kind, _watermark_next FROM azure.main.security_alerts() LIMIT 0;

example_queries.title: list_feeds
example_queries.description: List the catalog's security feeds from the credential-free manifest view (runs with no secret)
example_queries.sql: SELECT feed, source_endpoint, requires_secret FROM azure.main.feeds ORDER BY feed;

example_queries.description: Cold-start sync of open high-severity incidents
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, display_name, severity, status FROM azure.main.security_incidents() WHERE _row_kind = 'incident' AND severity = 'high' AND status = 'active'

example_queries.description: Incremental incident sync from a saved watermark
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, display_name, status FROM azure.main.security_incidents(since := '<_watermark_next>') WHERE _row_kind = 'incident'

example_queries.description: Read the watermark cursor to persist for the next scan
example_queries.sql: SELECT _watermark_next FROM azure.main.security_incidents() WHERE _row_kind = 'marker'

example_queries.description: Authoritative alert feed, high severity only
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, title, severity, category FROM azure.main.security_alerts() WHERE _row_kind = 'alert' AND severity = 'high'

example_queries.description: Active incidents ranked by how many distinct MITRE ATT&CK techniques their alerts carry in the authoritative security_alerts feed (incidents with no technique-tagged alert in the window are omitted)
example_queries.sql: SELECT i.id, i.display_name, i.severity, count(DISTINCT t.technique) AS technique_count, list_sort(list(DISTINCT t.technique)) AS techniques FROM azure.main.security_incidents() AS i JOIN (SELECT incident_id, unnest(mitre_techniques) AS technique FROM azure.main.security_alerts() WHERE _row_kind = 'alert') AS t ON t.incident_id = i.id WHERE i._row_kind = 'incident' AND i.status = 'active' GROUP BY i.id, i.display_name, i.severity ORDER BY technique_count DESC, i.id

example_queries.description: For incidents whose expanded alert set was capped (_alerts_truncated), list every alert from the authoritative security_alerts feed updated in the same lookback window
example_queries.sql: SELECT a.incident_id, a.id AS alert_id, a.title, a.severity, a.status FROM azure.main.security_alerts() AS a WHERE a._row_kind = 'alert' AND a.incident_id IN (SELECT id FROM azure.main.security_incidents() WHERE _row_kind = 'incident' AND _alerts_truncated) ORDER BY a.incident_id, a.id

example_queries.description: Cold-start sync of all alerts (alert rows only)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, title, severity, category FROM azure.main.security_alerts() WHERE _row_kind = 'alert'

example_queries.description: Incremental sync replaying a previously saved watermark cursor
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, title, status FROM azure.main.security_alerts(since := '<_watermark_next>') WHERE _row_kind = 'alert'

example_queries.description: High-severity alerts only
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, title, severity FROM azure.main.security_alerts() WHERE _row_kind = 'alert' AND severity = 'high'

example_queries.description: Read the watermark cursor to persist for the next sync
example_queries.sql: SELECT _watermark_next FROM azure.main.security_alerts() WHERE _row_kind = 'marker'

example_queries.description: Server-side severity pushdown via the OData filter argument (fetches fewer rows than a client-side WHERE)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, title, severity FROM azure.main.security_alerts(filter := 'severity eq ''high''') WHERE _row_kind = 'alert'

example_queries.description: Cold-start sync of all incidents (incident rows only)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, display_name, severity, status FROM azure.main.security_incidents() WHERE _row_kind = 'incident'

example_queries.description: The alerts correlated to each incident (convenience join; use security_alerts for completeness)
example_queries.sql: SELECT incident_id, title, severity FROM azure.main.security_incidents() WHERE _row_kind = 'alert'

example_queries.description: Server-side severity pushdown via the OData filter argument (fetches fewer rows than a client-side WHERE)
