tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Cloudflare Access

Cloudflare Access (Zero Trust application security): protected applications, access policies, identity providers, service tokens, groups, certificates, and authentication logs.

Use for questions about who can reach which internal application and how: Access applications and their policies, identity provider configuration, service tokens for machine access, mTLS certificates, and login/request audit logs. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **Apps** — Apps: Get an Access application; List Access applications; List short-lived certificate CAs; ….
- **AI Controls** — AI Controls: Resolve an MCP server OAuth redirect URI; List MCP Portals; Read details of an MCP Portal; ….
- **Identity Providers** — Identity Providers: Get an Access identity provider; List Access identity providers; List SCIM Group resources; ….
- **Users** — Users: Get active sessions; Get failed logins; Get last seen identity; ….
- **Certificates** — Certificates: Get an mTLS certificate; List mTLS certificates; List all mTLS hostname settings.
- **Groups** — Groups: Get an Access group; List Access groups.
- **Logs** — Logs: List Access JIT request logs; Get an Access JIT request log; Get Access authentication logs; ….
- **Service Tokens** — Service Tokens: Get a service token; List service tokens.
- **Organizations** — Organizations: Get your Zero Trust organization DoH settings; Get your Zero Trust organization.
- **Bookmarks** — Bookmarks: Get a Bookmark application; List Bookmark applications.
- **Custom Pages** — Custom Pages: Get a custom page; List custom pages.
- **More APIs** — Smaller API areas: Idp Federation Grants, Policies, Policy Tests, Saml Certificates, Tags, User Populations, Authenticator Device Aaguids, Gateway Ca, Keys.

# cloudflare.access.effective_redirect_uri

Resolve an MCP server OAuth redirect URI. Reads the effective redirect uri object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/access/ai-controls/mcp/portals/{portal_id}/servers/{server_id}/effective-redirect-uri`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. # Cloudflare Accounts & Identity

Cloudflare accounts and identity: the accounts a token can see, their members and roles, API tokens, permission groups, organizations, tenants, and the token's own user profile.

Start here to find account ids (cloudflare.accounts.accounts) for every account-scoped table, to audit membership and roles, or to inspect API tokens and permission groups. cloudflare.accounts.user describes the user that owns the current token.

## Sections

- **User** — User: Get user audit logs; Billing Profile Details; Get communication preferences; ….
- **Organizations** — Organizations: List account organizations; Get organization audit logs (Version 2); Get resource change history from an organization audit log entry (Version 2); ….
- **IAM** — IAM: List Account Permission Groups; Permission Group Details; Resource Group Details; ….
- **Shares** — Shares: List share resources by share ID; Get share excluded recipient by ID; List share excluded recipients by share ID; ….
- **Tenants** — Tenants: List Tenant Custom Nameservers; List tenant entitlements; Get tenant details; ….
- **Reporting** — Reporting: Get an account industry; List reporting policies; Get a reporting policy; ….
- **Subscriptions** — Subscriptions: Get Subscription; List Subscriptions; Get Cancel Reason; ….
- **Tokens** — Tokens: Token Details; List Tokens; Verify Token; ….
- **Resource Library** — Resource Library: List applications; Get application; List application categories; ….
- **Tags** — Tags: List tagged resources; List tag key summary; Get tags for an account-level resource; ….
- **Accounts** — Accounts: A single account by id (GET /accounts/{account_id}); Accounts the API token can access.
- **More APIs** — Smaller API areas: Members, Memberships, OAUTH Clients, Roles, SSO Connectors, Profile, OAUTH, API.

# cloudflare.accounts.tokens

List Tokens. One row per token, from Cloudflare GET `/user/tokens`.

## Endpoint

List all access tokens you created. Results include active, disabled, and recently-expired tokens when include_expired is set to true.

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `condition` | VARCHAR | — |
| `creator_email_at_creation` | VARCHAR | The email address of the user who created the token at the time of creation. Only present for Account Owned API Tokens when a creator email was available. |
| `expires_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | The expiration time on or after which the JWT MUST NOT be accepted for processing. |
| `id` | VARCHAR | Token identifier tag. |
| `issued_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | The time on which the token was created. |
| `last_used_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Last time the token was used. |
| `modified_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Last time the token was modified. |
| `name` | VARCHAR | Token name. |
| `not_before` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | The time before which the token MUST NOT be accepted for processing. |
| `policies` | VARCHAR | List of access policies assigned to the token. |
| `provisioner_id` | VARCHAR | The identifier of the service that provisioned the token. For an OAuth-provisioned token, this is the OAuth client identifier. Present when `provisioner_type` is present and null when the identifier is unavailable. |
| `provisioner_type` | VARCHAR | The type of service that provisioned the token. Only present for provisioned Account Owned API Tokens. |
| `status` | VARCHAR | Status of the token. One of: `active`, `disabled`, `expired`. |

# cloudflare.accounts.monitors

List Monitors. One row per monitor, from Cloudflare GET `/user/load_balancers/monitors`.

## Endpoint

List configured monitors for a user.

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_insecure` | BOOLEAN | Do not validate the certificate when monitor use HTTPS. This parameter is currently only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors. |
| `consecutive_down` | BIGINT | To be marked unhealthy the monitored origin must fail this healthcheck N consecutive times. |
| `consecutive_up` | BIGINT | To be marked healthy the monitored origin must pass this healthcheck N consecutive times. |
| `description` | VARCHAR | Object description. |
| `expected_body` | VARCHAR | A case-insensitive sub-string to look for in the response body. If this string is not found, the origin will be marked as unhealthy. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors. |
| `expected_codes` | VARCHAR | The expected HTTP response code or code range of the health check. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors. |
| `follow_redirects` | BOOLEAN | Follow redirects if returned by the origin. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors. |
| `header` | VARCHAR | The HTTP request headers to send in the health check. It is recommended you set a Host header by default. The User-Agent header cannot be overridden. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors. |
| `interval` | BIGINT | The interval between each health check. Shorter intervals may improve failover time, but will increase load on the origins as we check from multiple locations. |
| `method` | VARCHAR | The method to use for the health check. This defaults to 'GET' for HTTP/HTTPS based checks and 'connection_established' for TCP based health checks. |
| `path` | VARCHAR | The endpoint path you want to conduct a health check against. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors. |
| `port` | BIGINT | The port number to connect to for the health check. Required for TCP, UDP, and SMTP checks. HTTP and HTTPS checks should only define the port when using a non-standard port (HTTP: default 80, HTTPS: default 443). |
| `probe_zone` | VARCHAR | Assign this monitor to emulate the specified zone while probing. This parameter is only valid for HTTP and HTTPS monitors. |
| `retries` | BIGINT | The number of retries to attempt in case of a timeout before marking the origin as unhealthy. Retries are attempted immediately. |
| `timeout` | BIGINT | The timeout (in seconds) before marking the health check as failed. |
| `type` | VARCHAR | The protocol to use for the health check. Currently supported protocols are 'HTTP','HTTPS', 'TCP', 'ICMP-PING', 'UDP-ICMP', and 'SMTP'. One of: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `udp_icmp`, `icmp_ping`, `smtp`. |
| `created_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Example: `2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z`. |
| `id` | VARCHAR | Example: `f1aba936b94213e5b8dca0c0dbf1f9cc`. |
| `modified_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Example: `2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z`. |

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, type, created_on FROM cloudflare.accounts.monitors

# cloudflare.accounts.pools

List Pools. One row per pool, from Cloudflare GET `/user/load_balancers/pools`.

## Endpoint

List configured pools.

## Filters sent to the API

`monitor`

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check_regions` | VARCHAR | A list of regions from which to run health checks. Null means every Cloudflare data center. |
| `created_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Example: `2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z`. |
| `description` | VARCHAR | A human-readable description of the pool. |
| `disabled_at` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | This field shows up only if the pool is disabled. This field is set with the time the pool was disabled at. |
| `enabled` | BOOLEAN | Whether to enable (the default) or disable this pool. Disabled pools will not receive traffic and are excluded from health checks. Disabling a pool will cause any load balancers using it to failover to the next pool (if any). |
| `health_sources` | VARCHAR | A list of health sources, ordered from highest to lowest priority, used to evaluate individual origin health and overall pool health. The load balancer uses the first source that has data and falls back to the next. Currently accepted values are null or the exact array ["regional", "global"]; any other combination is rejected. Null (the default) behaves like ["local", "global"]. ["regional", "glo… |
| `id` | VARCHAR | Example: `17b5962d775c646f3f9725cbc7a53df4`. |
| `latitude` | DOUBLE | The latitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, longitude must also be set. |
| `load_shedding` | VARCHAR | Configures load shedding policies and percentages for the pool. |
| `longitude` | DOUBLE | The longitude of the data center containing the origins used in this pool in decimal degrees. If this is set, latitude must also be set. |
| `minimum_origins` | BIGINT | The minimum number of origins that must be healthy for this pool to serve traffic. If the number of healthy origins falls below this number, the pool will be marked unhealthy and will failover to the next available pool. |
| `modified_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Example: `2014-01-01T05:20:00.12345Z`. |
| `monitor` | VARCHAR | The ID of the Monitor to use for checking the health of origins within this pool. |
| `monitor_group` | VARCHAR | The ID of the Monitor Group to use for checking the health of origins within this pool. |
| `name` | VARCHAR | A short name (tag) for the pool. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores are allowed. |
| `networks` | VARCHAR | List of networks where Load Balancer or Pool is enabled. |
| `notification_email` | VARCHAR | This field is now deprecated. It has been moved to Cloudflare's Centralized Notification service https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/notifications/. The email address to send health status notifications to. This can be an individual mailbox or a mailing list. Multiple emails can be supplied as a comma delimited list. |
| `notification_filter` | VARCHAR | Filter pool and origin health notifications by resource type or health status. Use null to reset. |
| `origin_steering` | VARCHAR | Configures origin steering for the pool. Controls how origins are selected for new sessions and traffic without session affinity. |
| `origins` | VARCHAR | The list of origins within this pool. Traffic directed at this pool is balanced across all currently healthy origins, provided the pool itself is healthy. |

# cloudflare.accounts.usage

Get Organization Usage (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted). Returns every usage from Cloudflare GET `/organizations/{organization_id}/billable/usage` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: organization_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: from_, to_.

## Endpoint

Returns cost and usage data for all accounts within an organization,
aligned with the [FinOps FOCUS v1.3](https://focus.finops.org/focus-specification/v1-3/)
Cost and Usage dataset specification.

Each record represents one billable metric for one account on one day.
This includes all metered usage, including usage that falls within
free-tier allowances and may result in zero cost. The response
includes usage for every account belonging to the specified
organization.

**Note:** This endpoint serves `usage` records only; cost and pricing
fields are absent from responses. Rated costs are available per
account via `POST /accounts/{account_id}/billable/usage` with
`Metric: cost`.

When `from` and `to` are omitted, defaults to the start of the current
month through today. The maximum date range is 31 days.

An organization with no accounts, or an organization ID that does not
exist, returns a successful response with an empty result set rather
than an error.

Returns 37 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.accounts.organization_members

List organization members. Returns every organization member from Cloudflare GET `/organizations/{organization_id}/members` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: organization_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: status, user_email, user_email_startsWith, user_email_endsWith, page_token, page_size.

## Endpoint

List memberships for an Organization.

Authentication: A Global API key for a user with
`com.cloudflare.api.tenant.unit.member.list` is required. User API Tokens are not currently
supported.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.organization_id, r.id, r.status FROM (VALUES ('<organization_id>')) t(organization_id), cloudflare.accounts.organization_members(t.organization_id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only organization members matching a status: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, status, create_time FROM cloudflare.accounts.organization_members('<organization_id>', status := '<status>')

# cloudflare.accounts.audit_history

Get resource change history from an organization audit log entry (Version 2). Returns every audit history from Cloudflare GET `/organizations/{organization_id}/logs/audit/{id}/history` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: organization_id, id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: action_time, since, before.

## Endpoint

Returns the chronological change history for the resource identified by the given organization-scoped audit log entry.

The endpoint first locates the source audit log entry by `id` (using `action_time` to narrow the lookup window), derives identifying filters from that entry, and then returns matching audit logs within the `since`/`before` window.

The `result_info.history_status` field indicates the quality of the resource identification used:
- `exact`: Resource was identified by the resource URI.
- `approximate`: Resource was identified without the resource URI.
- `unavailable`: The source audit log entry did not contain enough information to identify the resource; an empty result is returned.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List audit historys for one organization and one id (organization_id, id: the URL path ids).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT action, actor, organization FROM cloudflare.accounts.audit_history('<organization_id>', '<id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Audit historys for each id in another relation (one API call per row).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.id, r.action, r.actor FROM (VALUES ('<id>')) t(id), cloudflare.accounts.audit_history('<organization_id>', t.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only audit historys matching a action_time: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT action, actor, organization FROM cloudflare.accounts.audit_history('<organization_id>', '<id>', action_time := '<action_time>')

# cloudflare.accounts.applications

List applications. Returns every application from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/resource-library/applications` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: filter, order_by, lookup, fields.

## Endpoint

List the applications available to an account, both the applications Cloudflare
curates and the custom applications the account has defined.

Results are paginated. Use `filter` and `search` to narrow the list, `order_by` to
sort it, and `fields` to reduce each result to only the properties you need.
Use `lookup` to find complete application names mentioned in a rule sentence,
ignoring case. Lookup does not correct misspellings. It ranks matches by
relevance and uses the same filters, fields, and pagination as listing.
`lookup` cannot be combined with `search`.

Invalid UTF-8 or a NUL character (U+0000) in any query parameter name or value
returns `400`.

The authenticated principal must have access to the account identified by
`account_id`.

Returns 20 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.accounts.account_tokens

List Tokens. Returns every account token from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/tokens` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: include_expired.

## Endpoint

List Account Owned API tokens created for this account. Callers with
`com.cloudflare.api.account.token.list_self` permission only receive
tokens they created. Results include active, disabled, and
recently-expired tokens when `include_expired` is set to true.

Returns 14 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List account tokens for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, status FROM cloudflare.accounts.account_tokens('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every account token across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.id, r.name FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.accounts.account_tokens(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only account tokens matching a include_expired: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, status FROM cloudflare.accounts.account_tokens('<account_id>', include_expired := '<include_expired>')

# cloudflare.accounts.zone_tags

Get tags for a zone-level resource. Reads the zone tags object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/tags`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieves tags for a specific zone-level resource.

Returns 9 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the zone tags object for one zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, type FROM cloudflare.accounts.zone_tags('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the zone tags for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.

# cloudflare.accounts.account_organizations

List account organizations. Returns every account organization from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/organizations` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column).

## Endpoint

Retrieve a list of the organizations that "contain" this account or are
managing it.

The returned list will be in order from "root" to "leaf", where the "leaf"
will be the organization that _immediately_ contains the specified
account.

Authentication: Use a Global API key, or a user-owned API Token scoped to the account with
the `Account Settings Read` permission, which grants `com.cloudflare.api.account.read`.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

Get organization. Fetches one organization from Cloudflare GET `/organizations/{organization_id}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: organization_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieve the details of a certain organization.

Authentication: A Global API key for a user with
`com.cloudflare.api.tenant.unit.read` is required. User API Tokens are not currently
supported and return HTTP `403` with error code `10000`.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Fetch one organization by organization_id; an unknown id returns no rows.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, create_time FROM cloudflare.accounts.organization('<organization_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the organization for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.organization_id, d.* EXCLUDE (organization_id) FROM (VALUES ('<organization_id>')) t(organization_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.accounts.organization(t.organization_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: organization_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The ID of the organization to retrieve.

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Example: `a7b9c3d2e8f4a1b5c6d0e9f2a3b7c4d8`.

# cloudflare.accounts.organization_accounts

List organization accounts. Returns every organization account from Cloudflare GET `/organizations/{organization_id}/accounts` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: organization_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: account_pubname, account_pubname_startsWith, account_pubname_endsWith, name, name_startsWith, name_endsWith, order_by, include_tags, include_total, page_token, page_size.

## Endpoint

Retrieve the accounts immediately attached to a specific organization. Accounts
attached to sub-organizations are not included.

Authentication: A Global API key for a user with
`com.cloudflare.api.tenant.unit.read` is required. User API Tokens are not currently
supported.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# Cloudflare AI

Cloudflare AI products: AI Gateway (logging, caching, and rate limiting in front of model providers), AI Search / AutoRAG indexes, Workers AI models, and Vectorize vector indexes.

Use for questions about AI traffic and retrieval infrastructure: AI Gateway gateways, their request logs, datasets and evaluations; AI Search (AutoRAG) instances and indexing jobs; available Workers AI models; and Vectorize indexes. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **AI Gateway** — AI Gateway: Get auto top-up configuration; List custom provider pricing rules; Get a custom provider pricing rule; ….
- **AI Search** — AI Search: List Item Chunks; List AI Search instances; Get an AI Search instance; ….
- **Vectorize** — Vectorize: Get Vectorize Index (Deprecated); List Vectorize Indexes (Deprecated); Get Vectorize Index; ….
- **Agent Memory** — Agent Memory: List namespaces; List memories; Get a memory; ….
- **AI** — AI: Download a Finetune Asset; List Finetunes; List Public Finetunes; ….
- **Autorag** — Autorag: Files; Get a Job Details; List Jobs; ….

# Cloudflare Notifications

Cloudflare Notifications: alert policies, delivery destinations (email, PagerDuty, webhooks), silences, and the history of alerts that fired for an account.

Use to audit what Cloudflare alerts are configured, where they are delivered, which are silenced, and what fired recently (alert history). Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **Alerting** — Alerting: List History; List PagerDuty services; List Notification policies; ….
- **Event Subscriptions** — Event Subscriptions: Get Event Subscription; List Event Subscriptions.

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Cloudflare Analytics

Cloudflare traffic and security analytics from the GraphQL Analytics API: HTTP requests by day or hour, adaptive request samples, firewall events, health checks, and Workers invocations.

Use for time-series questions — traffic volume, bandwidth, threats, cache ratios, firewall actions, Worker errors. Each is a function of a zone_id (account_id for Workers), a literal or per row of cloudflare.zones.zones, with a required window: since := … and until := …. Large windows are split automatically so results aren't truncated.

Firewall and health-check datasets are only available on Cloudflare plans that include them; on other plans the query fails with an explanation rather than returning empty results.

## Sections

- **HTTP Traffic** — Request, bandwidth, threat, and cache rollups for a zone by day, hour, or dimension.
- **Security Events** — WAF and firewall events for a zone, by action, source, country, and rule.
- **Health Checks** — Health-check probes of a zone's origins by hostname, region, origin IP, and status.
- **Workers** — Worker requests, errors, and subrequests for an account by script and status.

vgi.example_queries.description: Each zone's DNS record count beside the last 7 full days' requests and cache-hit percentage; a zone with records but 0 requests is a candidate for cleanup (cached_pct is NULL without traffic).
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH dns AS (SELECT z.id AS zone_id, z.name AS zone, count(*) AS dns_records FROM cloudflare.zones.zones z, cloudflare.dns.records(z.id) r GROUP BY ALL), traffic AS (SELECT t.zone_id, sum(t.requests) AS requests, sum(t.cached_requests) AS cached FROM cloudflare.zones.zones z, cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_daily(z.id, since := current_date - 7, until := current_date - 1) t GROUP BY ALL) SELECT d.zone, d.dns_records, coalesce(t.requests, 0) AS requests, round(100.0 * t.cached / nullif(t.requests, 0), 1) AS cached_pct FROM dns d LEFT JOIN traffic t USING (zone_id) ORDER BY requests DESC, d.zone

vgi.example_queries.description: requests per date for one zone over the last 7 full days.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, requests FROM cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_daily('<zone_id>', since := current_date - 7, until := current_date - 1) ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: requests per datetime for one zone over the last 6 hours.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datetime, requests FROM cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_hourly('<zone_id>', since := date_trunc('hour', now()) - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, until := date_trunc('hour', now())) ORDER BY datetime

vgi.example_queries.description: count per datetime and client_country, host for one zone over the last 6 hours.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datetime, client_country, host, count FROM cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_adaptive('<zone_id>', since := date_trunc('hour', now()) - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, until := date_trunc('hour', now())) ORDER BY datetime

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_adaptive

HTTP requests broken down by country, host, method, and status, from Cloudflare's GraphQL Analytics API (httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups). Call it with a zone_id — a literal, or per row of another query for a lateral join — and a required window, since := … and until := … (inclusive time buckets, UTC; constants or bind-time expressions such as current_date - 7 or now() - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, also in a lateral call; Cloudflare rejects windows older than the dataset's retention, a few days for hourly data). One row per time bucket and combination of client_country, host, method, status, with metrics count, response_bytes. Large windows are paged over several API calls so results aren't truncated.

## Columns

- `datetime` — the time bucket (UTC).
- `client_country` — Visitor country (ISO-2).
- `host` — Requested host.
- `method` — HTTP method.
- `status` — Edge response status code.
- `count` — Estimated requests, adjusted by Cloudflare for sampling. (`count` in GraphQL)
- `response_bytes` — Edge response bytes. (`sum` in GraphQL)

vgi.example_queries.description: count per datetime and client_country, host for one zone over the last 6 hours.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datetime, client_country, host, count FROM cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_adaptive('<zone_id>', since := date_trunc('hour', now()) - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, until := date_trunc('hour', now())) ORDER BY datetime

vgi.example_queries.description: Total count for every zone over the last 6 hours, one API call per zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS zone, sum(x.count) AS count FROM cloudflare.zones.zones p, cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_adaptive(p.id, since := date_trunc('hour', now()) - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, until := date_trunc('hour', now())) x GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY count DESC

# cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_traffic

HTTP traffic by path, user agent, browser, device, and security action. Counts are sampling-adjusted estimates, not sessions. Field access and retention depend on the zone plan. SQL predicates filter returned groups locally; use short since/until windows to bound API work, from Cloudflare's GraphQL Analytics API (httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups). Call it with a zone_id — a literal, or per row of another query for a lateral join — and a required window, since := … and until := … (inclusive time buckets, UTC; constants or bind-time expressions such as current_date - 7 or now() - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, also in a lateral call; Cloudflare rejects windows older than the dataset's retention, a few days for hourly data). One row per time bucket and combination of client_country, host, method, status, path, user_agent, browser, device_type, content_type, request_source, security_action, verified_bot_category, with metrics count, response_bytes, sample_interval. Large windows are paged over several API calls so results aren't truncated.

## Columns

- `datetime` — the time bucket (UTC).
- `client_country` — Client country (ISO-2).
- `host` — Requested host.
- `method` — HTTP method.
- `status` — Edge response status code.

- `response_bytes` — Estimated edge response bytes. (`sum` in GraphQL)
- `sample_interval` — Mean sampling interval; 1 means unsampled. (`avg` in GraphQL)

vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH dns AS (SELECT z.id AS zone_id, z.name AS zone, count(*) AS dns_records FROM cloudflare.zones.zones z, cloudflare.dns.records(z.id) r GROUP BY ALL), traffic AS (SELECT t.zone_id, sum(t.requests) AS requests, sum(t.cached_requests) AS cached FROM cloudflare.zones.zones z, cloudflare.analytics.http_requests_daily(z.id, since := current_date - 7, until := current_date - 1) t GROUP BY ALL) SELECT d.zone, d.dns_records, coalesce(t.requests, 0) AS requests, round(100.0 * t.cached / nullif(t.requests, 0), 1) AS cached_pct FROM dns d LEFT JOIN traffic t USING (zone_id) ORDER BY requests DESC, d.zone

# cloudflare.analytics.firewall_events

Firewall / WAF events grouped by action, source, country, and rule, from Cloudflare's GraphQL Analytics API (firewallEventsAdaptiveGroups). Call it with a zone_id — a literal, or per row of another query for a lateral join — and a required window, since := … and until := … (inclusive time buckets, UTC; constants or bind-time expressions such as current_date - 7 or now() - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, also in a lateral call; Cloudflare rejects windows older than the dataset's retention, a few days for hourly data). One row per time bucket and combination of action, source, client_country, host, rule_id, with metrics count. Large windows are paged over several API calls so results aren't truncated. Only available on plans that include this dataset.

## Columns

- `datetime` — the time bucket (UTC).
- `action` — Mitigation action (block, challenge, allow, ...).
- `source` — Firewall product that fired (waf, firewallrules, ...).
- `client_country` — Client country (ISO-2).
- `host` — Requested host.
- `rule_id` — Matched rule id.
- `count` — Number of firewall events. (`count` in GraphQL)

vgi.example_queries.description: count per datetime and action, source for one zone over the last 6 hours.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datetime, action, source, count FROM cloudflare.analytics.firewall_events('<zone_id>', since := date_trunc('hour', now()) - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, until := date_trunc('hour', now())) ORDER BY datetime

vgi.example_queries.description: Total count for every zone over the last 6 hours, one API call per zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS zone, sum(x.count) AS count FROM cloudflare.zones.zones p, cloudflare.analytics.firewall_events(p.id, since := date_trunc('hour', now()) - INTERVAL 6 HOUR, until := date_trunc('hour', now())) x GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY count DESC

# Cloudflare API Shield

Cloudflare API Shield (API Gateway) for a zone: discovered and managed API operations, endpoint schemas, hostnames, labels, and schema validation configuration.

Use to see which API endpoints Cloudflare has discovered or is protecting on a zone, the uploaded OpenAPI schemas used for validation, and their labels. Most objects are scoped to a zone: they are functions of its zone_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.zones.zones.

## Sections

- **API Gateway** — API Gateway: Get session identifier settings; Export discovered API operations as OpenAPI schemas; List discovered web and API operations; ….
- **Schema Validation** — Schema Validation: Get per-operation schema validation setting; List all uploaded schemas; List hosts covered by uploaded schemas; ….
- **Token Validation** — Token Validation: List token validation configurations; Get a token validation configuration; Get a token validation rule; ….

vgi.example_queries.description: List configs for one zone (zone_id is required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, created_at, credentials FROM cloudflare.api_gateway.config WHERE zone_id = '<zone_id>'

vgi.example_queries.description: Count configs for several zones at once (one API call each).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT zone_id, count(*) AS n FROM cloudflare.api_gateway.config WHERE zone_id IN ('<zone_id_1>', '<zone_id_2>') GROUP BY zone_id

vgi.example_queries.description: List discovery operations for one zone (zone_id is required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, features, last_updated FROM cloudflare.api_gateway.discovery_operations WHERE zone_id = '<zone_id>'

# cloudflare.api_gateway.user_schemas

Retrieve information about all schemas on a zone. Returns every user schema from Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/api_gateway/user_schemas` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: omit_source, validation_enabled.

## Endpoint

Lists all OpenAPI schemas uploaded to API Shield for the zone, including their validation status and associated operations. Deprecated; use `/zones/{zone_id}/schema_validation/schemas` instead.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS zone, r.name, r.created_at FROM cloudflare.zones.zones p, cloudflare.api_gateway.user_schemas(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only user schemas matching a omit_source: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, created_at, kind FROM cloudflare.api_gateway.user_schemas('<zone_id>', omit_source := '<omit_source>')

Arguments, in URL order: zone_id, schema_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: feature, host, method, endpoint, operation_status.

## Endpoint

Retrieves all operations from the schema. Operations that already exist in API Shield Endpoint Management will be returned as full operations.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List schemas operations for one zone and one schema (zone_id, schema_id: the URL path ids).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT endpoint, host, method FROM cloudflare.api_gateway.schemas_operations('<zone_id>', '<schema_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Schemas operations for each schema_id in another relation (one API call per row).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.schema_id, r.endpoint, r.host FROM (VALUES ('<schema_id>')) t(schema_id), cloudflare.api_gateway.schemas_operations('<zone_id>', t.schema_id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only schemas operations matching a feature: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT endpoint, host, method FROM cloudflare.api_gateway.schemas_operations('<zone_id>', '<schema_id>', feature := '<feature>')

# cloudflare.api_gateway.settings

Get global schema validation settings. Reads the settings object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/schema_validation/settings`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieves the current global schema validation settings for a zone.

Returns 3 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the settings object for one zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT validation_default_mitigation_action, validation_override_mitigation_action FROM cloudflare.api_gateway.settings('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the settings for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.api_gateway.settings(t.zone_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The default mitigation action used Mitigation actions are as follows: - `log` - log request when request does not conform to schema - `block` - deny access to the site when request does not conform to schema - `none` - skip running schema validation.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: validation_override_mitigation_action
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When not null, this overrides global both zone level and operation level mitigation actions. This can serve as a quick way to disable schema validation for the whole zone. - `"none"` will skip running schema validation entirely for the request.

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Cloudflare Billing

Cloudflare billing for an account: billable usage and pay-as-you-go usage records, for understanding what an account is charged for.

Use for cost and usage questions about an account's Cloudflare subscription. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **Billing** — Billing: Get account billing usage; Get Account Bad Debt; Get Account Credits; ….
- **Available Plans** — Available Plans: List Available Plans; Available Plan Details.
- **Billable** — Billable: List Account Billable Metrics (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted); Get Account Usage (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted).
- **Billable Usage** — Billable Usage: Get Account Billable Usage (Version 1, Alpha); Get Account Billable Usage Info (Version 1, Alpha).
- **Entitlements** — Entitlements: Get Account Entitlements; Get Zone Entitlements.
- **Payment Methods** — Payment Methods: Get Payment Method; List Payment Methods.
- **Available Rate Plans** — Available Rate Plans: List Available Rate Plans.
- **Subscription** — Subscription: Zone Subscription Details.

# cloudflare.billing.history

Get Account Billing History. Returns every history from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/billing/history` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: status.

## Endpoint

Gets the billing history for an account.

Returns 16 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List historys for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, status, type FROM cloudflare.billing.history('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every history across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.id, r.status FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.billing.history(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only historys matching a status: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, status, type FROM cloudflare.billing.history('<account_id>', status := '<status>')

# cloudflare.billing.unpaid_invoice

Get Unpaid Invoices. Reads the unpaid invoice object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/billing/unpaid-invoice`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

# cloudflare.billing.billable_metrics

List Account Billable Metrics (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted). Returns every billable metric from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/billable/usage/billable-metrics` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: from_, to_.

## Endpoint

Lists billable metrics available to the account through contracts and
subscriptions that overlap the requested period. Results are
deduplicated and ordered. If no qualifying contract exists, the
result is an empty array.

When `from` and `to` are omitted, the period defaults to the start of
the current month through today. The maximum date range is 31 days.

Returns 6 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List billable metrics for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT "DimensionKeys", "Id", "Name" FROM cloudflare.billing.billable_metrics('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every billable metric across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r."DimensionKeys", r."Id" FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.billing.billable_metrics(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only billable metrics matching a from_: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT "DimensionKeys", "Id", "Name" FROM cloudflare.billing.billable_metrics('<account_id>', from_ := '<from_>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: Id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Public catalog identifier of the billable metric.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: Name
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Human-readable billable metric name.

arguments.name: account_id
arguments.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

arguments.name: from_
arguments.description: Start date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `to` is set. When omitted along with `to`, defaults to the start of the current month. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.

arguments.name: to_
arguments.description: End date for the usage query (ISO 8601). Required if `from` is set. When omitted along with `from`, defaults to today. Filters by charge period (when consumption happened), not billing period. The maximum date range is 31 days.

examples: SELECT "DimensionKeys", "Id", "Name" FROM cloudflare.billing.billable_metrics('<account_id>')
SELECT p.name AS account, r."DimensionKeys", r."Id" FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.billing.billable_metrics(p.id) r
SELECT "DimensionKeys", "Id", "Name" FROM cloudflare.billing.billable_metrics('<account_id>', from_ := '<from_>')

result_columns.name: account_id
result_columns.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

result_columns.name: Id
result_columns.description: Public catalog identifier of the billable metric.

result_columns.name: Name
result_columns.description: Human-readable billable metric name.

# cloudflare.billing.usage

Get Account Usage (Version 2, Alpha, Restricted). Returns every usage from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/billable/usage` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: from_, to_.

## Endpoint

Returns cost and usage data for a single Cloudflare account, aligned
with the [FinOps FOCUS v1.3](https://focus.finops.org/focus-specification/v1-3/)
Cost and Usage dataset specification.

Each record represents one billable metric for one account on one day.
This includes all metered usage, including usage that falls within
free-tier allowances and may result in zero cost.

# cloudflare.billing.billable_usage

Get Account Billable Usage (Version 1, Alpha). Returns every billable usage from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/billable-usage` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: from_, to_.

## Endpoint

Returns billable usage data for the account.
When no query parameters are provided, returns usage for the current
billing period.

## Endpoint

Returns the list of entitlements (features and their allocations) for a given account. Each entitlement describes a product feature the account is permitted to use and the allocation value (boolean, count, range, enum, or string) that governs its behaviour.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.billing.zone_entitlements

Get Zone Entitlements. Returns every zone entitlement from Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/entitlements` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id (each is also returned as a column).

## Endpoint

Returns the list of entitlements (features and their allocations) for a given zone. Each entitlement describes a product feature the zone is permitted to use and the allocation value (boolean, count, range, enum, or string) that governs its behaviour.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List zone entitlements for one zone (zone_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, allocation, created_date FROM cloudflare.billing.zone_entitlements('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS zone, r.id, r.allocation FROM cloudflare.zones.zones p, cloudflare.billing.zone_entitlements(p.id) r

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: zone_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Zone id: the id column of cloudflare.zones.zones.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: allocation
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Represents the allocation value for an entitlement. The shape of `value` depends on `type`: `bool` uses a boolean, `max_count` uses an integer, `enum_number` uses an array of numbers, `range` uses an object with `min` and `max` integer fields, and `string` uses a string.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: created_date
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (microsecond precision, no timezone offset) when the entitlement was created. Format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff`.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: deleted_date
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the entitlement was deleted, or empty string if not deleted.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: edited_date
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (microsecond precision, no timezone offset) when the entitlement was last edited.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: feature
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Describes a product feature associated with an entitlement.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Entitlement identifier — equal to the feature key.

# Cloudflare DNS

Cloudflare DNS: records in each zone, DNSSEC, zone DNS settings, secondary DNS (zone transfers, peers, TSIG keys), DNS Firewall clusters, custom nameservers, and DNS analytics reports.

Use for anything about name resolution: which records exist and where they point (records), whether they are proxied, DNSSEC status, secondary DNS transfer setup, and DNS Firewall. Record functions take a zone_id; DNS Firewall and secondary-DNS peers take an account_id.

## Sections

- **Secondary DNS** — Secondary DNS: ACL Details; List ACLs; Secondary Zone Configuration Details; ….
- **DNS Settings** — DNS Settings: Get Custom Nameserver Set; List Custom Nameserver Sets; Show DNS Settings; ….
- **DNS Firewall** — DNS Firewall: Table; List DNS Firewall Clusters; DNS Firewall Cluster Details; ….
- **DNS Records** — DNS Records: A single DNS record (GET /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{dns_record_id}); DNS records in a zone: name, type, content, TTL, and whether Cloudflare proxies them; List Scanned DNS Records; ….
- **DNS Analytics** — DNS Analytics: By Time; Table.
- **Custom Ns** — Custom Ns: List Account Custom Nameservers; Get Account Custom Nameserver Related Zone Metadata.
- **Dnssec** — Dnssec: DNSSEC Details; List DNSSEC ZSKs.

vgi.example_queries.description: Across every zone, the A/AAAA/CNAME records Cloudflare could proxy but that are DNS-only: their targets are answered straight from DNS instead of sitting behind Cloudflare.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT z.name AS zone, r.type, r.name AS record, r.content FROM cloudflare.zones.zones z, cloudflare.dns.records(z.id) r WHERE r.type IN ('A', 'AAAA', 'CNAME') AND r.proxiable AND NOT r.proxied ORDER BY zone, record, r.type

vgi.example_queries.description: One row per zone with its SSL/TLS encryption mode, its Always Use HTTPS setting and its DNSSEC status, read from two settings lookups and the DNSSEC function.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT z.name AS zone, ssl.value AS ssl_mode, https.value AS always_use_https, d.status AS dnssec_status FROM cloudflare.zones.zones z, cloudflare.zones.setting(z.id, 'ssl') ssl, cloudflare.zones.setting(z.id, 'always_use_https') https, cloudflare.dns.dnssec(z.id) d ORDER BY zone

vgi.example_queries.description: List acls for one account (account_id is required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, ip_range FROM cloudflare.dns.acls WHERE account_id = '<account_id>'

vgi.example_queries.description: Count acls for several accounts at once (one API call each).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account_id, count(*) AS n FROM cloudflare.dns.acls WHERE account_id IN ('<account_id_1>', '<account_id_2>') GROUP BY account_id

vgi.example_queries.description: List custom ns for one account (account_id is required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT status, dns_records, ns_name FROM cloudflare.dns.custom_ns WHERE account_id = '<account_id>'

# cloudflare.dns.report

Table. Reads the report object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/dns_analytics/report`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieves a list of summarised aggregate metrics over a given time period.

See [Analytics API properties](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/reference/analytics-api-properties/) for detailed information about the available query parameters.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the report object for one zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT data, data_lag, max FROM cloudflare.dns.report('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the report for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.dns.report(t.zone_id) d ON true

# cloudflare.dns.records

DNS records in a zone: name, type, content, TTL, and whether Cloudflare proxies them. Returns every record from Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/dns_records` for the given path ids, paginated. ## Endpoint

Details about DNSSEC status and configuration.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT status, algorithm, digest FROM cloudflare.dns.dnssec('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT z.name AS zone, ssl.value AS ssl_mode, https.value AS always_use_https, d.status AS dnssec_status FROM cloudflare.zones.zones z, cloudflare.zones.setting(z.id, 'ssl') ssl, cloudflare.zones.setting(z.id, 'always_use_https') https, cloudflare.dns.dnssec(z.id) d ORDER BY zone

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.dns.dnssec(t.zone_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: dnssec_multi_signer
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: If true, multi-signer DNSSEC is enabled on the zone, allowing multiple providers to serve a DNSSEC-signed zone at the same time. This is required for DNSKEY records (except those automatically generated by Cloudflare) to be added to the zone. Note that this feature has some limitations. See [Cloudflare as Secondary](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/zone-transfers/cloudflare-as-secondary/setup/#dnssec) for details.

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: If true, enables the use of NSEC3 together with DNSSEC on the zone. If dnssec_presigned is instead set to false (default), NSEC3 records will be generated and signed at request time. See [DNSSEC with NSEC3](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/dnssec/enable-nsec3/…

# cloudflare.dns.bytime

By Time. Reads the bytime object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/dns_analytics/report/bytime`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieves a list of aggregate metrics grouped by time interval.

See [Analytics API properties](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/reference/analytics-api-properties/) for detailed information about the available query parameters.

Returns 9 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the bytime object for one zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT data, data_lag, max FROM cloudflare.dns.bytime('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the bytime for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.dns.bytime(t.zone_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: time_intervals
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Array of time intervals in the response data. Each interval is represented as an array containing two values: the start time, and the end time.

# Cloudflare Email

Cloudflare email products: Email Routing (addresses, routing rules, destination addresses) and Email Security (message investigation, allow/block policies, trusted domains, impersonation registry).

Use for questions about how mail to a domain is routed, and about Email Security detections: investigating suspicious messages, their action logs, and allow/block configuration. Email Routing settings and rules are per zone (destination addresses are per account); Email Security is account-scoped.

- **Email** — Email: List destination addresses; Get catch-all rule; Get sending subdomain complaint count; ….

List sending domain restrictions. Returns every sending domain restriction from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/email-security/settings/sending_domain_restrictions` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column).

## Endpoint

Returns a paginated list of sending domain restrictions. These restrictions enforce TLS requirements for emails from specific domains. Mail without TLS from restricted domains will be dropped unless the subdomain is in the exclude list. Supports sorting and searching.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List sending domain restrictions for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, comments, created_at FROM cloudflare.email.sending_domain_restrictions('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every sending domain restriction across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.id, r.comments FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.email.sending_domain_restrictions(p.id) r

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: comments

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Subdomains to exempt from TLS requirements.

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Deprecated, use `modified_at` instead. End of life: November 1, 2026.

# cloudflare.email.inspect

Inspect SPF Record. Reads the inspect object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/email/auth/spf/inspect`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Inspects a specific SPF TXT record and returns a parsed tree structure
in the spflimit-worker format.

The record ID must be provided via the `id` query parameter.

Returns a recursive tree showing:
- Parsed components with their qualifiers and types
- Nested includes recursively resolved within components
- Per-component and total lookup counts
- Detailed error information with context

Returns 6 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the inspect object for one zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT components, domain, errors FROM cloudflare.email.inspect('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the inspect for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.email.inspect(t.zone_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: zone_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Zone id: the id column of cloudflare.zones.zones.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: components
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Parsed SPF components (mechanisms)

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: domain
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Domain being inspected.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: errors
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: All errors encountered during inspection, collected from the entire tree. This includes errors from nested includes at any depth, providing a quick overview of all issues without needing to traverse the nested structure. Each error includes a `domain` field to identify where it occurred. Empty array if no errors (omitted from JSON when empty).

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: record
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Raw SPF record content.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: total_lookups
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Total number of DNS lookups performed across all includes.

arguments.name: zone_id
arguments.description: Zone id: the id column of cloudflare.zones.zones.

arguments.name: id
arguments.description: DNS record ID (rec_tag) to inspect.

examples: SELECT components, domain, errors FROM cloudflare.email.inspect('<zone_id>')
SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.email.inspect(t.zone_id) d ON true

# cloudflare.email.reputation

Get account reputation. Reads the reputation object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/reputation`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

Returns the authoritative Email Sending reputation state and active evaluation policy. Accounts without an evaluation are Healthy with null evaluation timestamps.

Returns 6 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the reputation object for one account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT status, active_policy, evaluated_at FROM cloudflare.email.reputation('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the reputation for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.account_id, d.* EXCLUDE (account_id) FROM (VALUES ('<account_id>')) t(account_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.email.reputation(t.account_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: active_policy
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The reputation policy thresholds currently applied to the account.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: evaluated_at
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When the account's reputation was last evaluated. Null when the account has never been evaluated.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: grace_started_at
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When the current At Risk suspension grace period started. This can be later than status_since if the grace period was restarted. Null outside At Risk. Automatic suspension remains subject to enforcement and suspension exemptions.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: status
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The account's current reputation status. One of: `healthy`, `warning`, `at_risk`, `suspended`.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: status_since
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When the account most recently transitioned into its current status. Null if the account has been Healthy since it was first tracked and has never changed status.

# cloudflare.email.submissions

List reclassify submissions. Returns every submission from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/email-security/submissions` for the given path ids, paginated. # Cloudflare Load Balancing

Cloudflare Load Balancing: load balancers, origin pools, health monitors, and their health and reference relationships.

Use to see how traffic is distributed across origins: pools and their origins, which monitors check them, and which load balancers reference each pool. Pools and monitors are account-scoped; load balancers are zone-scoped.

## Sections

- **Load Balancers** — Load Balancers: Account Load Balancer Details; List Account Load Balancers; Load Balancer Details; ….
- **Pools** — Pools: Pool Health Details; Pool Details; List Pools; ….
- **Monitors** — Monitors: Monitor Details; List Monitors; List Monitor References.
- **Monitor Groups** — Monitor Groups: Monitor Group Details; List Monitor Groups; List Monitor Group References.
- **Search** — Search: Search Resources.
- **Usage** — Usage: List Load Balancer Usage.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, created_on FROM cloudflare.load_balancing.load_balancers WHERE zone_id = '<zone_id>'

# Cloudflare Logs

Cloudflare logging: Logpush jobs and their destinations, available log datasets and fields, retention settings, and account audit logs.

Use to audit where logs are pushed (Logpush jobs and destinations), which datasets and fields are available, and to read the account audit log of configuration changes.

## Sections

- **Logs** — Logs: Get account audit logs (Version 2); List available account datasets; Get CMB config; ….
- **Logpush** — Logpush: Get transformer content; List Logpush jobs for a dataset; List Instant Logs jobs; ….
- **Observability** — Observability: View zone trace rules; View zone tracing settings.
- **Audit Logs** — Audit Logs: Get account audit logs.
- **Field Extractors** — Field Extractors: Get Field Extractor.

# cloudflare.logs.history

Get resource change history from an account audit log entry (Version 2). Returns every history from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/logs/audit/{id}/history` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: action_time, since, before.

## Endpoint

Returns the chronological change history for the resource identified by the given audit log entry.

The endpoint first locates the source audit log entry by `id` (using `action_time` to narrow the lookup window), derives identifying filters from that entry, and then returns matching audit logs within the `since`/`before` window.

The `result_info.history_status` field indicates the quality of the resource identification used:
- `exact`: Resource was identified by the resource URI.
- `approximate`: Resource was identified without the resource URI.
- `unavailable`: The source audit log entry did not contain enough information to identify the resource; an empty result is returned.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List historys for one account and one id (account_id, id: the URL path ids).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account, action, actor FROM cloudflare.logs.history('<account_id>', '<id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Historys for each id in another relation (one API call per row).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.id, r.account, r.action FROM (VALUES ('<id>')) t(id), cloudflare.logs.history('<account_id>', t.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only historys matching a action_time: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account, action, actor FROM cloudflare.logs.history('<account_id>', '<id>', action_time := '<action_time>')

arguments.description: Limits the returned results to logs older than the specified date. This can be a date string 2019-04-30 (interpreted in UTC) or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC3339.

arguments.description: Limits the returned results to logs newer than the specified date. This can be a date string 2019-04-30 (interpreted in UTC) or an absolute timestamp that conforms to RFC3339.

# cloudflare.logs.datasets

List account datasets. Returns every dataset from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/logs/explorer/datasets` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: include_zones.

# Cloudflare Magic Networking

Cloudflare network services: Magic Transit and Magic WAN (sites, tunnels, routes, connectors), BYOIP address management (prefixes, address maps), and Cloudflare Network Interconnect.

Use for network-layer infrastructure: IP prefixes you bring to Cloudflare, Magic WAN sites and connectors, GRE/IPsec tunnels, static routes, and interconnects. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **Magic** — Magic: Site ACL Details; List Site ACLs; List all allowlist prefixes; ….
- **Addressing** — Addressing: Address Map Details; List Address Maps; Fetch BGP Prefix; ….
- **CNI** — CNI: Get information about a CNI object; List existing CNI objects; Get the default customer name for LOA generation; ….
- **Mnm** — Mnm: List account configuration; List rules and account configuration; Get rule; ….
- **Pcaps** — Pcaps: List PCAPs Bucket Ownership; Get PCAP request; List packet capture requests.
- **IPS** — IPS: Cloudflare/JD Cloud IP Details.

vgi.example_queries.description: List acls for one account and one site (account_id, site_id are required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, description FROM cloudflare.magic.acls WHERE account_id = '<account_id>' AND site_id = '<site_id>'

vgi.example_queries.description: List address maps for one account (account_id is required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, can_delete, can_modify_ips FROM cloudflare.magic.address_maps WHERE account_id = '<account_id>'

vgi.example_queries.description: Count address maps for several accounts at once (one API call each).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account_id, count(*) AS n FROM cloudflare.magic.address_maps WHERE account_id IN ('<account_id_1>', '<account_id_2>') GROUP BY account_id

# cloudflare.magic.ips

Cloudflare/JD Cloud IP Details. Reads Cloudflare GET `/ips`, which takes no parameters.

## Endpoint

Get IPs used on the Cloudflare/JD Cloud network, see https://www.cloudflare.com/ips for Cloudflare IPs or https://developers.cloudflare.com/china-network/reference/infrastructure/ for JD Cloud IPs.

| `ipv6_cidrs` | VARCHAR | List of Cloudflare IPv6 CIDR addresses. |
| `jdcloud_cidrs` | VARCHAR | List IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs, only populated if `?networks=jdcloud` is used. |

List Prefix Delegations. Returns every delegation from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/addressing/prefixes/{prefix_id}/delegations` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, prefix_id (each is also returned as a column).

## Endpoint

List all delegations for a given account IP prefix.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List delegations for one account and one prefix (account_id, prefix_id: the URL path ids).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, cidr, created_at FROM cloudflare.magic.delegations('<account_id>', '<prefix_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Delegations for each prefix_id in another relation (one API call per row).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.prefix_id, r.id, r.cidr FROM (VALUES ('<prefix_id>')) t(prefix_id), cloudflare.magic.delegations('<account_id>', t.prefix_id) r

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: prefix_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Identifier of an IP Prefix.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: cidr
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: IP Prefix in Classless Inter-Domain Routing format.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: delegated_account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account identifier for the account to which prefix is being delegated.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Identifier of a Delegation.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: parent_prefix_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Identifier of an IP Prefix.

# cloudflare.magic.address_map

Address Map Details. Fetches one address map from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/addressing/address_maps/{address_map_id}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, address_map_id.

## Endpoint

Show a particular address map owned by the account.

Returns 12 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Fetch one address map by account_id, address_map_id; an unknown id returns no rows.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, can_delete, can_modify_ips FROM cloudflare.magic.address_map('<account_id>', '<address_map_id>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: address_map_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Identifier of an Address Map.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: can_delete
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: If set to false, then the Address Map cannot be deleted via API. This is true for Cloudflare-managed maps.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: can_modify_ips
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: If set to false, then the IPs on the Address Map cannot be modified via the API. This is true for Cloudflare-managed maps.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: default_sni
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: If you have legacy TLS clients which do not send the TLS server name indicator, then you can specify one default SNI on the map. If Cloudflare receives a TLS handshake from a client without an SNI, it will respond with the default SNI on those IPs. The default SNI can be any valid zone or subdomain owned by the account.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: description
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: An optional description field which may be used to describe the types of IPs or zones on the map.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: enabled
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Whether the Address Map is enabled or not. Cloudflare's DNS will not respond with IP addresses on an Address Map until the map is enabled.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Identifier of an Address Map.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: ips
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The set of IPs on the Address Map.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: memberships
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Zones and Accounts which will be assigned IPs on this Address Map. A zone membership will take priority over an account membership.

# cloudflare.magic.rules

List rules. Returns every rule from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/mnm/rules` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column).

## Endpoint

Lists network monitoring rules for account.

Returns 12 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List rules for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, type FROM cloudflare.magic.rules('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every rule across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.id, r.name FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.magic.rules(p.id) r

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: automatic_advertisement
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Toggle on if you would like Cloudflare to automatically advertise the IP Prefixes within the rule via Magic Transit when the rule is triggered. Only available for users of Magic Transit.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: bandwidth_threshold
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The number of bits per second for the rule. When this value is exceeded for the set duration, an alert notification is sent. Minimum of 1 and no maximum.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: duration
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The amount of time that the rule threshold must be exceeded to send an alert notification. The final value must be equivalent to one of the following 8 values ["1m","5m","10m","15m","20m","30m","45m","60m"].

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The id of the rule. Must be unique.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: name
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The name of the rule. Must be unique. Supports characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore (_), dash (-), period (.), and tilde (~). You can’t have a space in the rule name. Max 256 characters.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: packet_threshold
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The number of packets per second for the rule. When this value is exceeded for the set duration, an alert notification is sent. Minimum of 1 and no maximum.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: prefix_match
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Prefix match type to be applied for a prefix auto advertisement when using an advanced_ddos rule. One of: `exact`, `subnet`, `supernet`.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: prefixes
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The IP prefixes that are monitored for this rule. Must be a CIDR range like 203.0.113.0/24. Max 5000 different CIDR ranges.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: type
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: MNM rule type. One of: `threshold`, `zscore`, `advanced_ddos`.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: zscore_sensitivity
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Level of sensitivity set for zscore rules. One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: zscore_target
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Target of the zscore rule analysis. One of: `bits`, `packets`.

arguments.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

# cloudflare.magic.tcp_flow_protection_filters

List all TCP Flow Protection filters. Returns every tcp flow protection filter from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/magic/advanced_tcp_protection/configs/tcp_flow_protection/filters` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: mode.

## Endpoint

List all TCP Flow Protection filters for an account.

Returns 6 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List tcp flow protection filters for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, created_on, expression FROM cloudflare.magic.tcp_flow_protection_filters('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every tcp flow protection filter across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.id, r.created_on FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.magic.tcp_flow_protection_filters(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only tcp flow protection filters matching a mode: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, created_on, expression FROM cloudflare.magic.tcp_flow_protection_filters('<account_id>', mode := '<mode>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The filter's mode. Must be one of 'enabled', 'disabled', 'monitoring'.
