tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Cloudflare Radar

Cloudflare Radar: Internet-wide traffic, security, routing, DNS, and adoption trends observed across Cloudflare's network — summaries and time series by protocol, device, OS, location, and more.

Use for Internet-level questions that are not about your own account — e.g. global HTTP/3 adoption, attack trends, BGP route leaks, top domains, DNS query mixes. Radar functions take no account or zone; they return Cloudflare's published aggregates for the default time window.

## Sections

- **Attacks** — Attacks: Get top origin ASes of layer 7 attacks; Get top layer 3 attack pairs (origin and target locations); Get layer 3 attacks by bitrate summary; ….
- **HTTP** — HTTP: Get HTTP requests by bot class summary; Get top ASes by HTTP requests for a bot class; Get HTTP requests by user agent time series; ….
- **Email** — Email: Get email ARC validation summary; Get email DKIM validation summary; Get email DMARC validation summary; ….
- **DNS** — DNS: Get DNS queries by cache status summary; Get DNS summary by dimension; Get DNS queries time series; ….
- **BGP** — BGP: List ASes from global routing tables; Get top ASes by prefix count; Get tier-1 path segments for an AS; ….
- **As112** — As112: Get AS112 DNS queries by DNSSEC summary; Get top locations by AS112 DNS queries with DNSSEC support; Get AS112 DNS queries by EDNS summary; ….
- **AI** — AI: Get AI bots HTTP requests distribution by dimension; Get AI bots HTTP requests time series; Get time series distribution of AI bots HTTP requests by dimension; ….
- **Entities** — Entities: Get IRR AS-SETs that an AS is a member of; List autonomous systems; Get AS details by IP address; ….
- **CT** — CT: List certificate authorities; Get certificate authority details; Get certificate distribution by dimension; ….
- **Bots** — Bots: Get bot details; List bots; Get bots HTTP requests distribution by dimension; ….
- **Ranking** — Ranking: List Internet services categories; Get domain rank details; Get Internet services rank time series; ….
- **More APIs** — Smaller API areas: Leaked Credential Checks, Quality, Netflows, Origins, Annotations, Post Quantum, Tlds, Traffic Anomalies, Robots Txt, Geolocations, Tcp Resets Timeouts, Verified Bots, Datasets, Agent Readiness, Search.

# cloudflare.radar.support

Check Post-Quantum TLS support. Reads Cloudflare GET `/radar/post_quantum/tls/support`, which takes no parameters.

## Endpoint

Tests whether a hostname or IP address supports Post-Quantum (PQ) TLS key exchange. Returns information about the negotiated key exchange algorithm, whether it uses PQ cryptography, and any detected TLS implementation bugs (Split ClientHello, HRR failure, etc.).

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bugs` | VARCHAR | — |
| `host` | VARCHAR | The host that was tested. |
| `kex` | DOUBLE | TLS CurveID of the negotiated key exchange. |
| `kexName` | VARCHAR | Human-readable name of the key exchange algorithm. |
| `pq` | BOOLEAN | Whether the negotiated key exchange uses Post-Quantum cryptography (specifically X25519MLKEM768) |

Get TLD Performance Summary. Fetches one performance summary dimension from Cloudflare GET `/radar/tlds/performance/summary/{dimension}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: dimension.

## Endpoint

Returns a summary of TLD authoritative nameserver performance grouped by the specified dimension.

Returns 3 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Fetch one performance summary dimension by dimension; an unknown id returns no rows.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT meta, summary_0 FROM cloudflare.radar.performance_summary_dimension('<dimension>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the performance summary dimension for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.dimension, d.* EXCLUDE (dimension) FROM (VALUES ('<dimension>')) t(dimension) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.radar.performance_summary_dimension(t.dimension) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: dimension
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Dimension to summarize TLD nameserver latency by.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: meta
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Metadata for the results.

arguments.name: dimension
arguments.description: Dimension to summarize TLD nameserver latency by.

arguments.name: continent
arguments.description: Filters results by continent. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude continents from results. For example, `-EU,NA` excludes results from EU, but includes results from NA.

arguments.name: date_end
arguments.description: End of the date range (inclusive). Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateStart`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose…

arguments.name: date_range
arguments.description: Filters results by relative date range ending at the current time, with each value producing a separate series. Use `<n>d` for days (up to `364d`) or `<n>w` for weeks (up to `52w`). Append `control` to request the equivalent previous period for comparison: the comparison window is shifted back by t… Default: `7d`.

arguments.name: date_start
arguments.description: Start of the date range. Alternative to `dateRange`; provide together with `dateEnd`. When requesting comparison series, every series must resolve to the same duration as the main series. Each `dateStart`/`dateEnd` is floored to the nearest 15 minutes before evaluation, so windows whose durations m…

arguments.name: limit_per_group
arguments.description: Limits the number of objects per group to the top items within the specified time range. When item count exceeds the limit, extra items appear grouped under an "other" category. Only supported on high-cardinality dimensions; otherwise the request is rejected. Minimum value is 2.

arguments.name: location
arguments.description: Filters results by location. Specify a comma-separated list of alpha-2 codes. Prefix with `-` to exclude locations from results. For example, `-US,PT` excludes results from the US, but includes results from PT.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Array of names used to label the series in the response.

arguments.name: nameserver
arguments.description: Filters results by nameserver hostname.

arguments.name: tld
arguments.description: Filters results by top-level domain.

SELECT t.dimension, d.* EXCLUDE (dimension) FROM (VALUES ('<dimension>')) t(dimension) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.radar.performance_summary_dimension(t.dimension) d ON true

result_columns.description: Dimension to summarize TLD nameserver latency by.

Get time series distribution of HTTP authentication requests by dimension. Fetches one leaked credential checks timeseries groups dimension from Cloudflare GET `/radar/leaked_credential_checks/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: dimension.

## Endpoint

Retrieves the distribution of HTTP authentication requests, grouped by the specified dimension over time.

Returns 3 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Fetch one leaked credential checks timeseries groups dimension by dimension; an unknown id returns no rows.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT meta, serie_0 FROM cloudflare.radar.leaked_credential_checks_timeseries_groups_dimension('<dimension>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the leaked credential checks timeseries groups dimension for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.dimension, d.* EXCLUDE (dimension) FROM (VALUES ('<dimension>')) t(dimension) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.radar.leaked_credential_checks_timeseries_groups_dimension(t.dimension) d ON true

# cloudflare.radar.upstreams_timeseries

Get upstream composition time series for an AS. Reads the upstreams timeseries object at Cloudflare GET `/radar/bgp/routes/upstreams/{asn}/timeseries`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: asn.

## Endpoint

Retrieves the share of an AS’s observed paths carried by each direct upstream over time, derived from RouteViews RIB snapshots across all collectors (the combined product). Each upstream ASN is returned as its own series of shares (0–1); the least-significant upstreams beyond the requested limit are grouped into an "OTHER" series. Series share a common set of timestamps.

Returns 3 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.radar.asn

Get tier-1 path segments for an AS. Fetches one asn from Cloudflare GET `/radar/bgp/routes/paths/{asn}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: asn.

## Endpoint

Retrieves the paths an AS uses to reach the tier-1 clique, derived from RouteViews RIB snapshots. Each entry is an ordered AS-path segment (from the queried AS toward a tier-1) with the number of observed paths and peers, and the collectors that observed it. By default segments are merged across all active collectors; pass "collector" to scope to one. The response also includes an "asnInfo" map (keyed by ASN) with the name and country for every ASN in the returned segments plus the queried ASN (best-effort; null when unavailable).

Returns 5 columns, described in the declared result schema.

Get email security time series grouped by dimension. Fetches one security timeseries groups dimension from Cloudflare GET `/radar/email/security/timeseries_groups/{dimension}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: dimension.

## Endpoint

Retrieves the distribution of email security metrics grouped by dimension over time.

Returns 3 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Fetch one security timeseries groups dimension by dimension; an unknown id returns no rows.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT meta, serie_0 FROM cloudflare.radar.security_timeseries_groups_dimension('<dimension>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the security timeseries groups dimension for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.dimension, d.* EXCLUDE (dimension) FROM (VALUES ('<dimension>')) t(dimension) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.radar.security_timeseries_groups_dimension(t.dimension) d ON true

# Cloudflare Registrar

Cloudflare Registrar: domains registered or transferred through Cloudflare for an account, with registration and renewal details.

Use to list domains registered with Cloudflare Registrar and check their expiry, auto-renew, and lock status. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **Registrar** — Registrar: List extensions; Get Registration; Search for available domains; ….
- **Registrar Sandbox** — Registrar Sandbox: Search for available domains; List Registrations; Get extension; ….

vgi.example_queries.description: List account extensions for one account (account_id is required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT metadata, registration_schema, transfer_schema FROM cloudflare.registrar.account_extensions WHERE account_id = '<account_id>'

vgi.example_queries.description: Count account extensions for several accounts at once (one API call each).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account_id, count(*) AS n FROM cloudflare.registrar.account_extensions WHERE account_id IN ('<account_id_1>', '<account_id_2>') GROUP BY account_id

vgi.example_queries.description: List account registrations for one account (account_id is required: each maps to the URL path).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT status, auto_renew, created_at FROM cloudflare.registrar.account_registrations WHERE account_id = '<account_id>'

# cloudflare.registrar.domain_name

Get Registration. Fetches one domain name from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/registrar/registrations/{domain_name}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, domain_name.

## Endpoint

Returns the current state of a domain registration.

This is the canonical read endpoint for a domain you own. It returns
the full registration resource including current settings and expiration.
When the registration resource is ready, both `created_at` and `expires_at`
are present in the response.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Fetch one domain name by account_id, domain_name; an unknown id returns no rows.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT status, auto_renew, created_at FROM cloudflare.registrar.domain_name('<account_id>', '<domain_name>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: domain_name
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Domain name to retrieve.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: auto_renew
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Whether automatic renewal occurs before expiration.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: created_at
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When the domain was registered. Present when the registration resource exists.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: expires_at
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When the domain registration expires. Ready registrations include this value; only `registration_pending` and `transfer_pending` may return null.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: locked
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Whether the domain is locked for transfer.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: privacy_mode

# cloudflare.registrar.transfer_in_status

Get Transfer Status. Reads the transfer in status object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/registrar/registrations/{domain_name}/transfer-in-status`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, domain_name.

## Endpoint

Returns the current status of a domain transfer workflow.

Use this endpoint to poll transfer progress after initiating a transfer
with `POST /accounts/{account_id}/registrar/registrations/{domain_name}/transfer-in`.
The URL is provided in the `links.self` field of the transfer response.

### Transfer timelines
Transfers typically take 1–10 days due to ICANN-mandated approval windows.

### Workflow states

**Terminal states:** `succeeded` and `failed` are terminal and always
have `completed: true`.

**Non-terminal states:**
- `in_progress`: Transfer has been submitted to the registry and is being
  processed. Continue polling.
- `blocked`: The workflow is waiting on the losing registrar or registry
  to release the domain. This is the **most common state** for transfers
  and is entirely normal — it means the ICANN transfer approval window is
  in effect. The losing registrar has up to 5 days to approve or reject.
  Continue polling with longer intervals (e.g., every 30–60 minutes).
- `action_required`: The user needs to take action (e.g., the FOA email
  needs to be accepted). See `context` for details on what is needed.
- `pending`: Transfer workflow created but not yet started processing.

### Polling guidance
Adjust your polling interval based on the current workflow state:
- `pending` or `in_progress`: Poll every 30 seconds.
- `blocked`: The transfer is waiting on a third party (e.g., losing
  registrar approval). Poll every 30–60 minutes.
- `action_required`: Stop…

# cloudflare.registrar.domain_search

Search for available domains. Reads the domain search object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/registrar/domain-search`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

Searches for domain name suggestions based on a keyword, phrase, or partial domain name.
Returns a list of potentially available domains with pricing information.

**Important:** Results are non-authoritative and based on cached data. Always use the
`/domain-check` endpoint to verify real-time availability before attempting registration.

Suggestions are scoped to extensions supported for programmatic registration
via this API (`POST /registrations`). Domains on unsupported extensions will
not appear in results, even if they are available at the registry level.

### Use cases
- Brand name discovery (e.g., "acme corp" → acmecorp.com, acmecorp.dev)
- Keyword-based suggestions (e.g., "coffee shop" → coffeeshop.com, mycoffeeshop.net)
- Alternative extension discovery (e.g., "example.com" → example.com, example.app, example.xyz)

### Workflow
1. Call this endpoint with a keyword or domain name.
2. Present suggestions to the user.
3. Call `/domain-check` with the user's chosen domains to confirm real-time availability and pricing.
4. Proceed to `POST /registrations` only for supported non-premium domains
   where the Check response returns `registrable: true`.

**Note:** Searching with just a domain extension (e.g., "com" or ".app") is not supported. Provide a keyword or domain name.

# cloudflare.registrar.account_domain_search

Search for available domains. Reads the account domain search object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/registrar-sandbox/domain-search`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

Searches for domain name suggestions based on a keyword, phrase, or partial domain name.
Returns a list of potentially available domains with pricing information.

**Important:** Results are non-authoritative and based on cached data. Always use the
`/domain-check` endpoint to verify real-time availability before attempting registration.

Suggestions are scoped to extensions supported for programmatic registration
via this API (`POST /registrations`). Domains on unsupported extensions will
not appear in results, even if they are available at the registry level.

### Use cases
- Brand name discovery (e.g., "acme corp" → acmecorp.com, acmecorp.dev)
- Keyword-based suggestions (e.g., "coffee shop" → coffeeshop.com, mycoffeeshop.net)
- Alternative extension discovery (e.g., "example.com" → example.com, example.app, example.xyz)

### Workflow
1. Call this endpoint with a keyword or domain name.
2. Present suggestions to the user.
3. Call `/domain-check` with the user's chosen domains to confirm real-time availability and pricing.
4. Proceed to `POST /registrations` only for supported non-premium domains
   where the Check response returns `registrable: true`.

**Note:** Searching with just a domain extension (e.g., "com" or ".app") is not supported. Provide a keyword or domain name.

Returns 2 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.registrar.account_extensions

List extensions. Returns every account extension from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/registrar/extensions` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: name, sort_by.

from a previous response in an `If-None-Match` header to receive a
`304 Not Modified` when the data has not changed.

# Cloudflare Security

Cloudflare security and threat intelligence: Cloudforce One threat events and requests, Intel lookups (domains, IPs, ASNs), Security Center insights, URL scanner, brand protection, abuse reports, vulnerability scanner, and bot management.

Use for threat-intelligence and security-posture questions: what Cloudflare knows about a domain or IP, open Security Center insights, URL scan results, brand impersonation alerts, and Cloudforce One threat events. Mostly account-scoped; some bot and fraud settings are per zone.

## Sections

- **Cloudforce One** — Cloudforce One: Check if current user is allowlisted for Legal Response; Lists all Actors; Aggregate events by single or multiple columns with optional date filtering; ….
- **Cws** — Cws: List category APIs; List category applications; List basic-auth credentials for an account; ….
- **Security Center** — Security Center: Retrieves Issue Audit Log; Retrieves Account Audit Log; Retrieves Security Center Insight Counts by Class; ….
- **Intel** — Intel: Get Multiple Domain Details; Get Passive DNS by IP; Get Domain Details; ….
- **Abuse Reports** — Abuse Reports: List abuse reports against the account; Check whether a report can be appealed; List abuse report emails; ….
- **Vuln Scanner** — Vuln Scanner: Get credential; Get credential set; List credential sets; ….
- **Pay Per Use** — Pay Per Use: List enabled Pay Per Use domains; Get pay-per-use operator configuration; List pay-per-use operators; ….
- **Pay Per Crawl** — Pay Per Crawl: Get pay-per-crawl zone eligibility; Get the pay-per-crawl config; List pay-per-crawl crawlers; ….
- **Urlscanner** — Urlscanner: Get URL scan's HAR; Get URL scan; Search URL scans.
- **Managed Defense** — Managed Defense: Get repository; List repositories; Get reviewed vulnerability report; ….
- **Brand Protection** — Brand Protection: Download matches for logo queries by ID; Read matches for logo queries by ID; Read matches for string queries by ID; ….
- **More APIs** — Smaller API areas: Monetization, Botnet Feed, Challenges, Bot Management, AI Audit, Fraud Detection.

# cloudflare.security.v2_search Search URL scans. Reads the v2 search object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/v2/search`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id. ## Endpoint Use a subset of ElasticSearch Query syntax to filter scans. Some example queries:

- 'path:"/bundles/jquery.js"': Searches for scans who requested resources with the given path.
- 'page.asn:AS24940 AND hash:xxx': Websites hosted in AS24940 where a resource with the given hash was downloaded.
- 'page.domain:microsoft* AND verdicts.malicious:true AND NOT page.domain:microsoft.com': malicious scans whose hostname starts with "microsoft".

# cloudflare.security.bulk

Get Multiple Domain Details. Returns every bulk from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/intel/domain/bulk` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: domain, include_ranking, skip_ranking.

## Endpoint

Returns security details and statistics about multiple domains in a
single request.

**Behavior change — domain ranking is becoming opt-in.** This endpoint
previously included domain ranking data in every response and accepted
a `skip_ranking=true` query parameter to opt out. That parameter is
being deprecated and ranking will no longer be returned by default.
Callers that want ranking data must pass `include_ranking=true`. The
`skip_ranking` parameter will be silently ignored once the change ships.

# cloudflare.security.issues_severity

Returns every issues severity from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/intel/attack-surface-report/issues/severity` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: dismissed, issue_class, issue_type, product, source, severity, subject, issue_class_neq, issue_type_neq, product_neq, severity_neq, subject_neq.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.count, r.value FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.security.issues_severity(p.id) r

# cloudflare.security.graph

Query graph neighborhood from R2 Data Catalog. Reads the graph object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/cloudforce-one/events/graph`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

Expands the single-level relationship neighborhood of one or more seed nodes (event, indicator, or tag) from R2 Data Catalog. Seeds use compact id format (type:uuid), e.g. "event:550e8400-...". vgi.result_columns_schema.description: 0x-prefixed 20-byte hexadecimal Ethereum address. Mixed-case addresses must carry a valid EIP-55 checksum; all-lowercase or all-uppercase addresses are also accepted. The address must pass wallet screening whenever its rule is deployed or patched.

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: X402 payment scheme. "exact" requires the specified payment amount; "upto" permits a payment up to the specified amount. Both fixed-price schemes require the price field.

List abuse reports against the account. Reads the abuse reports object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/abuse-reports`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

List abuse reports made against domains or other content associated with the account. To list reports that the account submitted, use the submitted abuse reports endpoint instead.

Returns 2 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the abuse reports object for one account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT reports FROM cloudflare.security.abuse_reports('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the abuse reports for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.account_id, d.* EXCLUDE (account_id) FROM (VALUES ('<account_id>')) t(account_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.security.abuse_reports(t.account_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

arguments.name: account_id
arguments.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

arguments.name: created_after
arguments.description: Returns reports created after the specified date.

arguments.name: created_before
arguments.description: Returns reports created before the specified date.

arguments.name: domain
arguments.description: Filter by domain name related to the abuse report.

arguments.name: mitigation_status
arguments.description: Filter reports that have any mitigations in the given status.

arguments.name: sort
arguments.description: A property to sort by, followed by the order (id, cdate, domain, type, status)

arguments.description: Filter by the status of the report.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: Filter by the type of the report.

examples: SELECT reports FROM cloudflare.security.abuse_reports('<account_id>')
SELECT t.account_id, d.* EXCLUDE (account_id) FROM (VALUES ('<account_id>')) t(account_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.security.abuse_reports(t.account_id) d ON true

# cloudflare.security.usage_stats

Get pay-per-use usage statistics. Reads the usage stats object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/pay-per-use/usage-stats`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

Returns reported usage and the full gross value across all Pay Per Use zones in a publisher account over an explicit UTC range of at most 31 days. Usage from every domain and snapshotted price is summed by buyer. Ranges up to and including 7 days use hourly data points; longer ranges use daily data points. Because source data is aggregated hourly, both requested bounds are rounded down to the selected UTC interval and the resolved bounds are returned in the response. The resolved range must contain at least one complete interval. Empty periods are omitted. Buyers and their data points are paginated, while totals cover every buyer in the range. Values are raw usage counts and USD microcents; total_price_usd_microcents is the full value before the publisher revenue share.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.security.audit_log

Retrieves Account Audit Log. Returns every audit log from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/security-center/insights/audit-log` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: field_changed, changed_by, since, before.

## Endpoint

Lists audit log entries for all Security Center insights in the account, showing changes to insight status and classification.

Returns 10 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.security.zone_usage_stats

Get pay-per-use usage statistics for a zone. Reads the zone usage stats object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/pay-per-use/usage-stats`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Returns reported usage and the full gross value for one Pay Per Use zone over an explicit UTC range of at most 31 days. Usage from every snapshotted price is summed by buyer. Ranges up to and including 7 days use hourly data points; longer ranges use daily data points. Because source data is aggregated hourly, both requested bounds are rounded down to the selected UTC interval and the resolved bounds are returned in the response. The resolved range must contain at least one complete interval. Empty periods are omitted. Buyers and their data points are paginated, while totals cover every buyer in the range. Values are raw usage counts and USD microcents; total_price_usd_microcents is the full value before the publisher revenue share.

Returns 8 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.security.scan Search URL scans. Reads the scan object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/urlscanner/scan`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id. ## Endpoint Search scans by date and webpages' requests, including full URL (after redirects), hostname, and path.

# cloudflare.security.securitytxt

Retrieves security.txt. Reads the securitytxt object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/security-center/securitytxt`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieves the current security.txt file configuration for a zone, used for security vulnerability reporting.

Returns 10 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the securitytxt object for one zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT acknowledgments, canonical, contact FROM cloudflare.security.securitytxt('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the securitytxt for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.security.securitytxt(t.zone_id) d ON true

# cloudflare.security.policies

List policies. Returns every policy from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/cws/policies` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: name, policy_set_id, package_path.

## Endpoint

Returns a paginated list of policies in the account.

Returns 11 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List policys for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, created_at FROM cloudflare.security.policies('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.id, r.name FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.security.policies(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only policys matching a name: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, created_at FROM cloudflare.security.policies('<account_id>', name := '<name>')

# Cloudflare SSL/TLS

Cloudflare SSL/TLS: edge certificate packs, custom and keyless certificates, origin and client (mTLS) certificates, certificate authorities, Advanced Certificate Manager, and certificate transparency monitoring.

Use to audit certificates — what is deployed at the edge for a zone, when certificates expire, which client certificates exist for mTLS, and custom CSRs. Edge certificates are zone-scoped, mTLS certificates are account-scoped, and custom CSRs exist at both levels.

## Sections

- **Origin TLS Client Auth** — Origin TLS Client Auth: Get the Hostname Client Certificate; Get the Hostname Status for Client Authentication; List Hostname Associations; ….
- **SSL** — SSL: Get Certificate Pack; List Certificate Packs; Get Certificate Pack Quotas; ….
- **Custom CSRS** — Custom CSRS: Custom CSR Details; List Custom CSRs.
- **MTLS Certificates** — MTLS Certificates: List mTLS certificate associations; Get mTLS certificate; List mTLS certificates.
- **ACM** — ACM: Custom Origin Trust Store Details; List Custom Origin Trust Store Details; Total TLS Settings Details.
- **Certificates** — Certificates: Get Certificate; List Certificates.
- **Client Certificates** — Client Certificates: Client Certificate Details; List Client Certificates.
- **Custom Certificates** — Custom Certificates: SSL Configuration Details; List SSL Configurations.
- **Keyless Certificates** — Keyless Certificates: Get Keyless SSL Configuration; List Keyless SSL Configurations.
- **CT** — CT: Get CT Alerting Subscription.
- **Certificate Authorities** — Certificate Authorities: List Hostname Associations.
- **DCV Delegation** — DCV Delegation: Retrieve the DCV Delegation unique identifier.

# cloudflare.ssl.certificates

List Certificates. One row per certificate, from Cloudflare GET `/certificates`.

## Endpoint

List all existing Origin CA certificates for a given zone. You can use an Origin CA Key as your User Service Key or an API token when calling this endpoint ([see above](#requests)).

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `certificate` | VARCHAR | The Origin CA certificate. Will be newline-encoded. |
| `csr` | VARCHAR | The Certificate Signing Request (CSR). Must be newline-encoded. |
| `expires_on` | VARCHAR | When the certificate will expire. |
| `hostnames` | VARCHAR | Array of hostnames or wildcard names bound to the certificate. Hostnames must be fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) belonging to zones on your account (e.g., `example.com` or `sub.example.com`). Wildcards are supported only as a `*.` prefix for a single level (e.g., `*.example.com`). Double wildcards (`*.*.example.com`) and interior wildcards (`foo.*.example.com`) are not allowed. The wildcard … |
| `id` | VARCHAR | The x509 serial number of the Origin CA certificate. |
| `request_type` | VARCHAR | Signature type desired on certificate ("origin-rsa" (rsa), "origin-ecc" (ecdsa), or "keyless-certificate" (for Keyless SSL servers). |
| `requested_validity` | DOUBLE | The number of days for which the certificate should be valid. One of: `7`, `30`, `90`, `365`, `730`, `1095`, `5475`. |

# cloudflare.ssl.mtls_certificates

List mTLS certificates. Returns every mtls certificate from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/mtls_certificates` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: type.

## Endpoint

# Cloudflare Storage & Databases

Cloudflare storage and databases: R2 buckets and the R2 Data Catalog, D1 databases, Hyperdrive configurations, and other account storage resources.

Use to inventory where data lives on Cloudflare: R2 buckets and catalog tables, D1 databases, and Hyperdrive connection configs. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **R2** — R2: List Buckets; Get Bucket; Get Bucket CORS Policy; ….
- **Basin Catalog** — Basin Catalog: Get Basin Catalog details; Get catalog maintenance configuration; List namespaces in catalog; ….
- **R2 Catalog** — R2 Catalog: Get R2 catalog details; Get catalog credential status; Get catalog maintenance configuration; ….
- **D1** — D1: Get D1 database bookmark; List D1 Databases; Get D1 Database.
- **Storage** — Storage: List keys in a namespace; Get a namespace; List namespaces.
- **Hyperdrive** — Hyperdrive: List Hyperdrives; Get Hyperdrive.
- **Event Notifications** — Event Notifications: List Event Notification Rules; Get Event Notification Rules for a Queue.

# cloudflare.storage.objects

List Objects. Returns every object from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/r2/buckets/{bucket_name}/objects` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, bucket_name (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: prefix, delimiter, start_after.

## Endpoint

Lists objects in an R2 bucket. Returns object metadata including key, size, etag, last modified date, HTTP metadata, and custom metadata.

For most workloads, we recommend using R2's [S3-compatible API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/api/) or a [Worker with an R2 binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/workers/workers-api-reference/) instead.

Returns 10 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT custom_metadata, etag, http_metadata FROM cloudflare.storage.objects('<account_id>', '<bucket_name>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Objects for each bucket_name in another relation (one API call per row).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.bucket_name, r.custom_metadata, r.etag FROM (VALUES ('<bucket_name>')) t(bucket_name), cloudflare.storage.objects('<account_id>', t.bucket_name) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only objects matching a prefix: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT custom_metadata, etag, http_metadata FROM cloudflare.storage.objects('<account_id>', '<bucket_name>', prefix := '<prefix>')

# cloudflare.storage.tables_table_name

Get table details. Fetches one tables table name from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/basin-catalog/{bucket_name}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table_name}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, bucket_name, namespace, table_name.

## Endpoint

Returns full Apache Iceberg metadata for a single table: schema,
partition specs, sort orders, properties, and recent snapshot history.
Designed for catalog introspection UIs that need per-table details
without holding R2 credentials.

The `metadata.snapshots`, `metadata.snapshot-log`, and
`metadata.metadata-log` arrays are pruned to the most recent 10
entries by `timestamp-ms`. Use `total_snapshots` and
`returned_snapshots` to surface the truncation to end users.

Returns 10 columns, described in the declared result schema.

Limits the `snapshots`, `snapshot-log`, and `metadata-log` arrays to the most recent 10 entries (by `timestamp-ms`). Always keeps the current snap…

# Cloudflare Stream & Realtime

Cloudflare media: Stream videos, live inputs, captions, watermarks and signing keys; Realtime (RealtimeKit apps, meetings, livestreams) and Calls/TURN services.

Use for video and real-time media questions: uploaded Stream videos and their status, live inputs, watermark profiles, RealtimeKit meetings and sessions, and TURN keys. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **Realtime** — Realtime: Fetch active livestreams for a meeting; Fetch active livestream session details; Fetch active recording; ….
- **Images** — Images: Get source connectivity status; Variant details (flat); Get transformation flows; ….
- **Stream** — Stream: Get account Stream usage; List additional audio tracks on a video; List captions or subtitles; ….
- **Calls** — Calls: Retrieve SFU app details; List apps; List TURN keys; ….
- **MOQ** — MOQ: Get a relay; List relays; List tokens.
- **Media** — Media: Get account Media usage; Get zone Media usage.

# cloudflare.stream.zone_stream_usage

Get zone Stream usage. Returns every zone stream usage from Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/stream/usage` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: metrics, since, until, time_delta, filters.

# cloudflare.stream.zone_usage

Get zone Media usage. Returns every zone usage from Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/media/usage` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: metrics, since, until, time_delta, filters.

## Endpoint

Retrieve Media usage analytics for a zone. This endpoint shares the same backend handler as the Stream usage endpoint and returns identical Stream metrics (streamMinutesViewed). The gateway resolves the zone to its owning account and rewrites this path to the shared usage handler.

Returns 3 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List zone usages for one zone (zone_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT "streamMinutesViewed", ts FROM cloudflare.stream.zone_usage('<zone_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every zone usage across all of your zones, one API call per zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS zone, r."streamMinutesViewed", r.ts FROM cloudflare.zones.zones p, cloudflare.stream.zone_usage(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only zone usages matching a metrics: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT "streamMinutesViewed", ts FROM cloudflare.stream.zone_usage('<zone_id>', metrics := '<metrics>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: zone_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Zone id: the id column of cloudflare.zones.zones.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: streamMinutesViewed

arguments.name: zone_id
arguments.description: Zone id: the id column of cloudflare.zones.zones.

arguments.name: filters
arguments.description: Filter expressions to apply to the query. Format: field==value. Multiple filters can be combined.

arguments.name: metrics
arguments.description: Comma-separated list of metrics to include in the response. Available metrics depend on the endpoint. Billing usage supports: streamMinutesViewed, rateLimitingRequestsAllowed, loadBalancingQueries, argoAcceleratedBytes, workersRequests, workersKVReads, imageResizingRequests, spectrumBytesTransferre…

arguments.name: since
arguments.description: Start of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to 6 hours before the current time.

arguments.name: time_delta
arguments.description: Time unit to aggregate usage observations into. Data retention is approximately 18 months. The effective number of data points returned depends on the time range and granularity selected. For example, requesting hourly granularity over 18 months could produce up to ~13,000 data points; use the limi…

arguments.name: until
arguments.description: End of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to the current time.

# cloudflare.stream.v2

List images V2. Reads the v2 object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/images/v2`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

List up to 10000 images from CF Images, with up to 1000 results per page. Use the optional parameters below to get a specific range of images.
Pagination is supported via continuation_token.

**Metadata Filtering (Optional):**

You can optionally filter images by custom metadata fields using the `meta.<field>[<operator>]=<value>` syntax.

**Supported Operators:**
- `eq` / `eq:string` / `eq:number` / `eq:boolean` - Exact match
- `gt` / `gt:number` - Greater than (number only)
- `gte` / `gte:number` - Greater than or equal (number only)
- `lt` / `lt:number` - Less than (number only)
- `lte` / `lte:number` - Less than or equal (number only)
- `in` / `in:string` / `in:number` - Match any value in list (pipe-separated)

**Metadata Filter Constraints:**
- Maximum 5 metadata filters per request
- Maximum 5 levels of nesting (e.g., `meta.first.second.third.fourth.fifth`)
- Maximum 10 elements for list operators (`in`)
- Supports string, number, and boolean value types
- Range operators (`gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`) only accept numeric values

**Filter Consistency:**
Filters are combined with AND logic. The system does not validate whether filter combinations are logically consistent. For example, `meta.priority[eq:number]=5&meta.priority[lte:number]=3` will return zero results because no value can satisfy both conditions simultaneously. It is the caller's responsibility to ensure filter combinations make sense.

# cloudflare.stream.watermarks

List watermark profiles. Returns every watermark from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/stream/watermarks` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column).

## Endpoint

Lists all watermark profiles for an account.

Returns 12 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List watermarks for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, created, "downloadedFrom" FROM cloudflare.stream.watermarks('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every watermark across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.name, r.created FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.stream.watermarks(p.id) r

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The date and a time a watermark profile was created.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: downloadedFrom
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The source URL for a downloaded image. If the watermark profile was created via direct upload, this field is null.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: height
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The height of the image in pixels.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: name
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: A short description of the watermark profile.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: opacity
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The translucency of the image. A value of `0.0` makes the image completely transparent, and `1.0` makes the image completely opaque. Note that if the image is already semi-transparent, setting this to `1.0` will not make the image completely opaque.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: padding
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The whitespace between the adjacent edges (determined by position) of the video and the image. `0.0` indicates no padding, and `1.0` indicates a fully padded video width or length, as determined by the algorithm.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: position
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The location of the image. Valid positions are: `upperRight`, `upperLeft`, `lowerLeft`, `lowerRight`, and `center`. Note that `center` ignores the `padding` parameter.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: scale
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The size of the image relative to the overall size of the video. This parameter will adapt to horizontal and vertical videos automatically. `0.0` indicates no scaling (use the size of the image as-is), and `1.0 `fills the entire video.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: size
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The size of the image in bytes.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: uid
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The unique identifier for a watermark profile.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: width
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The width of the image in pixels.

# cloudflare.stream.usage

Get account Media usage. Returns every usage from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/media/usage` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: metrics, since, until, time_delta, filters.

## Endpoint

Retrieve Media usage analytics for an account. This endpoint shares the same backend handler as the Stream usage endpoint and returns identical Stream metrics (streamMinutesViewed). The gateway rewrites this path to the shared usage handler.

Returns 3 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List usages for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT "streamMinutesViewed", ts FROM cloudflare.stream.usage('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every usage across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r."streamMinutesViewed", r.ts FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.stream.usage(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only usages matching a metrics: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT "streamMinutesViewed", ts FROM cloudflare.stream.usage('<account_id>', metrics := '<metrics>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: streamMinutesViewed
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Number of Stream billable minutes viewed in this time period.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: ts
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Unix timestamp (epoch seconds) for the start of this time period.

arguments.name: account_id
arguments.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

arguments.name: filters
arguments.description: Filter expressions to apply to the query. Format: field==value. Multiple filters can be combined.

arguments.name: metrics
arguments.description: Comma-separated list of metrics to include in the response. Available metrics depend on the endpoint. Billing usage supports: streamMinutesViewed, rateLimitingRequestsAllowed, loadBalancingQueries, argoAcceleratedBytes, workersRequests, workersKVReads, imageResizingRequests, spectrumBytesTransferre…

arguments.name: since
arguments.description: Start of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to 6 hours before the current time.

arguments.name: time_delta
arguments.description: Time unit to aggregate usage observations into. Data retention is approximately 18 months. The effective number of data points returned depends on the time range and granularity selected. For example, requesting hourly granularity over 18 months could produce up to ~13,000 data points; use the limi…

arguments.name: until
arguments.description: End of the time range for the query (inclusive). ISO 8601 timestamp. Defaults to the current time.

examples: SELECT "streamMinutesViewed", ts FROM cloudflare.stream.usage('<account_id>')
SELECT p.name AS account, r."streamMinutesViewed", r.ts FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.stream.usage(p.id) r
SELECT "streamMinutesViewed", ts FROM cloudflare.stream.usage('<account_id>', metrics := '<metrics>')

result_columns.name: account_id
result_columns.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

result_columns.name: streamMinutesViewed
result_columns.description: Number of Stream billable minutes viewed in this time period.

result_columns.name: ts
result_columns.description: Unix timestamp (epoch seconds) for the start of this time period.

Fetch summary of transcripts for a session. Reads the summary object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/realtime/kit/{app_id}/sessions/{session_id}/summary`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, app_id, session_id.

## Endpoint

Returns a Summary URL to download the Summary of Transcripts for the session ID as plain text.

Returns 5 columns, described in the declared result schema.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: List videos. Returns every stream from Cloudflare GET /accounts/{account_id}/stream, across all pages, for the given account_id. Named arguments status, creator, type, asc_, video_name, start, end_, include_counts, id, name, live_input_id, before, after are sent to the API to filter there; any WHERE clause still applies to the rows returned. # cloudflare.stream.stream

List videos. Returns every stream from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/stream` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: status, creator, type, asc_, video_name, start, end_, include_counts, id, name, live_input_id, before, after.

## Endpoint

Lists up to 1000 videos from a single request. For a specific range, refer to the optional parameters.

Returns 27 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List streams for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT status, "allowedOrigins", "clippedFrom" FROM cloudflare.stream.stream('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every stream across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.status, r."allowedOrigins" FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.stream.stream(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only streams matching a status: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT status, "allowedOrigins", "clippedFrom" FROM cloudflare.stream.stream('<account_id>', status := '<status>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: allowedOrigins

# cloudflare.stream.relays

List relays. Returns every relay from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/moq/relays` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: created_before, created_after, asc_.

## Endpoint

Lists all MoQ relays for the account. Returns only metadata.
Config, status, and tokens are omitted.

Results are cursor-paginated (keyset on the `created` timestamp).
Use `created_before` / `created_after` with the `created` value of the
first/last item in a page to fetch the adjacent page. `result_info`
reports the page `count` and the `total` matching the cursor filters.

Returns 5 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List relays for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, created, modified FROM cloudflare.stream.relays('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every relay across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.name, r.created FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.stream.relays(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only relays matching a created_before: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, created, modified FROM cloudflare.stream.relays('<account_id>', created_before := '<created_before>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: uid
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Example: `a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890`.

arguments.name: account_id
arguments.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

arguments.name: asc_
arguments.description: Sort order by `created`. When true, results are returned oldest-first (ascending); otherwise newest-first (descending, the default).

arguments.name: created_after
arguments.description: Cursor for pagination. Returns relays created strictly after this RFC 3339 timestamp (typically the `created` value of the last item on the current page, to fetch the next page).

arguments.name: created_before
arguments.description: Cursor for pagination. Returns relays created strictly before this RFC 3339 timestamp (typically the `created` value of the first item on the current page, to fetch the previous page).

examples: SELECT name, created, modified FROM cloudflare.stream.relays('<account_id>')
SELECT p.name AS account, r.name, r.created FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.stream.relays(p.id) r
SELECT name, created, modified FROM cloudflare.stream.relays('<account_id>', created_before := '<created_before>')

# Cloudflare Legacy Firewall

Cloudflare firewall configuration for a zone: legacy firewall rules, IP access rules, user-agent blocking, and lockdown rules.

Use to audit older firewall-style configuration on a zone — IP access rules, user-agent blocks, and zone lockdowns. Most objects are scoped to a zone: they are functions of its zone_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.zones.zones.

## Sections

- **Rulesets** — Rulesets: List an account ruleset version's rules by tag; Get an account entry point ruleset; List an account entry point ruleset's versions; ….
- **Firewall** — Firewall: List IP Access rules; List WAF rule groups; Get a Zone Lockdown rule; ….
- **Leaked Credential Checks** — Leaked Credential Checks: Get a custom detection location of a zone; List the custom detection locations of a zone; Get the Leaked Credential Checks status for a zone.
- **AI Security** — AI Security: Get the AI Security for Apps custom topics of a zone; Get the AI Security for Apps status for a zone.
- **Filters** — Filters: Get a filter; List filters.
- **Content Upload Scan** — Content Upload Scan: List the Content Scanning custom expressions of a zone; Get the Content Scanning status for a zone.
- **Rate Limit Analytics** — Rate Limit Analytics: Get Rate Limiting Analytics.

# cloudflare.waf.rate_limit_analytics

Get Rate Limiting Analytics. Reads the rate limit analytics object at Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/rate_limit_analytics`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id.

## Endpoint

Returns rate limiting analytics for a zone over the specified time period.
The time period divides into time segments of a given length. Each segment
contains total action counts and action counts broken down by colo.

Returns 6 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the rate limit analytics object for one zone.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.zone_id, d.* EXCLUDE (zone_id) FROM (VALUES ('<zone_id>')) t(zone_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.waf.rate_limit_analytics(t.zone_id) d ON true

List firewall rules. Returns every rule from Cloudflare GET `/zones/{zone_id}/firewall/rules` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: zone_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: description, action, id, paused.

# Cloudflare Workers

Use for serverless application questions: which Workers exist and how they are deployed, their routes, versions, and settings; Queues and consumers; Workflows and their instances; Pipelines; Containers; and builds. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

- **Containers** — Containers: Get a single application by id; List Applications associated with your account; List all application versions; ….
- **Queues** — Queues: Get Queue Consumer; List Queue Consumers; Get Queue Metrics; ….
- **Secrets Store** — Secrets Store: View secret usage; Get a secret by ID; List store secrets; ….
- **Slurper** — Slurper: Get job details; List jobs; Get job logs; ….

# cloudflare.workers.step

Get full step output from instance. Reads the step object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/workflows/{workflow_name}/instances/{instance_id}/step`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, workflow_name, instance_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieves the full, untruncated output for a specific step on a workflow instance. Returns a flat status-shaped JSON body with step `status` ('running' | 'waiting' | 'complete' | 'errored'), `error` (nullable), and `output` (the step value, or null while running/waiting/errored). When the step returned a ReadableStream from step.do, the response is served as 'application/octet-stream' with the raw bytes as the body instead of JSON. A `status='running'` response with non-null `error` indicates the step is currently retrying after a prior attempt failed.

Returns 7 columns, described in the declared result schema.

Reads the sql object at Cloudflare GET /accounts/{account_id}/analytics_engine/sql: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. # cloudflare.workers.sql

Execute an Analytics Engine SQL query via query parameter. Reads the sql object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/analytics_engine/sql`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

Executes a SQL query against Workers Analytics Engine data. Pass the SQL query as a query parameter. The response uses newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) by default, or a single JSON object when the query includes a FORMAT JSON clause. Use the POST method for longer queries that may exceed URL length limits.

Returns 4 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the sql object for one account.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.account_id, d.* EXCLUDE (account_id) FROM (VALUES ('<account_id>')) t(account_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.workers.sql(t.account_id) d ON true

# cloudflare.workers.scripts

List Worker Scripts. Returns every script from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/workers/scripts` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: tags.

List Preview Deployments. Returns every previews deployment from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/workers/workers/{worker_id}/previews/{preview_id}/deployments` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, worker_id, preview_id (each is also returned as a column).

## Endpoint

List all deployments for a Preview.

Returns 28 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List previews deployments for one account and one worker and one preview (account_id, worker_id, preview_id: the URL path ids).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, created_on, annotations FROM cloudflare.workers.previews_deployments('<account_id>', '<worker_id>', '<preview_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Previews deployments for each preview_id in another relation (one API call per row).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.preview_id, r.id, r.created_on FROM (VALUES ('<preview_id>')) t(preview_id), cloudflare.workers.previews_deployments('<account_id>', '<worker_id>', t.preview_id) r

# cloudflare.workers.secrets_secret_name

Get Workers for Platforms Script Secret. Fetches one secrets secret name from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/workers/dispatch/namespaces/{dispatch_namespace}/scripts/{script_name}/secrets/{secret_name}`: one row when it exists, none when the id is unknown (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, dispatch_namespace, script_name, secret_name.

## Endpoint

Get a given secret binding (value omitted) on a script uploaded to a Workers for Platforms dispatch namespace.

Returns 12 columns, described in the declared result schema.

# cloudflare.workers.token

Create a workflow instance event subscription token. tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Cloudflare Zero Trust

Cloudflare Zero Trust: Gateway filtering rules and locations, Data Loss Prevention profiles and datasets, device enrollment and posture (WARP), Digital Experience Monitoring, tunnels, and risk scoring.

Use for secure-web-gateway and endpoint questions: Gateway DNS/HTTP/network rules, DLP detection profiles, enrolled devices and their posture, DEX tests and fleet status, Cloudflare Tunnels, and user risk scores. Most objects are scoped to an account: they are functions of its account_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

## Sections

- **DLP** — DLP: Get mapping; Get DLP account-level settings; Retrieve a specific data tag category; ….
- **Devices** — Devices: Get override codes (deprecated); Get device certificate provisioning status; List client versions; ….
- **Gateway** — Gateway: Get Zero Trust Gateway rule details; List application and application type mappings; Get Zero Trust SSH settings; ….
- **DEX** — DEX: List Cloudflare colos; List account commands; List devices eligible for remote captures; ….
- **Data Security** — Data Security: List DLP content findings; List all export jobs; Get a single export job; ….
- **One** — One: List integrations; Get application details; List applications; ….
- **Zerotrust** — Zerotrust: Get Initial Resolved IP Subnet; Get Zero Trust Connectivity Settings; List hostname routes; ….
- **ZT Risk Scoring** — ZT Risk Scoring: Get all behaviors and associated configuration; Get risk score integration by id; List all risk score integrations for the account; ….
- **Warp Connector** — Warp Connector: Get Mesh node HA configuration; List Mesh node connections; Get a Mesh node; ….
- **CFD Tunnel** — CFD Tunnel: List Cloudflare Tunnels; Get Tunnel configuration; List Cloudflare Tunnel connections; ….
- **Teamnet** — Teamnet: Get tunnel route by IP; Get tunnel route; List tunnel routes; ….
- **More APIs** — Smaller API areas: DLS, Browser Extension, Connectivity, Infrastructure, Tunnels.

# cloudflare.zero_trust.policy_logs

List policy invocation logs. Returns every policy log from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/data-security/posture/policy_logs` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: since, until, integration_id, policy_name.

## Endpoint

Returns a list of policy invocation logs for the given account, sourced from ClickHouse via Ready Analytics. Each entry represents one execution of a policy against a finding instance, including the actions (remediation jobs and webhooks) it dispatched.

Results are scoped to the requesting account's CASB integrations. The `integration_id` query parameter, when supplied, is intersected against the account's integration allowlist; values outside the allowlist are silently dropped.

Pagination is offset-based. The response does not include a total row count; clients should treat a result with fewer than `per_page` entries as the end of the list.

Returns 5 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List policy logs for one account (account_id: the URL path id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT actions, policy, timestamp FROM cloudflare.zero_trust.policy_logs('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Every policy log across all of your accounts, one API call per account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name AS account, r.actions, r.policy FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.zero_trust.policy_logs(p.id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only policy logs matching a since: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT actions, policy, timestamp FROM cloudflare.zero_trust.policy_logs('<account_id>', since := '<since>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: actions
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Actions dispatched by the policy consumer for this invocation. Both arrays are always present and may be empty.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: policy
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The policy configuration that fired.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: timestamp
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When the policy invocation was recorded by ClickHouse, in ClickHouse DateTime format (UTC).

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: trigger
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The finding instance that caused the policy to fire.

arguments.name: account_id
arguments.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

arguments.name: integration_id
arguments.description: Comma-separated list of CASB integration IDs to filter by. At most 100 values, each at most 128 characters. Values outside the account's tenancy allowlist are silently ignored. When omitted, results are scoped to the full allowlist.

arguments.name: policy_name
arguments.description: Comma-separated list of policy display names to filter by. At most 100 values, each at most 255 characters.

arguments.name: since
arguments.description: Lower bound on the log entry timestamp. Accepts ISO 8601 / RFC3339 or epoch seconds. Defaults to 7 days before `until`. The window between `since` and `until` cannot exceed 180 days.

arguments.name: until
arguments.description: Upper bound on the log entry timestamp. Accepts ISO 8601 / RFC3339 or epoch seconds. Defaults to the current time. Must be greater than or equal to `since`.

examples: SELECT actions, policy, timestamp FROM cloudflare.zero_trust.policy_logs('<account_id>')
SELECT p.name AS account, r.actions, r.policy FROM cloudflare.accounts.accounts p, cloudflare.zero_trust.policy_logs(p.id) r
SELECT actions, policy, timestamp FROM cloudflare.zero_trust.policy_logs('<account_id>', since := '<since>')

# cloudflare.zero_trust.instances

List instances of a finding. Returns every instance from Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/data-security/posture/findings/{finding_id}/instances` for the given path ids, paginated. Arguments, in URL order: account_id, finding_id (each is also returned as a column). Optional named arguments sent to the API: archived, max_affliction_date, min_affliction_date, remediation_statuses, finding_instance_ids, asset_ids.

## Endpoint

Lists all security finding instances for a given security finding.

Returns 9 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: List instances for one account and one finding (account_id, finding_id: the URL path ids).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, affliction_date, asset FROM cloudflare.zero_trust.instances('<account_id>', '<finding_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Instances for each finding_id in another relation (one API call per row).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.finding_id, r.id, r.affliction_date FROM (VALUES ('<finding_id>')) t(finding_id), cloudflare.zero_trust.instances('<account_id>', t.finding_id) r

vgi.example_queries.description: Only instances matching a archived: the named argument is sent to the API, which filters.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, affliction_date, asset FROM cloudflare.zero_trust.instances('<account_id>', '<finding_id>', archived := '<archived>')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: account_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: finding_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The `id` of a finding, as returned in each item of the List posture findings response. It is a base64-encoded identifier.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: affliction_date
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: When this specific instance was identified.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: asset
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Asset information including metadata and categorization.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: dlp_contexts
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: DLP context information if this is a content finding.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Unique identifier for the finding instance.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: is_archived
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Whether this finding instance has been archived.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: remediations
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: A list of the 10 most recent remediation jobs for this finding instance, ordered by creation time (most recent first). The 'stale' field indicates whether the remediation job was created before the finding instance's affliction_date (true) or after it (false). If there has never been a remediation job for this finding instance, this field will be an empty array.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: webhooks
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The most recent webhook job invocation for each webhook configuration associated with this finding instance. Each entry represents the latest job (any status) per webhook config. The 'stale' field indicates whether the job was invoked before the finding instance's current affliction_date. If no webhook jobs have been created, this field will be an empty array.

# cloudflare.zero_trust.audit_ssh_settings

Get Zero Trust SSH settings. Reads the audit ssh settings object at Cloudflare GET `/accounts/{account_id}/gateway/audit_ssh_settings`: one row, or none when it doesn't exist (404) or an argument is NULL. Arguments, in URL order: account_id.

## Endpoint

Retrieve all Zero Trust Audit SSH and SSH with Access for Infrastructure settings for an account.

Returns 5 columns, described in the declared result schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the audit ssh settings object for one account.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT created_at, public_key, seed_id FROM cloudflare.zero_trust.audit_ssh_settings('<account_id>')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the audit ssh settings for each row of another relation, keeping rows with no match.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.account_id, d.* EXCLUDE (account_id) FROM (VALUES ('<account_id>')) t(account_id) LEFT JOIN LATERAL cloudflare.zero_trust.audit_ssh_settings(t.account_id) d ON true

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Account id: the id column of cloudflare.accounts.accounts.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: public_key
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Provide the Base64-encoded HPKE public key that encrypts SSH session logs. See https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/use-cases/ssh/ssh-infrastructure-access/#enable-ssh-command-logging.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: seed_id
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Identify the seed ID.

arguments.name: account_id

# cloudflare.zero_trust.colos

# Cloudflare Zones

Cloudflare zones (domains) and their per-zone configuration: settings, caching, page and configuration rules, custom pages and hostnames, waiting rooms, Spectrum, Page Shield, speed, and origin configuration.

Start here to find zone ids (cloudflare.zones.zones) for every zone-scoped table, or to audit a zone's configuration: settings, cache rules, custom hostnames (SSL for SaaS), waiting rooms, and Page Shield scripts. Most objects are scoped to a zone: they are functions of its zone_id — pass an id, or take ids per row from cloudflare.zones.zones.

## Sections

- **Settings** — Settings: Get aegis setting; Get Auto-Origin TLS KEX enrollment status for the given zone; Get Automatic Platform Optimization setting; ….
- **Cache** — Cache: Get Cache Reserve setting; Get Cache Reserve Clear; List origin cloud region mappings; ….
- **Page Shield** — Page Shield: Get a detected connection; List detected connections; Get a detected cookie; ….
- **Waiting Rooms** — Waiting Rooms: Preview active event details; Event details; List events; ….
- **Custom Pages** — Custom Pages: Get a custom asset; List custom assets; Get a custom page; ….
- **Flagship** — Flagship: Get app; List apps; List flag changelog entries; ….
- **Analytics** — Analytics: Query analytics datasets; Get analytics by Co-locations; Get dashboard; ….
- **Spectrum** — Spectrum: Get Spectrum application configuration; Get analytics by time; Get current aggregated analytics; ….
- **Speed API** — Speed API: Get quota and availability; List tested webpages; Get a page test result; ….
- **Rules** — Rules: Get a list item; Get list items; Get lists; ….
- **Web3** — Web3: IPFS Universal Path Gateway Content List Details; IPFS Universal Path Gateway Content List Entry Details; List Web3 Hostnames; ….
- **More APIs** — Smaller API areas: Custom Hostnames, Smart Shield, Origin, Healthchecks, RUM, Snippets, Diagnostics, Hold, Hostnames, Pagerules, Argo, Zones, Managed Headers, Precursor, Cloud Connector, URL Normalization.

# cloudflare.zones.zones

Zones (domains) accessible to the API token. One row per zone, from Cloudflare GET `/zones`.

## Endpoint

Lists, searches, sorts, and filters your zones. Listing zones across more than 500 accounts
is currently not allowed.

## Filters sent to the API

`name`, `status`, `account_id`

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | VARCHAR | Zone id (primary key / join key). |
| `name` | VARCHAR | Zone name (domain). |
| `status` | VARCHAR | Zone status: active, pending, initializing, moved, deleted. |
| `paused` | BOOLEAN | Whether the zone is paused (Cloudflare not proxying). |
| `type` | VARCHAR | Zone type: full, partial (CNAME setup), secondary. |
| `development_mode` | BIGINT | Seconds remaining in development mode (0 = off). |
| `account_id` | VARCHAR | Owning account id. |
| `account_name` | VARCHAR | Owning account name. |
| `name_servers` | VARCHAR | Assigned Cloudflare name servers (JSON array). |
| `created_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | When the zone was created. |
| `modified_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | When the zone was last modified. |
| `activated_on` | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | When the zone was activated. |

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, status FROM cloudflare.zones.zones

# cloudflare.zones.sql

Query analytics datasets. Reads Cloudflare GET `/analytics/sql`, which takes no parameters.

## Endpoint

Executes a SQL query against the analytics datasets available to the caller. SQL placeholders can be bound with query parameters named `param_<name>`, such as `param_status=404` for `$status`. A trailing `FORMAT JSON`, `FORMAT JSONEachRow`, `FORMAT TabSeparated`, or `FORMAT TSV` is supported for all datasets. Without FORMAT, each backend retains its existing default JSON response.

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | VARCHAR | Query result rows keyed by the selected column names. |
| `rows` | BIGINT | Number of rows in `data`. |
| `statistics` | VARCHAR | — |
