workers.summary: Dagster as SQL: assets, materializations, asset checks, partitions, runs, steps, jobs, schedules and sensors from Dagster+ or an open-source dagster-webserver, read through its GraphQL API.
workers.doc_md:
# Dagster

Query [Dagster](https://dagster.io) from DuckDB: the asset graph, materialization history, asset checks, partition status, runs and their steps, and the jobs, schedules and sensors that launch them. Works with open-source `dagster-webserver` and with Dagster+.

Connect by creating a DuckDB secret of type `dagster` after attaching: `base_url` for open-source Dagster, or `organization`, `deployment` and `api_token` for Dagster+.

The `unified` schema exposes runs and task runs in the shape shared by Query.Farm's other orchestrator workers, so pipelines from several orchestrators can be compared in one query.
workers.readme_sql:
SELECT job_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'FAILURE') AS failures
FROM dagster.main.runs
WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY job_name ORDER BY failures DESC;

example_queries.description: How many deployments of each type the organization has
example_queries.sql: SELECT deployment_type, count(*) AS deployments FROM dagster.main.deployments GROUP BY deployment_type ORDER BY deployment_type

example_queries.description: Every code location and whether it loaded
example_queries.sql: SELECT location_name, load_status, error_message FROM dagster.main.code_locations ORDER BY location_name

example_queries.description: What each repository defines
example_queries.sql: SELECT location_name, repository_name, job_count, schedule_count FROM dagster.main.repositories ORDER BY location_name, repository_name

example_queries.description: Op jobs, how many schedules launch each, and the owning team tag
example_queries.sql: SELECT job_name, len(schedule_names) AS schedules, tags['team'] AS team FROM dagster.main.jobs WHERE NOT is_asset_job ORDER BY job_name

example_queries.description: Every schedule and whether it is running
example_queries.sql: SELECT schedule_name, job_name, cron_schedule, status FROM dagster.main.schedules ORDER BY schedule_name

example_queries.description: Every sensor, its type and what it launches
example_queries.sql: SELECT sensor_name, sensor_type, status, target_jobs FROM dagster.main.sensors ORDER BY sensor_name

example_queries.description: Resources and how many jobs depend on each
example_queries.sql: SELECT resource_name, resource_type, len(jobs_using) AS jobs FROM dagster.main.resources ORDER BY resource_name

example_queries.description: Pools with steps waiting for a slot
example_queries.sql: SELECT concurrency_key, slot_count, pending_step_count FROM dagster.main.concurrency_keys WHERE pending_step_count > 0 ORDER BY pending_step_count DESC

example_queries.description: Failure counts per job since the start of 2026
example_queries.sql: SELECT job_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'FAILURE') AS failures, count(*) AS runs FROM dagster.main.runs WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01' GROUP BY job_name ORDER BY failures DESC

example_queries.description: The ten slowest successful runs
example_queries.sql: SELECT run_id, job_name, duration_seconds FROM dagster.main.runs WHERE status = 'SUCCESS' ORDER BY duration_seconds DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Assets by staleness: never-materialized ones first
example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, group_name, last_materialized_at FROM dagster.main.assets ORDER BY last_materialized_at NULLS FIRST, asset_key

example_queries.description: Partitioned assets with failed partitions
example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, failed_partition_count, partition_count FROM dagster.main.assets WHERE is_partitioned AND failed_partition_count > 0 ORDER BY asset_key

example_queries.description: Row counts recorded by each raw_orders materialization since 2026
example_queries.sql: SELECT materialized_at, run_id, CAST(metadata->>'row_count' AS BIGINT) AS row_count FROM dagster.main.asset_materializations WHERE asset_key = 'raw_orders' AND materialized_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01' ORDER BY materialized_at DESC

example_queries.description: How often each asset has been materialized
example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, count(*) AS materializations, max(materialized_at) AS latest FROM dagster.main.asset_materializations GROUP BY asset_key ORDER BY asset_key

example_queries.description: Checks failing on the latest materialization
example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, check_name, latest_severity FROM dagster.main.asset_checks WHERE latest_status = 'FAILED' ORDER BY asset_key, check_name

example_queries.description: Failure rate of each asset check
example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, check_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT passed) AS failures, count(*) AS runs FROM dagster.main.asset_check_executions GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY failures DESC, asset_key

example_queries.description: Partition health per asset
example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, status, count(*) AS partitions FROM dagster.main.asset_partitions GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY asset_key, status

example_queries.description: Partitions of daily_events still to backfill
example_queries.sql: SELECT partition_key FROM dagster.main.asset_partitions WHERE asset_key = 'daily_events' AND status <> 'MATERIALIZED' ORDER BY partition_index

example_queries.description: Status, job and duration of one run (paste a run id from dagster.main.runs)
example_queries.sql: SELECT status, job_name, duration_seconds FROM dagster.main.run('00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003')

example_queries.description: Status and duration of each step of one run
example_queries.sql: SELECT step_key, status, duration_seconds FROM dagster.main.run_step_stats('00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003') ORDER BY step_key

example_queries.description: Which step of a failed run failed, and the root-cause error
example_queries.sql: SELECT step_key, error_class, error_message FROM dagster.main.run_events('00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003') WHERE event_type = 'STEP_FAILURE' ORDER BY step_key

example_queries.description: Run counts per job in the cross-orchestrator status vocabulary
example_queries.sql: SELECT job_name, dagster.main.unified_run_status(status) AS status, count(*) AS runs FROM dagster.main.runs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY job_name, status

example_queries.description: Normalize a few Dagster statuses
example_queries.sql: SELECT s, dagster.main.unified_run_status(s) AS status FROM (VALUES ('FAILURE'), ('CANCELED'), ('STARTING'), ('success')) t(s) ORDER BY s;

example_queries.description: Run counts by normalized status
example_queries.sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS runs FROM dagster.unified.runs GROUP BY status ORDER BY status

example_queries.description: Which steps fail most often
example_queries.sql: SELECT task_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') AS failures FROM dagster.unified.task_runs GROUP BY task_name ORDER BY failures DESC, task_name

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Dagster-native tables and per-run functions, grouped by category: definitions (what code defines: jobs, schedules, sensors, resources and the code locations serving them), assets (the asset graph with lineage, materialization history with metadata as JSON, data-quality checks and their executions, and partition-by-partition status), runs (run history with step counts and triggers, plus functions that take a run id for step timing and the event log with root-cause errors) and instance (concurrency pools; Dagster+ deployments).

Start broad, then drill in: find failed runs, then read their steps and events by run id; find assets with failed partitions or failing checks, then read their history. Asset keys are 'a/b' strings. History tables page through the API, so filter on asset key, run id, status or a time range whenever you can: those filters are sent to Dagster.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Dagster-native tables: definitions (jobs, schedules, sensors, resources, code locations), assets (materializations, checks, partitions) and runs.

Per-run table functions take a run id and return its steps or its event log. Filters on run ids, statuses, job names, asset keys, partitions and time ranges are pushed to Dagster's API.

tags.vgi.doc_md: Schedules with their cron expression, live state and next tick.

vgi.example_queries.description: Every schedule and whether it is running

tags.vgi.title: Dagster Schedules

columns.name: location_name

columns.name: execution_timezone
columns.comment: Timezone the cron expression is evaluated in.

columns.name: default_status
columns.comment: Status declared in code: RUNNING or STOPPED.

columns.name: next_tick_at

tables.name: assets
tables.comment: Software-defined assets with lineage, owners, partition counts and latest materialization

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per software-defined asset: `asset_key` ('a/b'), `asset_key_path`, `group_name`, `description`, `kinds`, flags (`is_partitioned`, `is_materializable`, `is_observable`, `has_asset_checks`), lineage (`dependency_keys`, `depended_by_keys`), `owners`, `tags` (`MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)`), repository/location, partition counts (`partition_count`, `materialized_partition_count`, `failed_partition_count`) and `last_materialized_at` / `last_materialization_run_id`. An `asset_key` = or IN filter is sent to Dagster.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Software-defined assets with lineage, ownership, partition health and latest materialization.

vgi.example_queries.description: Assets by staleness: never-materialized ones first
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, group_name, last_materialized_at FROM dagster.main.assets ORDER BY last_materialized_at NULLS FIRST, asset_key

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, failed_partition_count, partition_count FROM dagster.main.assets WHERE is_partitioned AND failed_partition_count > 0 ORDER BY asset_key

columns.name: job_names

columns.name: partition_count

columns.name: failed_partition_count

columns.name: materializing_partition_count

columns.name: last_materialized_at
columns.comment: Latest materialization time; NULL if never materialized.

columns.name: url

tables.name: resources

tags.vgi.doc_md: Top-level resources and their consumers. Config values are masked: only keys and env-var names.

vgi.example_queries.description: Resources and how many jobs depend on each

tags.vgi.title: Dagster Resources

tables.name: asset_partitions
tables.comment: Every partition of every partitioned asset, with its materialization status

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per partition of each partitioned asset: `asset_key`, `partition_key`, `partition_index` (order in the definition) and `status` (MATERIALIZED, FAILED, MATERIALIZING or MISSING = never materialized). Use it to find gaps before a backfill. One request per asset; an asset_key = / IN filter is pushed down.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Partition-by-partition materialization status of partitioned assets.

vgi.example_queries.description: Partition health per asset
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, status, count(*) AS partitions FROM dagster.main.asset_partitions GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY asset_key, status

vgi.example_queries.description: Partitions of daily_events still to backfill
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT partition_key FROM dagster.main.asset_partitions WHERE asset_key = 'daily_events' AND status <> 'MATERIALIZED' ORDER BY partition_index

tags.vgi.title: Dagster Asset Partitions

columns.name: partition_key
columns.comment: Partition key; multi-partition keys join dimensions with '|'.

tables.name: runs
tables.comment: Runs in the deployment, newest first, with filter pushdown

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Every run in the deployment, newest first, paged 100 at a time. Columns: `run_id`, `job_name`, `status` (Dagster RunStatus: SUCCESS, FAILURE, CANCELED, STARTED, QUEUED, ...), `created_at`, `enqueued_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `updated_at`, `duration_seconds`, `trigger`, `tags` (`MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)`), `asset_selection`, step counts, `materializations`, re-execution ids and `url`. Filters on run_id (=, IN), status (=, IN), job_name (=), created_at and updated_at (ranges) are sent to Dagster, so filter on them rather than scanning all history. Per-run detail: `run_events(run_id)` and `run_step_stats(run_id)`.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Run history, newest first. `run_id`, `status`, `job_name`, `created_at` and `updated_at` filters are pushed to Dagster's `RunsFilter`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Failure counts per job since the start of 2026
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT job_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'FAILURE') AS failures, count(*) AS runs FROM dagster.main.runs WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01' GROUP BY job_name ORDER BY failures DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: The ten slowest successful runs
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT run_id, job_name, duration_seconds FROM dagster.main.runs WHERE status = 'SUCCESS' ORDER BY duration_seconds DESC LIMIT 10

tags.vgi.title: Dagster Run History

columns.name: duration_seconds

columns.name: trigger

columns.name: tags
columns.comment: Run tags as a MAP, e.g. tags['dagster/schedule_name'].

columns.name: asset_selection
columns.comment: Assets the run targeted, as 'a/b' keys; NULL for op jobs.

columns.name: materializations
columns.comment: Number of asset materializations the run produced.

columns.name: root_run_id
columns.comment: First run of a re-execution chain; NULL for an original run.

columns.name: parent_run_id
columns.comment: Run this one re-executed; NULL for an original run.

columns.name: mode
columns.comment: Legacy execution mode (always 'default' on current Dagster).

columns.name: url
columns.comment: Link to the run in the Dagster UI.

tables.name: sensors

tags.vgi.doc_md: Sensors with their type, live state and the jobs they launch.

tags.vgi.doc_md: Jobs in every repository, with tags and the schedules and sensors that launch them.

vgi.example_queries.description: Op jobs, how many schedules launch each, and the owning team tag

tags.vgi.title: Dagster Jobs

columns.name: repository_name
columns.comment: Repository (Definitions object) the row belongs to.

columns.name: location_name
columns.comment: Code location that serves the repository.

columns.name: is_asset_job
columns.comment: True for jobs that materialize assets.

columns.name: tags

tables.name: asset_materializations
tables.comment: Materialization history of every asset, newest first per asset

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Every materialization event: `asset_key`, `materialized_at`, `run_id`, `partition`, `step_key`, `label`, `description`, `tags` (`MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)`) and `metadata` (a JSON object of the event's metadata, e.g. `metadata->>'row_count'`). Assets are read one at a time, newest first, 200 events per request. Pushed down: asset_key (=, IN), materialized_at (ranges) and partition (=, IN). Always filter on asset_key and/or a time range on large deployments.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Materialization history with metadata. `asset_key`, `materialized_at` and `partition` filters are sent to Dagster.

vgi.example_queries.description: Row counts recorded by each raw_orders materialization since 2026
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT materialized_at, run_id, CAST(metadata->>'row_count' AS BIGINT) AS row_count FROM dagster.main.asset_materializations WHERE asset_key = 'raw_orders' AND materialized_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01' ORDER BY materialized_at DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: How often each asset has been materialized
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, count(*) AS materializations, max(materialized_at) AS latest FROM dagster.main.asset_materializations GROUP BY asset_key ORDER BY asset_key

tags.vgi.title: Dagster Asset Materializations

columns.name: materialized_at

columns.name: partition

columns.name: tags

Checks are read one at a time, newest first. asset_key (=, IN) and check_name (=, IN) filters narrow which checks are read.
tags.vgi.doc_md: History of asset check executions with their evaluation results.

vgi.example_queries.description: Failure rate of each asset check
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_key, check_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT passed) AS failures, count(*) AS runs FROM dagster.main.asset_check_executions GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY failures DESC, asset_key

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Cross-orchestrator tables with a fixed column layout shared by every Query.Farm orchestrator worker (Airflow, Prefect, Temporal, Databricks, dbt, GitHub Actions), so a UNION ALL of the same table across catalogs lines up. ## unified

Dagster runs and steps in the shared orchestrator shape, with statuses normalized to queued, running, success, failed, cancelled and skipped.

workers.title: Databricks Workspace
workers.tagline: Databricks jobs, runs, clusters, SQL warehouses, query history and pipelines as SQL in DuckDB (Python)
workers.subtitle: Jobs, runs, clusters, SQL warehouses, query history and pipelines as SQL tables
workers.summary: The Databricks workspace control plane as SQL tables: Lakeflow Jobs and their runs, clusters, SQL warehouses and query history, declarative pipelines, Git folders and secret scopes. Read-only.
workers.doc_md:
# Databricks

Query a Databricks workspace's jobs, runs, clusters, SQL warehouses, query history and pipelines with SQL: the operational metadata you would otherwise click through in the UI or script against the REST API. Works with AWS, Azure and GCP workspaces. Read-only.

Credentials come from a DuckDB secret of type `databricks`, created **after** `ATTACH`:

```sql
-- Personal access token
CREATE SECRET dbx (TYPE databricks, HOST 'https://dbc-a1b2c3d4-e5f6.cloud.databricks.com', TOKEN 'dapi...');
-- OAuth machine-to-machine (service principal), exchanged at <host>/oidc/v1/token
CREATE SECRET dbx (TYPE databricks, HOST 'https://adb-123.7.azuredatabricks.net',
                   CLIENT_ID '...', CLIENT_SECRET '...');
-- Azure AD (Entra ID) access token
CREATE SECRET dbx (TYPE databricks, HOST 'https://adb-123.7.azuredatabricks.net', AZURE_TOKEN '...');
```

Filters on job and run ids, run start times, cluster state, query start time, warehouse, user and status are pushed into the API's own parameters, so a query for last night's failed runs reads only those runs.

Not covered: table data (use a Databricks SQL connector), billable usage (`system.billing`), and anything that changes the workspace.
workers.readme_sql:
-- Which tasks failed in last night's job runs, and with what message?
SELECT r.run_name, r.run_id, t.task_key, t.state_message
FROM databricks.main.job_runs r
JOIN databricks.main.job_run_tasks t USING (run_id)
WHERE r.result_state = 'FAILED' AND r.start_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-14 00:00:00+00'
  AND t.result_state = 'FAILED';

-- The error and stack trace of every task of one run:
SELECT task_key, error, error_trace FROM databricks.main.run_output(2002) WHERE error IS NOT NULL;

example_queries.description: Scheduled jobs and their cron expressions
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, schedule_cron, schedule_timezone FROM databricks.main.jobs WHERE trigger_type = 'periodic' AND NOT schedule_paused ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Failed runs of one job in November 2026 (job_id and the start_time range are sent to the API)
example_queries.sql: SELECT run_id, start_time, state_message FROM databricks.main.job_runs WHERE job_id = 101 AND result_state = 'FAILED' AND start_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01' ORDER BY start_time

example_queries.description: Tasks that needed retries
example_queries.sql: SELECT run_id, task_key, count(*) AS attempts FROM databricks.main.job_run_tasks GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*) > 1 ORDER BY attempts DESC

example_queries.description: Running clusters and their owners (state is sent to the API)
example_queries.sql: SELECT cluster_name, creator_user_name, spark_version, num_workers FROM databricks.main.clusters WHERE state = 'RUNNING' ORDER BY cluster_name

example_queries.description: Resize and termination events of one cluster
example_queries.sql: SELECT timestamp, type, current_num_workers, target_num_workers, reason_code FROM databricks.main.cluster_events WHERE cluster_id = '0915-120000-shared01' AND type IN ('RESIZING', 'TERMINATING') ORDER BY timestamp

example_queries.description: Policies and how many clusters use each
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name, count(c.cluster_id) AS clusters FROM databricks.main.cluster_policies p LEFT JOIN databricks.main.clusters c USING (policy_id) GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY p.name

example_queries.description: Pool utilisation
example_queries.sql: SELECT instance_pool_name, used_count, idle_count, max_capacity FROM databricks.main.instance_pools ORDER BY instance_pool_name

example_queries.description: Warehouses by size and type
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, cluster_size, warehouse_type, enable_serverless_compute, state FROM databricks.main.sql_warehouses ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Failed queries per warehouse in one day (time range and status are sent to the API)
example_queries.sql: SELECT w.name, count(*) AS failed FROM databricks.main.query_history q JOIN databricks.main.sql_warehouses w USING (warehouse_id) WHERE q.status = 'FAILED' AND q.query_start_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-14' AND q.query_start_time < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-15' GROUP BY w.name ORDER BY failed DESC

example_queries.description: Unhealthy pipelines
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, state, latest_update_state FROM databricks.main.pipelines WHERE health = 'UNHEALTHY' ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Update outcomes per pipeline
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.name, u.state, count(*) AS updates FROM databricks.main.pipeline_updates u JOIN databricks.main.pipelines p USING (pipeline_id) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY p.name, u.state

example_queries.description: Error events of one pipeline (pipeline_id and level are sent to the API)
example_queries.sql: SELECT timestamp, flow_name, message FROM databricks.main.pipeline_events WHERE pipeline_id = 'pl-orders-0001' AND level = 'ERROR' ORDER BY timestamp

example_queries.description: Git folders not on main
example_queries.sql: SELECT path, url, branch FROM databricks.main.repos WHERE branch <> 'main' ORDER BY path

example_queries.description: Secret scopes per backend
example_queries.sql: SELECT backend_type, list(scope ORDER BY scope) AS scopes FROM databricks.main.secret_scopes GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY backend_type

example_queries.description: Error messages of the failed tasks of one job run
example_queries.sql: SELECT task_key, attempt_number, error FROM databricks.main.run_output(2002) WHERE error IS NOT NULL ORDER BY task_key

example_queries.description: Notebooks per language under a user's home folder
example_queries.sql: SELECT language, count(*) AS notebooks FROM databricks.main.workspace_objects('/Users/alice@example.com', recursive := true) WHERE object_type = 'NOTEBOOK' GROUP BY language ORDER BY notebooks DESC

example_queries.description: Slowest statements per user
example_queries.sql: SELECT user_name, max(duration_seconds) AS slowest_s, sum(read_bytes) AS bytes_read FROM databricks.main.query_history WHERE status = 'FINISHED' GROUP BY user_name ORDER BY slowest_s DESC

example_queries.description: Run outcomes and median duration per job
example_queries.sql: SELECT run_name, result_state, count(*) AS runs, median(run_duration_seconds) AS median_s FROM databricks.main.job_runs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY run_name, result_state

example_queries.description: Why clusters last terminated
example_queries.sql: SELECT termination_code, count(*) AS clusters FROM databricks.main.clusters WHERE state = 'TERMINATED' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY clusters DESC

example_queries.description: Slowest task per job
example_queries.sql: SELECT job_id, task_key, max(execution_duration_seconds) AS worst_s FROM databricks.main.job_run_tasks WHERE result_state = 'SUCCESS' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY worst_s DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Jobs per owning team tag
example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['team'] AS team, count(*) AS jobs FROM databricks.main.jobs GROUP BY team ORDER BY jobs DESC

example_queries.description: Notebook exit values of the successful tasks of a run
example_queries.sql: SELECT task_key, notebook_result FROM databricks.main.run_output(2101, include_result := true) WHERE result_state = 'SUCCESS' ORDER BY task_key

example_queries.description: Runs per status
example_queries.sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS runs FROM databricks.unified.runs GROUP BY status ORDER BY status

example_queries.description: Task outcomes joined to their runs
example_queries.sql: SELECT r.pipeline, t.status, count(*) AS tasks FROM databricks.unified.task_runs t JOIN databricks.unified.runs r USING (run_id) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY r.pipeline, t.status

example_queries.description: Task attempts per unified status
example_queries.sql: SELECT databricks.unified.unified_status(coalesce(result_state, life_cycle_state)) AS status, count(*) AS tasks FROM databricks.main.job_run_tasks GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY status

example_queries.description: Failure rate per pipeline since November
example_queries.sql: SELECT pipeline, avg((status = 'failed')::INT) AS failure_rate FROM databricks.unified.runs WHERE started_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01' GROUP BY pipeline ORDER BY failure_rate DESC

example_queries.description: Normalize Databricks result and life-cycle states
example_queries.sql: SELECT s AS state, databricks.unified.unified_status(s) AS status FROM (VALUES ('SUCCESS'), ('FAILED'), ('UPSTREAM_FAILED'), ('CANCELED'), ('RUNNING'), ('WAITING_FOR_RETRY')) t(s) ORDER BY s;

example_queries.description: A run with no state yet (NULL) counts as queued
example_queries.sql: SELECT databricks.unified.unified_status(NULL::VARCHAR) AS status;

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Native Databricks resources, one table per REST collection, plus table functions for a run's output and for browsing the workspace tree. The model: a job has runs; a run has task attempts (a retried task is one row per try), each with its own task run id whose output (error, stack trace, logs) can be fetched. Compute and SQL tables describe where work ran. Join on the shared id columns (job_id, run_id, cluster_id, policy_id, warehouse_id, pipeline_id). States are Databricks' own upper-case values. Ids, run start-time ranges, active vs completed state, cluster state and source, query start time, warehouse, user and status, pipeline ids, event level and time ranges are pushed down to the API.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Databricks workspace resources as tables. A job has runs; a run has task attempts (a retried task appears once per try), each with its own task run id and output.

Filter by job, run and time range wherever you can: those predicates become API parameters, so the worker reads only the matching runs instead of the whole history.

Secrets stay in Databricks: secret scopes are listed by name only, and secret-looking Spark config and job parameter values are masked.

functions.name: run_output
functions.comment: Error, stack trace, logs and notebook exit metadata of every task of one Databricks job run

tags.vgi.doc_llm: run_output(run_id, include_result := false, max_log_chars := 65536) returns the output of a job run: one row per task run (every attempt) when run_id is a job run, or one row for a task run id (job_run_tasks.task_run_id). tags.vgi.doc_llm: Cross-orchestrator tables with columns identical across the Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Temporal, Databricks, dbt and GitHub workers, for UNION ALL. runs(orchestrator, run_id, pipeline, status, raw_status, trigger, queued_at, started_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, url) and task_runs(orchestrator, run_id, task_run_id, task_name, status, raw_status, attempt, started_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, url). status is one of queued, running, success, failed, cancelled, skipped; Databricks UPSTREAM_FAILED maps to skipped. run_id is the Jobs run id as text; pipeline is the run name (job name). raw_status is result_state, else life_cycle_state. task_runs has one row per task attempt; attempt is 1-based. Pushed down: run_id, status (active vs completed) and started_at ranges.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## unified

Job runs and task attempts in the shape every Query.Farm orchestrator worker shares, so you can `UNION ALL` Databricks with Airflow, Dagster, Prefect and others.

Databricks' `UPSTREAM_FAILED` counts as `skipped` so each failure is counted once, and each retry of a task is its own task run with a 1-based `attempt`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Task attempts per unified status
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT databricks.unified.unified_status(coalesce(result_state, life_cycle_state)) AS status, count(*) AS tasks FROM databricks.main.job_run_tasks GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY status

functions.name: unified_status
functions.comment: Map a Databricks Jobs run or task state onto queued/running/success/failed/cancelled/skipped

tags.vgi.doc_llm: unified_status(state) maps a Databricks Jobs result_state or life_cycle_state to the shared orchestrator vocabulary used by the unified schema: SUCCESS and SUCCESS_WITH_FAILURES→success; FAILED, TIMEDOUT, MAXIMUM_CONCURRENT_RUNS_REACHED, INTERNAL_ERROR→failed; CANCELED→cancelled; UPSTREAM_FAILED, UPSTREAM_CANCELED, EXCLUDED, DISABLED, SKIPPED→skipped; QUEUED, PENDING, BLOCKED, WAITING_FOR_RETRY→queued; RUNNING, TERMINATING→running. Case-insensitive; unknown and NULL map to queued. Pass coalesce(result_state, life_cycle_state). No credentials or API calls.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## unified_status(state)

Normalize a Databricks Jobs state to `queued`, `running`, `success`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `skipped`, exactly as `unified.runs` and `unified.task_runs` do. Pass the `result_state` of a terminated run, else its `life_cycle_state`.

`UPSTREAM_FAILED` becomes `skipped`: the failure is counted once, on the upstream task.

vgi.example_queries.description: Task attempts per unified status
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT databricks.unified.unified_status(coalesce(result_state, life_cycle_state)) AS status, count(*) AS tasks FROM databricks.main.job_run_tasks GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY status

vgi.executable_examples.description: Normalize Databricks result and life-cycle states
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT s AS state, databricks.unified.unified_status(s) AS status FROM (VALUES ('SUCCESS'), ('FAILED'), ('UPSTREAM_FAILED'), ('CANCELED'), ('RUNNING'), ('WAITING_FOR_RETRY')) t(s) ORDER BY s

vgi.executable_examples.description: A run with no state yet (NULL) counts as queued
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT databricks.unified.unified_status(NULL::VARCHAR) AS status

tags.vgi.title: Unified Status From Databricks State

arguments.name: state
arguments.description: A Databricks Jobs result_state (SUCCESS, FAILED, CANCELED, UPSTREAM_FAILED, ...) or, for a run that has not terminated, its life_cycle_state (QUEUED, PENDING, RUNNING, ...). Case-insensitive; NULL maps to queued.

examples: SELECT databricks.unified.unified_status(coalesce(result_state, life_cycle_state)) AS status, count(*) AS tasks FROM databricks.main.job_run_tasks GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY status
SELECT s AS state, databricks.unified.unified_status(s) AS status FROM (VALUES ('SUCCESS'), ('FAILED'), ('UPSTREAM_FAILED'), ('CANCELED'), ('RUNNING'), ('WAITING_FOR_RETRY')) t(s) ORDER BY s;
SELECT databricks.unified.unified_status(NULL::VARCHAR) AS status;

workers.title: Datadog Observability
workers.tagline: Datadog metrics, logs, spans, monitors, SLOs and incidents as SQL in DuckDB (Python)
workers.subtitle: Metrics, logs, spans, monitors, SLOs and incidents from Datadog as DuckDB tables.
workers.summary: Datadog as SQL: query metrics, search logs, spans, events and the audit trail, and list monitors, SLOs, incidents, dashboards, synthetic tests, hosts and users, on any Datadog site. Read-only.
workers.doc_md:
# Datadog

Datadog in DuckDB SQL through the [Datadog API](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/): metric queries as long rows, log, span, event and audit search with your `WHERE` clause translated into Datadog search syntax, log and span analytics, and monitors, SLOs, incidents, dashboards, synthetics, hosts, users and the service catalog as tables.

Credentials come from a DuckDB secret of type `datadog`, created **after** `ATTACH`:

```sql
-- US1 (datadoghq.com) is the default site
CREATE SECRET dd (TYPE datadog, API_KEY '...', APP_KEY '...');
-- any other site: datadoghq.eu, us3.datadoghq.com, us5.datadoghq.com, ap1.datadoghq.com,
-- ap2.datadoghq.com, ddog-gov.com
CREATE SECRET dd (TYPE datadog, API_KEY '...', APP_KEY '...', SITE 'datadoghq.eu');
```

Use an application key scoped to read permissions (metrics_read, logs_read_data, apm_read, monitors_read, incident_read, dashboards_read, synthetics_read, user_access_read, audit_logs_read, usage_read). The worker never writes to Datadog.
workers.readme_sql:
-- Which production services logged the most errors yesterday?
SELECT service, count(*) AS errors
FROM datadog.main.logs('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-14 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-15 00:00:00+00')
WHERE status = 'error' AND env = 'prod'
GROUP BY service ORDER BY errors DESC;

example_queries.description: Metric names by namespace
example_queries.sql: SELECT split_part(metric, '.', 1) AS namespace, count(*) AS metrics FROM datadog.main.metrics GROUP BY namespace ORDER BY metrics DESC

example_queries.description: Average CPU per production host over one hour
example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['host'] AS host, avg(value) AS avg_cpu FROM datadog.main.metrics_query('avg:system.cpu.user{env:prod} by {host}', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') GROUP BY host ORDER BY avg_cpu DESC

example_queries.description: Type and unit of one metric
example_queries.sql: SELECT type, unit, per_unit FROM datadog.main.metric_metadata('system.net.bytes_rcvd')

example_queries.description: Tag cardinality per key for one metric
example_queries.sql: SELECT key, count(*) AS distinct_values FROM datadog.main.metric_tags('system.cpu.user') GROUP BY key ORDER BY distinct_values DESC

example_queries.description: Production error logs per service for one day (status and env run in Datadog)
example_queries.sql: SELECT service, count(*) AS errors FROM datadog.main.logs('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-02 00:00:00+00') WHERE status = 'error' AND env = 'prod' GROUP BY service ORDER BY errors DESC

example_queries.description: Log volume per service and status for one day, counted in Datadog
example_queries.sql: SELECT groups['service'] AS service, groups['status'] AS status, value AS logs FROM datadog.main.logs_aggregate('env:prod', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-02 00:00:00+00', group_by := 'service,status') ORDER BY logs DESC

example_queries.description: p95 latency and error rate per endpoint of one service
example_queries.sql: SELECT resource_name, count(*) AS spans, quantile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.95) AS p95_s, avg(is_error::INT) AS error_rate FROM datadog.main.spans('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') WHERE service = 'web' AND env = 'prod' GROUP BY resource_name ORDER BY p95_s DESC

example_queries.description: p99 latency per endpoint, computed in Datadog (span durations are in nanoseconds)
example_queries.sql: SELECT groups['resource_name'] AS endpoint, value / 1e6 AS p99_ms FROM datadog.main.spans_aggregate('service:web env:prod', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00', group_by := 'resource_name', aggregation := 'pc99', metric := '@duration') ORDER BY p99_ms DESC

example_queries.description: GitHub deploy events per day for one month
example_queries.sql: SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS day, count(*) AS deploys FROM datadog.main.events('tags:deploy', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00') WHERE source = 'github' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day

example_queries.description: Who changed what during one week
example_queries.sql: SELECT user_email, asset_type, count(*) AS changes FROM datadog.main.audit_events('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-08 00:00:00+00') WHERE action = 'modified' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY changes DESC

example_queries.description: A service filter whose value contains quotes
example_queries.sql: SELECT datadog.main.search_term('service', 'checkout "v2"') AS term

example_queries.description: Read one key from a tag list
example_queries.sql: SELECT datadog.main.tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core', 'legacy'])['team'] AS team

example_queries.description: Distribution metrics with percentiles
example_queries.sql: SELECT metric, configured_tags FROM datadog.main.metrics WHERE metric_type = 'distribution' AND include_percentiles ORDER BY metric

example_queries.description: Logs correlated with error spans through the trace id
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.service, s.resource_name, l.message FROM datadog.main.spans('status:error', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') s JOIN datadog.main.logs('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') l ON l.trace_id = s.trace_id ORDER BY s.service

example_queries.description: Request counts per minute for one service
example_queries.sql: SELECT date_trunc('minute', ts) AS minute, sum(value) AS requests FROM datadog.main.metrics_query('sum:trace.http.request.hits{service:web}.as_count()', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute

example_queries.description: The 50 latest 5xx logs of one service, with a facet read from attributes
example_queries.sql: SELECT ts, host, message, attributes->>'$.http.status_code' AS http_status FROM datadog.main.logs('service:web @http.status_code:>=500', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-02 00:00:00+00', max_rows := 50, newest_first := true) ORDER BY ts DESC

example_queries.description: Hourly p95 of a log measure
example_queries.sql: SELECT ts, value AS p95_ms FROM datadog.main.logs_aggregate('service:web', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 06:00:00+00', aggregation := 'pc95', metric := '@duration', rollup := '1h') ORDER BY ts

example_queries.description: Split a tag list into a map and read keys
example_queries.sql: SELECT m['env'] AS env, m['team'] AS team, m['legacy'] AS legacy FROM (SELECT datadog.main.tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core', 'team:web', 'legacy']) AS m);

example_queries.description: An OR query over a list of hosts, ready to paste into logs()
example_queries.sql: SELECT string_agg(datadog.main.search_term('host', h), ' OR ' ORDER BY h) AS hosts_query FROM (VALUES ('web-1'), ('web-2')) t(h)

example_queries.description: OR several values into one query
example_queries.sql: SELECT string_agg(datadog.main.search_term('host', h), ' OR ' ORDER BY h) AS q FROM (VALUES ('web-1'), ('web-2')) t(h);

example_queries.description: Monitors currently alerting, by priority
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, priority FROM datadog.resources.monitors WHERE overall_state = 'Alert' ORDER BY priority NULLS LAST, name

example_queries.description: Hosts alerting on any monitor
example_queries.sql: SELECT group_tags['host'] AS host, list(monitor_name ORDER BY monitor_name) AS monitors FROM datadog.resources.monitor_groups WHERE status = 'Alert' GROUP BY host ORDER BY host

example_queries.description: Active downtimes and what they mute
example_queries.sql: SELECT scope, monitor_id, end_at FROM datadog.resources.downtimes WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY end_at NULLS LAST

example_queries.description: SLOs per team with their targets
example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['team'] AS team, name, target, timeframe FROM datadog.resources.slos ORDER BY team, name

example_queries.description: Mean time to resolve per severity

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Datadog telemetry for the secret's organization. metrics_query runs a metric query (the query editor syntax, e.g. 'avg:system.cpu.user{env:prod} by {host}') over an explicit window and returns one row per point; read group values from tags['host']. The search functions take a Datadog search query plus from_time and to_time and page with Datadog's cursor; filtering on their typed columns in SQL is pushed into the search query, so `WHERE service = 'web' AND status = 'error'` searches only those logs. Use max_rows with newest_first := true for the latest N. JSON attribute predicates are applied by DuckDB after reading; put facet filters such as @http.status_code:>=500 in the query text instead. logs_aggregate / spans_aggregate group by facets in Datadog and return (groups `MAP`, ts, value) rows. Spans join logs on trace_id. The metrics table lists metric names; metric_metadata and metric_tags describe one metric.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Telemetry: metric queries, log / span / event / audit search and analytics.

`WHERE` predicates on service, status, host, env (and the other hoisted columns) become Datadog search terms; predicates on `ts` narrow the request window. Put facet filters in the query text.

vgi.example_queries.description: Metric names by namespace
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT split_part(metric, '.', 1) AS namespace, count(*) AS metrics FROM datadog.main.metrics GROUP BY namespace ORDER BY metrics DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Average CPU per production host over one hour
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['host'] AS host, avg(value) AS avg_cpu FROM datadog.main.metrics_query('avg:system.cpu.user{env:prod} by {host}', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') GROUP BY host ORDER BY avg_cpu DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Type and unit of one metric
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT type, unit, per_unit FROM datadog.main.metric_metadata('system.net.bytes_rcvd')

vgi.example_queries.description: Tag cardinality per key for one metric
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT key, count(*) AS distinct_values FROM datadog.main.metric_tags('system.cpu.user') GROUP BY key ORDER BY distinct_values DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Production error logs per service for one day (status and env run in Datadog)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT service, count(*) AS errors FROM datadog.main.logs('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-02 00:00:00+00') WHERE status = 'error' AND env = 'prod' GROUP BY service ORDER BY errors DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Log volume per service and status for one day, counted in Datadog
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT groups['service'] AS service, groups['status'] AS status, value AS logs FROM datadog.main.logs_aggregate('env:prod', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-02 00:00:00+00', group_by := 'service,status') ORDER BY logs DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: p95 latency and error rate per endpoint of one service
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT resource_name, count(*) AS spans, quantile_cont(duration_seconds, 0.95) AS p95_s, avg(is_error::INT) AS error_rate FROM datadog.main.spans('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') WHERE service = 'web' AND env = 'prod' GROUP BY resource_name ORDER BY p95_s DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: p99 latency per endpoint, computed in Datadog (span durations are in nanoseconds)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT groups['resource_name'] AS endpoint, value / 1e6 AS p99_ms FROM datadog.main.spans_aggregate('service:web env:prod', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00', group_by := 'resource_name', aggregation := 'pc99', metric := '@duration') ORDER BY p99_ms DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: GitHub deploy events per day for one month
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS day, count(*) AS deploys FROM datadog.main.events('tags:deploy', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00') WHERE source = 'github' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day

vgi.example_queries.description: Who changed what during one week
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT user_email, asset_type, count(*) AS changes FROM datadog.main.audit_events('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-08 00:00:00+00') WHERE action = 'modified' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY changes DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: A service filter whose value contains quotes
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datadog.main.search_term('service', 'checkout "v2"') AS term

vgi.example_queries.description: Read one key from a tag list
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datadog.main.tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core', 'legacy'])['team'] AS team

functions.name: spans
functions.comment: Search APM spans in a time window; SQL filters on service/env/resource/status run in Datadog

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Search APM spans (POST /api/v2/spans/events/search) with a Datadog search query between from_time and to_time (positional). Columns: span_id, trace_id, parent_id, ts (start), end_ts, duration_seconds, service, env, host, resource_name, operation_name, span_type, status ('ok' or 'error'), is_error, tags `MAP`, attributes `JSON`. SQL predicates on service, env, host, resource_name, operation_name, status and trace_id are appended to the query; ts predicates narrow the window. Named: max_rows, newest_first. Join logs on trace_id. For latency percentiles over many spans prefer spans_aggregate.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## spans(query, from_time, to_time, max_rows := NULL, newest_first := false)

APM span search; filters on service, env, resource and status run in Datadog.

vgi.example_queries.description: Logs correlated with error spans through the trace id
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT s.service, s.resource_name, l.message FROM datadog.main.spans('status:error', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') s JOIN datadog.main.logs('*', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') l ON l.trace_id = s.trace_id ORDER BY s.service

functions.name: metrics_query
functions.comment: Query Datadog metrics over a time window and return one row per series point

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Run a Datadog metric query (the query editor syntax: 'avg:system.cpu.user{env:prod} by {host}', functions and arithmetic allowed, several queries comma-separated) over [from_time, to_time] (both `TIMESTAMPTZ`, positional) through GET /api/v1/query. Returns long rows: metric, tags `MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)` with the series' group-by tags (tags['host']), ts `TIMESTAMPTZ`, value `DOUBLE` (NULL in a gap), plus scope, expression, query_index, aggr, unit and interval_seconds. Datadog picks the rollup from the window length (append .rollup(avg, 60) to the query to fix it). The shape matches other metric workers' long format: alias tags as labels and the rows UNION ALL BY NAME with them.

vgi.example_queries.description: Request counts per minute for one service
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date_trunc('minute', ts) AS minute, sum(value) AS requests FROM datadog.main.metrics_query('sum:trace.http.request.hits{service:web}.as_count()', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 01:00:00+00') GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Search logs (POST /api/v2/logs/events/search) matching a Datadog search query (positional, e.g. 'service:web @http.status_code:>=500'; '*' for all) between from_time and to_time (`TIMESTAMPTZ`, positional). Columns: id, ts, status, service, host, env and source (hoisted tags), message, trace_id, tags `MAP`, attributes `JSON` (custom facets: attributes->>'$.http.method'). SQL predicates on service, status, host, env and source (=, <>, IN, OR of equalities, IS NOT NULL) are appended to the query, and ts predicates narrow the window. Named: max_rows caps the rows read, newest_first := true pages from the newest log, indexes (comma-separated) and storage_tier ('indexes', 'online-archives', 'flex'). Pages of up to 1,000 logs follow Datadog's cursor. For counts over large volumes prefer logs_aggregate.

functions.name: tag_map
functions.comment: Turn a list of Datadog key:value tags into a MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR) keyed by tag key

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Convert a list of Datadog tags (key:value strings) into a `MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)` keyed by tag key, split at the first colon, exactly as the worker builds every tags column: a bare tag maps to '' and a key that repeats keeps all its values joined with ','. Use it on tag lists the worker returns as lists (dashboard tags, downtimes.monitor_tags) or on your own data. NULL in, NULL out. Runs offline.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## tag_map(tags)

`tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core'])['team']` returns `core`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read one key from a tag list
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datadog.main.tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core', 'legacy'])['team'] AS team

vgi.executable_examples.description: Split a tag list into a map and read keys
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT m['env'] AS env, m['team'] AS team, m['legacy'] AS legacy FROM (SELECT datadog.main.tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core', 'team:web', 'legacy']) AS m)

tags.vgi.title: Tag List to Map

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: Datadog tags, each a key:value string (a bare tag without a colon is allowed).

examples: SELECT datadog.main.tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core', 'legacy'])['team'] AS team
SELECT m['env'] AS env, m['team'] AS team, m['legacy'] AS legacy FROM (SELECT datadog.main.tag_map(['env:prod', 'team:core', 'team:web', 'legacy']) AS m);

functions.name: search_term
functions.comment: Build a Datadog search term attribute:"value" with the value quoted and escaped

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Return the Datadog search term attribute:"value" for each row, with backslashes and double quotes in the value escaped, so arbitrary text (user input, values read from another table) can be put into the query argument of logs, spans, events or audit_events without changing the query's structure. attribute is used as written: a reserved attribute (service, host, status, env, source), a tag key, or a facet such as @http.url. NULL in, NULL out. Runs offline; no Datadog call.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## search_term(attribute, value)

A quoted, escaped search term: `search_term('service', 'web')` returns `service:"web"`.

vgi.example_queries.description: A service filter whose value contains quotes
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT datadog.main.search_term('service', 'checkout "v2"') AS term

vgi.example_queries.description: An OR query over a list of hosts, ready to paste into logs()
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT string_agg(datadog.main.search_term('host', h), ' OR ' ORDER BY h) AS hosts_query FROM (VALUES ('web-1'), ('web-2')) t(h)

vgi.executable_examples.description: Quote and escape a value
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT datadog.main.search_term('service', 'checkout "v2"') AS term

vgi.executable_examples.description: OR several values into one query
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT string_agg(datadog.main.search_term('host', h), ' OR ' ORDER BY h) AS q FROM (VALUES ('web-1'), ('web-2')) t(h)

tags.vgi.title: Search Term Builder

arguments.name: attribute
arguments.description: Attribute, tag key or @facet to match, e.g. 'service'.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: The exact value to match; quoted and escaped.

examples: SELECT datadog.main.search_term('service', 'checkout "v2"') AS term
SELECT string_agg(datadog.main.search_term('host', h), ' OR ' ORDER BY h) AS hosts_query FROM (VALUES ('web-1'), ('web-2')) t(h)
SELECT datadog.main.search_term('service', 'checkout "v2"') AS term;
SELECT string_agg(datadog.main.search_term('host', h), ' OR ' ORDER BY h) AS q FROM (VALUES ('web-1'), ('web-2')) t(h);

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Datadog configuration and records for the secret's organization, as opposed to telemetry: alerting and its current state, maintenance windows, service-level objectives and their error budgets, incidents, dashboards, synthetic checks, the host inventory, the people and access model, the service catalog and monthly usage metering. Tables page through Datadog's list endpoints on every query; time-ranged history and single-object detail come from table functions that take the object id and a window. Tags from every source are merged into one `MAP` you can index (tags['team']). Join alerting to owners through tags['team'] = the team handle, and telemetry (spans, logs) to the service catalog on the service name.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## resources

Monitors, downtimes, SLOs, incidents, dashboards, synthetics, hosts, users, teams, roles, the service catalog and usage metering.

Every table pages through its list endpoint; tags are maps you can index (`tags['team']`).

vgi.example_queries.description: Monitors currently alerting, by priority
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, priority FROM datadog.resources.monitors WHERE overall_state = 'Alert' ORDER BY priority NULLS LAST, name

vgi.example_queries.description: Hosts alerting on any monitor
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT group_tags['host'] AS host, list(monitor_name ORDER BY monitor_name) AS monitors FROM datadog.resources.monitor_groups WHERE status = 'Alert' GROUP BY host ORDER BY host

vgi.example_queries.description: Active downtimes and what they mute
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT scope, monitor_id, end_at FROM datadog.resources.downtimes WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY end_at NULLS LAST

vgi.example_queries.description: SLOs per team with their targets
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['team'] AS team, name, target, timeframe FROM datadog.resources.slos ORDER BY team, name

vgi.example_queries.description: Mean time to resolve per severity
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT severity, count(*) AS incidents, avg(time_to_resolve_seconds) / 3600 AS mttr_hours FROM datadog.resources.incidents WHERE status = 'resolved' GROUP BY severity ORDER BY severity

vgi.example_queries.description: Dashboards per author
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT author_handle, count(*) AS dashboards FROM datadog.resources.dashboards GROUP BY author_handle ORDER BY dashboards DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Live tests per type and subtype
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT type, subtype, count(*) AS tests FROM datadog.resources.synthetics_tests WHERE status = 'live' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY tests DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Hosts per environment and agent version
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['env'] AS env, agent_version, count(*) AS hosts FROM datadog.resources.hosts GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY env, agent_version

vgi.example_queries.description: Hosts per role
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT value AS role, count(*) AS hosts FROM datadog.resources.host_tags WHERE key = 'role' GROUP BY role ORDER BY hosts DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Active users without MFA
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT email, name FROM datadog.resources.users WHERE status = 'Active' AND NOT service_account AND NOT mfa_enabled ORDER BY email

vgi.example_queries.description: Largest teams
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT handle, user_count FROM datadog.resources.teams ORDER BY user_count DESC, handle

vgi.example_queries.description: Roles by membership
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, user_count FROM datadog.resources.roles ORDER BY user_count DESC, name

vgi.example_queries.description: Tier-1 services per team
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT team, list(service ORDER BY service) AS services FROM datadog.resources.services WHERE tier = '1' GROUP BY team ORDER BY team

vgi.example_queries.description: October SLI and error budget left for one SLO
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT sli_value, target, error_budget_remaining_pct FROM datadog.resources.slo_history('abc123def456', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00') WHERE group_name IS NULL

vgi.example_queries.description: Widget types used on one dashboard
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT w.value->>'$.definition.type' AS widget_type, count(*) AS widgets FROM datadog.resources.dashboard('abc-def-ghi') d, json_each(d.widgets) w GROUP BY widget_type ORDER BY widgets DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Success rate and median duration per location for one test
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT location, avg(passed::INT) AS success_rate, median(duration_ms) AS median_ms FROM datadog.resources.synthetics_results('abc-123-xyz', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00', TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-02 00:00:00+00') GROUP BY location ORDER BY success_rate

vgi.example_queries.description: Monthly infrastructure host count (99th percentile) over five months
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT month, value AS infra_hosts FROM datadog.resources.usage_summary(DATE '2026-06-01', end_month := DATE '2026-10-01') WHERE usage_type = 'infra_host_top99p' ORDER BY month

tags.vgi.title: Datadog Resources

tables.name: services
tables.comment: Service catalog definitions: owning team, tier, lifecycle, languages, contacts and links.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per service definition (GET /api/v2/services/definitions, schema v2.2). service is the dd-service name used in service:<name> tags on spans, logs and metrics; team, tier and lifecycle describe ownership. contacts and links are JSON arrays; definition holds the whole document.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Service catalog entries with ownership, tier and lifecycle.

vgi.example_queries.description: Tier-1 services per team
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT team, list(service ORDER BY service) AS services FROM datadog.resources.services WHERE tier = '1' GROUP BY team ORDER BY team

vgi.example_queries.description: Services without an owner
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT service, lifecycle FROM datadog.resources.services WHERE team IS NULL ORDER BY service

tags.vgi.title: Service Catalog

columns.name: service
columns.comment: Service name (dd-service), as used in service:<name> tags.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Service type: web, db, cache, function, custom ...

columns.name: tags
columns.comment: Tags declared in the definition, as a MAP.

columns.name: last_modified_at
columns.comment: When the definition was last changed.

columns.name: ingestion_source
columns.comment: Where the definition came from: api, github, ui ...

tables.name: teams
tables.comment: Teams with handle, description and member count.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per team (GET /api/v2/team). handle is what team:<handle> tags use, so monitors, services and SLOs join to teams through tags['team'] = handle or services.team = handle.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Teams and their member counts.

vgi.example_queries.description: Largest teams
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT handle, user_count FROM datadog.resources.teams ORDER BY user_count DESC, handle

vgi.example_queries.description: Monitors owned by each team
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.handle, count(m.id) AS monitors FROM datadog.resources.teams t LEFT JOIN datadog.resources.monitors m ON m.tags['team'] = t.handle GROUP BY t.handle ORDER BY monitors DESC

tags.vgi.title: Team Directory

columns.name: handle
columns.comment: Team handle, used in team:<handle> tags.

columns.name: modified_at
columns.comment: When the team was last changed.

tables.name: dashboards
tables.comment: Every dashboard: title, layout, author and timestamps.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per dashboard (GET /api/v1/dashboard, paged). layout_type is 'ordered' (timeboard) or 'free' (screenboard). The listing has no widgets; call dashboard(id) for the full definition.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Every dashboard. The widget JSON comes from `dashboard(id)`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Dashboards per author
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT author_handle, count(*) AS dashboards FROM datadog.resources.dashboards GROUP BY author_handle ORDER BY dashboards DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Stale dashboards
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT title, modified_at FROM datadog.resources.dashboards WHERE modified_at < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01 00:00:00+00' ORDER BY modified_at

tags.vgi.title: Dashboard List

columns.name: url
columns.comment: Link to the dashboard in the Datadog app.

tables.name: roles
tables.comment: Access roles defined in the organization, with how many users hold each one.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per role (GET /api/v2/roles), with user_count. users.role_ids reference roles.id.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Roles and how many users hold each.

vgi.example_queries.description: Roles by membership
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, user_count FROM datadog.resources.roles ORDER BY user_count DESC, name

tags.vgi.title: Access Roles

columns.name: modified_at
columns.comment: When the role was last changed.

tables.name: slos
tables.comment: Service level objectives with their type, targets and tags.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per SLO (GET /api/v1/slo). target / timeframe / warning come from the first threshold, thresholds lists all of them. Metric SLOs carry numerator / denominator queries, monitor SLOs carry monitor_ids. WHERE id = 'x' (or IN) is sent as ids=. For the measured SLI and remaining error budget over a window call slo_history(id, from_time, to_time).
tags.vgi.doc_md: SLOs and their targets. Measured values come from `slo_history`.

vgi.example_queries.description: SLOs per team with their targets
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['team'] AS team, name, target, timeframe FROM datadog.resources.slos ORDER BY team, name

tags.vgi.title: Service Level Objectives

columns.name: target
columns.comment: Target of the primary threshold, in percent (e.g. 99.9).

columns.name: timeframe
columns.comment: Timeframe of the primary threshold: 7d, 30d, 90d, custom.

columns.name: warning
columns.comment: Warning level of the primary threshold, in percent.

columns.name: monitor_ids
columns.comment: Identifiers of the monitors behind a monitor-based SLO (monitors.id values).

columns.name: denominator
columns.comment: Total-events query of a metric SLO.

columns.name: modified_at
columns.comment: When the SLO was last changed.

columns.name: url
columns.comment: Link to the SLO in the Datadog app.

tables.name: users
tables.comment: Users of the organization with status, MFA, service-account flag and role ids.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per user (GET /api/v2/users). status is Active, Pending or Disabled; WHERE status = 'x' is sent as filter[status]. role_ids lists the user's roles: unnest it and join roles.id for role names.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Users with status, MFA and roles.

vgi.example_queries.description: Active users without MFA
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT email, name FROM datadog.resources.users WHERE status = 'Active' AND NOT service_account AND NOT mfa_enabled ORDER BY email

vgi.example_queries.description: Users per role
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT r.name AS role, count(*) AS users FROM datadog.resources.users u, unnest(u.role_ids) AS t(role_id) JOIN datadog.resources.roles r ON r.id = t.role_id GROUP BY role ORDER BY users DESC

tags.vgi.title: Organization Users

columns.name: verified
columns.comment: True once the email is verified.

columns.name: mfa_enabled
columns.comment: True when multi-factor authentication is on.

columns.name: modified_at
columns.comment: When the user was last changed.

tables.name: host_tags
tables.comment: Every tag of every host, one row per host and tag, split into key and value.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per (host, tag) from GET /api/v1/tags/hosts. key and value split the tag at its first colon (a bare tag has value ''). Use it to count hosts per role or env, or to find hosts missing a tag.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Host tags as rows: one per host and tag.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hosts per role
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT value AS role, count(*) AS hosts FROM datadog.resources.host_tags WHERE key = 'role' GROUP BY role ORDER BY hosts DESC

tags.vgi.title: Host Tag Assignments

columns.name: value
columns.comment: Tag value ('' for a bare tag).

tables.name: incidents
tables.comment: Datadog incidents with status, severity, impact, timestamps and time-to-resolve metrics.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per incident (GET /api/v2/incidents). Columns follow the shared incident vocabulary: incident_id, title, status (active, stable, resolved), severity (SEV-1 .. SEV-5, UNKNOWN), created_at, resolved_at, time_to_resolve_seconds and url, so the table UNIONs with other incident sources. incident_number is the public #n. services and teams are lists from the incident fields; every field is also in fields JSON. Compute MTTR as avg(time_to_resolve_seconds).
tags.vgi.doc_md: Incidents with severity, impact and time-to-resolve.

vgi.example_queries.description: Mean time to resolve per severity
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT severity, count(*) AS incidents, avg(time_to_resolve_seconds) / 3600 AS mttr_hours FROM datadog.resources.incidents WHERE status = 'resolved' GROUP BY severity ORDER BY severity

vgi.example_queries.description: Open incidents and the services they hit
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT incident_number, title, severity, services FROM datadog.resources.incidents WHERE status <> 'resolved' ORDER BY created_at

tags.vgi.title: Incident Records

columns.name: incident_number
columns.comment: Public incident number shown in the app (#42).

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.comment: When the incident was resolved; NULL while open.

columns.name: modified_at
columns.comment: When the incident record last changed.

columns.name: time_to_detect_seconds
columns.comment: Seconds from impact start to detection.

columns.name: time_to_internal_response_seconds
columns.comment: Seconds from detection to the first response.

columns.name: teams
columns.comment: Teams the incident is assigned to.

columns.name: commander_user_id
columns.comment: User id of the incident commander.

columns.name: fields
columns.comment: Every incident field (state, severity, root cause, custom fields), JSON.

columns.name: url
columns.comment: Link to the incident in the Datadog app.

tables.name: monitor_groups
tables.comment: One row per monitor and group (e.g. per host) with that group's state and last trigger times.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The per-group states of every monitor (GET /api/v1/monitor?group_states=all). A multi-alert monitor has one row per group such as 'host:web-1,env:prod' (group_tags splits it into a `MAP`); a simple monitor has one row with group_name '*'. WHERE monitor_id = n fetches just that monitor. Use it to find which hosts or services are alerting: WHERE status = 'Alert'.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Which groups of each monitor are alerting, and since when.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hosts alerting on any monitor
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT group_tags['host'] AS host, list(monitor_name ORDER BY monitor_name) AS monitors FROM datadog.resources.monitor_groups WHERE status = 'Alert' GROUP BY host ORDER BY host

vgi.example_queries.description: Groups of one monitor (fetched by id)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT group_name, status, last_triggered_at FROM datadog.resources.monitor_groups WHERE monitor_id = 1001 ORDER BY group_name

tags.vgi.title: Monitor Group States

columns.name: group_name
columns.comment: Group the state belongs to, e.g. 'host:web-1,env:prod' ('*' for a simple monitor).

columns.name: group_tags

columns.name: status
columns.comment: State of this group: OK, Alert, Warn, No Data ...

columns.name: last_nodata_at
columns.comment: When the group last reported no data.

columns.name: last_notified_at
columns.comment: When the group last sent a notification.

tables.name: synthetics_tests
tables.comment: Synthetic API and browser tests: type, status, locations, frequency and tags.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per synthetic test (GET /api/v1/synthetics/tests). type is api, browser or mobile; subtype names the API test kind (http, ssl, dns ...). status is live or paused. monitor_id joins to monitors. Run history comes from synthetics_results(public_id, from_time, to_time).
tags.vgi.doc_md: Synthetic tests. Their runs come from `synthetics_results`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Live tests per type and subtype
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT type, subtype, count(*) AS tests FROM datadog.resources.synthetics_tests WHERE status = 'live' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY tests DESC

tags.vgi.title: Synthetic Tests

columns.name: subtype

columns.name: monitor_id
columns.comment: Monitor that alerts on the test (monitors.id).

columns.name: locations
columns.comment: Locations the test runs from, e.g. 'aws:eu-central-1'.

columns.name: url
columns.comment: Link to the test in the Datadog app.

tables.name: downtimes
tables.comment: Monitor downtimes: scope, target monitor or monitor tags, schedule and status.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per downtime (GET /api/v2/downtime). status is active, scheduled, ended or canceled; WHERE status = 'active' asks Datadog for current downtimes only. A downtime targets either one monitor (monitor_id) or monitors by tag (monitor_tags) within a scope such as env:staging. start_at / end_at give the current or first window; recurring schedules are in schedule JSON.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Monitor downtimes and what they mute.

vgi.example_queries.description: Active downtimes and what they mute
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT scope, monitor_id, end_at FROM datadog.resources.downtimes WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY end_at NULLS LAST

tags.vgi.title: Monitor Downtimes

columns.name: monitor_id
columns.comment: Identifier of the single monitor muted (monitors.id; an id, not a quantity).

columns.name: monitor_tags
columns.comment: Monitor tags selecting the muted monitors, if it targets tags.

columns.comment: Start of the (current or first) downtime window.

columns.name: end_at
columns.comment: End of the window; NULL for an indefinite downtime.

columns.name: schedule

columns.name: modified_at

columns.name: canceled_at
columns.comment: When the downtime was canceled, if it was.

tables.name: hosts
tables.comment: Hosts reporting to Datadog with their status, tags, agent version and recent CPU and load.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per host (GET /api/v1/hosts, paged). tags merges the tags of every source (agent, cloud provider, user) into one `MAP`: tags['env']. up is true while the host reports. WHERE host_name = 'x' is sent as Datadog's host filter and re-checked. cpu_pct / iowait_pct / load are the infrastructure list's recent values; use metrics_query for history.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Hosts, their tags and recent CPU and load.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hosts per environment and agent version
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['env'] AS env, agent_version, count(*) AS hosts FROM datadog.resources.hosts GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY env, agent_version

vgi.example_queries.description: Busiest hosts
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT host_name, cpu_pct, load FROM datadog.resources.hosts WHERE up ORDER BY cpu_pct DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

tags.vgi.title: Infrastructure Hosts

columns.name: host_name

columns.name: id

columns.name: sources

columns.name: tags
columns.comment: Host tags from every source as a MAP.

tables.name: monitors
tables.comment: Datadog monitors with their query, overall state, priority, tags and options.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per monitor (GET /api/v1/monitor, paged). overall_state is OK, Alert, Warn, No Data, Ignored, Skipped or Unknown; priority is 1 (highest) to 5 or NULL. tags is a `MAP`, so tags['team'] gives the owning team. WHERE name = 'x' is sent as Datadog's name filter (substring) and re-checked; WHERE id = n fetches that one monitor. Per-group states live in monitor_groups; links open url.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Monitors and their current overall state. Per-group states are in `monitor_groups`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Monitors currently alerting, by priority
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, priority FROM datadog.resources.monitors WHERE overall_state = 'Alert' ORDER BY priority NULLS LAST, name

vgi.example_queries.description: Monitor count per owning team
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT tags['team'] AS team, count(*) AS monitors FROM datadog.resources.monitors GROUP BY team ORDER BY monitors DESC

tags.vgi.title: Alert Monitors

columns.name: id
columns.comment: Numeric identifier of the monitor (an id, not a quantity).

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Monitor type, e.g. 'metric alert', 'log alert', 'service check'.

columns.name: overall_state
columns.comment: Current overall state: OK, Alert, Warn, No Data, Ignored, Skipped, Unknown.
