tags.vgi.doc_md:
## holdings_scan

The backing scan for the **`holdings` table** — prefer the table. Hive-partitioned by `fund_ticker`. Pass one fund's ticker as the argument (`holdings_scan(fund_ticker => 'QYLD')`) for a single fund, or call `holdings_scan()` with no argument and let a `WHERE fund_ticker` predicate push in (see the example queries). `fund_ticker` is distinct from the constituent `ticker` column.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, weight_percent FROM globalx.main.holdings_scan(fund_ticker => 'QYLD') ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Two funds at once via a pushed IN filter on the no-argument scan
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, count(*) FROM globalx.main.holdings_scan() WHERE fund_ticker IN ('QYLD', 'COPX') GROUP BY fund_ticker

workers.doc_md:
## Invesco ETFs

Invesco US ETF data, exposed as DuckDB tables and table functions.

The **fund** is the unit of the data and is keyed by an exchange `ticker` (e.g. `RSP`) — begin at the catalog to discover that key, then drill into a fund. Fund holdings are **current-only**: Invesco reports a single effective date per fund, so there is no historical time travel (unlike some other providers).

### Sources

- [Invesco ETFs](https://www.invesco.com/us/en/financial-products/etfs.html) — the US ETF lineup and per-fund pages this data comes from.
- [Invesco terms of use](https://www.invesco.com/us/en/resources/terms-of-use.html) — terms that govern use of the site's data.

Data is provided for informational use; review Invesco's terms before redistribution.

example_queries.title: cheapest_etfs
example_queries.description: The cheapest Invesco ETFs by expense ratio
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, expense_ratio_percent FROM invesco.main.products ORDER BY expense_ratio_percent LIMIT 5;

example_queries.title: top_holdings
example_queries.description: The top holdings of the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM invesco.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'RSP' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.description: Cheapest Invesco ETFs by expense ratio
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, expense_ratio_percent FROM invesco.main.products ORDER BY expense_ratio_percent LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Top holdings of RSP
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM invesco.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'RSP' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Recent NAV history for RSP
example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

example_queries.description: Screen the catalog, then drill into a fund's holdings (join on fund_ticker = products.ticker)
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker, p.name, p.expense_ratio_percent, h.ticker AS holding, h.weight_percent FROM invesco.main.products p JOIN invesco.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE p.ticker = 'RSP' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Which S&P 500 Equal Weight funds hold NVIDIA, and at what weight: screen products by strategy, then join to holdings (the ticker filter is pushed into the holdings scan; the join itself is not, so every fund's holdings are read once)
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker, p.name, h.weight_percent FROM invesco.main.products p JOIN invesco.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE p.strategy LIKE 'IDXEQ - S&P 500 Equal Weight%' AND h.ticker = 'NVDA' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC

example_queries.description: Portfolio overlap of QQQ and RSP: how many holdings they share (matched by CUSIP) and the overlap percent, the sum over shared holdings of the smaller of the two weights
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS shared_holdings, round(sum(least(q.weight_percent, r.weight_percent)), 2) AS overlap_percent FROM invesco.main.holdings q JOIN invesco.main.holdings r ON r.cusip = q.cusip WHERE q.fund_ticker = 'QQQ' AND r.fund_ticker = 'RSP'

example_queries.description: RSP's trailing-12-month distribution yield (per-share distributions over the last year divided by the latest NAV) next to its 30-day SEC yield
example_queries.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT sum(amount_per_share) AS ttm_per_share FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 1 YEAR AS DATE))) SELECT f.ticker, round(100 * d.ttm_per_share / f.nav, 2) AS ttm_distribution_yield_percent, f.sec_yield_30day_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP') f CROSS JOIN d

example_queries.description: RSP's 2025 NAV total return without reinvestment: the NAV change from 2024-12-31 to 2025-12-31 plus the per-share distributions with a 2025 ex-date, as a percent of the starting NAV
example_queries.sql: WITH n AS (SELECT arg_min(nav, as_of_date) AS start_nav, arg_max(nav, as_of_date) AS end_nav FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2024-12-31', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')), d AS (SELECT sum(amount_per_share) AS paid FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')) SELECT round(100 * (end_nav / start_nav - 1), 2) AS nav_change_percent, round(100 * paid / start_nav, 2) AS distributions_percent, round(100 * ((end_nav + paid) / start_nav - 1), 2) AS total_return_percent FROM n CROSS JOIN d

example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, ticker, weight_percent FROM invesco.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('RSP', 'SPHQ')

example_queries.description: A bond fund also fills coupon / maturity / rating
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, coupon_percent, maturity_date, rating, weight_percent FROM invesco.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'BSCR' LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Fixed-income ETFs
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, expense_ratio_percent FROM invesco.main.products WHERE asset_class = 'Fixed Income' ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Look up a single fund by ticker
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, expense_ratio_percent FROM invesco.main.products WHERE ticker = 'RSP'

example_queries.description: Top 10 holdings of RSP via the backing scan
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM invesco.main.holdings() WHERE fund_ticker = 'RSP' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Two partitions at once (fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, count(*) FROM invesco.main.holdings() WHERE fund_ticker IN ('RSP', 'SPHQ') GROUP BY fund_ticker

example_queries.description: Key characteristics for RSP
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, primary_benchmark, pe_ratio, expense_ratio_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP')

example_queries.description: Size, holdings count, and 30-day SEC yield
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, net_assets, num_holdings, sec_yield_30day_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP')

example_queries.description: 1-year fund return vs its benchmark
example_queries.sql: SELECT return_1y_percent, benchmark_return_1y_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP')

example_queries.description: Recent RSP distributions
example_queries.sql: SELECT ex_date, amount_per_share FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP') ORDER BY ex_date DESC LIMIT 8

example_queries.description: Total distributions since a start date
example_queries.sql: SELECT sum(amount_per_share) AS total FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01')

example_queries.description: NAV range over a bounded window
example_queries.sql: SELECT min(nav), max(nav) FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Detailed current portfolio holdings for Invesco ETFs as a hive-partitioned table. It is partitioned by fund_ticker (the FUND's ticker, distinct from the constituent `ticker` column): filter `WHERE fund_ticker = '…'` (or `fund_ticker IN (…)`) to pick funds, or scan with no filter to stream EVERY fund's holdings (a couple hundred funds — slow, so prefer a filter). tags.vgi.doc_md:
## holdings

Detailed **current** fund holdings as a **hive-partitioned table**, partitioned by `fund_ticker` (the fund's ticker). `fund_ticker` is distinct from `ticker` (the constituent's own ticker). Filter `WHERE fund_ticker = 'RSP'` for one fund, or scan with no filter to stream every fund (see the example queries).

`WHERE fund_ticker IN ('RSP','SPHQ')` fans out per partition; an unfiltered scan streams every fund (a couple hundred partitions — slow). Holdings are **current-only** (Invesco reports one effective date; no time travel). `weight_percent` is in percent points (0.33 = 0.33%).

functions.name: fund_details
functions.comment: A wide one-row snapshot of a single fund's key facts and characteristics: identifiers, expense ratio, net assets, NAV and closing price, premium/discount, 30-day SEC yield, valuation ratios (P/E, forward P/E, P/B, ROE), annualized returns, and the primary benchmark with its return. `fund` is a ticker like RSP.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One-row detail snapshot for a fund: identifiers, expense ratio, net assets, holdings count, latest NAV/closing price, premium/discount, 30-day SEC yield, valuation ratios (P/E, forward P/E, P/B, return on equity, weighted-average market cap), annualized returns (1y/3y/5y/10y/since inception), and the primary benchmark and its 1-year return. Percent columns are in percent points; pe_ratio / forward_pe_ratio / pb_ratio are ratios (not percents). Deeper than the products row for a single fund.

## fund_details

A wide one-row snapshot of a fund's key facts and characteristics — the details beyond what `products` carries (net assets, holdings count, premium/discount, valuation ratios, benchmark comparison). Percent columns are in percent points; `pe_ratio`, `forward_pe_ratio`, and `pb_ratio` are ratios.

It returns exactly one row; for the whole lineup use `products` (see the example queries).

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, primary_benchmark, pe_ratio, expense_ratio_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP')

vgi.example_queries.description: Size, holdings count, and 30-day SEC yield
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, net_assets, num_holdings, sec_yield_30day_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP')

vgi.example_queries.description: 1-year fund return vs its benchmark
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT return_1y_percent, benchmark_return_1y_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP')

functions.comment: Distribution history for a fund — one row per distribution with ex, record, and payable dates, the total per-share amount, and its ordinary-income / capital-gain / return-of-capital components. `fund` is a ticker; bound the ex-date range with start_date/end_date.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Distribution (dividend / capital-gain) history for a fund: ex / record / payable dates, the total per-share amount, and its ordinary-income, short/long-term capital-gain, and return-of-capital components. Amounts are per-share dollars, not percents. Bound the ex-date range with start_date/end_date.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## distributions

Distribution history, one row per distribution. Amounts are **per-share** dollars (not percentages), with the ordinary-income / capital-gain / return-of-capital breakdown. Bound the ex-date range with `start_date`/`end_date` (see the example queries).

vgi.example_queries.description: Recent RSP distributions
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ex_date, amount_per_share FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP') ORDER BY ex_date DESC LIMIT 8

vgi.example_queries.description: Total distributions since a start date
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT sum(amount_per_share) AS total FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01')

vgi.example_queries.description: RSP's trailing-12-month distribution yield (per-share distributions over the last year divided by the latest NAV) next to its 30-day SEC yield
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT sum(amount_per_share) AS ttm_per_share FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 1 YEAR AS DATE))) SELECT f.ticker, round(100 * d.ttm_per_share / f.nav, 2) AS ttm_distribution_yield_percent, f.sec_yield_30day_percent FROM invesco.main.fund_details('RSP') f CROSS JOIN d

functions.name: nav_history
functions.comment: Daily net-asset-value history for a fund — one row per weekday with the NAV, over the last ~10 years. `fund` is a ticker; bound the valuation-date range with start_date/end_date.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Daily NAV time series for a fund over the last ~10 years (Invesco does not publish older NAVs), one row per weekday: the date and the net asset value per share. A weekday market holiday repeats the prior day's NAV. Bound the range with start_date/end_date. Use it for NAV-based return series. This is fund NAV, not intraday candles.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## nav_history

Daily NAV history over the last ~10 years, one row per weekday (a market holiday repeats the prior NAV). Bound the range with `start_date`/`end_date` (inclusive SQL `DATE`s; omit for the full history). This is **fund NAV**, not an intraday candle series (see the example queries).

vgi.example_queries.description: Daily RSP NAV since a start date
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: NAV range over a bounded window
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT min(nav), max(nav) FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')

vgi.example_queries.description: RSP's 2025 NAV total return without reinvestment: the NAV change from 2024-12-31 to 2025-12-31 plus the per-share distributions with a 2025 ex-date, as a percent of the starting NAV
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH n AS (SELECT arg_min(nav, as_of_date) AS start_nav, arg_max(nav, as_of_date) AS end_nav FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2024-12-31', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')), d AS (SELECT sum(amount_per_share) AS paid FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')) SELECT round(100 * (end_nav / start_nav - 1), 2) AS nav_change_percent, round(100 * paid / start_nav, 2) AS distributions_percent, round(100 * ((end_nav + paid) / start_nav - 1), 2) AS total_return_percent FROM n CROSS JOIN d

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: as_of_date
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Valuation date.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: nav
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Net asset value per share.

arguments.name: fund
arguments.description: The fund to look up, given as an exchange ticker like 'RSP' (a raw CUSIP also works). Required, first positional argument.

arguments.name: end_date
arguments.description: Optional inclusive upper bound on the valuation-day range — omit for no upper bound. Named end_date because END is a reserved SQL keyword.

arguments.name: start_date
arguments.description: Optional inclusive lower bound on the valuation-day range — omit for the full published history (about the last ten years). Filters client-side.

examples: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC
SELECT min(nav), max(nav) FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')

WITH n AS (SELECT arg_min(nav, as_of_date) AS start_nav, arg_max(nav, as_of_date) AS end_nav FROM invesco.main.nav_history('RSP', start_date := DATE '2024-12-31', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')), d AS (SELECT sum(amount_per_share) AS paid FROM invesco.main.distributions('RSP', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01', end_date := DATE '2025-12-31')) SELECT round(100 * (end_nav / start_nav - 1), 2) AS nav_change_percent, round(100 * paid / start_nav, 2) AS distributions_percent, round(100 * ((end_nav + paid) / start_nav - 1), 2) AS total_return_percent FROM n CROSS JOIN d

workers.doc_md:
## iShares ETFs

iShares (BlackRock) US fund data, exposed as DuckDB tables and table functions.

Two ideas run through everything. First, the **fund** is the unit of the data and is keyed by an exchange `ticker` (e.g. `IVV`) — begin at the catalog to discover that key, then drill into a fund. Second, fund holdings are **point-in-time**: you can ask for a fund's constituents as of any past business day, which makes day-over-day portfolio comparison possible.

### Sources

- [iShares ETF screener](https://www.ishares.com/us/products/etf-investments) — the US fund lineup the catalog is read from.
- [Example fund page (IVV)](https://www.ishares.com/us/products/239726/ishares-core-sp-500-etf) — a fund page with the holdings, distributions and NAV data exposed here.
- [BlackRock terms and conditions](https://www.blackrock.com/corporate/compliance/terms-and-conditions) — terms that govern use of the site's data.

Data is provided for informational use; review iShares' terms before redistribution.

example_queries.title: largest_etfs
example_queries.description: The largest iShares ETFs by net assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM ishares.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.title: top_holdings
example_queries.description: The top holdings of the iShares Core S&P 500 ETF
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.description: Ten largest iShares ETFs by net assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM ishares.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Top holdings of IVV
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Join holdings to the catalog: a fund's top holdings alongside its fund-level facts (holdings.fund_ticker = products.ticker)
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.fund_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, h.ticker, h.name, h.weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings h JOIN ishares.main.products p ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker = 'IVV' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Recent daily NAV history for IVV
example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM ishares.main.nav_history('IVV', start_date := DATE '2026-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

example_queries.description: Portfolio drift: IVV's ten largest current stock holdings beside their weight on 2025-12-31 (the holdings table joined to itself read AT that date, matched on ISIN) and the change in percentage points
example_queries.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT isin, ticker, name, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' AND asset_class = 'Equity'), prev AS (SELECT isin, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings AT (TIMESTAMP => DATE '2025-12-31') WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' AND asset_class = 'Equity') SELECT cur.ticker, cur.name, round(prev.weight_percent, 2) AS weight_2025_12_31, round(cur.weight_percent, 2) AS weight_now, round(cur.weight_percent - prev.weight_percent, 2) AS change_pp FROM cur LEFT JOIN prev USING (isin) ORDER BY cur.weight_percent DESC, cur.ticker LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Portfolio overlap of IVV (S&P 500) and IUSG (S&P 900 Growth): how many stocks both hold and the overlapping weight (sum over shared stocks of the smaller of the two weights, percent points)
example_queries.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT fund_ticker, isin, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('IVV', 'IUSG') AND asset_class = 'Equity') SELECT count(*) AS shared_stocks, round(sum(least(a.weight_percent, b.weight_percent)), 1) AS overlap_percent FROM h a JOIN h b ON a.isin = b.isin WHERE a.fund_ticker = 'IVV' AND b.fund_ticker = 'IUSG'

example_queries.description: Bond funds bottom-up: weight-averaged yield to maturity and duration computed from the holdings of AGG, HYG and TLT, beside each fund's published 30-day SEC yield from products
example_queries.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT fund_ticker, sum(weight_percent * ytm_percent) / sum(weight_percent) AS ytm, sum(weight_percent * duration) / sum(weight_percent) AS dur FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('AGG', 'HYG', 'TLT') AND ytm_percent IS NOT NULL AND duration IS NOT NULL GROUP BY fund_ticker) SELECT p.ticker, p.fund_name, round(h.ytm, 2) AS weighted_ytm_percent, round(h.dur, 2) AS weighted_duration_years, p.thirty_day_sec_yield_percent FROM h JOIN ishares.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker ORDER BY weighted_duration_years

example_queries.description: IVV's trailing-12-month distribution yield recomputed from distributions (per-share payouts over the last year) and the latest nav_history NAV, beside the twelve_month_yield_percent that products publishes
example_queries.sql: WITH ttm AS (SELECT sum(total_distribution) AS dist FROM ishares.main.distributions('IVV', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 1 YEAR AS DATE))), nav AS (SELECT max(as_of_date) AS nav_date, arg_max(nav, as_of_date) AS nav FROM ishares.main.nav_history('IVV', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 14 DAY AS DATE))) SELECT p.ticker, nav.nav_date, round(ttm.dist, 4) AS ttm_distributions, round(nav.nav, 2) AS latest_nav, round(100 * ttm.dist / nav.nav, 2) AS computed_ttm_yield_percent, p.twelve_month_yield_percent FROM ttm, nav, ishares.main.products p WHERE p.ticker = 'IVV'

example_queries.description: IVV holdings as of a past date (time travel)
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings AT (TIMESTAMP => DATE '2025-12-31') WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV'

example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('IVV', 'AGG')

example_queries.description: Ten largest iShares ETFs by net assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM ishares.main.products WHERE product_view = 'etf' ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Cheapest bond ETFs by expense ratio
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, expense_ratio_percent FROM ishares.main.products WHERE asset_class = 'Fixed Income' ORDER BY expense_ratio_percent LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Look up a single fund by ticker

example_queries.description: Top 10 holdings of IVV via the backing scan
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings() WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Functions that return iShares fund data at two levels. At the catalog level you screen the whole lineup on key facts and resolve a fund's key. At the fund level you drill into one fund — its holdings (for any past business day, enabling day-over-day comparison), its characteristics, and its distribution and NAV history. A fund is keyed by its exchange `ticker` (e.g. `IVV`); resolve the key at the catalog level first.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## iShares fund data

Work happens at two levels. **Catalog level:** screen the lineup on key facts and find a fund's key. **Fund level:** drill into a single fund — its constituents, characteristics, and time series. A fund is keyed by its exchange `ticker` (e.g. `IVV`).

Holdings are point-in-time: request a fund's constituents as of any past business day to compare a portfolio across dates.

vgi.example_queries.description: Ten largest iShares ETFs by net assets
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM ishares.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Top holdings of IVV
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Join holdings to the catalog: a fund's top holdings alongside its fund-level facts (holdings.fund_ticker = products.ticker)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.fund_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, h.ticker, h.name, h.weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings h JOIN ishares.main.products p ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker = 'IVV' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Recent daily NAV history for IVV
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM ishares.main.nav_history('IVV', start_date := DATE '2026-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Portfolio drift: IVV's ten largest current stock holdings beside their weight on 2025-12-31 (the holdings table joined to itself read AT that date, matched on ISIN) and the change in percentage points
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH cur AS (SELECT isin, ticker, name, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' AND asset_class = 'Equity'), prev AS (SELECT isin, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings AT (TIMESTAMP => DATE '2025-12-31') WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV' AND asset_class = 'Equity') SELECT cur.ticker, cur.name, round(prev.weight_percent, 2) AS weight_2025_12_31, round(cur.weight_percent, 2) AS weight_now, round(cur.weight_percent - prev.weight_percent, 2) AS change_pp FROM cur LEFT JOIN prev USING (isin) ORDER BY cur.weight_percent DESC, cur.ticker LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Portfolio overlap of IVV (S&P 500) and IUSG (S&P 900 Growth): how many stocks both hold and the overlapping weight (sum over shared stocks of the smaller of the two weights, percent points)
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT fund_ticker, isin, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('IVV', 'IUSG') AND asset_class = 'Equity') SELECT count(*) AS shared_stocks, round(sum(least(a.weight_percent, b.weight_percent)), 1) AS overlap_percent FROM h a JOIN h b ON a.isin = b.isin WHERE a.fund_ticker = 'IVV' AND b.fund_ticker = 'IUSG'

vgi.example_queries.description: Bond funds bottom-up: weight-averaged yield to maturity and duration computed from the holdings of AGG, HYG and TLT, beside each fund's published 30-day SEC yield from products
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT fund_ticker, sum(weight_percent * ytm_percent) / sum(weight_percent) AS ytm, sum(weight_percent * duration) / sum(weight_percent) AS dur FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('AGG', 'HYG', 'TLT') AND ytm_percent IS NOT NULL AND duration IS NOT NULL GROUP BY fund_ticker) SELECT p.ticker, p.fund_name, round(h.ytm, 2) AS weighted_ytm_percent, round(h.dur, 2) AS weighted_duration_years, p.thirty_day_sec_yield_percent FROM h JOIN ishares.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker ORDER BY weighted_duration_years

vgi.example_queries.description: IVV's trailing-12-month distribution yield recomputed from distributions (per-share payouts over the last year) and the latest nav_history NAV, beside the twelve_month_yield_percent that products publishes
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH ttm AS (SELECT sum(total_distribution) AS dist FROM ishares.main.distributions('IVV', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 1 YEAR AS DATE))), nav AS (SELECT max(as_of_date) AS nav_date, arg_max(nav, as_of_date) AS nav FROM ishares.main.nav_history('IVV', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 14 DAY AS DATE))) SELECT p.ticker, nav.nav_date, round(ttm.dist, 4) AS ttm_distributions, round(nav.nav, 2) AS latest_nav, round(100 * ttm.dist / nav.nav, 2) AS computed_ttm_yield_percent, p.twelve_month_yield_percent FROM ttm, nav, ishares.main.products p WHERE p.ticker = 'IVV'

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Detailed portfolio holdings for iShares funds as a hive-partitioned, time-travel table. It is partitioned by fund_ticker (the FUND's ticker, distinct from the constituent `ticker` column): filter `WHERE fund_ticker = '…'` (or `fund_ticker IN (…)`) to pick funds, or scan with no filter to stream EVERY fund's holdings (hundreds of funds — slow, so prefer a filter). The as-of date is a time-travel coordinate: omit it for the latest holdings, or read a past day with `AT (TIMESTAMP => DATE '2025-12-31')` — any business day back to ~inception, not just the featured holding_dates. Rows come back weight-descending; weight_percent is in percent points (7.38 = 7.38%); fixed-income funds also fill coupon/maturity/duration/ytm. Join on fund_ticker to products.ticker for fund-level facts.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## holdings

Detailed fund holdings as a **hive-partitioned, time-travel table**. Partitioned by `fund_ticker` (the fund's ticker) with the as-of date as the **time-travel version**. `fund_ticker` is distinct from `ticker` (the constituent's own ticker). Filter `WHERE fund_ticker = 'IVV'` for one fund's latest holdings, or read a past date with `AT (TIMESTAMP => DATE '2025-12-31')` (see the example queries).

`WHERE fund_ticker IN ('IVV','AGG')` fans out per partition; an unfiltered scan streams every fund (hundreds of partitions — slow). `weight_percent` is in percent points (7.38 = 7.38%).

vgi.example_queries.description: Portfolio overlap of IVV (S&P 500) and IUSG (S&P 900 Growth): how many stocks both hold and the overlapping weight (sum over shared stocks of the smaller of the two weights, percent points)
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT fund_ticker, isin, weight_percent FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('IVV', 'IUSG') AND asset_class = 'Equity') SELECT count(*) AS shared_stocks, round(sum(least(a.weight_percent, b.weight_percent)), 1) AS overlap_percent FROM h a JOIN h b ON a.isin = b.isin WHERE a.fund_ticker = 'IVV' AND b.fund_ticker = 'IUSG'

vgi.example_queries.description: Bond funds bottom-up: weight-averaged yield to maturity and duration computed from the holdings of AGG, HYG and TLT, beside each fund's published 30-day SEC yield from products
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT fund_ticker, sum(weight_percent * ytm_percent) / sum(weight_percent) AS ytm, sum(weight_percent * duration) / sum(weight_percent) AS dur FROM ishares.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('AGG', 'HYG', 'TLT') AND ytm_percent IS NOT NULL AND duration IS NOT NULL GROUP BY fund_ticker) SELECT p.ticker, p.fund_name, round(h.ytm, 2) AS weighted_ytm_percent, round(h.dur, 2) AS weighted_duration_years, p.thirty_day_sec_yield_percent FROM h JOIN ishares.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker ORDER BY weighted_duration_years

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## products

The iShares US product catalog as a base table — one row per fund. It takes no arguments; query it directly and filter with a WHERE clause (e.g. `WHERE product_view = 'etf' ORDER BY net_assets DESC`; see the example queries). It returns every product type; narrow it on product_view, ticker, asset_class, and so on. Percent columns (`*_percent`) are in **percent points** (an expense ratio of 0.03 means 0.03%). The ticker column is the key for the other functions.

## holding_dates

The as-of dates iShares features for a fund's holdings — the latest day plus recent month-/year-ends. Use it to pick a date for `holdings()`.

This is *not* the full set of valid dates: `holdings` accepts any business day back to inception, not just these (see the example queries).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One-row detail snapshot for a fund: index tracked, shares outstanding, premium/discount, trading volume, bid-ask spread, holdings count, valuation ratios (P/E, P/B), 3-year beta and standard deviation, yields, and the investment objective plus key benefits. tags.vgi.doc_md:
## fund_details

A wide one-row snapshot of a fund's key facts and characteristics — the details beyond what `products` carries (index, spread, valuation, risk, and the fund's narrative). Percent columns are in percent points. `objective` is clean plain text; `key_benefits_html` is raw HTML (the `_html` suffix signals the format).

It returns exactly one row; for the whole lineup use `products` (see the example queries).

functions.comment: Full distribution history for a fund — one row per distribution with ex/record/payable dates and the per-share total split into income, short- and long-term capital gains, and return of capital. `fund` is a ticker; bound the ex-date range with start_date/end_date.

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## distributions

Full distribution history, one row per distribution. Amounts are **per-share** dollars (not percentages). Bound the ex-date range with `start_date`/`end_date` (see the example queries).

vgi.example_queries.description: Recent IVV distributions
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ex_date, total_distribution FROM ishares.main.distributions('IVV') ORDER BY ex_date DESC LIMIT 8

vgi.example_queries.description: Total distributions since a start date
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT sum(total_distribution) AS ttm_income FROM ishares.main.distributions('IVV', start_date := DATE '2025-01-01')

vgi.example_queries.description: IVV's trailing-12-month distribution yield recomputed from distributions (per-share payouts over the last year) and the latest nav_history NAV, beside the twelve_month_yield_percent that products publishes
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH ttm AS (SELECT sum(total_distribution) AS dist FROM ishares.main.distributions('IVV', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 1 YEAR AS DATE))), nav AS (SELECT max(as_of_date) AS nav_date, arg_max(nav, as_of_date) AS nav FROM ishares.main.nav_history('IVV', start_date := CAST(current_date - INTERVAL 14 DAY AS DATE))) SELECT p.ticker, nav.nav_date, round(ttm.dist, 4) AS ttm_distributions, round(nav.nav, 2) AS latest_nav, round(100 * ttm.dist / nav.nav, 2) AS computed_ttm_yield_percent, p.twelve_month_yield_percent FROM ttm, nav, ishares.main.products p WHERE p.ticker = 'IVV'

workers.doc_md:
## J.P. Morgan ETFs

J.P. Morgan Asset Management US ETF data, exposed as DuckDB tables and a table function.

The **fund** is the unit of the data and is keyed by an exchange `ticker` (e.g. `JEPI`) — begin at the catalog to discover that key, then drill into a fund. Fund holdings are **current-only**: J.P. Morgan reports a single effective date per fund, so there is no historical time travel, and no distribution or NAV time series is published.

### Sources

- [J.P. Morgan ETF fund explorer](https://am.jpmorgan.com/us/en/asset-management/adv/products/fund-explorer/etf) — the US ETF lineup the catalog is read from.
- [J.P. Morgan Asset Management terms of use](https://am.jpmorgan.com/us/en/asset-management/adv/terms-of-use/) — terms that govern use of the site's data.

Data is provided for informational use; review J.P. Morgan's terms before redistribution.

example_queries.title: largest_etfs
example_queries.description: The largest J.P. Morgan ETFs by assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, net_assets FROM jpmorgan.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.title: top_holdings
example_queries.description: The top holdings of the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'JEPI' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.description: Largest J.P. Morgan ETFs by assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, net_assets FROM jpmorgan.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Top holdings of JEPI
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'JEPI' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Full characteristics for JEPI
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, primary_benchmark, expense_ratio_percent, sec_yield_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.fund_details('JEPI')

example_queries.description: Screen the catalog, then drill into a fund's holdings (join on fund_ticker = products.ticker)
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker, p.name, p.net_assets, h.ticker AS holding, h.weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.products p JOIN jpmorgan.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE p.ticker = 'JEPI' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Which J.P. Morgan U.S. equity ETFs hold Apple, largest weight first (catalog joined to holdings on fund_ticker)
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker AS fund_ticker, p.name AS fund_name, h.weight_percent, h.market_value FROM jpmorgan.main.products p JOIN jpmorgan.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE p.asset_class = 'U.S. Equity' AND h.ticker = 'AAPL' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC, p.ticker

example_queries.description: Largest positions JEPI and JEPQ both hold (holdings joined to itself on CUSIP), ranked by the smaller of the two weights
example_queries.sql: SELECT a.ticker, a.name, a.weight_percent AS jepi_weight_percent, b.weight_percent AS jepq_weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings a JOIN jpmorgan.main.holdings b ON a.cusip = b.cusip WHERE a.fund_ticker = 'JEPI' AND b.fund_ticker = 'JEPQ' ORDER BY least(a.weight_percent, b.weight_percent) DESC, a.ticker LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: How concentrated each active U.S. equity ETF is: combined weight of its 10 largest positions, its position count, and its assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker, p.name, p.net_assets, round(sum(h.weight_percent) FILTER (WHERE h.holding_rank <= 10), 2) AS top10_weight_percent, count(*) AS positions FROM jpmorgan.main.products p JOIN jpmorgan.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE p.asset_class = 'U.S. Equity' AND p.management_style = 'Active' GROUP BY p.ticker, p.name, p.net_assets ORDER BY top10_weight_percent DESC, p.ticker

example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, ticker, weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('JEPI', 'JPST')

example_queries.description: A bond fund also fills coupon / maturity
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, coupon_percent, maturity_date, weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'JPST' LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Fixed-income ETFs
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, sec_yield_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.products WHERE asset_class LIKE 'Fixed Income%' ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Look up a single fund by ticker
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, nav, sec_yield_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.products WHERE ticker = 'JEPI'

example_queries.description: Size, holdings count, and Morningstar rating
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, net_assets, num_holdings, morningstar_rating FROM jpmorgan.main.fund_details('JEPI')

example_queries.description: 1-year and since-inception NAV returns
example_queries.sql: SELECT return_1y_percent, return_since_inception_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.fund_details('JEPI')

example_queries.description: Top 10 holdings of JEPI via the backing scan
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings() WHERE fund_ticker = 'JEPI' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Two partitions at once (fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, count(*) FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings() WHERE fund_ticker IN ('JEPI', 'JPST') GROUP BY fund_ticker

tables.name: holdings
tables.comment: Detailed current fund holdings (full position list), hive-partitioned by fund_ticker (filter WHERE fund_ticker = … for one fund, or scan unfiltered for all). Current-only — no time travel; as_of_date reflects J.P. Morgan's reported effective date.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Detailed current portfolio holdings for J.P. Morgan ETFs as a hive-partitioned table — the FULL published position list per fund. It is partitioned by fund_ticker (the FUND's ticker, distinct from the constituent `ticker` column): filter `WHERE fund_ticker = '…'` (or `fund_ticker IN (…)`) to pick funds, or scan with no filter to stream EVERY fund's holdings (75 funds — slow, so prefer a filter). Holdings are current-only — J.P. Morgan reports a single effective date (the as_of_date column), with no historical time travel. Rows come back weight-descending; weight_percent is in percent points (1.71 = 1.71%); bond funds also fill coupon/maturity/rating. Join on fund_ticker to products.ticker for fund-level facts.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## holdings

Detailed **current** fund holdings as a **hive-partitioned table** (the full published position list per fund), partitioned by `fund_ticker` (the fund's ticker). `fund_ticker` is distinct from `ticker` (the constituent's own ticker). Filter `WHERE fund_ticker = 'JEPI'` for one fund, or scan with no filter to stream every fund (see the example queries).

`WHERE fund_ticker IN ('JEPI','JPST')` fans out per partition; an unfiltered scan streams every fund (75 partitions — slow). Holdings are **current-only** (J.P. Morgan reports one effective date; no time travel). `weight_percent` is in percent points (1.71 = 1.71%).

vgi.example_queries.description: Top 10 current holdings of JEPI
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'JEPI' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Which J.P. Morgan U.S. equity ETFs hold Apple, largest weight first (catalog joined to holdings on fund_ticker)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker AS fund_ticker, p.name AS fund_name, h.weight_percent, h.market_value FROM jpmorgan.main.products p JOIN jpmorgan.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE p.asset_class = 'U.S. Equity' AND h.ticker = 'AAPL' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC, p.ticker

vgi.example_queries.description: Largest positions JEPI and JEPQ both hold (holdings joined to itself on CUSIP), ranked by the smaller of the two weights
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT a.ticker, a.name, a.weight_percent AS jepi_weight_percent, b.weight_percent AS jepq_weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings a JOIN jpmorgan.main.holdings b ON a.cusip = b.cusip WHERE a.fund_ticker = 'JEPI' AND b.fund_ticker = 'JEPQ' ORDER BY least(a.weight_percent, b.weight_percent) DESC, a.ticker LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: How concentrated each active U.S. equity ETF is: combined weight of its 10 largest positions, its position count, and its assets
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker, p.name, p.net_assets, round(sum(h.weight_percent) FILTER (WHERE h.holding_rank <= 10), 2) AS top10_weight_percent, count(*) AS positions FROM jpmorgan.main.products p JOIN jpmorgan.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE p.asset_class = 'U.S. Equity' AND p.management_style = 'Active' GROUP BY p.ticker, p.name, p.net_assets ORDER BY top10_weight_percent DESC, p.ticker

vgi.example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, ticker, weight_percent FROM jpmorgan.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('JEPI', 'JPST')

vgi.example_queries.description: A bond fund also fills coupon / maturity

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## products

The J.P. Morgan US ETF catalog as a base table — one row per fund. It takes no arguments; query it directly and filter with a WHERE clause (e.g. `WHERE asset_class = 'U.S. Equity' ORDER BY net_assets DESC`; see the example queries). Percent columns (`*_percent`) are in **percent points** (a return of 7.77 means 7.77%). The `ticker` column is the key for the other functions. The expense ratio is not in this bulk feed — use `fund_details` for it.

workers.doc_md:
## Schwab Asset Management ETFs

Schwab Asset Management US ETF data, exposed as DuckDB tables.

The **fund** is the unit of the data and is keyed by an exchange `ticker` (e.g. `SCHD`) — begin at the catalog to discover that key, then drill into a fund's holdings. Holdings are the current published portfolio (Schwab does not publish historical holdings).

### Sources

- [Schwab Asset Management ETFs](https://www.schwabassetmanagement.com/products/etfs) — the Schwab ETF lineup.
- [Example fund page (SCHD)](https://www.schwabassetmanagement.com/products/schd) — a fund page with the fund facts and holdings exposed here.

Data is provided for informational use; review Schwab's terms before redistribution.

example_queries.title: largest_etfs
example_queries.description: The largest Schwab ETFs by net assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM schwab.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.title: top_holdings
example_queries.description: The top holdings of the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.description: Ten largest Schwab ETFs by net assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM schwab.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Top holdings of SCHD
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Concentration vs cost: the share of each large-cap fund's assets in its 10 largest positions, beside its position count and expense ratio from the catalog
example_queries.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT fund_ticker, weight_percent, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY fund_ticker ORDER BY weight_percent DESC) AS rn FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHG', 'SCHV', 'SCHX')) SELECT p.ticker, p.fund_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, count(*) AS num_positions, round(sum(r.weight_percent) FILTER (WHERE r.rn <= 10), 2) AS top10_weight_percent FROM ranked r JOIN schwab.main.products p ON p.ticker = r.fund_ticker GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY top10_weight_percent DESC

example_queries.description: Fund overlap: how many of the growth ETF SCHG's positions the broad large-cap ETF SCHX also holds, and the overlapping weight (sum of the smaller of the two weights per shared CUSIP)
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS shared_positions, round(sum(least(g.weight_percent, x.weight_percent)), 2) AS overlap_weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings g JOIN schwab.main.holdings x ON g.cusip = x.cusip WHERE g.fund_ticker = 'SCHG' AND x.fund_ticker = 'SCHX' AND g.cusip <> ''

example_queries.description: Look-through exposure: the 10 stocks SCHD, SCHG, SCHV and SCHX together hold the most dollars of, estimated as each fund's net assets times the holding's weight
example_queries.sql: SELECT h.ticker, any_value(h.name) AS name, count(*) AS funds, round(sum(p.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100) / 1e9, 2) AS est_value_usd_bn FROM schwab.main.holdings h JOIN schwab.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHG', 'SCHV', 'SCHX') AND h.ticker <> '' GROUP BY h.ticker ORDER BY est_value_usd_bn DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: The largest positions of the International Equity ETF
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, weight_percent, market_value FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHF' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, name, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHF')

example_queries.description: Join holdings to the catalog for fund-level facts (name + expense ratio)
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.fund_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, h.name, h.weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings h JOIN schwab.main.products p ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Cheapest funds by expense ratio
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, expense_ratio_percent FROM schwab.main.products ORDER BY expense_ratio_percent LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Look up a single fund by ticker
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, expense_ratio_percent FROM schwab.main.products WHERE ticker = 'SCHD'

example_queries.description: Top 10 holdings of SCHD, passing the fund ticker as the argument
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings_scan(fund_ticker => 'SCHD') ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Same, via a pushed-down fund_ticker filter (no argument)
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings_scan() WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Two partitions at once (fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, count(*) FROM schwab.main.holdings_scan() WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHF') GROUP BY fund_ticker

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Schwab fund data

Work happens at two levels. **Catalog level:** screen the lineup on key facts and find a fund's key. **Fund level:** drill into a single fund's constituents. A fund is keyed by its exchange `ticker` (e.g. `SCHD`).

Holdings are the current published portfolio; Schwab does not publish historical holdings.

vgi.example_queries.description: Ten largest Schwab ETFs by net assets
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM schwab.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Top holdings of SCHD
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Concentration vs cost: the share of each large-cap fund's assets in its 10 largest positions, beside its position count and expense ratio from the catalog
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT fund_ticker, weight_percent, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY fund_ticker ORDER BY weight_percent DESC) AS rn FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHG', 'SCHV', 'SCHX')) SELECT p.ticker, p.fund_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, count(*) AS num_positions, round(sum(r.weight_percent) FILTER (WHERE r.rn <= 10), 2) AS top10_weight_percent FROM ranked r JOIN schwab.main.products p ON p.ticker = r.fund_ticker GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY top10_weight_percent DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Fund overlap: how many of the growth ETF SCHG's positions the broad large-cap ETF SCHX also holds, and the overlapping weight (sum of the smaller of the two weights per shared CUSIP)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS shared_positions, round(sum(least(g.weight_percent, x.weight_percent)), 2) AS overlap_weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings g JOIN schwab.main.holdings x ON g.cusip = x.cusip WHERE g.fund_ticker = 'SCHG' AND x.fund_ticker = 'SCHX' AND g.cusip <> ''

vgi.example_queries.description: Look-through exposure: the 10 stocks SCHD, SCHG, SCHV and SCHX together hold the most dollars of, estimated as each fund's net assets times the holding's weight
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT h.ticker, any_value(h.name) AS name, count(*) AS funds, round(sum(p.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100) / 1e9, 2) AS est_value_usd_bn FROM schwab.main.holdings h JOIN schwab.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHG', 'SCHV', 'SCHX') AND h.ticker <> '' GROUP BY h.ticker ORDER BY est_value_usd_bn DESC LIMIT 10

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Detailed portfolio holdings for Schwab ETFs as a hive-partitioned table. It is partitioned by fund_ticker (the FUND's ticker, distinct from the constituent `ticker` column): filter `WHERE fund_ticker = '…'` (or `fund_ticker IN (…)`) to pick funds, or scan with no filter to stream EVERY fund's holdings (~35 funds — slow, and a broad bond fund can list thousands of constituents, so prefer a filter). Schwab publishes CURRENT holdings only, so there is no historical as-of date; as_of_date is the published page's own date. Rows come back weight-descending; weight_percent is in percent points (4.49 = 4.49%). market_value is abbreviated on the page so it is approximate. Join on fund_ticker to products.ticker for fund-level facts (e.g. net_assets × weight_percent / 100 estimates a position's dollars), but name the funds literally on holdings: the fund_ticker filter is pushed down only as a literal = / IN list, not through a join to products or an IN (SELECT …) subquery, which would stream every fund first.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## holdings

Detailed fund holdings as a **hive-partitioned table**, partitioned by `fund_ticker` (the fund's ticker). `fund_ticker` is distinct from `ticker` (the constituent's own symbol). Filter `WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD'` for one fund's holdings (see the example queries).

`WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD','SCHF')` fans out per partition; an unfiltered scan streams every fund (~35 partitions — slow). Schwab publishes **current holdings only** (no historical dates). `weight_percent` is in percent points (4.49 = 4.49%); `market_value` is approximate (abbreviated on the page).

vgi.example_queries.description: Top 10 current holdings of SCHD
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Concentration vs cost: the share of each large-cap fund's assets in its 10 largest positions, beside its position count and expense ratio from the catalog
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT fund_ticker, weight_percent, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY fund_ticker ORDER BY weight_percent DESC) AS rn FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHG', 'SCHV', 'SCHX')) SELECT p.ticker, p.fund_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, count(*) AS num_positions, round(sum(r.weight_percent) FILTER (WHERE r.rn <= 10), 2) AS top10_weight_percent FROM ranked r JOIN schwab.main.products p ON p.ticker = r.fund_ticker GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY top10_weight_percent DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Fund overlap: how many of the growth ETF SCHG's positions the broad large-cap ETF SCHX also holds, and the overlapping weight (sum of the smaller of the two weights per shared CUSIP)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS shared_positions, round(sum(least(g.weight_percent, x.weight_percent)), 2) AS overlap_weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings g JOIN schwab.main.holdings x ON g.cusip = x.cusip WHERE g.fund_ticker = 'SCHG' AND x.fund_ticker = 'SCHX' AND g.cusip <> ''

vgi.example_queries.description: Look-through exposure: the 10 stocks SCHD, SCHG, SCHV and SCHX together hold the most dollars of, estimated as each fund's net assets times the holding's weight
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT h.ticker, any_value(h.name) AS name, count(*) AS funds, round(sum(p.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100) / 1e9, 2) AS est_value_usd_bn FROM schwab.main.holdings h JOIN schwab.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHG', 'SCHV', 'SCHX') AND h.ticker <> '' GROUP BY h.ticker ORDER BY est_value_usd_bn DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: The largest positions of the International Equity ETF
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, weight_percent, market_value FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHF' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, name, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHF')

vgi.example_queries.description: Join holdings to the catalog for fund-level facts (name + expense ratio)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.fund_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, h.name, h.weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings h JOIN schwab.main.products p ON h.fund_ticker = p.ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## products

The Schwab US ETF catalog as a base table — one row per fund. It takes no arguments; query it directly and filter with a WHERE clause (e.g. `WHERE morningstar_category = 'Large Value' ORDER BY net_assets DESC`; see the example queries). Percent columns (`*_percent`) are in **percent points** (an expense ratio of 0.06 means 0.06%). The ticker column is the key for the holdings table.

## holdings_scan

The backing scan for the **`holdings` table** — prefer the table. Hive-partitioned by `fund_ticker`: pass a fund's ticker as the argument (`holdings_scan(fund_ticker => 'SCHD')`) for one fund, or omit it and filter `WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD'` so the filter is pushed down (see the example queries). `fund_ticker` is distinct from the constituent `ticker` column.

vgi.example_queries.description: Top 10 holdings of SCHD, passing the fund ticker as the argument
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings_scan(fund_ticker => 'SCHD') ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Same, via a pushed-down fund_ticker filter (no argument)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, weight_percent FROM schwab.main.holdings_scan() WHERE fund_ticker = 'SCHD' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Two partitions at once (fan-out)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, count(*) FROM schwab.main.holdings_scan() WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SCHD', 'SCHF') GROUP BY fund_ticker

workers.doc_md:
## SPDR ETFs

SPDR / State Street (SSGA) US ETF data, exposed as DuckDB tables and a table function.

The **fund** is the unit of the data and is keyed by an exchange `ticker` (e.g. `SPY`) — begin at the catalog to discover that key, then drill into a fund's holdings or NAV history. Holdings are the current published portfolio (SSGA does not publish historical holdings).

### Sources

- [State Street fund finder](https://www.ssga.com/us/en/intermediary/fund-finder) — the SPDR ETF lineup the catalog is read from.
- [State Street terms and conditions](https://www.ssga.com/us/en/footer/terms-and-conditions) — terms that govern use of the site's data.

Data is provided for informational use; review SSGA's terms before redistribution.

example_queries.title: largest_etfs
example_queries.description: The largest SPDR ETFs by net assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM spdr.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.title: top_holdings
example_queries.description: The top holdings of the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SPY' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.description: Ten largest SPDR ETFs by net assets
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM spdr.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Top holdings of SPY
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SPY' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Recent daily NAV history for SPY
example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY', start_date := DATE '2026-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

example_queries.description: Largest single holding of each of the five biggest SPDR equity ETFs, with its weight and approximate dollar size (the catalog picks the funds; holding_rank = 1 is applied inside the holdings scan, which still reads every fund's file because the join key is not pushed down)
example_queries.sql: WITH biggest AS (SELECT ticker, net_assets FROM spdr.main.products WHERE asset_class = 'Equity' ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 5) SELECT b.ticker AS fund, h.name AS top_holding, h.weight_percent, round(b.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100 / 1e9, 1) AS position_usd_billions FROM biggest b JOIN spdr.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = b.ticker WHERE h.holding_rank = 1 ORDER BY b.net_assets DESC

example_queries.description: Approximate dollar size of SPY's ten largest positions: each holding's weight applied to the fund's net assets from the products catalog (USD billions)
example_queries.sql: SELECT h.holding_rank, h.name, h.ticker, h.weight_percent, round(p.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100 / 1e9, 1) AS position_usd_billions FROM spdr.main.holdings h JOIN spdr.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker = 'SPY' ORDER BY h.holding_rank LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: SPY's price-only NAV change from the prior year-end NAV (base_nav_date) to SSGA's latest performance date, next to the YTD total return the catalog reports for that date (the gap reflects distributions, which a NAV-per-share series excludes)
example_queries.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ticker, performance_as_of, ytd_return_percent FROM spdr.main.products WHERE ticker = 'SPY'), n AS (SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY', start_date := current_date - 500)) SELECT p.ticker, p.performance_as_of, max(n.as_of_date) FILTER (WHERE n.as_of_date < date_trunc('year', p.performance_as_of)) AS base_nav_date, round(100 * (arg_max(n.nav, n.as_of_date) / arg_max(n.nav, n.as_of_date) FILTER (WHERE n.as_of_date < date_trunc('year', p.performance_as_of)) - 1), 2) AS nav_change_percent, p.ytd_return_percent FROM p JOIN n ON n.as_of_date <= p.performance_as_of GROUP BY p.ticker, p.performance_as_of, p.ytd_return_percent ORDER BY p.ticker

example_queries.description: A bond fund fills coupon / maturity / par value
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, coupon_percent, maturity_date, par_value FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'BIL' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, name, weight_percent FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SPY', 'BIL')

example_queries.description: Cheapest equity ETFs by expense ratio
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, expense_ratio_percent FROM spdr.main.products WHERE asset_class = 'Equity' ORDER BY expense_ratio_percent LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Look up a single fund by ticker
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, expense_ratio_percent FROM spdr.main.products WHERE ticker = 'SPY'

example_queries.description: Position count and summed weight for two funds (partition fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, count(*) AS positions, round(sum(weight_percent), 2) AS total_weight FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SPY', 'BIL') GROUP BY fund_ticker ORDER BY positions DESC

example_queries.description: Recent daily total net assets for SPY
example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, total_net_assets FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC LIMIT 5

## SPDR fund data

Work happens at two levels. **Catalog level:** screen the lineup on key facts and find a fund's key. **Fund level:** drill into a single fund — its constituents and its NAV time series. A fund is keyed by its exchange `ticker` (e.g. `SPY`).

Holdings are the current published portfolio; SSGA does not publish historical holdings.

vgi.example_queries.description: Ten largest SPDR ETFs by net assets
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, fund_name, net_assets FROM spdr.main.products ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Top holdings of SPY
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SPY' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Recent daily NAV history for SPY
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY', start_date := DATE '2026-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Largest single holding of each of the five biggest SPDR equity ETFs, with its weight and approximate dollar size (the catalog picks the funds; holding_rank = 1 is applied inside the holdings scan, which still reads every fund's file because the join key is not pushed down)
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH biggest AS (SELECT ticker, net_assets FROM spdr.main.products WHERE asset_class = 'Equity' ORDER BY net_assets DESC LIMIT 5) SELECT b.ticker AS fund, h.name AS top_holding, h.weight_percent, round(b.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100 / 1e9, 1) AS position_usd_billions FROM biggest b JOIN spdr.main.holdings h ON h.fund_ticker = b.ticker WHERE h.holding_rank = 1 ORDER BY b.net_assets DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Approximate dollar size of SPY's ten largest positions: each holding's weight applied to the fund's net assets from the products catalog (USD billions)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT h.holding_rank, h.name, h.ticker, h.weight_percent, round(p.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100 / 1e9, 1) AS position_usd_billions FROM spdr.main.holdings h JOIN spdr.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker = 'SPY' ORDER BY h.holding_rank LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: SPY's price-only NAV change from the prior year-end NAV (base_nav_date) to SSGA's latest performance date, next to the YTD total return the catalog reports for that date (the gap reflects distributions, which a NAV-per-share series excludes)
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ticker, performance_as_of, ytd_return_percent FROM spdr.main.products WHERE ticker = 'SPY'), n AS (SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY', start_date := current_date - 500)) SELECT p.ticker, p.performance_as_of, max(n.as_of_date) FILTER (WHERE n.as_of_date < date_trunc('year', p.performance_as_of)) AS base_nav_date, round(100 * (arg_max(n.nav, n.as_of_date) / arg_max(n.nav, n.as_of_date) FILTER (WHERE n.as_of_date < date_trunc('year', p.performance_as_of)) - 1), 2) AS nav_change_percent, p.ytd_return_percent FROM p JOIN n ON n.as_of_date <= p.performance_as_of GROUP BY p.ticker, p.performance_as_of, p.ytd_return_percent ORDER BY p.ticker

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Detailed portfolio holdings for SPDR / State Street ETFs as a hive-partitioned table. It is partitioned by fund_ticker (the FUND's ticker, distinct from the constituent `ticker` column): filter `WHERE fund_ticker = '…'` (or `fund_ticker IN (…)`) to pick funds, or scan with no filter to stream EVERY fund's holdings (~180 funds — slow, so prefer a filter). SSGA publishes CURRENT holdings only, so there is no historical as-of date; as_of_date is the published file's own date. Rows come back weight-descending; weight_percent is in percent points (7.38 = 7.38%). Equity funds fill ticker/sector/shares_held; bond funds fill coupon/maturity/par_value/market_value. Join on fund_ticker to products.ticker for fund-level facts.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## holdings

Detailed fund holdings as a **hive-partitioned table**, partitioned by `fund_ticker` (the fund's ticker). `fund_ticker` is distinct from `ticker` (the constituent's own ticker). Filter `WHERE fund_ticker = 'SPY'` for one fund's holdings (see the example queries).

`WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SPY','BIL')` fans out per partition; an unfiltered scan streams every fund (~180 partitions — slow). SSGA publishes **current holdings only** (no historical dates). `weight_percent` is in percent points (7.38 = 7.38%).

vgi.example_queries.description: Top 10 current holdings of SPY
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ticker, weight_percent FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'SPY' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: A bond fund fills coupon / maturity / par value
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, coupon_percent, maturity_date, par_value FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'BIL' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, name, weight_percent FROM spdr.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('SPY', 'BIL')

vgi.example_queries.description: Approximate dollar size of SPY's ten largest positions: each holding's weight applied to the fund's net assets from the products catalog (USD billions)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT h.holding_rank, h.name, h.ticker, h.weight_percent, round(p.net_assets * h.weight_percent / 100 / 1e9, 1) AS position_usd_billions FROM spdr.main.holdings h JOIN spdr.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker = 'SPY' ORDER BY h.holding_rank LIMIT 10

## products

The SPDR / State Street US ETF catalog as a base table — one row per fund. It takes no arguments; query it directly and filter with a WHERE clause (e.g. `WHERE asset_class = 'Equity' ORDER BY net_assets DESC`; see the example queries). Percent columns (`*_percent`) are in **percent points** (an expense ratio of 0.09 means 0.09%). The ticker column is the key for the other functions.

functions.name: nav_history
functions.comment: Daily net-asset-value history for a fund back to inception — one row per business day with NAV per share, shares outstanding, and total net assets. `fund` is a ticker; bound the range with start_date/end_date (recommended, as old funds return thousands of rows).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Daily NAV time series for a fund back to inception: NAV per share, shares outstanding, and total net assets. Use it for NAV-based return series, drawdowns, and asset-growth analysis. This is fund NAV, not market-price candles — for traded prices use a market-data source. Old funds return thousands of rows, so bound with start_date/end_date.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## nav_history

Daily NAV history back to inception, one row per business day. This is **fund NAV**, not a market-price candle series. Old funds return thousands of rows — bound with `start_date`/`end_date` (see the example queries).

vgi.example_queries.description: SPY NAV since the start of the year
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY', start_date := DATE '2026-01-01') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Recent daily total net assets for SPY
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, total_net_assets FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC LIMIT 5

vgi.example_queries.description: SPY's price-only NAV change from the prior year-end NAV (base_nav_date) to SSGA's latest performance date, next to the YTD total return the catalog reports for that date (the gap reflects distributions, which a NAV-per-share series excludes)
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ticker, performance_as_of, ytd_return_percent FROM spdr.main.products WHERE ticker = 'SPY'), n AS (SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY', start_date := current_date - 500)) SELECT p.ticker, p.performance_as_of, max(n.as_of_date) FILTER (WHERE n.as_of_date < date_trunc('year', p.performance_as_of)) AS base_nav_date, round(100 * (arg_max(n.nav, n.as_of_date) / arg_max(n.nav, n.as_of_date) FILTER (WHERE n.as_of_date < date_trunc('year', p.performance_as_of)) - 1), 2) AS nav_change_percent, p.ytd_return_percent FROM p JOIN n ON n.as_of_date <= p.performance_as_of GROUP BY p.ticker, p.performance_as_of, p.ytd_return_percent ORDER BY p.ticker

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: as_of_date
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Valuation date.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: nav
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Net asset value per share.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: shares_outstanding
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Shares outstanding.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: total_net_assets
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Total net assets (fund AUM) in the fund's currency.

arguments.name: fund
arguments.description: The fund to look up, given as an exchange ticker like 'SPY'. Required, first positional argument.

arguments.name: end_date
arguments.description: Optional inclusive upper bound on the day range — omit for no upper bound. Named end_date because END is a reserved SQL keyword.

arguments.name: start_date
arguments.description: Optional inclusive lower bound on the day range — omit for no lower bound. Filters client-side.

SELECT as_of_date, total_net_assets FROM spdr.main.nav_history('SPY') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC LIMIT 5

workers.tagline: Vanguard US ETF data (catalog + holdings) as DuckDB tables over VGI
workers.subtitle: Screen the Vanguard US ETF lineup and query current fund holdings, distributions and daily NAV and price history.
workers.summary: Vanguard US ETF data from Vanguard's public product feed: screen the lineup on fund facts, inspect what a fund currently holds, and pull per-fund distribution and NAV/price history — vgi-etf-vanguard
workers.doc_md:
## Vanguard ETFs

Vanguard US ETF data, exposed as DuckDB tables and table functions.

The **fund** is the unit of the data and is keyed by an exchange `ticker` (e.g. `VOO`) — begin at the catalog to discover that key, then drill into a fund. Fund holdings are **current-only**: Vanguard reports a single as-of date per fund, so there is no historical time travel (unlike some other providers).

### Sources

- [Vanguard ETF list](https://investor.vanguard.com/investment-products/list/etfs) — the US ETF lineup the catalog is read from.
- [Example fund profile (VOO)](https://investor.vanguard.com/investment-products/etfs/profile/voo) — a fund page with the holdings, distributions and price history exposed here.

Data is provided for informational use; review Vanguard's terms before redistribution.

example_queries.title: cheapest_etfs
example_queries.description: The cheapest Vanguard ETFs by expense ratio
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, long_name, expense_ratio_percent FROM vanguard.main.products ORDER BY expense_ratio_percent LIMIT 5;

example_queries.title: top_holdings
example_queries.description: The top holdings of the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM vanguard.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'VOO' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 5;

example_queries.description: Cheapest Vanguard ETFs by expense ratio
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, long_name, expense_ratio_percent FROM vanguard.main.products ORDER BY expense_ratio_percent LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Top holdings of VOO
example_queries.sql: SELECT ticker, name, weight_percent FROM vanguard.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'VOO' ORDER BY weight_percent DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Recent NAV history for VOO
example_queries.sql: SELECT as_of_date, nav FROM vanguard.main.nav_history('VOO', period := '1Y') ORDER BY as_of_date DESC

example_queries.description: NVIDIA's portfolio weight in four Vanguard equity ETFs alongside each fund's name and expense ratio (holdings joined to products); a fund that doesn't hold it (the value fund VTV) drops out
example_queries.sql: SELECT h.fund_ticker, p.long_name, p.expense_ratio_percent, h.holding_rank, h.weight_percent FROM vanguard.main.holdings h JOIN vanguard.main.products p ON p.ticker = h.fund_ticker WHERE h.fund_ticker IN ('VOO', 'VTI', 'VUG', 'VTV') AND h.ticker = 'NVDA' ORDER BY h.weight_percent DESC

example_queries.description: Portfolio overlap between VOO and VUG: how many constituents they share and the overlapping weight (the sum, over shared stocks, of the smaller of the two funds' weights)
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS shared_holdings, round(sum(least(a.weight_percent, b.weight_percent)), 2) AS overlap_percent FROM vanguard.main.holdings a JOIN vanguard.main.holdings b ON a.ticker = b.ticker WHERE a.fund_ticker = 'VOO' AND b.fund_ticker = 'VUG' AND a.ticker <> ''

example_queries.description: BND's trailing-12-month distribution yield (per-share distributions over the past year divided by the current price from products) next to its published SEC yield
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.ticker, p.price, p.yield_percent AS sec_yield_percent, count(*) AS payouts, round(sum(d.per_share_amount), 4) AS paid_per_share, round(100 * sum(d.per_share_amount) / p.price, 2) AS trailing_12m_yield_percent FROM vanguard.main.distributions('BND', start_date := (CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL 1 YEAR)::DATE) d CROSS JOIN vanguard.main.products p WHERE p.ticker = 'BND' GROUP BY p.ticker, p.price, p.yield_percent ORDER BY p.ticker

example_queries.description: VOO's approximate 1-year total return: the NAV change over the past year plus the distributions paid in the same window (payouts not reinvested)
example_queries.sql: WITH nav AS (SELECT arg_min(nav, as_of_date) AS start_nav, arg_max(nav, as_of_date) AS end_nav FROM vanguard.main.nav_history('VOO', period := '1Y')), paid AS (SELECT sum(per_share_amount) AS per_share FROM vanguard.main.distributions('VOO', start_date := (CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL 1 YEAR)::DATE)) SELECT nav.start_nav, nav.end_nav, round(paid.per_share, 4) AS distributions_per_share, round(100 * (nav.end_nav / nav.start_nav - 1), 2) AS nav_return_percent, round(100 * ((nav.end_nav + paid.per_share) / nav.start_nav - 1), 2) AS total_return_percent FROM nav CROSS JOIN paid ORDER BY total_return_percent

example_queries.description: Two funds at once (partition fan-out)
example_queries.sql: SELECT fund_ticker, ticker, weight_percent FROM vanguard.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker IN ('VOO', 'VTI')

example_queries.description: A bond fund also fills coupon / maturity / face
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, coupon_percent, maturity, weight_percent FROM vanguard.main.holdings WHERE fund_ticker = 'BND' LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Bond ETFs with their 1-year return
