workers.title: Fivetran ELT
workers.tagline: Fivetran connections, schemas, sync history and account metadata as SQL in DuckDB (TypeScript)
workers.subtitle: Fivetran connections, sync status and history, schema config, destinations, transformations and access as SQL tables.
workers.summary: Fivetran's ELT control plane as SQL: connections and their sync status, schema config, sync history, destinations, transformations, users and teams, read-only from the Fivetran REST API.
workers.doc_md:
# Fivetran

Query a Fivetran account from DuckDB: connections and their health, schema/table/column configuration (blocking and hashing), sync history, destinations, transformations, users, teams and access, webhooks and hybrid deployment agents. Read-only.

Create a `fivetran` secret with an API key and secret (`API_KEY`, `API_SECRET`) — a user key or a system key. Filters are translated into Fivetran path and query parameters where the API supports them; cursor paging and HTTP 429 `Retry-After` are handled for you.

**Not in the REST API:** monthly active rows (MAR), usage/cost, log events and transformation run history. Those come from the Fivetran Platform Connector.

### Sources and references

- [Fivetran REST API reference](https://fivetran.com/docs/rest-api/api-reference) — the endpoints this worker reads
- [Authentication](https://fivetran.com/docs/rest-api/getting-started) — API key + secret, or a system key
- [Pagination](https://fivetran.com/docs/rest-api/pagination) — `cursor` / `limit`
- [Sync history](https://fivetran.com/docs/rest-api/api-reference/connections/connection-sync-history) — 7-day window
- [Fivetran Platform Connector](https://fivetran.com/docs/logs/fivetran-platform) — logs, MAR and usage (not in the REST API)

example_queries.title: connections_columns
example_queries.description: The connections table's status columns (binds only; create a fivetran secret and drop LIMIT 0 for rows)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, service, setup_state, sync_state, succeeded_at, failed_at FROM fivetran.main.connections LIMIT 0;

example_queries.title: runs_columns
example_queries.description: The unified.runs columns (binds only; create a fivetran secret and drop LIMIT 0 for rows)
example_queries.sql: SELECT orchestrator, run_id, pipeline, status, started_at FROM fivetran.unified.runs LIMIT 0;

example_queries.description: Which account the secret points at
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, account_name FROM fivetran.main.accounts

example_queries.description: Enabled human users by most recent login (both filters push down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT email, role, logged_in_at FROM fivetran.main.users WHERE active AND user_type = 'REGULAR_USER' ORDER BY logged_in_at DESC NULLS LAST

example_queries.description: Service accounts holding API keys
example_queries.sql: SELECT email FROM fivetran.main.users WHERE has_api_key AND user_type = 'SERVICE_ACCOUNT' ORDER BY email

example_queries.description: Teams and their account roles
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, role FROM fivetran.main.teams ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Who is in which team
example_queries.sql: SELECT t.name AS team, u.email, m.role FROM fivetran.main.team_users m JOIN fivetran.main.teams t ON t.id = m.team_id JOIN fivetran.main.users u ON u.id = m.user_id ORDER BY team, u.email

example_queries.description: Destination roles of one team (team_id pushes down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_id, group_id, role FROM fivetran.main.team_groups WHERE team_id = 't_data_eng' ORDER BY group_id

example_queries.description: Connection grants per team
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_id, count(*) AS connections FROM fivetran.main.team_connections GROUP BY team_id ORDER BY connections DESC

example_queries.description: Direct destination roles per user
example_queries.sql: SELECT u.email, g.name AS destination_group, m.role FROM fivetran.main.user_groups m JOIN fivetran.main.users u ON u.id = m.user_id JOIN fivetran.main.groups g ON g.id = m.group_id ORDER BY u.email

example_queries.description: Connections one user can manage (user_id pushes down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT user_id, connection_id, role FROM fivetran.main.user_connections WHERE user_id = 'u_grace' ORDER BY connection_id

example_queries.description: Connection count per group
example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, count(c.id) AS connections FROM fivetran.main.groups g LEFT JOIN fivetran.main.connections c ON c.group_id = g.id GROUP BY g.name ORDER BY connections DESC

example_queries.description: Active users of one destination group (both filters push down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT email, role FROM fivetran.main.group_users WHERE group_id = 'g_warehouse' AND active ORDER BY email

example_queries.description: Destinations that are broken or incomplete
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, service, region FROM fivetran.main.destinations WHERE setup_status <> 'CONNECTED' ORDER BY id

example_queries.description: Configured log destinations
example_queries.sql: SELECT service, enabled FROM fivetran.main.log_services ORDER BY service

example_queries.description: All open connection errors, newest first
example_queries.sql: SELECT c.schema_name, e.title, e.created_at FROM fivetran.main.connection_errors e JOIN fivetran.main.connections c ON c.id = e.connection_id ORDER BY e.created_at DESC

example_queries.description: Active webhooks notified when syncs end
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, url FROM fivetran.main.webhooks WHERE active AND list_contains(events, 'sync_end') ORDER BY id

example_queries.description: Read one field of a connection's state
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, state->>'lsn' AS lsn FROM fivetran.main.connection_states WHERE connection_id = 'c_postgres'

example_queries.description: Current destination-level roles
example_queries.sql: SELECT name FROM fivetran.main.roles WHERE list_contains(scope, 'DESTINATION') AND NOT is_deprecated ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Blocked (disabled) tables across all connections
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, schema_name, table_name FROM fivetran.main.connection_tables WHERE NOT enabled ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: Enabled tables by sync mode
example_queries.sql: SELECT sync_mode, count(*) AS tables FROM fivetran.main.connection_tables WHERE enabled GROUP BY sync_mode ORDER BY tables DESC

example_queries.description: Warning codes by number of affected tables
example_queries.sql: SELECT code, count(*) AS tables FROM fivetran.main.connection_warnings GROUP BY code ORDER BY tables DESC

example_queries.description: Schema enablement of one connection
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, schema_name, enabled_table_count, table_count FROM fivetran.main.connection_schemas WHERE connection_id = 'c_postgres' ORDER BY schema_name

example_queries.description: Private links and their state
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, cloud_provider, link_state FROM fivetran.main.private_links ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Active connections that are broken or whose last sync failed
example_queries.sql: SELECT schema_name, service, setup_state, failed_at FROM fivetran.main.connections WHERE NOT paused AND (setup_state <> 'connected' OR failed_at > coalesce(succeeded_at, TIMESTAMPTZ '1970-01-01')) ORDER BY failed_at DESC

example_queries.description: Open user tasks in one group (group_id pushes down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT schema_name, t.code, t.message FROM fivetran.main.connections, unnest(tasks) AS u(t) WHERE group_id = 'g_lake' ORDER BY schema_name

example_queries.description: Active transformations with their latest outcome and runtime
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, type, status, last_ended_at - last_started_at AS last_runtime FROM fivetran.main.transformations WHERE NOT paused ORDER BY last_started_at DESC

example_queries.description: Models built by dbt Core transformations (type pushes down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, unnest(output_model_names) AS model FROM fivetran.main.transformations WHERE type = 'DBT_CORE' ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: Connections per source type, with readable names
example_queries.sql: SELECT ct.name, count(*) AS connections FROM fivetran.main.connections c JOIN fivetran.main.connector_types ct ON ct.id = c.service GROUP BY ct.name ORDER BY connections DESC

example_queries.description: Proxy agent health
example_queries.sql: SELECT display_name, status, connector_count FROM fivetran.main.proxy_agents ORDER BY display_name

example_queries.description: Agents of one group with health and load (group_id pushes down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT display_name, version, online, len(usage) AS connections FROM fivetran.main.hybrid_deployment_agents WHERE group_id = 'g_lake' ORDER BY display_name

example_queries.description: Failure counts and mean sync duration per connection (last 7 days)
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'FAILURE') AS failures, count(*) AS syncs, avg(duration_seconds) AS avg_seconds FROM fivetran.main.syncs GROUP BY connection_id ORDER BY failures DESC

example_queries.description: Recent syncs of one connection (connection and time window push down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, status, reason, started_at FROM fivetran.main.syncs WHERE connection_id = 'c_postgres' AND started_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-14 00:00:00+00' ORDER BY started_at DESC

example_queries.description: System keys with manage permissions
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, p.resource_type, p.access_level FROM fivetran.main.system_keys, unnest(permissions) AS u(p) WHERE p.access_level = 'MANAGE' ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Transformations per dbt project
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.id, count(t.id) AS transformations FROM fivetran.main.transformation_projects p LEFT JOIN fivetran.main.transformations t ON t.project_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY p.id

example_queries.description: Columns hashed for PII
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, table_name, column_name FROM fivetran.main.connection_columns WHERE hashed ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: Blocked and hashed column counts per connection
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT enabled) AS blocked, count(*) FILTER (WHERE hashed) AS hashed FROM fivetran.main.connection_columns GROUP BY connection_id ORDER BY connection_id

example_queries.description: Run outcomes per Fivetran connection in the unified shape
example_queries.sql: SELECT pipeline, status, count(*) AS runs FROM fivetran.unified.runs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY pipeline, status

example_queries.description: Failed syncs since a date (UNION ALL with other orchestrators' unified.runs)
example_queries.sql: SELECT orchestrator, pipeline, run_id, started_at FROM fivetran.unified.runs WHERE status = 'failed' AND started_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-14 00:00:00+00' ORDER BY started_at DESC

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Every connection, formerly called connector (GET /v1/connections): id, group_id, service (source type), schema_name (the destination schema prefix that names the connection), paused, sync_frequency (minutes), schedule_type, daily_sync_time, the flattened status (setup_state connected/incomplete/broken, sync_state scheduled/syncing/paused/rescheduled, update_state on_schedule/delayed, schema_status, is_historical_sync, rescheduled_for), succeeded_at and failed_at (last successful / failed sync), tasks and warnings (`LIST` of `STRUCT` code/message/details — tasks are actions a user must take), networking ids, a dashboard url and config as JSON with secret-looking values masked. A connection is failing when failed_at > succeeded_at (or succeeded_at IS NULL). WHERE id = / IN fetches those connections directly; group_id = / IN and schema_name = push down as query parameters. service has no API filter and is applied locally. Join group_id to groups.id (and destinations.id), service to connector_types.id, and hybrid_deployment_agent_id / proxy_agent_id / private_link_id to those tables' id.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## connections

Connections with source type, schedule, setup/sync state, last success and failure, and open tasks.

**Pushdown:** `id` (= / IN) → GET /v1/connections/{id}; `group_id` (= / IN) → `group_id`; `schema_name =` → `schema`. `service` and the status columns are filtered locally.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT schema_name, service, setup_state, failed_at FROM fivetran.main.connections WHERE NOT paused AND (setup_state <> 'connected' OR failed_at > coalesce(succeeded_at, TIMESTAMPTZ '1970-01-01')) ORDER BY failed_at DESC
vgi.example_queries.description: Active connections that are broken or whose last sync failed

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT schema_name, t.code, t.message FROM fivetran.main.connections, unnest(tasks) AS u(t) WHERE group_id = 'g_lake' ORDER BY schema_name
vgi.example_queries.description: Open user tasks in one group (group_id pushes down)

tables.name: syncs
tables.comment: Sync runs of each connection over the last 7 days

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Individual syncs (GET /v1/connections/{id}/sync-history): connection_id, id (the sync id), status (COMPLETED, FAILURE, CANCELED, INCOMPLETE, RESCHEDULED, PAUSED), reason (why it did not complete), started_at, ended_at (NULL while running), duration_seconds and the extract / process / load volumes. The REST API keeps only the last 7 days: a pushed started_at range becomes the start_time / end_time window (clamped to those 7 days; without one the full 7 days is read). Without a pushed connection filter it lists every connection first and then makes one more API call per connection, so filter on connection_id (= or IN) when you can. Older history lives in the Fivetran Platform Connector, not the REST API.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## syncs

Sync runs per connection (last 7 days) with outcome, timing and data volume.

**Pushdown:** `connection_id` (= / IN) selects connections (path parameter); `started_at` ranges → `start_time` / `end_time` (clamped to the API's 7-day window).

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'FAILURE') AS failures, count(*) AS syncs, avg(duration_seconds) AS avg_seconds FROM fivetran.main.syncs GROUP BY connection_id ORDER BY failures DESC
vgi.example_queries.description: Failure counts and mean sync duration per connection (last 7 days)

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, status, reason, started_at FROM fivetran.main.syncs WHERE connection_id = 'c_postgres' AND started_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-14 00:00:00+00' ORDER BY started_at DESC
vgi.example_queries.description: Recent syncs of one connection (connection and time window push down)

vgi.categories.name: unified
vgi.categories.title: Unified Orchestration
vgi.categories.description: Runs in the column shape shared by every orchestrator worker, for UNION ALL across tools.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Cross-orchestrator views. unified.runs has the exact column set every orchestration worker (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Temporal, Databricks, dbt, GitHub, Fivetran) exposes, so their runs UNION ALL into one table. Fivetran contributes its syncs (last 7 days). There is no unified.task_runs: Fivetran syncs have extract/process/load volumes but no timed sub-tasks.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## unified

Fivetran syncs in the shared `unified.runs` shape, for UNION ALL with the runs of other orchestration workers (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Temporal, Databricks, dbt, GitHub).

Each sync of the last 7 days is one run: `pipeline` is the connection's schema name, `status` is mapped onto queued / running / success / failed / cancelled / skipped and `raw_status` keeps Fivetran's own value.

There is no `unified.task_runs`: a Fivetran sync reports extract / process / load volumes but no timed sub-tasks.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT pipeline, status, count(*) AS runs FROM fivetran.unified.runs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY pipeline, status
vgi.example_queries.description: Run outcomes per Fivetran connection in the unified shape

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT orchestrator, pipeline, run_id, started_at FROM fivetran.unified.runs WHERE status = 'failed' AND started_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-14 00:00:00+00' ORDER BY started_at DESC
vgi.example_queries.description: Failed syncs since a date (UNION ALL with other orchestrators' unified.runs)

tags.vgi.title: Unified Orchestration Runs

WHERE pipeline = / IN narrows the connection listing (schema parameter) and started_at ranges become the API's time window.

workers.title: Fixed-Width Records
workers.tagline: Read and write fixed-width / flat-file / mainframe data in DuckDB with SQL — Perl unpack / Python struct / COBOL copybooks (COMP-3, EBCDIC, OCCURS, REDEFINES). A VGI worker.
workers.subtitle: Parse, write, and inspect fixed-width, struct-template, and COBOL copybook records as typed columns.
workers.summary: Fixed-width / Perl-unpack / Python-struct / COBOL-copybook record parsing and formatting for SQL.
workers.doc_md:
# fixed

Fixed-width / flat-file record parsing and formatting over Apache Arrow. Brings Perl-`unpack`, Python-`struct`, and COBOL-copybook style layouts to SQL so you can ingest and emit mainframe and legacy flat-file data without an external ETL step.

A layout spec is given in one of three auto-detected formats — a Perl/Python `unpack` **template** string (e.g. `A10 N s>`), a **JSON** field list, or a COBOL **copybook** — and maps each field to a typed column (`BIGINT` / `REAL` / `DOUBLE` / `VARCHAR` / `BOOLEAN`, `DECIMAL(p,s)` for COMP-3 / zoned / implied-point numbers, `LIST` for `OCCURS` / `OCCURS … DEPENDING ON`, `STRUCT` for groups, nested JSON `fields`, and REDEFINES). Encodings are `ascii` (default) or `ebcdic` (CP037); record framing is `newline` (default), `fixed`, `rdw`, or `rdw_blocked`. The spec format is auto-detected from the spec text; on the table functions you can force it with `format =>` ('template' / 'json' / 'copybook') when a layout would otherwise be ambiguous. With the defaults (newline framing, ascii encoding) the common call is just `(record, spec)`.

Decoding a record into a `STRUCT` and re-encoding that `STRUCT` back to bytes are exact inverses, and whole files can be scanned, written, or introspected — including heterogeneous multi-record-type files (a UNION per record type) — without leaving SQL.

## Sources and references

- [Perl pack / unpack templates](https://perldoc.perl.org/functions/pack) — the template letters the `template` spec format follows
- [Python struct format strings](https://docs.python.org/3/library/struct.html) — byte-order and size prefixes
- [COBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COBOL) — copybook PIC, COMP-3, OCCURS and REDEFINES clauses
- [GnuCOBOL](https://gnucobol.sourceforge.io/) — a free COBOL compiler and manual for checking copybook layouts

example_queries.description: Decode a fixed-width record into a typed struct with a template spec.
example_queries.sql: SELECT fixed.main.unpack_fixed('JohnDoe  00042', 'A8 N')

example_queries.description: Encode a struct back into a fixed-width record blob.
example_queries.sql: SELECT fixed.main.pack_fixed({'name': 'Jo', 'id': 7}, 'A2 N')

example_queries.description: Introspect how a layout spec resolves — fields, types, byte offsets — without reading data.
example_queries.sql: SELECT * FROM fixed.main.describe_fixed('name:A10 qty:9(5)')

example_queries.description: Write a relation out to a fixed-width file and report the write summary.
example_queries.sql: SELECT rows_written, bytes_written FROM fixed.main.write_fixed((FROM (VALUES ('ALICE', 5)) AS v(name, qty)), '/tmp/fixed_example.dat', 'name:A10 qty:9(5)')

example_queries.description: Scan a sample fixed-width accounts file (pinned to a release tag) into typed rows.
example_queries.sql: SELECT * FROM fixed.main.read_fixed('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/accounts.dat', 'name:A10 qty:9(5)')

example_queries.description: Convert an ASCII newline feed (10-char name, 5-digit qty) into a fixed-length EBCDIC mainframe file with a packed-decimal COMP-3 quantity by piping read_fixed into write_fixed; returns 3 rows and 39 bytes (13-byte records, no separators).
example_queries.sql: SELECT rows_written, bytes_written FROM fixed.main.write_fixed((FROM fixed.main.read_fixed('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/accounts.dat', 'name:A10 qty:9(5)')), '/tmp/fixed_example_ebcdic.dat', '01 ACCT. 05 NAME PIC X(10). 05 QTY PIC S9(5) COMP-3.', encoding => 'ebcdic', framing => 'fixed')

example_queries.description: Extract only the detail (D) records of a header/detail/trailer file with read_multi and write them to a flat sku/qty fixed-width file with write_fixed, dropping the header and trailer; returns 2 rows and 32 bytes.
example_queries.sql: SELECT rows_written, bytes_written FROM fixed.main.write_fixed((SELECT d.sku, d.qty FROM (SELECT union_extract(record, 'D') AS d FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}') WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D')), '/tmp/fixed_example_details.dat', 'sku:A10 qty:9(5)')

example_queries.description: Reconcile a header/detail/trailer batch: report the header's company, the number of detail records and their total qty, the trailer's declared record count, and whether the detail count matches it (ACME CORP, 2 details, qty 49, trailer 2, balanced).
example_queries.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT record FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}')) SELECT max(union_extract(record, 'H').co) AS company, count(*) FILTER (WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D') AS detail_records, sum(union_extract(record, 'D').qty) AS total_qty, max(union_extract(record, 'T').cnt) AS trailer_count, count(*) FILTER (WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D') = max(union_extract(record, 'T').cnt) AS balanced FROM r

example_queries.title: unpack_pack_roundtrip
example_queries.description: Decode a fixed-width record into a typed struct, then encode that struct back into the original record bytes — pack_fixed and unpack_fixed are exact inverses.
example_queries.sql:
SELECT fixed.main.unpack_fixed('JohnDoe  00042', 'name:A8 qty:9(5)') AS decoded;
SELECT fixed.main.pack_fixed(fixed.main.unpack_fixed('JohnDoe  00042', 'name:A8 qty:9(5)'), 'name:A8 qty:9(5)')::VARCHAR = 'JohnDoe  00042' AS round_trips;

example_queries.description: Introspect how a layout spec resolves — one row per field with its dotted path, DuckDB type, byte offset, and width — without reading any data.

example_queries.description: Write a relation out to a fixed-width file with COPY ... TO and scan it straight back into typed rows with read_fixed.
example_queries.sql:
COPY (FROM (VALUES ('ALICE', 5), ('BOB', 7)) AS v(name, qty)) TO '/tmp/fixed_executable_example.dat' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', spec 'name:A10 qty:9(5)');

example_queries.description: Read an undelimited header/detail/trailer file (every record type padded to one 21-byte length, so framing => 'fixed') into a UNION column and project the detail rows' sku and qty.

example_queries.description: Count records of each type in a multi-record file that contains an unknown record type ('Z'): the spec's "default": "D" decodes it as a detail record instead of failing the read.

example_queries.description: Profile a newline-delimited fixed-width feed of 7-digit ids (a sample file pinned to a release tag): count the rows and report the id range.

example_queries.description: Unpack an EBCDIC (CP037) record; the encoding also governs zoned/COMP-3 sign nibbles.

example_queries.description: EBCDIC round-trip: unpack an EBCDIC record ('Jo' then a 4-byte big-endian 7) and pack it back with the same encoding, confirming the bytes are reproduced.
example_queries.sql: SELECT fixed.main.pack_fixed(fixed.main.unpack_fixed(rec, 'name:A2 id:N', 'ebcdic'), 'name:A2 id:N', 'ebcdic') = rec AS round_trips FROM (SELECT '\xD1\x96\x00\x00\x00\x07'::BLOB AS rec)

agent_tasks: I have one fixed-width record 'JOHN      00042' where the first 10 characters are an account name and the next 5 are a zero-padded quantity. Parse it and return the quantity as a single integer column named qty.

The file data/large.dat is a newline-delimited fixed-width feed where each record is a single 7-digit zero-padded id. Profile it: return one row with a column named records (the record count), a column named min_id, and a column named max_id.

A nightly job drops one or more fixed-width account files into data/, named acct1.dat, acct2.dat, and so on. Each record is a 10-character account name followed by a 5-digit zero-padded quantity. Read all of the acct*.dat files at once and return the total quantity across every record as a single column named total_qty.

We received a mainframe extract at data/ebcdic_comp3.dat. It is EBCDIC-encoded and fixed-length (no line delimiters between records). Each record is a 5-byte name (PIC X(5)) followed by a signed packed-decimal amount PIC S9(3)V99 COMP-3. Decode the file and return the largest amount as a single column named max_amount.

We need to emit a single fixed-width record for an export. The layout is a 10-character left-justified, space-padded account name followed by a 5-digit zero-padded quantity. Build the record for account name 'ALICE' with quantity 5 and return the resulting record text as a single column named record.

A mainframe ingest job needs an account record encoded the way the host expects it: the name as a 5-byte EBCDIC field (PIC X(5)) followed by a signed packed-decimal amount PIC S9(3)V99 COMP-3. Encode name 'ACME' with amount 123.45 and return the resulting record bytes as an uppercase hex string in a single column named record_hex.

Export two accounts to a newline-delimited fixed-width file at data/_agent_write.dat, where each record is a 10-character left-justified name followed by a 5-digit zero-padded quantity: ALICE with quantity 5 and BOB with quantity 999. Return the write summary with a column named rows_written and a column named bytes_written.

I have the fixed-width layout 'name:A10 qty:9(5)' — a 10-character name followed by a 5-digit zero-padded quantity. Without reading any data, work out the byte offset at which the qty field begins and return it as a single column named qty_offset.

This multi-record layout has a 1-byte record-type discriminator at offset 0 and two record types: a header 'H' with one field, and a detail 'D' with a 10-char sku and a 5-digit qty. The spec is {"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}]}}. Without reading any data, return how many fields the 'D' record type declares, as a single column named field_count.

The file data/multi.dat is a heterogeneous fixed-width feed whose records have a 1-byte record-type tag at offset 0: 'H' header, 'D' detail, 'T' trailer. Each record's first byte is the tag; a detail record is the tag plus a 10-char sku and a 5-digit qty. The layout spec is {"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}. Read the file and return how many detail ('D') records it contains, as a single column named detail_count.

I have one heterogeneous record 'DWIDGET    00042'. Its first byte is a record-type tag; 'D' means a detail record laid out as the tag byte, a 10-character sku, then a 5-digit zero-padded qty. The multi-record spec is {"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}]}}. Decode the record and return its qty as a single column named qty.

Round-trip the heterogeneous file data/multi.dat: read it into its UNION representation and write it straight back out to data/_task_multi_out.dat using the same multi-record layout, then report how many records were written as a single column named rows_written. The layout spec (for both the read and the write) is {"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}.

The newline-delimited file data/accounts.dat holds account records: a 10-character space-padded name followed by a 5-digit zero-padded quantity. The mainframe wants each account re-encoded as an EBCDIC record: the name as PIC X(10) followed by the quantity as a signed packed-decimal PIC S9(5) COMP-3. For every account in the file, return the account name (trailing spaces trimmed) in a VARCHAR column named name and the encoded record bytes as an uppercase hex VARCHAR in a column named record_hex, one row per account, ordered by name.
Using the fixed-format worker's built-in reference table, list how many record-framing modes it supports. Return the count as a single column named framing_modes.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Functions for working with fixed-width / flat-file records in SQL: decode a record into a typed `STRUCT`, encode a `STRUCT` back into record bytes (the exact inverse), scan a fixed-width file into rows, write a relation to a fixed-width file, decode or emit heterogeneous multi-record-type files (a UNION per record type, selected by a discriminator), and introspect how a spec resolves (fields, types, byte offsets) without reading data. Layouts are template strings, JSON specs (which may nest a `fields` array for `STRUCT`/`LIST`-of-`STRUCT` sub-records), or COBOL copybooks (auto-detected; force with `format =>` on the table functions). Field kinds map to columns as text/hex → `VARCHAR`, integers → `BIGINT`, COMP-3/zoned/implied-point → `DECIMAL(p,s)`, OCCURS and OCCURS DEPENDING ON → `LIST`, group/nested-fields/REDEFINES → `STRUCT`. Encodings are ascii (default) or ebcdic (CP037); framing is newline (default), fixed, rdw, or rdw_blocked. With the defaults the common call is just `(record, spec)`.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# fixed.main

The single (and only) schema for the `fixed` worker — the catalog name matches the `ATTACH` name, so qualify calls as `fixed.main.<fn>(...)`.

It provides functions for parsing a record into a `STRUCT` and encoding a `STRUCT` back to bytes (an exact inverse pair), scanning and emitting whole fixed-width files (including heterogeneous multi-record-type files as a UNION per record type), and introspecting a layout — one row per field with its dotted path, type, byte offset, width, and OCCURS info — without reading data.

Layouts are given as Perl/Python `unpack` templates, JSON field specs (which may nest a `fields` array for `STRUCT`/`LIST`-of-`STRUCT` sub-records), or COBOL copybooks (auto-detected; override with `format =>` on the table functions). Encodings are `ascii` (default) or `ebcdic` (CP037); record framing is `newline` (default), `fixed`, `rdw`, or `rdw_blocked`.

Field kinds map to columns as:

- text / hex → `VARCHAR`
- integers → `BIGINT`
- COMP-3 / zoned / implied-point → `DECIMAL(p,s)`
- OCCURS and OCCURS … DEPENDING ON → `LIST`
- group / nested-fields / REDEFINES → `STRUCT`

tags.vgi.doc_llm: A static lookup table of the fixed-format worker's own vocabulary, so an agent can discover the valid option tokens and type mappings before building a `spec`. One row per (topic, token): the `topic` column groups the rows into `spec_format` (the three auto-detected layout formats — template, json, copybook), `encoding` (ascii / ebcdic), `framing` (newline / fixed / rdw / rdw_blocked), `compression` (auto / none / gzip / zstd), and `field_kind` (how each layout field kind maps to a DuckDB column type). The `token` column is the accepted value (or field-kind name), `maps_to` is the resulting DuckDB type for field_kind rows (empty otherwise), and `description` explains it. Query it to enumerate the legal `encoding =>` / `framing =>` / `compression =>` / `format =>` values, or to see which DuckDB type a COMP-3 or OCCURS field becomes.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# spec_reference

A browsable, credential-free registry of the `fixed` worker's own vocabulary — query it to discover valid option values and type mappings before constructing a layout `spec`.

Each row is a (topic, token) pair:

- **topic** — one of `spec_format`, `encoding`, `framing`, `compression`, or `field_kind`.
- **token** — the accepted value for that topic (or the field-kind name).
- **maps_to** — for `field_kind` rows, the DuckDB column type the kind maps to; empty otherwise.
- **description** — a one-line explanation.

For example, filter `topic = 'framing'` to list the record-framing modes, or `topic = 'field_kind'` to see how a COMP-3 or OCCURS field is typed.

vgi.example_queries.description: List the record-framing modes the worker accepts, with their meanings.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT token, description FROM fixed.main.spec_reference WHERE topic = 'framing' ORDER BY token

vgi.example_queries.description: Show how each layout field kind maps to a DuckDB column type.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT token AS field_kind, maps_to AS duckdb_type FROM fixed.main.spec_reference WHERE topic = 'field_kind' ORDER BY token

tags.vgi.title: Spec Format Reference

columns.name: token
columns.comment: The accepted option value within the topic, or the field-kind name for 'field_kind' rows.

columns.name: maps_to
columns.comment: For 'field_kind' rows, the DuckDB column type the kind maps to; an empty string for the option-token rows.

columns.name: description
columns.comment: A one-line explanation of the token.

functions.name: read_multi
functions.comment: Read a heterogeneous (multi-record-type) flat file into a UNION column

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Scan a heterogeneous fixed-width / flat file whose records have DIFFERENT layouts — e.g. a header, many detail rows, and a trailer — selected by a 'record type' discriminator field. The `spec` is a JSON object: a `discriminator` ({offset, width} of the bytes that identify each record's type) and a `records` map of tag → field list (each field list uses the same JSON field syntax as `read_fixed`'s JSON spec, so every field type / group / OCCURS works per record type). Each record is framed per `framing =>` ('newline' the default, 'fixed', 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'), its discriminator bytes pick the matching variant, and it is decoded with that variant's layout. The result is a single column `record` of type UNION — one `STRUCT` variant per record type, the variant names being the discriminator tags. Use `union_tag(record)` to get a row's record type and `union_extract(record, 'D')` to pull out a given variant's `STRUCT`. An unmatched discriminator value is an error unless the spec gives a `default` tag. `path` may glob and may be a cloud URL. `framing`, `encoding`, `compression`, and `record_length` are NAMED arguments.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Scan a heterogeneous flat file whose records have different layouts selected by a discriminator field. The JSON `spec` declares a `discriminator` ({offset,width}) and a `records` map of tag → JSON field list; the result is one UNION column `record` with a `STRUCT` variant per record type. Use `union_tag(record)` / `union_extract(record, 'TAG')`. Named args: `framing =>`, `encoding =>`, `compression =>`, `record_length =>`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Read an undelimited header/detail/trailer file (every record type padded to one 21-byte length, so framing => 'fixed') into a UNION column and project the detail rows' sku and qty.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT union_extract(record, 'D').sku AS sku, union_extract(record, 'D').qty AS qty FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi_fixed.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5},{"type":"filler","width":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6},{"type":"filler","width":14}]}}', framing => 'fixed') WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D' ORDER BY sku

vgi.example_queries.description: Count records of each type in a multi-record file that contains an unknown record type ('Z'): the spec's "default": "D" decodes it as a detail record instead of failing the read.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT union_tag(record) AS record_type, count(*) AS n FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi_bad.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]},"default":"D"}') GROUP BY record_type ORDER BY record_type

vgi.example_queries.description: Extract only the detail (D) records of a header/detail/trailer file with read_multi and write them to a flat sku/qty fixed-width file with write_fixed, dropping the header and trailer; returns 2 rows and 32 bytes.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT rows_written, bytes_written FROM fixed.main.write_fixed((SELECT d.sku, d.qty FROM (SELECT union_extract(record, 'D') AS d FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}') WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D')), '/tmp/fixed_example_details.dat', 'sku:A10 qty:9(5)')

vgi.example_queries.description: Reconcile a header/detail/trailer batch: report the header's company, the number of detail records and their total qty, the trailer's declared record count, and whether the detail count matches it (ACME CORP, 2 details, qty 49, trailer 2, balanced).
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT record FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}')) SELECT max(union_extract(record, 'H').co) AS company, count(*) FILTER (WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D') AS detail_records, sum(union_extract(record, 'D').qty) AS total_qty, max(union_extract(record, 'T').cnt) AS trailer_count, count(*) FILTER (WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D') = max(union_extract(record, 'T').cnt) AS balanced FROM r

tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
The result is always a **single** column, `record`, whose UNION variants are determined by the multi-record `spec` argument — one `STRUCT` variant per record type, named by that record type's discriminator tag. Read a row's record type with `union_tag(record)` and pull a variant's `STRUCT` with `union_extract(record, '<tag>')`.

For example, the header/detail/trailer spec used in the examples below (record types `H`, `D`, `T`) yields:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `record` | UNION(H STRUCT(co VARCHAR), D STRUCT(sku VARCHAR, qty BIGINT), T STRUCT(cnt BIGINT)) | A sparse UNION with one `STRUCT` variant per record type in the spec — here `H` (header), `D` (detail), and `T` (trailer). |
tags.vgi.title: Read Multi-Record-Type File

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: Path(s) to the file(s) to read: a single path or a list of paths. May glob (e.g. 'data/*.dat') or be a cloud URL ('s3://bucket/key' or 'https://host/file'). Credentials come from the matching DuckDB secret, scoped per path.

arguments.name: spec
arguments.description: The multi-record JSON layout: a `discriminator` ({offset, width}) plus a `records` map of record-type tag → JSON field list (the same field syntax as read_fixed's JSON spec). An optional `default` tag handles unmatched values. Determines the UNION variants of the output `record` column.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.description: Byte encoding of the file: 'ascii' (the default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037). The discriminator bytes are transcoded out of EBCDIC before matching.

arguments.name: framing
arguments.description: How records are delimited: 'newline' (the default), 'fixed' (back-to-back equal-length records — every record type padded to a common length), 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'.

arguments.name: record_length
arguments.description: Per-record length in BYTES for 'fixed' framing; ignored otherwise. Defaults to the longest record type's layout length.

arguments.name: compression
arguments.description: Input compression: 'auto' (default — detect gzip/zstd from magic bytes), 'none', 'gzip', or 'zstd'. Decompression happens before framing/decoding.

arguments.name: max_decompressed_bytes
arguments.description: Safety cap on total DECOMPRESSED bytes per file (default 16 GiB). Only applies to gzip/zstd input.

arguments.name: endpoint
arguments.description: Custom S3 endpoint for an `s3://` path (e.g. MinIO/R2 'host:9000'); a scheme is inferred from `use_ssl` when omitted. Overrides any endpoint from a CREATE SECRET.

arguments.name: region
arguments.description: AWS region for an `s3://` path. Overrides the region from a CREATE SECRET.

arguments.name: url_style
arguments.description: S3 addressing for an `s3://` path: 'path' (path-style, e.g. MinIO) or 'vhost' (the default). Overrides a CREATE SECRET's URL_STYLE.

arguments.name: use_ssl
arguments.description: Whether to use TLS for an `s3://` path's custom endpoint (default true). Set false for a plain-HTTP endpoint such as a local MinIO.

SELECT union_tag(record) AS record_type, count(*) AS n FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi_bad.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]},"default":"D"}') GROUP BY record_type ORDER BY record_type

SELECT rows_written, bytes_written FROM fixed.main.write_fixed((SELECT d.sku, d.qty FROM (SELECT union_extract(record, 'D') AS d FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}') WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D')), '/tmp/fixed_example_details.dat', 'sku:A10 qty:9(5)')

WITH r AS (SELECT record FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}')) SELECT max(union_extract(record, 'H').co) AS company, count(*) FILTER (WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D') AS detail_records, sum(union_extract(record, 'D').qty) AS total_qty, max(union_extract(record, 'T').cnt) AS trailer_count, count(*) FILTER (WHERE union_tag(record) = 'D') = max(union_extract(record, 'T').cnt) AS balanced FROM r

result_columns.name: record
result_columns.type: UNION(H STRUCT(co VARCHAR), D STRUCT(sku VARCHAR, qty BIGINT), T STRUCT(cnt BIGINT))
result_columns.description: A sparse UNION with one `STRUCT` variant per record type in the spec — here `H` (header), `D` (detail), and `T` (trailer).

functions.name: write_multi
functions.comment: Write a relation's UNION column to a multi-record-type file (inverse of read_multi)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Write a relation whose single UNION column holds heterogeneous records back out to a multi-record-type fixed-width / flat file — the inverse of read_multi. The `data` relation (passed as a subquery, e.g. `(FROM read_multi(...))` or a `(SELECT ...)`) must have exactly ONE column: a sparse UNION whose variant names are the discriminator tags of the `spec` (the exact shape read_multi emits). For each row the active variant gives its record type and its `STRUCT` field values; the matching variant layout encodes those fields, the discriminator field is stamped with the tag, the records are framed per the named `framing =>` argument ('newline' the default, 'fixed', 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'), encoded under named `encoding =>` ('ascii' the default, or 'ebcdic'/CP037), optionally compressed via `compression =>`, and streamed to `path` (overwritten if it exists). The `spec` is the SAME multi-record JSON as read_multi: a `discriminator` ({offset,width}) plus a `records` map of tag → JSON field list. `encoding`, `framing`, and `compression` are NAMED arguments. Use it to emit header/detail/trailer or other heterogeneous mainframe flat files from SQL. Returns exactly one summary row: `rows_written BIGINT` and `bytes_written BIGINT`.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Write a relation's single UNION column out to a heterogeneous multi-record-type fixed-width file — the inverse of read_multi. The relation is a subquery with one UNION column whose variant names are the spec's discriminator tags. The `spec` is the same multi-record JSON (`discriminator` + `records`). Each row's active variant is encoded with its layout and the discriminator stamped with the tag. Optional NAMED args: `encoding =>` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing =>` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), `compression =>`. Returns one row `(rows_written BIGINT, bytes_written BIGINT)`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Round-trip a heterogeneous flat file: read it into a UNION column and write it back out to a new multi-record file, reporting the counts.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT rows_written, bytes_written FROM fixed.main.write_multi((FROM fixed.main.read_multi('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/multi.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}')), '/tmp/fixed_example_multi_out.dat', '{"discriminator":{"offset":0,"width":1},"records":{"H":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"co","type":"str","width":20}],"D":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"sku","type":"str","width":10},{"name":"qty","type":"int","digits":5}],"T":[{"type":"filler","width":1},{"name":"cnt","type":"int","digits":6}]}}')

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: rows_written
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Number of records written to the file across all record types.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: bytes_written
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Total number of bytes written to the file, including record framing and any compression.

tags.vgi.title: Write Multi-Record-Type File

arguments.name: data
arguments.description: The input relation to write out, supplied as a subquery (e.g. `(FROM read_multi(...))`). It must have exactly ONE column: a UNION whose variant names are the discriminator tags of `spec`.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: Path of the multi-record file to create; it is overwritten if it already exists. May also be an 's3://bucket/key' URL (AWS S3, or R2/MinIO/GCS-HMAC via a `CREATE SECRET (TYPE s3, …, ENDPOINT …)`) — credentials come from the matching DuckDB secret, scoped to the URL. Writing to 'http(s)://' is not supported.

arguments.name: spec
arguments.description: The multi-record JSON layout (the same spec read_multi uses): a `discriminator` ({offset, width}) plus a `records` map of record-type tag → JSON field list. The UNION column's variant names must match these tags.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.description: Byte encoding to write: 'ascii' (the default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037). The discriminator tag is transcoded to this encoding.

arguments.name: framing
arguments.description: How to delimit records in the output: 'newline' (the default), 'fixed', 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'.

arguments.name: compression
arguments.description: Compress the output: 'auto' (the default — gzip if the path ends '.gz', zstd if '.zst', else raw), 'none', 'gzip', or 'zstd'. The whole file is compressed.

arguments.name: endpoint
arguments.description: Custom S3 endpoint for an `s3://` path (e.g. MinIO/R2 'host:9000'); a scheme is inferred from `use_ssl` when omitted. Overrides any endpoint from a CREATE SECRET.

arguments.name: region
arguments.description: AWS region for an `s3://` path. Overrides the region from a CREATE SECRET.

arguments.name: url_style
arguments.description: S3 addressing for an `s3://` path: 'path' (path-style, e.g. MinIO) or 'vhost' (the default). Overrides a CREATE SECRET's URL_STYLE.

arguments.name: use_ssl
arguments.description: Whether to use TLS for an `s3://` path's custom endpoint (default true). Set false for a plain-HTTP endpoint such as a local MinIO.

functions.name: read_fixed
functions.comment: Read a fixed-width file (template / JSON / copybook spec) into rows

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Scan a fixed-width / flat-file data file into typed rows. `path` may be a glob (e.g. '/data/*.dat'); matching files are read in sorted order and their rows concatenated. Each record is framed per the named `framing =>` argument ('newline' the default, 'fixed', 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked') and decoded into a row of typed columns according to the layout `spec` — a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook (format auto-detected unless you pass `format =>` 'template' / 'json' / 'copybook'). In a template spec, prefix each field with a name to set its column name, e.g. `'name:A10 qty:9(5)'`; unnamed fields become positional `field_1`, `field_2`, …. The named `encoding =>` argument is 'ascii' (default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037). The named `record_length =>` argument is the per-record length in BYTES; it is only used for 'fixed' framing (back-to-back records of equal length) and defaults to the length implied by the `spec`; it is ignored for the other framings. `format`, `encoding`, `framing`, and `record_length` are all NAMED arguments. The returned column set is dynamic: it is determined by the spec, with OCCURS becoming `LIST` columns and groups / REDEFINES becoming `STRUCT` columns. Use it to ingest mainframe or legacy flat-file data into SQL. This is the file-scanning counterpart of unpack_fixed and the inverse of write_fixed.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Scan a fixed-width file into rows, decoding each record per the layout `spec` (template, JSON, or COBOL copybook). `path` may glob (e.g. `read_fixed('/data/*.dat', 'A10 N')`), reading matching files in sorted order. Optional NAMED args: `format =>`, `encoding =>` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing =>` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), and `record_length =>` (per-record length in bytes, used only for `fixed` framing). The returned columns are dynamic — they depend on the spec, with OCCURS → `LIST` and group/REDEFINES → `STRUCT`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Profile a newline-delimited fixed-width feed of 7-digit ids (a sample file pinned to a release tag): count the rows and report the id range.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS records, min(id) AS min_id, max(id) AS max_id FROM fixed.main.read_fixed('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/large.dat', 'id:9(7)')

vgi.example_queries.description: Read two account files at once (a list of paths or URLs; a local path may also be a glob such as 'data/acct*.dat') with a 10-char name and 5-digit qty, and total the quantity across every record.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT sum(qty) AS total_qty FROM fixed.main.read_fixed(['https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/acct1.dat', 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-fixedformat/v0.12.0/data/acct2.dat'], 'name:A10 qty:9(5)')

tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
The returned columns are **dynamic** — determined by the layout `spec`, one column per top-level field. Column names come from the field names in the spec — name your fields (e.g. `name:A10 qty:9(5)`); **unnamed** template fields become positional `field_1`, `field_2`, …. Column types follow the field kind: text/hex → `VARCHAR`, integer → `BIGINT`, float/double → `REAL`/`DOUBLE`, COMP-3 / zoned / implied-point decimal → `DECIMAL(p,s)`, `?` boolean → `BOOLEAN`, OCCURS / repeat → `LIST` of the element type, and group / REDEFINES → `STRUCT` of the child fields.

For the spec `name:A10 qty:9(5)` the result columns are:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `VARCHAR` | The 10-byte text field decoded from bytes 0–9. |
| `qty` | `BIGINT` | The 5-digit zoned integer decoded from bytes 10–14. |

For the single-field spec `id:9(7)` the result is one column:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `BIGINT` | The 7-digit zoned integer decoded from bytes 0–6. |
tags.vgi.title: Read Fixed-Width File

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: Path(s) to the fixed-width file(s) to read: a single path, or a list of paths to read several files in one call (their rows are concatenated in order). A path may be a glob (e.g. 'data/*.dat') to scan matching files in sorted order, or a cloud URL: 's3://bucket/key' (AWS S3, or R2/MinIO/GCS-HMAC via a `CREATE SECRET (TYPE s3, …, ENDPOINT …)`) or 'https://host/file'. Credentials come from the matching DuckDB secret, resolved per path scope — so a list spanning several buckets picks the right secret for each.

arguments.name: spec
arguments.description: The record layout to decode each row with: a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook. Determines the output column names and types; format is auto-detected unless `format` is given.

arguments.name: format
arguments.description: Force how `spec` is interpreted: 'template', 'json', or 'copybook'. Omit to auto-detect.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.description: Byte encoding of the file: 'ascii' (the default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037).

arguments.name: framing
arguments.description: How records are delimited in the file: 'newline' (the default), 'fixed' (back-to-back records of equal length), 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'.

arguments.name: record_length
arguments.description: The length of each record in BYTES. Used only for 'fixed' framing (back-to-back equal-length records); ignored for the other framings. Defaults to the length implied by the layout `spec`.

arguments.name: compression
arguments.description: Input compression: 'auto' (the default — detect gzip/zstd from the file's magic bytes, else read raw), 'none', 'gzip', or 'zstd'. Applies to local and cloud paths alike; decompression happens before framing/decoding.

arguments.name: max_decompressed_bytes

functions.name: copy_to_fixed
functions.comment: Write the COPY source out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file (the COPY-TO counterpart of write_fixed)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Write a query or table out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file — the COPY-TO counterpart of write_fixed. It is invoked as a COPY statement (not called directly):

```sql
COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', spec '<layout>');
```

The writer uses a DISTINCT format name 'fixed.fixed_out' (catalog-qualified by the ATTACH name) because the VGI SDK advertises FROM and TO as separate formats. Each input column is matched to a layout field BY NAME, encoded to record bytes per the `spec` option (a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook; auto-detected unless `format` is given), framed per `framing`, and written to `<path>` (overwritten if it exists). Options are named: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), plus `endpoint`/`region`/`url_style`/`use_ssl` for `s3://` destinations. NOTE: CREATE SECRET credentials are NOT forwarded on the COPY-TO path — use named S3 overrides, ambient credentials, or write_fixed for secret-backed cloud writes.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Write a relation to a fixed-width file:

```sql
COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', spec '<layout>');
```

Input columns map to layout fields by name. Named options: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding`, `framing`, and S3 overrides. The COPY-TO counterpart of `write_fixed`.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
`copy_to_fixed` is invoked through `COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', …)`, not as a table function, so it returns **no result set of its own**. The COPY source rows are encoded to fixed-width records and written to `<path>` (overwritten if it exists); each input column is matched to a layout field **by name** before encoding. DuckDB reports only a single value — the number of rows written:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Count` | BIGINT | The number of source rows written to the file, reported by DuckDB as the `COPY … TO` statement's result. |

functions.name: write_fixed
functions.comment: Write a relation to a fixed-width file (inverse of read_fixed)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Write an input relation out to a fixed-width / flat-file data file — the inverse of read_fixed. The `data` relation is passed as a subquery (e.g. `(FROM tbl)` or `(SELECT ...)`). Each input row's columns are matched by name to the layout fields, encoded to record bytes per the `spec` (Perl/Python `unpack` template, JSON field list, or COBOL copybook; format auto-detected unless you pass `format =>` 'template' / 'json' / 'copybook'), framed per the named `framing =>` argument ('newline' the default, 'fixed', 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'), encoded under named `encoding =>` ('ascii' the default, or 'ebcdic'/CP037), and streamed to `path` (overwritten if it exists). `format`, `encoding`, and `framing` are NAMED arguments. Use it to emit mainframe or legacy flat-file output from SQL. Returns exactly one summary row with two columns: `rows_written BIGINT` (number of records written) and `bytes_written BIGINT` (total bytes written including framing).
tags.vgi.doc_md: Write a relation to a fixed-width file, encoding each row per the layout `spec`. The relation is a subquery, e.g. `write_fixed((FROM tbl), '/tmp/out.dat', 'A10 N')`. Optional NAMED args: `format =>`, `encoding =>` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing =>` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'). The inverse of `read_fixed`; returns one row `(rows_written BIGINT, bytes_written BIGINT)`.

functions.name: copy_fixed
functions.comment: Read a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file into the COPY target table (the COPY-FROM counterpart of read_fixed)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Load a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file straight into a DuckDB table — the COPY-FROM counterpart of read_fixed. It is invoked as a COPY statement (not called directly):

```sql
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', spec '<layout>');
```

The format name is catalog-qualified by the ATTACH name (e.g. 'fixed.fixed'). Each record is decoded per the `spec` option (a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook; auto-detected unless `format` is given) and the decoded columns are assigned to the COPY target table's columns BY POSITION and cast to each target column's type, so the spec must produce the same number of columns in the same order. Options are named: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), `record_length` (bytes, 'fixed' framing only), plus `endpoint`/`region`/`url_style`/`use_ssl` for `s3://` sources. `path` may be local, `s3://`, or `http(s)://`. Use it to ingest mainframe or legacy flat-file data into an existing table without a read_fixed call.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Load a fixed-width file into a table:

```sql
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', spec '<layout>');
```

Decoded columns map to the target table's columns by position (cast to each type). Named options: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding`, `framing`, `record_length`, and S3 overrides. The COPY-FROM counterpart of `read_fixed`.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
`copy_fixed` is invoked through `COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', …)`, not as a table function, so it returns **no result set of its own**. The rows decoded from the file are inserted into the COPY **target table**, and DuckDB reports the number of rows loaded as the statement's `Count`. The materialized columns are therefore the target table's own columns — each decoded field is mapped to a target column **by position** and cast to that column's type, so the `spec` must produce the same number of columns, in the same order, as the table.

For a target table `accounts(name VARCHAR, qty INTEGER)` loaded with the spec `name:A10 qty:9(5)`, the loaded columns are:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | VARCHAR | The target column populated from the first decoded field (bytes 0–9). |
| `qty` | INTEGER | The target column populated from the second decoded field, cast from the 5-digit value. |

The decoded columns are assigned to the COPY target table's columns by position, so the spec must produce the same number of columns in the same order (each cast to the target column's type).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a single fixed-width / flat-file record (a `VARCHAR` or `BLOB`) into a typed `STRUCT` whose fields are named and typed by the layout spec, controlling the byte `encoding`. This 3-argument overload adds a positional `encoding` argument: 'ascii' (the default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037). EBCDIC affects not only character fields but also the sign nibbles of zoned and COMP-3 (packed-decimal) numbers. The spec is a Perl/Python `unpack` template string, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook (auto-detected), and supports packed/zoned decimals, OCCURS lists (→ `LIST`), groups and REDEFINES (→ `STRUCT`). In a template spec, prefix each field with a name to set its `STRUCT` field name, e.g. `'name:A10 qty:9(5)'`; unnamed fields become `field_1`, `field_2`, …. The spec is a bind-time constant so the `STRUCT` output type is known at plan time. This is the inverse of pack_fixed when the same encoding is supplied to both.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Parse a fixed-width record into a `STRUCT` under an explicit byte encoding, e.g. `unpack_fixed(rec, 'A8 N', 'ebcdic')`. The third argument is `encoding` — 'ascii' (default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037), which also governs zoned/COMP-3 sign nibbles. It is positional, not named.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Encode a `STRUCT` of field values back into a single fixed-width / flat-file record blob, controlling the byte `encoding`. This 3-argument overload adds a positional `encoding` argument: 'ascii' (the default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037). EBCDIC affects not only character fields but also the sign nibbles of zoned and COMP-3 (packed-decimal) numbers. The layout is the same kind of spec `unpack_fixed` uses (Perl/Python `unpack` template, JSON field list, or COBOL copybook); field values are matched to layout fields with padding, justification, packed/zoned decimals and sign handling applied per the spec. tags.vgi.doc_md: Format a `STRUCT` into a fixed-width record blob under an explicit byte encoding, e.g. `pack_fixed({'name': 'Jo', 'id': 7}, 'A2 N', 'ebcdic')`. functions.comment: Parse one heterogeneous (multi-record-type) record into a DuckDB UNION using the multi-record spec, assuming ASCII bytes

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a single record from a heterogeneous (multi-record-type) feed into a DuckDB UNION value — the scalar counterpart of read_multi. The `spec` is the same multi-record JSON object (a `discriminator` of {offset, width} plus a `records` map of record-type tag → JSON field list); the record's discriminator bytes pick the variant to decode it with. The result is a UNION with one `STRUCT` variant per record type, named by the discriminator tag — use `union_tag(...)` for the record type and `union_extract(..., 'TAG')` to pull a variant's `STRUCT`. An unmatched discriminator value errors unless the spec gives a `default` tag. The 3-argument overload adds a positional `encoding` ('ascii' default, or 'ebcdic'/CP037, which also governs the discriminator bytes). The spec is a bind-time constant so the UNION type is known at plan time.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Parse one multi-record-type record into a UNION value, e.g. `union_tag(unpack_multi(rec, '<spec>'))`. The JSON `spec` declares a `discriminator` and a `records` map of tag → field list. Optional 3rd positional `encoding` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'). The scalar counterpart of read_multi.

workers.title: FOCUS Cloud Cost Normalization
workers.tagline: AWS, Azure and GCP billing exports normalized to FinOps FOCUS in DuckDB (Python)
workers.subtitle: Normalizes AWS, Azure and Google Cloud billing exports into the FinOps FOCUS schema.
workers.summary: Normalize AWS, Azure and Google Cloud billing exports into the FinOps FOCUS 1.x schema, so one DuckDB query covers every cloud, with exact decimal money and conformance checks.
workers.doc_md:
# FOCUS cost normalization

Turn AWS, Azure and Google Cloud billing exports into the FinOps Foundation's [FOCUS](https://focus.finops.org) schema inside DuckDB: one query, every cloud.

- **Readers** for AWS CUR 2.0, Azure cost exports, GCP billing export dumps and native FOCUS files.
- **Exact money**: `DECIMAL(19,6)`, never `DOUBLE`, rounded half-to-even.
- **Auditable**: every mapping rule is a row you can query.
- **Conformance**: check any FOCUS file against the spec.

FOCUS column definitions are © FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) Series contributors, used under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

example_queries.description: Amortized spend by cloud and service category across AWS, Azure and GCP exports
example_queries.sql: SELECT ProviderName, ServiceCategory, sum(EffectiveCost) AS effective_cost FROM (SELECT * FROM focus.main.focus('sample://aws_cur2') UNION ALL SELECT * FROM focus.main.focus('sample://azure/contoso-actual-cost-202607.csv') UNION ALL SELECT * FROM focus.main.focus('sample://gcp/gcp_billing_export_v1_01A2B3_202607.parquet')) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY effective_cost DESC

example_queries.description: July invoice cost by team tag in the AWS CUR 2.0 sample
example_queries.sql: SELECT Tags['team'] AS team, sum(BilledCost) AS billed FROM focus.main.focus('sample://aws_cur2', billing_period := '2026-07') WHERE Tags['team'] IS NOT NULL GROUP BY team ORDER BY billed DESC

example_queries.description: Map raw CUR 2.0 rows written inline to FOCUS
example_queries.sql: SELECT ChargeCategory, CommitmentDiscountStatus, BilledCost, EffectiveCost FROM focus.main.to_focus((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Usage', 1.9584, NULL, NULL), ('SavingsPlanCoveredUsage', 3.9168, 2.7408, 'arn:aws:savingsplans::1:savingsplan/x')) AS t(line_item_line_item_type, line_item_unblended_cost, savings_plan_savings_plan_effective_cost, savings_plan_savings_plan_a_r_n))) ORDER BY BilledCost

example_queries.description: Checks a native FOCUS 1.2 export does not pass as FOCUS 1.3
example_queries.sql: SELECT check_name, column_name, status FROM focus.main.focus_validate('sample://focus12', spec_version := '1.3') WHERE status <> 'pass' ORDER BY check_name, column_name

example_queries.description: Error-level checks of the mapped GCP billing export sample
example_queries.sql: SELECT check_name, column_name, failing_rows, sample_value FROM focus.main.focus_validate('sample://gcp/gcp_billing_export_v1_01A2B3_202607.parquet') WHERE severity = 'error' ORDER BY failing_rows DESC, check_name

example_queries.description: Classify EC2
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_service_category('aws', 'AmazonEC2') AS category

example_queries.description: Classify Cosmos DB
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_service_subcategory('azure', 'Azure Cosmos DB') AS subcategory

example_queries.description: AWS reserved-instance fee
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_charge_category('aws', 'RIFee') AS category

example_queries.description: Where GCP list cost goes
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_map_column('gcp', 'cost_at_list') AS focus_columns

example_queries.description: An invalid ChargeFrequency
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_validate_value('ChargeFrequency', 'Monthly') AS problem

example_queries.description: A lower-case ChargeCategory is rejected by FOCUS 1.0
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_validate_value('ChargeCategory', 'usage', '1.0') AS problem

example_queries.description: Effective-to-list cost ratio of the AWS sample without DOUBLE rounding
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_divide(sum(EffectiveCost), sum(ListCost)) AS effective_over_list FROM focus.main.focus('sample://aws_cur2')

example_queries.description: Effective rate per resource in the AWS sample
example_queries.sql: SELECT ResourceId, focus.main.focus_effective_rate(sum(EffectiveCost), sum(PricingQuantity)) AS rate FROM focus.main.focus('sample://aws_cur2') WHERE ChargeCategory = 'Usage' AND ResourceId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ResourceId ORDER BY rate DESC

example_queries.description: Database services per provider
example_queries.sql: SELECT provider, count(*) AS services FROM focus.main.service_map WHERE service_category = 'Databases' GROUP BY provider ORDER BY provider

example_queries.description: Where AWS EffectiveCost comes from
example_queries.sql: SELECT len(source_columns) AS inputs, filter_pushdown FROM focus.main.provider_map WHERE source = 'aws_cur2' AND focus_column = 'EffectiveCost'

example_queries.description: Columns pushed into the Parquet scan per source
example_queries.sql: SELECT source, count(*) FILTER (WHERE filter_pushdown) AS pushed FROM focus.main.provider_map WHERE source <> 'focus' GROUP BY source ORDER BY source

example_queries.description: AWS line item types that are FOCUS purchases
example_queries.sql: SELECT charge_type, charge_frequency FROM focus.main.charge_type_map WHERE source = 'aws_cur2' AND charge_category = 'Purchase' ORDER BY charge_type

example_queries.description: Allowed ChargeCategory values in FOCUS 1.2
example_queries.sql: SELECT unnest(allowed_values) AS v FROM focus.main.focus_columns WHERE spec_version = '1.2' AND column_name = 'ChargeCategory' ORDER BY v

example_queries.description: Columns added in FOCUS 1.3
example_queries.sql: SELECT column_name FROM focus.main.focus_columns WHERE spec_version = '1.3' AND column_name NOT IN (SELECT column_name FROM focus.main.focus_columns WHERE spec_version = '1.2') ORDER BY column_name

example_queries.description: July 2026 AWS sample: billed vs amortized cost per charge category
example_queries.sql: SELECT ChargeCategory, sum(BilledCost) AS billed, sum(EffectiveCost) AS effective FROM focus.main.focus('sample://aws_cur2', billing_period := '2026-07') GROUP BY ChargeCategory ORDER BY ChargeCategory;

example_queries.description: AWS, Azure and GCP services
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_service_category(p, s) AS c FROM (VALUES ('aws', 'AmazonRDS', 1), ('azure', 'Virtual Machines', 2), ('gcp', 'Cloud Storage', 3), ('aws', 'NotAService', 4)) t(p, s, i) ORDER BY i;

example_queries.description: ServiceProviderName only exists from 1.3
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_validate_value('ServiceProviderName', 'AWS', '1.2') AS v12, focus.main.focus_validate_value('ServiceProviderName', 'AWS', '1.3') AS v13;

example_queries.description: Hourly rate of 24 hours costing 2.7408
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_effective_rate(2.7408, 24) AS rate;

example_queries.description: AWS unblended cost
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_map_column('aws_cur2', 'lineItem/UnblendedCost') AS cols;

example_queries.description: An unused column
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_map_column('azure', 'CostCenter') IS NULL AS unused;

example_queries.description: Ten over three, and a zero denominator
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_divide(10, 3) AS r, focus.main.focus_divide(1, 0) AS z;

example_queries.description: One per provider
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_charge_category(p, t) AS c FROM (VALUES ('aws', 'SavingsPlanCoveredUsage', 1), ('azure', 'Purchase', 2), ('gcp', 'tax', 3)) v(p, t, i) ORDER BY i;

example_queries.description: Subcategories
example_queries.sql: SELECT focus.main.focus_service_subcategory('aws', 'AmazonRDS') AS a, focus.main.focus_service_subcategory('gcp', 'Cloud Run') AS b;

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The `main` schema holds everything: table functions that read billing export files or map rows from any DuckDB query into FOCUS, a conformance report, reference tables for the FOCUS spec and the mapping rules, and scalars that classify provider services and charge types or divide decimals exactly. Readers take a positional path plus named arguments: source ('auto' detects the export format per file; 'aws_cur2', 'azure', 'azure_amortized', 'gcp' or 'focus' force it), spec_version ('1.0' to '1.4', default '1.2'), billing_period ('YYYY-MM') and money_scale (decimal places on cost columns). Pass a subquery, not a table name, to the mapping function. Provider arguments of the scalars are 'aws', 'azure' or 'gcp'. Use the bundled `sample://` exports to explore before pointing at real data.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Readers turn billing exports into FOCUS rows; a mapping function does the same for rows DuckDB has already read; a validator reports spec conformance.

Reference tables publish the FOCUS spec (1.0-1.4) and every mapping rule. Scalars classify services and charges and divide money exactly.

Try it on the bundled synthetic exports: `sample://aws_cur2`, `sample://azure`, `sample://gcp`, `sample://focus12`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Amortized spend by cloud and service category across AWS, Azure and GCP exports
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ProviderName, ServiceCategory, sum(EffectiveCost) AS effective_cost FROM (SELECT * FROM focus.main.focus('sample://aws_cur2') UNION ALL SELECT * FROM focus.main.focus('sample://azure/contoso-actual-cost-202607.csv') UNION ALL SELECT * FROM focus.main.focus('sample://gcp/gcp_billing_export_v1_01A2B3_202607.parquet')) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY effective_cost DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: July invoice cost by team tag in the AWS CUR 2.0 sample
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT Tags['team'] AS team, sum(BilledCost) AS billed FROM focus.main.focus('sample://aws_cur2', billing_period := '2026-07') WHERE Tags['team'] IS NOT NULL GROUP BY team ORDER BY billed DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Map raw CUR 2.0 rows written inline to FOCUS
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ChargeCategory, CommitmentDiscountStatus, BilledCost, EffectiveCost FROM focus.main.to_focus((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('Usage', 1.9584, NULL, NULL), ('SavingsPlanCoveredUsage', 3.9168, 2.7408, 'arn:aws:savingsplans::1:savingsplan/x')) AS t(line_item_line_item_type, line_item_unblended_cost, savings_plan_savings_plan_effective_cost, savings_plan_savings_plan_a_r_n))) ORDER BY BilledCost

vgi.example_queries.description: Checks a native FOCUS 1.2 export does not pass as FOCUS 1.3
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT check_name, column_name, status FROM focus.main.focus_validate('sample://focus12', spec_version := '1.3') WHERE status <> 'pass' ORDER BY check_name, column_name

vgi.example_queries.description: Error-level checks of the mapped GCP billing export sample
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT check_name, column_name, failing_rows, sample_value FROM focus.main.focus_validate('sample://gcp/gcp_billing_export_v1_01A2B3_202607.parquet') WHERE severity = 'error' ORDER BY failing_rows DESC, check_name

vgi.example_queries.description: An invalid ChargeFrequency

vgi.example_queries.description: Effective-to-list cost ratio of the AWS sample without DOUBLE rounding

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per column per FOCUS version (1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4) of the Cost and Usage dataset, compiled from the FinOps Foundation specification: column_name, display_name, description, column_type, feature_level (Mandatory/Conditional/Recommended), allows_nulls, data_type, duckdb_type (what this worker emits), value_format, allowed_values (a `VARCHAR[]`, or NULL) and introduced. Filter on spec_version. Use it to list mandatory columns, look up allowed values (e.g. ChargeCategory) or diff versions.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## focus_columns

Column definitions © FOCUS contributors, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

functions.name: focus_validate
functions.comment: Check billing export files against the FOCUS spec: required columns, nulls, allowed values

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Validate billing data against a FOCUS version. Reads the same paths and sources as focus() (native FOCUS files are checked as-is; provider exports are checked after mapping) and returns one row per check: check_name (column_present, not_null, allowed_values, subcategory_matches_category, charge_period_order, billing_period_order, currency_code, consumed_quantity_usage_only, commitment_status_requires_id, custom_column_prefix, column_name_case), column_name, severity (error/warning/info), status (pass/fail/not_applicable), rows_checked, failing_rows, sample_value and detail. Filter WHERE status = 'fail' for the problems. spec_version defaults to '1.2'.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## focus_validate(path, source := 'auto', spec_version := '1.2', file_format := 'auto')

One row per conformance check, with the failing row count and a sample offending value. Filter on `status = 'fail'` for the problems.

vgi.example_queries.description: Checks a native FOCUS 1.2 export does not pass as FOCUS 1.3
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT check_name, column_name, status FROM focus.main.focus_validate('sample://focus12', spec_version := '1.3') WHERE status <> 'pass' ORDER BY check_name, column_name

vgi.example_queries.description: Error-level checks of the mapped GCP billing export sample
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT check_name, column_name, failing_rows, sample_value FROM focus.main.focus_validate('sample://gcp/gcp_billing_export_v1_01A2B3_202607.parquet') WHERE severity = 'error' ORDER BY failing_rows DESC, check_name
