workers.title: iCalendar (.ics) Parsing
workers.tagline: Parse iCalendar (.ics) events & todos for DuckDB (Java, iCal4j)
workers.subtitle: Turn .ics calendar feeds into queryable events, to-dos and feed health checks.
workers.summary: iCalendar (.ics) events, todos, and metadata parsing (iCal4j)
workers.doc_md:
# iCalendar (.ics) Parsing in SQL

![iCal4j logo](https://www.ical4j.org/images/logo-48.png)

**Query iCalendar feeds directly in DuckDB SQL** — turn `.ics` calendar files into queryable rows of events, to-dos, and calendar metadata, powered by the battle-tested [iCal4j](https://github.com/ical4j/ical4j) RFC 5545 parser.

This VGI extension brings full iCalendar parsing to your SQL workflow. If you work with calendar exports from Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, Apple Calendar, or any RFC 5545-compliant feed, you can load and analyze that data without a separate ETL step. It is built for data engineers, analysts, and developers who want to ingest calendar feeds, run scheduling analytics, deduplicate events, audit recurrence rules, or validate `.ics` files entirely in SQL.

Under the hood the worker wraps [iCal4j](https://www.ical4j.org/), the mature open-source Java library implementing the iCalendar specification ([RFC 5545](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545)). Parsing runs with relaxed, Outlook-compatible compatibility hints so messy real-world feeds load cleanly, and every timestamp is normalised to UTC and surfaced as `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`. Results stream back to DuckDB over Apache Arrow, so large feeds are processed efficiently and bad or unparsable input never crashes a query — it simply yields no rows, `NULL`, or `false`.

## What you can do

The worker exposes both **table functions**, which expand a feed into one row per calendar entry (surfacing fields such as uid, summary, description, start/end or due timestamps, all-day flag, location, status, organizer, attendees, recurrence rule, priority, and percent-complete), and **scalar functions** for quick, row-level answers such as reading a calendar's display name, tallying entries, or validating a feed.

Every function takes the same polymorphic argument: a `VARCHAR` file path (the worker opens and reads the file) or a `BLOB` of raw `.ics` bytes (parsed in place), making it easy to query files on disk or calendar data already stored in a column. Recurrence rules are surfaced as their raw RRULE strings rather than expanded into individual occurrences.

## Learn more

- [iCal4j source repository](https://github.com/ical4j/ical4j)
- [iCal4j documentation](https://www.ical4j.org/)
- [RFC 5545 (iCalendar specification)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545)

example_queries.description: List the events in an iCalendar feed.
example_queries.sql: SELECT summary, location FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) ORDER BY dtstart;

example_queries.description: List the to-dos in an iCalendar feed.
example_queries.sql: SELECT summary, status FROM ical.main.ical_todos(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) ORDER BY due;

example_queries.description: Read the calendar display name.
example_queries.sql: SELECT ical.main.ical_calendar_name(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS calendar_name;

example_queries.description: Count the events in a feed.
example_queries.sql: SELECT ical.main.ical_event_count(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS event_count;

example_queries.description: Validate an iCalendar feed.
example_queries.sql: SELECT ical.main.is_valid_ical(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS is_valid;

example_queries.description: Health-check a column of stored feeds: the scalars accept columns (table functions do not). Both example_calendars samples come back valid (Ops Calendar 2 events, Team Calendar 1); a truncated export comes back false, NULL, 0. Cast text to `BLOB`: a `VARCHAR` is read as a file path.
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ical.main.is_valid_ical(feed::BLOB) AS is_valid, ical.main.ical_calendar_name(feed::BLOB) AS parsed_name, ical.main.ical_event_count(feed::BLOB) AS parsed_events FROM (SELECT name, feed FROM ical.main.example_calendars UNION ALL SELECT 'truncated_export', 'BEGIN:VCALENDAR') AS f ORDER BY name;

example_queries.description: Find double-booked events: self-join ical_events on overlapping [dtstart, dtend) ranges. Returns Design review with Customer call, overlapping 09:30-10:00 UTC; Team sync starts as Customer call ends, so it is not a conflict.
example_queries.sql: SELECT a.summary AS first_event, b.summary AS second_event, greatest(a.dtstart, b.dtstart) AS overlap_start, least(a.dtend, b.dtend) AS overlap_end FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Design Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Design review','DTSTART:20240402T090000Z','DTEND:20240402T100000Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Customer call','DTSTART:20240402T093000Z','DTEND:20240402T101500Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d3@query.farm','SUMMARY:Team sync','DTSTART:20240402T101500Z','DTEND:20240402T110000Z','END:VEVENT','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS a JOIN ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Design Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Design review','DTSTART:20240402T090000Z','DTEND:20240402T100000Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Customer call','DTSTART:20240402T093000Z','DTEND:20240402T101500Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d3@query.farm','SUMMARY:Team sync','DTSTART:20240402T101500Z','DTEND:20240402T110000Z','END:VEVENT','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS b ON a.uid < b.uid AND a.dtstart < b.dtend AND b.dtstart < a.dtend ORDER BY overlap_start, first_event;

example_queries.description: List, for each event, the to-dos that fall due within 7 days of its start, by joining ical_events to ical_todos on a time window. iCalendar does not link to-dos to events, so the pairing is by time only: the Ops Calendar's one to-do, Update changelog (due 2024-03-12 17:00 UTC), pairs with both Deploy release and Retro.
example_queries.sql: SELECT e.summary AS event, e.dtstart, t.summary AS todo, t.due FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Ops Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Deploy release','DTSTART:20240310T150000Z','DTEND:20240310T160000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Retro','DTSTART:20240311T170000Z','DTEND:20240311T173000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:ops-todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Update changelog','DUE:20240312T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS e JOIN ical.main.ical_todos(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Ops Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Deploy release','DTSTART:20240310T150000Z','DTEND:20240310T160000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Retro','DTSTART:20240311T170000Z','DTEND:20240311T173000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:ops-todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Update changelog','DUE:20240312T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS t ON t.due BETWEEN e.dtstart AND e.dtstart + INTERVAL 7 DAY ORDER BY e.dtstart, t.due;

example_queries.description: List the built-in sample iCalendar feeds, richest first, with their display name and event/to-do counts.
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, calendar_name, event_count, todo_count FROM ical.main.example_calendars ORDER BY event_count DESC, name;

example_queries.description: List the outstanding to-dos from an iCalendar feed by due date.
example_queries.sql: SELECT summary, status, percent_complete FROM ical.main.ical_todos(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) WHERE status <> 'COMPLETED' ORDER BY due;

example_queries.description: List every event in an iCalendar feed by start time.
example_queries.sql: SELECT summary, location, all_day FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) ORDER BY dtstart;

END:VTODO
END:VCALENDAR

Using this worker, report for every event how many to-dos that are not COMPLETED fall due before the event starts. Events with no such to-do must still appear, with 0. Return one row per event with exactly two columns, in this order: the event SUMMARY (text) and the count (integer), ordered by event start time.
This worker ships a built-in registry of sample iCalendar feeds. Using the worker, find which built-in sample calendar has the most events, and return that calendar's display name.

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# iCalendar functions

Parse iCalendar (`.ics`) feeds directly in SQL over Apache Arrow, powered by [iCal4j](https://www.ical4j.org/) ([RFC 5545](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545)).

The functions in this schema cover three areas:

- **Events** — expand a feed into event rows, or tally them.
- **To-dos** — expand a feed into task rows.
- **Calendar metadata** — read calendar-level properties and validate feed health.

Every function accepts the same polymorphic argument: a `VARCHAR` file path (the worker reads the file) or a `BLOB` of raw `.ics` bytes (parsed in place). Timestamps are normalised to UTC and surfaced as `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`, and bad or NULL input never crashes a query.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT summary, location FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) ORDER BY dtstart;
vgi.example_queries.description: List the events in an iCalendar feed.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT summary, status FROM ical.main.ical_todos(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) ORDER BY due;
vgi.example_queries.description: List the to-dos in an iCalendar feed.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ical.main.ical_calendar_name(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS calendar_name;

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ical.main.ical_event_count(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS event_count;

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT ical.main.is_valid_ical(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS is_valid;

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, ical.main.is_valid_ical(feed::BLOB) AS is_valid, ical.main.ical_calendar_name(feed::BLOB) AS parsed_name, ical.main.ical_event_count(feed::BLOB) AS parsed_events FROM (SELECT name, feed FROM ical.main.example_calendars UNION ALL SELECT 'truncated_export', 'BEGIN:VCALENDAR') AS f ORDER BY name;

Both example_calendars samples come back valid (Ops Calendar 2 events, Team Calendar 1); a truncated export comes back false, NULL, 0. Cast text to `BLOB`: a `VARCHAR` is read as a file path.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT a.summary AS first_event, b.summary AS second_event, greatest(a.dtstart, b.dtstart) AS overlap_start, least(a.dtend, b.dtend) AS overlap_end FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Design Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Design review','DTSTART:20240402T090000Z','DTEND:20240402T100000Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Customer call','DTSTART:20240402T093000Z','DTEND:20240402T101500Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d3@query.farm','SUMMARY:Team sync','DTSTART:20240402T101500Z','DTEND:20240402T110000Z','END:VEVENT','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS a JOIN ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Design Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Design review','DTSTART:20240402T090000Z','DTEND:20240402T100000Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Customer call','DTSTART:20240402T093000Z','DTEND:20240402T101500Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d3@query.farm','SUMMARY:Team sync','DTSTART:20240402T101500Z','DTEND:20240402T110000Z','END:VEVENT','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS b ON a.uid < b.uid AND a.dtstart < b.dtend AND b.dtstart < a.dtend ORDER BY overlap_start, first_event;
vgi.example_queries.description: Find double-booked events: self-join ical_events on overlapping [dtstart, dtend) ranges. Returns Design review with Customer call, overlapping 09:30-10:00 UTC; Team sync starts as Customer call ends, so it is not a conflict.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT e.summary AS event, e.dtstart, t.summary AS todo, t.due FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Ops Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Deploy release','DTSTART:20240310T150000Z','DTEND:20240310T160000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Retro','DTSTART:20240311T170000Z','DTEND:20240311T173000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:ops-todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Update changelog','DUE:20240312T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS e JOIN ical.main.ical_todos(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Ops Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Deploy release','DTSTART:20240310T150000Z','DTEND:20240310T160000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:ops-2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Retro','DTSTART:20240311T170000Z','DTEND:20240311T173000Z','STATUS:CONFIRMED','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:ops-todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Update changelog','DUE:20240312T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS t ON t.due BETWEEN e.dtstart AND e.dtstart + INTERVAL 7 DAY ORDER BY e.dtstart, t.due;
vgi.example_queries.description: List, for each event, the to-dos that fall due within 7 days of its start, by joining ical_events to ical_todos on a time window. iCalendar does not link to-dos to events, so the pairing is by time only: the Ops Calendar's one to-do, Update changelog (due 2024-03-12 17:00 UTC), pairs with both Deploy release and Retro.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: A curated, browsable registry of ready-to-use example iCalendar (`.ics`) feeds, one per row. Query it first to discover what a well-formed feed looks like and to obtain a sample you can study or copy. Columns: `name` (a short slug id), `calendar_name` (the feed's X-WR-CALNAME display name), `event_count` (how many VEVENTs the sample has), `todo_count` (how many VTODOs it has), `description` (a one-line summary), and `feed` (the raw iCalendar text). The view takes no arguments and needs no credentials. The scalar helpers (`is_valid_ical`, `ical_calendar_name`, `ical_event_count`) accept this column directly: pass `feed::BLOB` (a plain `VARCHAR` is read as a file path). The table functions `ical_events` and `ical_todos` accept only literal arguments, so paste the feed text inline as a `BLOB` literal rather than passing this column or a subquery.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## example_calendars

A small, built-in catalog of sample **iCalendar** (`.ics`) feeds you can query without supplying any input. It exists so you can see a well-formed feed and the kinds of calendar this worker understands before calling the parsing functions, which all require a feed argument.

Each row describes one sample: a slug `name`, the `calendar_name` display name (X-WR-CALNAME), a precomputed `event_count` and `todo_count`, a short `description`, and the raw `feed` text itself. Browse it, sort by `event_count`, or copy a `feed` literal into `ical_events`, `ical_todos`, or the scalar helpers to experiment.

The view is defined over an inline `VALUES` list, so it scans instantly with no network access and no credentials.

vgi.example_queries.description: Health-check a column of stored feeds: the scalars accept columns (table functions do not). Both example_calendars samples come back valid (Ops Calendar 2 events, Team Calendar 1); a truncated export comes back false, NULL, 0. Cast text to `BLOB`: a `VARCHAR` is read as a file path.

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
# ical_todos

Parse an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed into **one row per VTODO** (task). Use it to pull outstanding to-dos out of a shared calendar for task tracking or reporting.

**Input** (typed overloads): a `VARCHAR` file path the worker opens, or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes.

**Output**: uid, summary, UTC-normalised `due` (`TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`), status (`NEEDS-ACTION` / `IN-PROCESS` / `COMPLETED` / `CANCELLED`), priority (0-9), and percent complete (0-100).

**Edge cases**: a NULL argument or an unparsable feed yields *no rows* (never an error). A feed with only events (no VTODOs) yields no rows.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Parses an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed into one row per VTODO (task), backed by iCal4j (RFC 5545).

Accepts a `VARCHAR` file path or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes. The `due` column is normalised to UTC and surfaced as `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`. Filter on `status` to separate open from completed tasks. Bad or NULL input yields no rows rather than an error.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT summary, status, percent_complete FROM ical.main.ical_todos(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Team Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:event-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Sprint Planning','DESCRIPTION:Plan the next two-week sprint.','DTSTART:20240115T093000Z','DTEND:20240115T103000Z','LOCATION:Conference Room A','STATUS:CONFIRMED','ORGANIZER:mailto:alice@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:bob@query.farm','ATTENDEE:mailto:carol@query.farm','RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO','SEQUENCE:3','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VTODO','UID:todo-1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Write release notes','DUE:20240120T170000Z','STATUS:NEEDS-ACTION','PRIORITY:2','PERCENT-COMPLETE:40','END:VTODO','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) WHERE status <> 'COMPLETED' ORDER BY due;
vgi.example_queries.description: List the outstanding to-dos from an iCalendar feed by due date.

functions.comment: Parse an iCalendar (.ics) feed into one row per VEVENT: uid, summary, UTC-normalised start/end, all-day flag, location, status, organizer, attendees array, recurrence rule, sequence, category tags, url, and created/last-modified timestamps (iCal4j).

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
# ical_events

Parse an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed into **one row per VEVENT**. Use it to ingest a calendar feed for scheduling analytics, reporting, or joining events against other tables.

**Input** (typed overloads): a `VARCHAR` file path the worker opens, or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes.

**Output**: uid, summary, description, UTC-normalised `dtstart`/`dtend` (`TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`), an `all_day` flag, location, status, organizer, an `attendees VARCHAR[]` array, the recurrence `rrule`, `sequence`, a `categories VARCHAR[]` tag array, `url`, and the UTC-normalised `created` / `last_modified` audit timestamps.

**Edge cases**: a NULL argument or a feed that fails to parse yields *no rows* (never an error). `DATE`-valued starts set `all_day = true`; recurrences are surfaced as the raw RRULE string, not expanded.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Parses an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed into one row per VEVENT, backed by iCal4j (RFC 5545).

Accepts a `VARCHAR` file path or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes. Timestamps are normalised to UTC and surfaced as `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`. Bad or NULL input yields no rows rather than an error. Recurrence rules appear as the raw RRULE string in the `rrule` column.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT a.summary AS first_event, b.summary AS second_event, greatest(a.dtstart, b.dtstart) AS overlap_start, least(a.dtend, b.dtend) AS overlap_end FROM ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Design Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Design review','DTSTART:20240402T090000Z','DTEND:20240402T100000Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Customer call','DTSTART:20240402T093000Z','DTEND:20240402T101500Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d3@query.farm','SUMMARY:Team sync','DTSTART:20240402T101500Z','DTEND:20240402T110000Z','END:VEVENT','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS a JOIN ical.main.ical_events(array_to_string(['BEGIN:VCALENDAR','VERSION:2.0','PRODID:-//Query Farm//vgi-ical//EN','X-WR-CALNAME:Design Calendar','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d1@query.farm','SUMMARY:Design review','DTSTART:20240402T090000Z','DTEND:20240402T100000Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d2@query.farm','SUMMARY:Customer call','DTSTART:20240402T093000Z','DTEND:20240402T101500Z','END:VEVENT','BEGIN:VEVENT','UID:d3@query.farm','SUMMARY:Team sync','DTSTART:20240402T101500Z','DTEND:20240402T110000Z','END:VEVENT','END:VCALENDAR'], chr(10))::BLOB) AS b ON a.uid < b.uid AND a.dtstart < b.dtend AND b.dtstart < a.dtend ORDER BY overlap_start, first_event;

functions.name: ical_events
functions.comment: Parse an iCalendar (.ics) feed into one row per VEVENT: uid, summary, UTC-normalised start/end, all-day flag, location, status, organizer, attendees array, recurrence rule, sequence, category tags, url, and created/last-modified timestamps (iCal4j).

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
# ical_events

Parse an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed into **one row per VEVENT**. Use it to ingest a calendar feed for scheduling analytics, reporting, or joining events against other tables.

**Input** (typed overloads): a `VARCHAR` file path the worker opens, or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes.

**Output**: uid, summary, description, UTC-normalised `dtstart`/`dtend` (`TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`), an `all_day` flag, location, status, organizer, an `attendees VARCHAR[]` array, the recurrence `rrule`, `sequence`, a `categories VARCHAR[]` tag array, `url`, and the UTC-normalised `created` / `last_modified` audit timestamps.

**Edge cases**: a NULL argument or a feed that fails to parse yields *no rows* (never an error). `DATE`-valued starts set `all_day = true`; recurrences are surfaced as the raw RRULE string, not expanded.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Parses an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed into one row per VEVENT, backed by iCal4j (RFC 5545).

Accepts a `VARCHAR` file path or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes. Timestamps are normalised to UTC and surfaced as `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`. Bad or NULL input yields no rows rather than an error. Recurrence rules appear as the raw RRULE string in the `rrule` column.

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
# ical_event_count

Return the **number of VEVENTs** in an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed without materialising the rows. Use it as a cheap probe — e.g. to skip empty feeds or rank feeds by activity.

**Input** (typed overloads): a `VARCHAR` file path the worker opens, or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes.

**Output**: an `INTEGER` count. NULL input yields NULL; an empty or unparsable feed yields `0` (never an error).
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Counts the VEVENTs in an iCalendar (`.ics`) feed.

Accepts a `VARCHAR` file path or a `BLOB` of `.ics` bytes and returns an `INTEGER`. A NULL argument returns NULL; an empty or unparsable feed returns `0`. Cheaper than materialising and counting rows from the event table function when you only need the tally.

workers.title: Image Toolkit
workers.tagline: Image info, EXIF/GPS, perceptual hashing & thumbnails for DuckDB (Rust)
workers.subtitle: Decode images, read EXIF and GPS tags, spot near-duplicates by perceptual hash, and make thumbnails.
workers.summary: Image decoding, EXIF metadata, perceptual hashing, thumbnailing and format conversion over Apache Arrow.
workers.doc_md:
# image — Image Inspection, EXIF/GPS, Perceptual Hashing & Thumbnails in SQL

![image logo](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/49300799?s=240&v=4)

Decode images, read EXIF and GPS metadata, compute perceptual hashes for near-duplicate detection, and generate thumbnails directly in DuckDB SQL — no external tooling or file wrangling required. The `image` worker brings a full image-processing toolbox to the `img` catalog, turning ordinary `BLOB` columns of PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF and WebP bytes into queryable, structured data.

This extension is for anyone cataloguing, deduplicating, or auditing image collections from SQL: data engineers building media pipelines, analysts hunting near-duplicate or geotagged photos, and teams that want EXIF and perceptual-hash features right next to their existing DuckDB tables. Everything runs in-process over Apache Arrow, so image-derived columns join against the rest of your data without ever leaving the database.

## How it works

The worker is powered by the pure-Rust [`image`](https://github.com/image-rs/image) crate ([docs](https://docs.rs/image)) for decoding, resizing and format conversion; [`kamadak-exif`](https://github.com/kamadak/exif-rs) ([docs](https://docs.rs/kamadak-exif)) for parsing EXIF tags and GPS coordinates; and [`image_hasher`](https://github.com/abonander/img_hash) ([docs](https://docs.rs/image_hasher)) for 64-bit perceptual hashes. Image bytes are passed as DuckDB `BLOB` values and `NULL` inputs flow through to `NULL` results, so the capabilities compose cleanly inside larger queries.

## When to reach for it

Reach for this worker to catalogue a folder of images by their format and dimensions, to read capture metadata and geotags for auditing or mapping, to find near-duplicate or reposted photos by perceptual similarity, and to normalize or preview a mixed set of images — all without leaving SQL or standing up an external image-processing service. Malformed or truncated bytes yield a graceful `NULL` or a clear error, so it is safe to run across messy data at scale.

example_queries.description: Decode an image BLOB's header and read its detected format.
Compute the 64-bit DCT perceptual hash of an image BLOB.
Hamming distance between the phash of a PNG and the phash of its lossless BMP re-encode: 0 of 64 bits, so the copy is perceptually identical.

Find near-duplicates in a set of images: hash each image once with phash, then rank every pair by phash_distance. The BMP re-encode of a.png scores 0 against it; the unrelated b.png is 17 bits away from both.
example_queries.sql: WITH images(name, data) AS (SELECT 'a.png', from_hex('89504e470d0a1a0a0000000d4948445200000002000000020802000000fdd49a73000000164944415478da6360608812608862601088121088020009be01a9f633974e0000000049454e44ae426082') UNION ALL SELECT 'b.png', from_hex('89504e470d0a1a0a0000000d4948445200000004000000040802000000269309290000002e4944415478da1d864901003008c3f246045ad0819acac355c778e4c0c0e1efaba4aa22a627ba6332130bb4f2de03fd2e1413e2c4ad370000000049454e44ae426082') UNION ALL SELECT 'a_copy.bmp', img.main.convert(from_hex('89504e470d0a1a0a0000000d4948445200000002000000020802000000fdd49a73000000164944415478da6360608812608862601088121088020009be01a9f633974e0000000049454e44ae426082'), 'bmp')), hashed AS (SELECT name, img.main.phash(data) AS h FROM images) SELECT x.name AS image, y.name AS other, img.main.phash_distance(x.h, y.h) AS distance FROM hashed x JOIN hashed y ON x.name < y.name ORDER BY distance, image, other;

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# img.main

The primary schema of the image worker. It groups its capabilities into a few areas: **inspection** of an image's header (format, dimensions, color model), reading embedded **metadata** (EXIF tags and decimal GPS), perceptual **hashing** for near-duplicate detection, and image **transformation** (thumbnailing and format conversion).

Every function takes a single image `BLOB` (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, or WebP); a NULL input flows through to a NULL result, and undecodable bytes surface a clear error. Everything runs in-process over Apache Arrow, so image-derived columns join cleanly against the rest of your data.

Hamming distance between the phash of a PNG and the phash of its lossless BMP re-encode: 0 of 64 bits, so the copy is perceptually identical.

Find near-duplicates in a set of images: hash each image once with phash, then rank every pair by phash_distance. The BMP re-encode of a.png scores 0 against it; the unrelated b.png is 17 bits away from both.

workers.subtitle: Pull indicators of compromise out of threat reports and defang or refang them safely.
workers.summary: Defensive CTI tooling: extract and defang/refang indicators of compromise (IOCs) from free text.
workers.doc_md:
# IOC Extraction & Defang/Refang for DuckDB

Pull indicators of compromise (IOCs) out of cyber-threat-intelligence (CTI) reports and defang or refang them with plain SQL — no Python notebook, regex cheat-sheet, or external service required. The `ioc` extension turns DuckDB into an IOC parser that recognizes IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, domains, URLs, e-mail addresses, file hashes (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512) and CVE identifiers, and converts between live indicators (`http://evil.com`) and the *defanged* form (`hxxp[://]evil[.]com`) that analysts use to share malware artifacts safely. It is built for threat hunters, incident responders, SOC analysts and data engineers who already keep logs, alerts and reports in DuckDB and want indicator extraction to be just another column expression.

This is a purely **defensive** tool: it reads and rewrites indicators that already exist in your text — it never generates attacks, resolves names, or touches the network. Extraction is powered by the Rust [`regex`](https://github.com/rust-lang/regex) crate ([documentation](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/)), whose linear-time, backtracking-free engine matches large reports without catastrophic blowup. The worker is a standalone binary that DuckDB attaches over Apache Arrow IPC, so results stream back as native Arrow columns. A key design choice is *refang-before-extract*: every extractor (and `is_ioc` / `extract_iocs`) first refangs a copy of its input, so indicators that were defanged in a report — `10[.]0[.]0[.]5`, `bad[at]evil[.]com`, `hxxp://evil[.]com` — are still found. Only defanging and refanging themselves skip that step.

Reach for it whenever indicators live inside free text rather than tidy columns: enriching an alerts or tickets table, building a watchlist from an incident report, sanitizing artifacts before sharing them, or joining extracted indicators against a threat feed. Functions are grouped into extraction, defang/refang and classification, and each carries its own worked examples.
workers.readme_sql:
LOAD vgi;
ATTACH 'ioc' (TYPE vgi, LOCATION 'github-auto://Query-farm/vgi-ioc@v0.4.1');
SET search_path = 'ioc.main';

-- Make an indicator safe to paste into a report.
SELECT defang('http://evil.com/x');          -- → 'hxxp[://]evil[.]com/x'

-- Turn a defanged indicator back into live form.
SELECT refang('hxxp://evil[.]com');          -- → 'http://evil.com'

-- Pull indicators out of a (defanged) report. Extractors refang internally.
SELECT UNNEST(extract_ipv4('beacon from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5'));   -- → '10.0.0.5'
SELECT UNNEST(extract_cves('exploiting CVE-2024-1234'));     -- → 'CVE-2024-1234'

-- Classify a hash by length.
SELECT hash_type('d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e');        -- → 'md5'

-- Does this text contain any IOC?
SELECT is_ioc('CVE-2021-44228 in the logs');                 -- → true

-- Every distinct IOC as typed rows (table function).
SELECT type, value
FROM extract_iocs('beacon to hxxp://evil[.]com from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5')
ORDER BY type, value;
-- type | value
-- ipv4 | 10.0.0.5
-- url  | http://evil.com

-- Combine them: label each extracted indicator with its group via the ioc_types registry.
SELECT t.kind, i.type, i.value
FROM extract_iocs('phish from ops[at]evil[.]com exploiting CVE-2021-44228 via 10[.]0[.]0[.]5') AS i
JOIN ioc_types AS t ON t.name = i.type
ORDER BY t.kind, i.type;
-- kind          | type  | value
-- email         | email | ops@evil.com
-- network       | ipv4  | 10.0.0.5
-- vulnerability | cve   | CVE-2021-44228

example_queries.description: Extract every distinct indicator from a defanged report as (type, value) rows.
example_queries.sql: SELECT type, value FROM ioc.main.extract_iocs('beacon to hxxp://evil[.]com from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5') ORDER BY type, value

example_queries.description: Count the indicators in a report, grouped by type.
example_queries.sql: SELECT type, count(*) AS n FROM ioc.main.extract_iocs('c2 hxxp://evil[.]com from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5 and bad[at]evil[.]com') GROUP BY type ORDER BY type

example_queries.description: Defang a live URL so it is safe to paste into a report.
example_queries.sql: SELECT ioc.main.defang('http://evil.com/x') AS safe

example_queries.description: Pull the defanged IPv4 addresses out of a report, one per row.
example_queries.sql: SELECT UNNEST(ioc.main.extract_ipv4('beacon from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5')) AS ip

example_queries.description: Classify a hex digest by algorithm.
example_queries.sql: SELECT ioc.main.hash_type('d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e') AS algorithm

example_queries.description: Label every indicator pulled from a defanged report with its coarse group (network, email, hash, vulnerability) and the single-type extractor for it, by joining extract_iocs to the ioc_types registry.
example_queries.sql: SELECT t.kind, i.type, i.value, t.extractor FROM ioc.main.extract_iocs('dropper hxxps://cdn[.]evil[.]com/a.exe (sha256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855) beacons to 203[.]0[.]113[.]7, exploits CVE-2021-44228, phish from ops[at]evil[.]com') AS i JOIN ioc.main.ioc_types AS t ON t.name = i.type ORDER BY t.kind, i.type, i.value

example_queries.description: Turn a live incident note into a safe-to-share watchlist: extract every indicator with extract_iocs, then defang each value so none of them is clickable.
example_queries.sql: SELECT i.type, ioc.main.defang(i.value) AS shareable FROM ioc.main.extract_iocs('beacon to http://evil.com/gate.php from 10.0.0.5, contact bad@evil.com') AS i ORDER BY i.type, shareable

example_queries.description: For each alert in a table, list the file hashes it mentions with their algorithm: unnest extract_hashes over the alert text and label each hash with hash_type (alerts without hashes produce no rows).
example_queries.sql: WITH alerts(id, body) AS (VALUES (1, 'dropped d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e and da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709'), (2, 'user reset password'), (3, 'payload e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855')) SELECT a.id, h.hash, ioc.main.hash_type(h.hash) AS algorithm FROM alerts AS a, UNNEST(ioc.main.extract_hashes(a.body)) AS h(hash) ORDER BY a.id, algorithm

example_queries.description: Triage a ticket queue: keep only tickets whose text contains any indicator (is_ioc), then count the IPv4 addresses, URLs and CVEs each one mentions.
example_queries.sql: WITH tickets(id, body) AS (VALUES (1, 'beacon to hxxp://evil[.]com/x from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5'), (2, 'password reset for jsmith'), (3, 'exploiting CVE-2024-1234 via 10[.]0[.]0[.]5 and 10[.]0[.]0[.]9'), (4, 'printer offline on floor 3')) SELECT id, len(ioc.main.extract_ipv4(body)) AS n_ips, len(ioc.main.extract_urls(body)) AS n_urls, len(ioc.main.extract_cves(body)) AS n_cves FROM tickets WHERE ioc.main.is_ioc(body) ORDER BY id

example_queries.description: List the network-layer indicator types and the function that extracts each.
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, extractor FROM ioc.main.ioc_types WHERE kind = 'network' ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Count how many indicator types fall into each coarse group.
example_queries.sql: SELECT kind, count(*) AS n_types FROM ioc.main.ioc_types GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind

example_queries.description: Count the distinct indicators found in a report, grouped by indicator type.
example_queries.sql: SELECT type, count(*) AS n FROM ioc.main.extract_iocs('beacon to hxxp://evil[.]com from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5 and bad[at]evil[.]com') GROUP BY type ORDER BY type

example_queries.description: Keep only the network-layer indicators (IPs, domains, URLs) from a report.
example_queries.sql: SELECT value FROM ioc.main.extract_iocs('c2 hxxp://evil[.]com from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5') WHERE type IN ('ipv4', 'ipv6', 'url', 'domain') ORDER BY value

example_queries.description: Pull a defanged URL out of a report (returns 'http://evil.com/x').
example_queries.sql: SELECT UNNEST(ioc.main.extract_urls('payload from hxxp://evil[.]com/x'));

example_queries.description: Refang a defanged URL back to live form (returns 'http://evil.com').

example_queries.description: Pull a defanged e-mail address out of a report (returns 'bad@evil.com').
example_queries.sql: SELECT UNNEST(ioc.main.extract_emails('phish from bad[at]evil[.]com'));

example_queries.description: Pull a bare defanged domain out of a report (returns 'evil.example.com').

Return a single boolean value that is true when the text 'exploiting CVE-2024-1234 in the wild' contains any indicator of compromise, and false otherwise.
From the defanged report 'callback from 10[.]0[.]0[.]5 and 192[.]168[.]1[.]1', return the IPv4 addresses one address per row (a single column of scalar address strings, not a list).
From the text 'C2 at 2001:db8::1 observed', return the IPv6 addresses, one address per row (a single column of scalar address strings, not a list).
From the defanged text 'payload from hxxp://evil[.]com/x', return the URLs in live (clickable) form, one URL per row.
From the defanged text 'callback to evil[.]example[.]com', return the bare domain names, one domain per row.

From the text 'exploiting CVE-2024-1234 in the wild', return the CVE identifiers, one per row.
Return a single value: the defanged indicator 'hxxp://evil[.]com' restored to its live, canonical form.
Using the ioc_types reference table in the ioc worker, return a single count of how many distinct indicator types it can recognize.

From the defanged report 'c2 hxxp://evil[.]com/p and 198[.]51[.]100[.]4, sender ops[at]evil[.]com, dropper sha1 da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709, exploits CVE-2023-4863 and CVE-2024-3094', count the distinct indicators in each coarse indicator group as defined by the ioc worker's indicator type registry (groups such as network, email, hash, vulnerability). tags.vgi.doc_md:
## IOC extraction & defang/refang

Indicator-of-compromise tooling for cyber-threat intelligence, served over Apache Arrow. Pull IPv4/IPv6 addresses, domains, URLs, e-mails, file hashes and CVE identifiers out of free-text reports with plain SQL, and convert between live and *defanged* indicator forms.

### Key concepts

- **Refang-before-extract** — every extractor refangs a copy of its input first, so indicators defanged in a report (`hxxp://evil[.]com`, `10[.]0[.]0[.]5`, `bad[at]evil[.]com`) are still found.
- **Defang / refang** — neutralize live indicators so they are safe to paste into a ticket or chat, or restore them to live form.
- **Deduplicated, typed output** — the all-in-one extractor returns one `(type, value)` row per distinct indicator.

### When to use it

Reach for this schema when indicators live inside free text rather than tidy columns — enriching an alerts table, building a watchlist from an incident report, or sanitizing artifacts before sharing them. Browse the functions below, grouped by category, each with its own worked examples.

Columns: `name` (the type, e.g. ipv4, sha256, cve), `kind` (a coarse group: network, email, hash, or vulnerability), `extractor` (the scalar function that pulls this type out of text, e.g. extract_ipv4), `example` (a short defanged sample value), and `description`. Query it to discover what the worker extracts and which function to call, before running the specific extractor or the all-in-one extract_iocs table function. Ten rows, one per type; no arguments, no network, always safe to scan.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## `ioc_types` — indicator type registry

A small, static reference table you can browse to see exactly which indicator-of-compromise types this worker recognizes and which function extracts each. Handy as a first stop before calling a specific extractor.

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the indicator type — `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `domain`, `url`, `email`, `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `sha512`, `cve` |
| `kind` | coarse group: `network`, `email`, `hash`, or `vulnerability` |
| `extractor` | the scalar function that pulls this type out of text |
| `example` | a short defanged sample value |
| `description` | one-line notes on how the type is matched |

Ten rows, one per type. It is backed by an inline literal list, so scanning it needs no network or credentials. To pull every type out of a report at once, use the `extract_iocs` table function instead.

vgi.example_queries.description: List the network-layer indicator types and the function that extracts each.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, extractor FROM ioc.main.ioc_types WHERE kind = 'network' ORDER BY name

vgi.example_queries.description: Count how many indicator types fall into each coarse group.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT kind, count(*) AS n_types FROM ioc.main.ioc_types GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind

vgi.example_queries.description: Label every indicator pulled from a defanged report with its coarse group (network, email, hash, vulnerability) and the single-type extractor for it, by joining extract_iocs to the ioc_types registry.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.kind, i.type, i.value, t.extractor FROM ioc.main.extract_iocs('dropper hxxps://cdn[.]evil[.]com/a.exe (sha256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855) beacons to 203[.]0[.]113[.]7, exploits CVE-2021-44228, phish from ops[at]evil[.]com') AS i JOIN ioc.main.ioc_types AS t ON t.name = i.type ORDER BY t.kind, i.type, i.value

functions.name: extract_iocs
functions.comment: Extract every distinct IOC from text as (type, value) rows (refangs first; deduplicated)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Scan free text and return every distinct indicator of compromise as (type, value) rows, one row per indicator. Covered types are ipv4, ipv6, url, email, domain, md5, sha1, sha256, sha512, and cve. The text is refanged first so defanged indicators are found, results are deduplicated, and URL/e-mail hosts are not double-reported as bare domains. The text argument is a bind-time constant; a NULL or empty text yields zero rows. Use this as the one-shot table function when you want all indicator types at once instead of calling each extractor separately.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Extract every distinct IOC from text as `(type, value)` rows: one row per indicator, across all supported types at once. The input is refanged first so defanged indicators are still found, results are deduplicated, and a URL or e-mail host is not double-reported as a bare domain.

workers.title: ISO 20022 Payments
workers.tagline: Parse ISO 20022 (pacs/camt/pain) and SWIFT MT payment messages in DuckDB with SQL — no egress. A VGI worker.
workers.subtitle: Parse SWIFT MT and ISO 20022 MX payment messages into typed SQL rows, locally with no network calls.
workers.summary: Parse SWIFT MT and ISO 20022 MX payment messages into typed, queryable rows. Local-only, no network, no egress.
workers.doc_md:
# iso20022 — SWIFT MT & ISO 20022 MX Payment Parsing in SQL

**Turn SWIFT MT and ISO 20022 MX payment messages into typed, queryable rows directly in DuckDB.** ATTACH the worker over Apache Arrow and parse FIN/MT files and MX XML documents locally — one typed row per message, transaction, or statement entry — so payments become plain relational data instead of something you feed to a bespoke parser.

It is built for **bank / fintech / payment-processor** data teams doing reconciliation, ISO 20022 migration dual-running QA (MT vs MX equivalence), and sanctions/feature extraction. Money is parsed with exact decimals (no float drift) so amount-equality joins hold; dates use the SWIFT century pivot and ISO 8601. **Data residency:** the worker makes zero outbound calls and parses every message locally — debtor/creditor names, IBANs, and amounts never leave the host.

Reach for it whenever you have MT statements or transfers, or camt/pacs/pain XML, on disk (or inline) and want them as rows. It provides file-glob **readers** (one row per message, transaction, or statement), per-message **exploders** that unnest statement entries and lines, and **inspection scalars** that sniff the MT type, read a field, return the exact settled amount, and validate a message. Money is parsed as exact decimals so amount-equality joins hold, and dates use the SWIFT century pivot plus ISO 8601. The parsers are built on permissive open-source components and the open, freely published ISO 20022 message standard ([iso20022.org](https://www.iso20022.org/)); the [source repository](https://github.com/Query-farm/vgi-iso20022) carries the full catalog and examples.

## Sources and references

- [ISO 20022 message definitions](https://www.iso20022.org/iso-20022-message-definitions) — the published pacs, pain and camt schemas the MX readers follow
- [Swift: About ISO 20022](https://www.swift.com/standards/iso-20022) — the MT-to-MX migration and the CBPR+ usage rules `validate` checks
- [Swift: IBAN](https://www.swift.com/standards/data-standards/iban-international-bank-account-number) — the IBAN format and check digits the validator applies

example_queries.description: Sniff the SWIFT MT message type of an inline FIN message.
example_queries.sql:
SELECT iso20022.main.iso20022_mt_type('{1:F01X}{2:I103X}{4:
:20:R
-}') AS mt

example_queries.description: Read the exact :32A: interbank settled amount of an inline MT103 as a fixed-scale decimal.
example_queries.sql:
SELECT iso20022.main.iso20022_mt103_amount('{1:F01X}{2:I103X}{4:
:20:R
:32A:260101EUR1234,56
-}') AS amount

example_queries.description: Validate an inline pacs.008 message and read the ok flag.
example_queries.sql: SELECT (iso20022.main.iso20022_validate('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>M</MsgId></GrpHdr></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>')).ok AS ok

example_queries.description: Migration QA: pair an MT103 with its pacs.008 twin on end_to_end_id and check that the settled amount, currency, and UETR agree in both formats.
example_queries.sql:
SELECT m.end_to_end_id, m.ccy, m.amount AS mt_amount, p.amount AS mx_amount, m.amount = p.amount AND m.ccy = p.ccy AS amount_match, m.uetr = p.uetr AS uetr_match FROM iso20022.main.mt103_read('{1:F01ACMEDEFFAXXX0000000000}{2:I103DEUTDEFFXXXXN}{3:{121:e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab}}{4:
:20:TXN-REF-1
:23B:CRED
:32A:260101EUR1234,56
:50K:/DE89370400440532013000
ACME CORP
:59:/FR1420041010050500013M02606
WIDGETS SARL
:71A:SHA
:72:/EToE/E2E-REF-001
-}') AS m JOIN iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>PACS-MSG-1</MsgId></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-REF-001</EndToEndId><UETR>e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1234.56</IntrBkSttlmAmt></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') AS p USING (end_to_end_id) ORDER BY m.end_to_end_id

example_queries.description: Status reconciliation: join each pacs.008 credit transfer to the pacs.002 status report on UETR to see which payments settled (ACSC) and which were rejected, with the reason code.
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.end_to_end_id, p.creditor_name, p.amount, p.ccy, s.tx_status, s.status_reason_code FROM iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>BATCH-7</MsgId></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-A</EndToEndId><UETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000a</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1500.00</IntrBkSttlmAmt><Cdtr><Nm>WIDGETS SARL</Nm></Cdtr></CdtTrfTxInf><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-B</EndToEndId><UETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000b</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">98000.00</IntrBkSttlmAmt><Cdtr><Nm>GADGETS GMBH</Nm></Cdtr></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') AS p LEFT JOIN iso20022.main.pacs002_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.002.001.10"><FIToFIPmtStsRpt><GrpHdr><MsgId>STS-7</MsgId></GrpHdr><OrgnlGrpInfAndSts><OrgnlMsgId>BATCH-7</OrgnlMsgId></OrgnlGrpInfAndSts><TxInfAndSts><OrgnlUETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000a</OrgnlUETR><TxSts>ACSC</TxSts></TxInfAndSts><TxInfAndSts><OrgnlUETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000b</OrgnlUETR><TxSts>RJCT</TxSts><StsRsnInf><Rsn><Cd>AM04</Cd></Rsn></StsRsnInf></TxInfAndSts></FIToFIPmtStsRpt></Document>') AS s ON s.orig_uetr = p.uetr ORDER BY p.end_to_end_id

example_queries.description: Statement roll-forward check: explode each MT940 statement's :61: lines, net credits against debits, and compare opening balance + net movement with the reported closing balance (here STMT-2 is off by 50.50).
example_queries.sql:
SELECT transaction_ref, opening_balance, sum(CASE WHEN credit_debit IN ('D', 'RC') THEN -amount ELSE amount END) AS net_movement, closing_balance, opening_balance + net_movement = closing_balance AS balanced FROM iso20022.main.mt940_lines((SELECT transaction_ref, opening_balance, closing_balance, raw FROM iso20022.main.mt940_read('{1:F01X}{2:O940X}{4:
:20:STMT-1
:25:DE89370400440532013000
:28C:1/1
:60F:C260101EUR1000,00
:61:2601020102C500,00NTRFNONREF//BANK-A
:61:2601030103D250,50NMSCCUST-REF//BANK-B
:62F:C260103EUR1249,50
-}{1:F01X}{2:O940X}{4:
:20:STMT-2
:25:DE89370400440532013000
:28C:2/1
:60F:C260103EUR1249,50
:61:2601040104D100,00NMSCREF-2//BANK-C
:62F:C260104EUR1200,00
-}'))) GROUP BY transaction_ref, opening_balance, closing_balance ORDER BY transaction_ref

example_queries.sql: SELECT message_type, reader_function, exploder_function FROM iso20022.main.supported_messages WHERE exploder_function IS NOT NULL ORDER BY message_type

example_queries.description: Parse an inline pain.001 customer credit-transfer initiation: read the debtor, instructed amount, and creditor for each CdtTrfTxInf.
example_queries.sql: SELECT msg_id, pmt_method, debtor_name, amount, ccy, creditor_name FROM iso20022.main.pain001_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pain.001.001.09"><CstmrCdtTrfInitn><GrpHdr><MsgId>PAIN-1</MsgId><CreDtTm>2026-01-01T09:00:00Z</CreDtTm><CtrlSum>1234.56</CtrlSum><InitgPty><Nm>ACME CORP</Nm></InitgPty></GrpHdr><PmtInf><PmtInfId>PMT-1</PmtInfId><PmtMtd>TRF</PmtMtd><ReqdExctnDt><Dt>2026-01-02</Dt></ReqdExctnDt><Dbtr><Nm>ACME CORP</Nm></Dbtr><DbtrAcct><Id><IBAN>DE89370400440532013000</IBAN></Id></DbtrAcct><DbtrAgt><FinInstnId><BICFI>DEUTDEFF</BICFI></FinInstnId></DbtrAgt><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-REF-001</EndToEndId></PmtId><Amt><InstdAmt Ccy="EUR">1234.56</InstdAmt></Amt><Cdtr><Nm>WIDGETS SARL</Nm></Cdtr><CdtrAcct><Id><IBAN>FR1420041010050500013M02606</IBAN></Id></CdtrAcct><RmtInf><Ustrd>INVOICE 998877</Ustrd></RmtInf></CdtTrfTxInf></PmtInf></CstmrCdtTrfInitn></Document>') WHERE amount > 1000;

example_queries.description: Parse an inline pacs.008 FI-to-FI customer credit transfer: read the exact interbank settlement amount, UETR, and parties.
example_queries.sql: SELECT msg_id, uetr, ccy, instructed_amount, debtor_name, creditor_name FROM iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>PACS-MSG-1</MsgId><CreDtTm>2026-01-01T10:00:00Z</CreDtTm><NbOfTxs>1</NbOfTxs><SttlmInf><SttlmMtd>INDA</SttlmMtd></SttlmInf></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><InstrId>INSTR-1</InstrId><EndToEndId>E2E-REF-001</EndToEndId><UETR>e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1234.56</IntrBkSttlmAmt><IntrBkSttlmDt>2026-01-01</IntrBkSttlmDt><ChrgBr>SHAR</ChrgBr><Dbtr><Nm>ACME CORP</Nm></Dbtr><DbtrAcct><Id><IBAN>DE89370400440532013000</IBAN></Id></DbtrAcct><DbtrAgt><FinInstnId><BICFI>DEUTDEFF</BICFI></FinInstnId></DbtrAgt><Cdtr><Nm>WIDGETS SARL</Nm></Cdtr><CdtrAcct><Id><IBAN>FR1420041010050500013M02606</IBAN></Id></CdtrAcct><CdtrAgt><FinInstnId><BICFI>BNPAFRPP</BICFI></FinInstnId></CdtrAgt><Purp><Cd>GDDS</Cd></Purp><RmtInf><Ustrd>INVOICE 998877</Ustrd></RmtInf></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') WHERE instructed_amount > 1000;

example_queries.sql:
SELECT value_date, credit_debit, amount, transaction_type_id FROM iso20022.main.mt940_lines((SELECT raw FROM iso20022.main.mt940_read('{1:F01ACMEDEFFAXXX0000000000}{2:O940DEUTDEFFXXXXN}{4:
:20:STMT-1
:25:DE89370400440532013000
:28C:12345/1
:60F:C260101EUR1000,00
:61:2601020102C500,00NTRFNONREF//BANK-A
:86:GROCERY STORE PAYMENT
:61:2601030103D250,50NMSCCUST-REF//BANK-B
:86:RENT
:62F:C260103EUR1249,50
-}')));

:34F:EURD0,00
:34F:EURC1000,00
:61:2601020102C500,00NTRFNONREF//BANK-A

-}')));

example_queries.description: Parse an inline MT202 (general financial institution transfer / cover) and read its settled amount and beneficiary institution.
example_queries.sql:
SELECT transaction_ref, related_ref, ccy, amount, beneficiary_inst FROM iso20022.main.mt202_read('{1:F01ACMEDEFFAXXX0000000000}{2:I202DEUTDEFFXXXXN}{3:{121:11111111-2222-4333-8444-555566667777}}{4:
:20:FI-REF-9
:21:REL-REF-9

:52A:CHASUS33

:50K:/111
UNDERLYING DEBTOR
:59:/222
UNDERLYING CREDITOR
:70:COVER FOR MT103

:20:INTERIM-1

:61:2601020102C500,00NTRFNONREF//BANK-A

:90D:5EUR2500,00
:90C:3EUR1500,00
-}') WHERE account IS NOT NULL;

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Functions to parse SWIFT MT and ISO 20022 MX payment messages: file-glob readers (mt103_read … camt054_read), per-message entry/line exploders, and scalars for type sniffing, field access, exact amount, and validation.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## The `iso20022` worker schema

This is the single schema for the worker. Everything it exposes turns SWIFT MT and ISO 20022 MX payment messages into typed, relational rows you can query directly in SQL, with **no network access and no egress** — messages are parsed on the host.

The objects fall into three groups:

- **Message readers** scan a glob of message files on disk and return one typed row per message, transaction, or statement.
- **Statement exploders** take an already-selected statement or notification and unnest it into its individual entries or lines, carrying every input column through so children correlate back to the parent.
- **Message inspection** scalars sniff the message type, pull individual fields and the exact settled amount out of a single inline message, validate it against structural and CBPR+ rules, and report the worker version.

Money is parsed with exact decimals so amount-equality joins hold, and dates use the SWIFT century pivot plus ISO 8601. Each function documents its result columns and carries a runnable example.

vgi.example_queries.description: Sniff the SWIFT MT message type of an inline FIN message.
vgi.example_queries.sql:
SELECT iso20022.main.iso20022_mt_type('{1:F01X}{2:I103X}{4:
:20:R
-}') AS mt

vgi.example_queries.description: Read the exact :32A: interbank settled amount of an inline MT103 as a fixed-scale decimal.
vgi.example_queries.sql:
SELECT iso20022.main.iso20022_mt103_amount('{1:F01X}{2:I103X}{4:
:20:R
:32A:260101EUR1234,56
-}') AS amount

vgi.example_queries.description: Validate an inline pacs.008 message and read the ok flag.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT (iso20022.main.iso20022_validate('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>M</MsgId></GrpHdr></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>')).ok AS ok

vgi.example_queries.description: Migration QA: pair an MT103 with its pacs.008 twin on end_to_end_id and check that the settled amount, currency, and UETR agree in both formats.
vgi.example_queries.sql:
SELECT m.end_to_end_id, m.ccy, m.amount AS mt_amount, p.amount AS mx_amount, m.amount = p.amount AND m.ccy = p.ccy AS amount_match, m.uetr = p.uetr AS uetr_match FROM iso20022.main.mt103_read('{1:F01ACMEDEFFAXXX0000000000}{2:I103DEUTDEFFXXXXN}{3:{121:e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab}}{4:
:20:TXN-REF-1
:23B:CRED
:32A:260101EUR1234,56
:50K:/DE89370400440532013000
ACME CORP
:59:/FR1420041010050500013M02606
WIDGETS SARL
:71A:SHA
:72:/EToE/E2E-REF-001
-}') AS m JOIN iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>PACS-MSG-1</MsgId></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-REF-001</EndToEndId><UETR>e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1234.56</IntrBkSttlmAmt></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') AS p USING (end_to_end_id) ORDER BY m.end_to_end_id

vgi.example_queries.description: Status reconciliation: join each pacs.008 credit transfer to the pacs.002 status report on UETR to see which payments settled (ACSC) and which were rejected, with the reason code.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.end_to_end_id, p.creditor_name, p.amount, p.ccy, s.tx_status, s.status_reason_code FROM iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>BATCH-7</MsgId></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-A</EndToEndId><UETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000a</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1500.00</IntrBkSttlmAmt><Cdtr><Nm>WIDGETS SARL</Nm></Cdtr></CdtTrfTxInf><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-B</EndToEndId><UETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000b</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">98000.00</IntrBkSttlmAmt><Cdtr><Nm>GADGETS GMBH</Nm></Cdtr></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') AS p LEFT JOIN iso20022.main.pacs002_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.002.001.10"><FIToFIPmtStsRpt><GrpHdr><MsgId>STS-7</MsgId></GrpHdr><OrgnlGrpInfAndSts><OrgnlMsgId>BATCH-7</OrgnlMsgId></OrgnlGrpInfAndSts><TxInfAndSts><OrgnlUETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000a</OrgnlUETR><TxSts>ACSC</TxSts></TxInfAndSts><TxInfAndSts><OrgnlUETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000b</OrgnlUETR><TxSts>RJCT</TxSts><StsRsnInf><Rsn><Cd>AM04</Cd></Rsn></StsRsnInf></TxInfAndSts></FIToFIPmtStsRpt></Document>') AS s ON s.orig_uetr = p.uetr ORDER BY p.end_to_end_id

:60F:C260101EUR1000,00
:61:2601020102C500,00NTRFNONREF//BANK-A
:61:2601030103D250,50NMSCCUST-REF//BANK-B
:62F:C260103EUR1249,50
-}{1:F01X}{2:O940X}{4:
:20:STMT-2
:25:DE89370400440532013000

:60F:C260103EUR1249,50
:61:2601040104D100,00NMSCREF-2//BANK-C

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## supported_messages

A browsable registry of the message types this worker parses — one row per type with its `family`, `reader_function`, optional `exploder_function`, and a short `description`. Filter it (for example on `exploder_function IS NOT NULL`) to find which messages have an entry/line exploder. Local-only, no network.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT message_type, reader_function, exploder_function FROM iso20022.main.supported_messages WHERE exploder_function IS NOT NULL ORDER BY message_type

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Read pain.001 Credit Initiations

Scan a glob of ISO 20022 pain.001 (CstmrCdtTrfInitn) XML files into one row per CdtTrfTxInf, with the PmtInf debtor block carried down: control sum, requested execution date, debtor/creditor names + IBANs + BICs, amount and currency, end-to-end id, UETR, and remittance info. Use it to ingest outbound payment initiations.

The argument may be the **message text supplied inline** (handy for a single message or an example), a file path, or a glob that scans many files. All reads are local on the worker host — no network, no egress; payment data never leaves the machine. See the result columns for the full schema.

vgi.executable_examples.description: Parse an inline pain.001 customer credit-transfer initiation: read the debtor, instructed amount, and creditor for each CdtTrfTxInf.
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT msg_id, pmt_method, debtor_name, amount, ccy, creditor_name FROM iso20022.main.pain001_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pain.001.001.09"><CstmrCdtTrfInitn><GrpHdr><MsgId>PAIN-1</MsgId><CreDtTm>2026-01-01T09:00:00Z</CreDtTm><CtrlSum>1234.56</CtrlSum><InitgPty><Nm>ACME CORP</Nm></InitgPty></GrpHdr><PmtInf><PmtInfId>PMT-1</PmtInfId><PmtMtd>TRF</PmtMtd><ReqdExctnDt><Dt>2026-01-02</Dt></ReqdExctnDt><Dbtr><Nm>ACME CORP</Nm></Dbtr><DbtrAcct><Id><IBAN>DE89370400440532013000</IBAN></Id></DbtrAcct><DbtrAgt><FinInstnId><BICFI>DEUTDEFF</BICFI></FinInstnId></DbtrAgt><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-REF-001</EndToEndId></PmtId><Amt><InstdAmt Ccy="EUR">1234.56</InstdAmt></Amt><Cdtr><Nm>WIDGETS SARL</Nm></Cdtr><CdtrAcct><Id><IBAN>FR1420041010050500013M02606</IBAN></Id></CdtrAcct><RmtInf><Ustrd>INVOICE 998877</Ustrd></RmtInf></CdtTrfTxInf></PmtInf></CstmrCdtTrfInitn></Document>') WHERE amount > 1000

functions.name: pacs008_read
functions.comment: Read pacs.008 customer credit transfers into rows (one per CdtTrfTxInf).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Scan a glob of ISO 20022 pacs.008 (FIToFICstmrCdtTrf) XML files into one row per CdtTrfTxInf, with debtor/creditor names, IBANs, BICs, the exact settled amount and currency, end-to-end id, UETR, charge bearer, purpose, and remittance info. Use it for payment reconciliation and MT103<->pacs.008 migration-QA joins.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Read pacs.008 Credit Transfers

Scan a glob of ISO 20022 pacs.008 (FIToFICstmrCdtTrf) XML files into one row per CdtTrfTxInf, with debtor/creditor names, IBANs, BICs, the exact settled amount and currency, end-to-end id, UETR, charge bearer, purpose, and remittance info. Use it for payment reconciliation and MT103<->pacs.008 migration-QA joins.

The argument may be the **message text supplied inline** (handy for a single message or an example), a file path, or a glob that scans many files. All reads are local on the worker host — no network, no egress; payment data never leaves the machine. See the result columns for the full schema.

vgi.example_queries.description: Migration QA: pair an MT103 with its pacs.008 twin on end_to_end_id and check that the settled amount, currency, and UETR agree in both formats.
vgi.example_queries.sql:
SELECT m.end_to_end_id, m.ccy, m.amount AS mt_amount, p.amount AS mx_amount, m.amount = p.amount AND m.ccy = p.ccy AS amount_match, m.uetr = p.uetr AS uetr_match FROM iso20022.main.mt103_read('{1:F01ACMEDEFFAXXX0000000000}{2:I103DEUTDEFFXXXXN}{3:{121:e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab}}{4:
:20:TXN-REF-1
:23B:CRED
:32A:260101EUR1234,56
:50K:/DE89370400440532013000
ACME CORP
:59:/FR1420041010050500013M02606
WIDGETS SARL
:71A:SHA
:72:/EToE/E2E-REF-001
-}') AS m JOIN iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>PACS-MSG-1</MsgId></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-REF-001</EndToEndId><UETR>e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1234.56</IntrBkSttlmAmt></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') AS p USING (end_to_end_id) ORDER BY m.end_to_end_id

vgi.example_queries.description: Status reconciliation: join each pacs.008 credit transfer to the pacs.002 status report on UETR to see which payments settled (ACSC) and which were rejected, with the reason code.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.end_to_end_id, p.creditor_name, p.amount, p.ccy, s.tx_status, s.status_reason_code FROM iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>BATCH-7</MsgId></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-A</EndToEndId><UETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000a</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1500.00</IntrBkSttlmAmt><Cdtr><Nm>WIDGETS SARL</Nm></Cdtr></CdtTrfTxInf><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><EndToEndId>E2E-B</EndToEndId><UETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000b</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">98000.00</IntrBkSttlmAmt><Cdtr><Nm>GADGETS GMBH</Nm></Cdtr></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') AS p LEFT JOIN iso20022.main.pacs002_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.002.001.10"><FIToFIPmtStsRpt><GrpHdr><MsgId>STS-7</MsgId></GrpHdr><OrgnlGrpInfAndSts><OrgnlMsgId>BATCH-7</OrgnlMsgId></OrgnlGrpInfAndSts><TxInfAndSts><OrgnlUETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000a</OrgnlUETR><TxSts>ACSC</TxSts></TxInfAndSts><TxInfAndSts><OrgnlUETR>0a1b2c3d-0000-4aaa-8bbb-00000000000b</OrgnlUETR><TxSts>RJCT</TxSts><StsRsnInf><Rsn><Cd>AM04</Cd></Rsn></StsRsnInf></TxInfAndSts></FIToFIPmtStsRpt></Document>') AS s ON s.orig_uetr = p.uetr ORDER BY p.end_to_end_id

vgi.executable_examples.description: Parse an inline pacs.008 FI-to-FI customer credit transfer: read the exact interbank settlement amount, UETR, and parties.
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT msg_id, uetr, ccy, instructed_amount, debtor_name, creditor_name FROM iso20022.main.pacs008_read('<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pacs.008.001.08"><FIToFICstmrCdtTrf><GrpHdr><MsgId>PACS-MSG-1</MsgId><CreDtTm>2026-01-01T10:00:00Z</CreDtTm><NbOfTxs>1</NbOfTxs><SttlmInf><SttlmMtd>INDA</SttlmMtd></SttlmInf></GrpHdr><CdtTrfTxInf><PmtId><InstrId>INSTR-1</InstrId><EndToEndId>E2E-REF-001</EndToEndId><UETR>e3bf1c2a-1111-4aaa-8bbb-1234567890ab</UETR></PmtId><IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="EUR">1234.56</IntrBkSttlmAmt><IntrBkSttlmDt>2026-01-01</IntrBkSttlmDt><ChrgBr>SHAR</ChrgBr><Dbtr><Nm>ACME CORP</Nm></Dbtr><DbtrAcct><Id><IBAN>DE89370400440532013000</IBAN></Id></DbtrAcct><DbtrAgt><FinInstnId><BICFI>DEUTDEFF</BICFI></FinInstnId></DbtrAgt><Cdtr><Nm>WIDGETS SARL</Nm></Cdtr><CdtrAcct><Id><IBAN>FR1420041010050500013M02606</IBAN></Id></CdtrAcct><CdtrAgt><FinInstnId><BICFI>BNPAFRPP</BICFI></FinInstnId></CdtrAgt><Purp><Cd>GDDS</Cd></Purp><RmtInf><Ustrd>INVOICE 998877</Ustrd></RmtInf></CdtTrfTxInf></FIToFICstmrCdtTrf></Document>') WHERE instructed_amount > 1000

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Explode MT940 Statement Lines

Explode the :61: statement lines of one or more MT940 end-of-day statements — each :61: line joined to its following :86: narrative — into one row per line. Pass a relation whose `raw` column (or the column named by `msg :=`) holds each statement: for example the output of `mt940_read('…')`, or any relation exposing a `raw` message column, or an inline statement. Every input column is passed through, repeated once per child line, so lines correlate back to their parent statement. Each output line carries `line_idx`, `value_date` and `entry_date` (`DATE`), the `credit_debit` mark (C/D/RC/RD), positive `amount` `DECIMAL(38,9)`, `transaction_type_id` (e.g. NTRF/NMSC), `customer_ref`/`bank_ref`, the flattened `narrative`, and `narrative_struct` `MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)` for structured `?NN`/`>NN` narratives.

## Calling it

This is a table-in-out function: pass the relation to explode as a subquery, e.g. `mt940_lines((SELECT raw FROM <reader>('…')))`, or feed it any relation that exposes a `raw` message column (rename it with `msg := 'col'`). Every input column is passed through unchanged, repeated once per child row, so results correlate back to the parent.

## Result schema

The passthrough input columns come first, followed by the fixed child columns — their names, types, and meanings are documented in `vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md`, and a runnable call is in `vgi.executable_examples`. Local-only — no network, no egress.

vgi.example_queries.description: Statement roll-forward check: explode each MT940 statement's :61: lines, net credits against debits, and compare opening balance + net movement with the reported closing balance (here STMT-2 is off by 50.50).
vgi.example_queries.sql:
SELECT transaction_ref, opening_balance, sum(CASE WHEN credit_debit IN ('D', 'RC') THEN -amount ELSE amount END) AS net_movement, closing_balance, opening_balance + net_movement = closing_balance AS balanced FROM iso20022.main.mt940_lines((SELECT transaction_ref, opening_balance, closing_balance, raw FROM iso20022.main.mt940_read('{1:F01X}{2:O940X}{4:
:20:STMT-1
:25:DE89370400440532013000
:28C:1/1
:60F:C260101EUR1000,00
:61:2601020102C500,00NTRFNONREF//BANK-A
:61:2601030103D250,50NMSCCUST-REF//BANK-B
:62F:C260103EUR1249,50
-}{1:F01X}{2:O940X}{4:
:20:STMT-2
:25:DE89370400440532013000
:28C:2/1
:60F:C260103EUR1249,50
:61:2601040104D100,00NMSCREF-2//BANK-C
:62F:C260104EUR1200,00
-}'))) GROUP BY transaction_ref, opening_balance, closing_balance ORDER BY transaction_ref

vgi.executable_examples.description: Read an MT940 statement inline, then explode its :61: lines (one row per line, joined to its :86: narrative).
vgi.executable_examples.sql:
SELECT value_date, credit_debit, amount, transaction_type_id FROM iso20022.main.mt940_lines((SELECT raw FROM iso20022.main.mt940_read('{1:F01ACMEDEFFAXXX0000000000}{2:O940DEUTDEFFXXXXN}{4:
:20:STMT-1
:25:DE89370400440532013000
:28C:12345/1
:60F:C260101EUR1000,00
:61:2601020102C500,00NTRFNONREF//BANK-A
:86:GROCERY STORE PAYMENT
:61:2601030103D250,50NMSCCUST-REF//BANK-B
:86:RENT
:62F:C260103EUR1249,50
-}')))

When the input is the output of a `*_read` function (or any relation that exposes a `raw` message column), that `raw` column is passed through too.

| --- | --- | --- |
| raw | VARCHAR | Passthrough: the parent message text carried from the input relation (present whenever the input exposes a `raw` column). |
| line_idx | INTEGER | Ordinal within the statement. |
| value_date | DATE | :61: subfield 1 (YYMMDD). |
| entry_date | DATE | :61: subfield 2 (MMDD; year from value_date). |
| credit_debit | VARCHAR | :61: subfield 3 mark: C/D/RC/RD. |

| customer_ref | VARCHAR | :61: subfield 6 up to //. |
| bank_ref | VARCHAR | :61: subfield 6 after //. |
| supplementary | VARCHAR | :61: subfield 7. |
| narrative | VARCHAR | :86: flattened (continuations joined). |
| narrative_struct | MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR) | :86: structured ?NN/>NN subfields. |

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Scan a glob of SWIFT MT202 / MT202 COV (general financial-institution transfer) text files into one row per message: references, value date, amount and currency, the institution chain, and — for cover messages — the underlying customer block (is_cover, cov_ordering_customer, cov_beneficiary, cov_remittance_info).
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# Read MT202 / MT202 COV FI Transfers

Scan a glob of SWIFT MT202 / MT202 COV (general financial-institution transfer) text files into one row per message: references, value date, amount and currency, the institution chain, and — for cover messages — the underlying customer block (is_cover, cov_ordering_customer, cov_beneficiary, cov_remittance_info).

The argument may be the **message text supplied inline** (handy for a single message or an example), a file path, or a glob that scans many files. All reads are local on the worker host — no network, no egress; payment data never leaves the machine. See the result columns for the full schema.

vgi.executable_examples.description: Parse an inline MT202 (general financial institution transfer / cover) and read its settled amount and beneficiary institution.
vgi.executable_examples.sql:
SELECT transaction_ref, related_ref, ccy, amount, beneficiary_inst FROM iso20022.main.mt202_read('{1:F01ACMEDEFFAXXX0000000000}{2:I202DEUTDEFFXXXXN}{3:{121:11111111-2222-4333-8444-555566667777}}{4:
:20:FI-REF-9
:21:REL-REF-9
:32A:260102USD5000000,00
:52A:CHASUS33
:58A:DEUTDEFF
:50K:/111
UNDERLYING DEBTOR
:59:/222
UNDERLYING CREDITOR
:70:COVER FOR MT103
-}') WHERE amount > 1000000

# Read camt.054 Debit/Credit Notifications

Scan a glob of ISO 20022 camt.054 (BkToCstmrDbtCdtNtfctn) XML files into one row per notification, sharing the camt.053 statement column layout (account, period, balances when present, entry count).
