Each chunk_days (7) of window is one export request; Mixpanel allows 60 per hour.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## events

Raw events from the [Raw Event Export API](https://docs.mixpanel.com/reference/raw-event-export), streamed and resumable.

Arguments: `from_date`, `to_date` ('YYYY-MM-DD'), `where_expr` (a Mixpanel expression), `lookback_days` (7), `chunk_days` (7).

**Pushdown:** `event_time` ranges choose the export `from_date`/`to_date` (±1 day for legacy project-time-zone projects); `event_name =`/`IN` becomes the `event` array; string `=`/`IN` on the property-backed columns becomes a `where` expression. Everything is re-applied exactly.

vgi.example_queries.description: Sign-ups per operating system over three days (event name and dates are sent to Mixpanel)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT os, count(*) AS signups FROM mixpanel.main.events() WHERE event_name = 'Sign Up' AND event_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01' AND event_time < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-04' GROUP BY os ORDER BY signups DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Revenue per user from Purchase events
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT distinct_id, count(*) AS purchases, sum((properties->>'revenue')::DOUBLE) AS revenue FROM mixpanel.main.events(from_date := '2026-11-01', to_date := '2026-11-03') WHERE event_name = 'Purchase' GROUP BY distinct_id ORDER BY revenue DESC

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## unified

Events, users, cohorts and data-dictionary definitions with the column names shared by the Query.Farm product-analytics workers (Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog), so the same query runs against each.

Columns a tool cannot fill are NULL rather than missing: Mixpanel has no event uuid (the `$insert_id` is used), no user properties on raw events and no cohort definitions in its cohort list.

Use the `main` schema for every Mixpanel field, the reports and the cohort member lists.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT platform, count(DISTINCT distinct_id) AS users FROM mixpanel.unified.events WHERE event_time >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01' AND event_time < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-04' GROUP BY platform ORDER BY users DESC

workers.summary: Read-only Major League Baseball standings and player statistics from MLB's Stats API
workers.doc_md:
# MLB standings and player statistics

Query current and historical Major League Baseball data directly from SQL. The catalog contains team standings and complete batting, pitching, and fielding season lines, plus advanced metrics, career totals, team splits, and per-game logs.

## Data model

Current tables are the quickest entry point. Parameterized functions select seasons, leagues, game types, qualified pools, or individual players. Multi-team season totals never claim to belong to one club: use the team-split functions when attribution matters.

All access is read-only and requires no credential. Rate statistics are exact decimals; baseball innings remain display strings alongside exact integer outs.

## Sources and references

* [MLB Stats API](https://statsapi.mlb.com/): the keyless MLB Advanced Media API every function calls.
* [MLB.com Stats](https://www.mlb.com/stats): the official leaderboards the qualified pools mirror.
* [MLB data copyright notice](https://gdx.mlb.com/components/copyright.txt): the terms that apply to Stats API data.
* [MLB-StatsAPI wiki](https://github.com/toddrob99/MLB-StatsAPI/wiki): a community reference for the Stats API's endpoints and parameters.

example_queries.title: current_standings_are_populated
example_queries.description: MLB regular-season standings contain team rows.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) > 0 AS populated FROM mlb.main.current_standings;

example_queries.title: current_batting_has_players
example_queries.description: The complete current batting pool has stable player identifiers.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) > 0 AND count(player_id) = count(*) AS populated FROM mlb.main.current_batting;

example_queries.title: baseball_innings_are_exact
example_queries.description: Every displayed pitching inning count agrees with the exact outs count.
example_queries.sql: SELECT bool_and(outs >= 0) AS valid_outs FROM mlb.main.current_pitching WHERE innings_pitched IS NOT NULL;

example_queries.description: Current division tables in official rank order.
example_queries.sql: SELECT division_name, division_rank, team_name, wins, losses, games_back FROM mlb.main.current_standings ORDER BY division_name, division_rank

example_queries.description: Teams with the best run differential.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, wins, losses, run_differential FROM mlb.main.current_standings ORDER BY run_differential DESC

example_queries.description: Each 2025 division winner's lowest-ERA qualified pitcher, joining standings() to pitching_stats() on team_id (pitchers traded mid-season have no team_id and are excluded).
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.division_name, s.team_name, s.wins, p.player_name, p.innings_pitched, p.strikeouts, p.era FROM mlb.main.standings(season := 2025) s JOIN mlb.main.pitching_stats(season := 2025, qualified_only := true) p ON p.team_id = s.team_id WHERE s.division_rank = 1 QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.team_id ORDER BY p.era, p.player_id) = 1 ORDER BY s.division_name

example_queries.description: 2025 hitters with at least 50 plate appearances who also pitched, joining batting_stats() to pitching_stats() on player_id; mostly position players in mop-up relief, led by two-way Shohei Ohtani.
example_queries.sql: SELECT b.player_name, b.position_abbreviation, b.plate_appearances, b.ops, p.games_pitched, p.innings_pitched, p.era FROM mlb.main.batting_stats(season := 2025) b JOIN mlb.main.pitching_stats(season := 2025) p USING (player_id) WHERE b.plate_appearances >= 50 ORDER BY p.games_pitched DESC, b.player_name LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: 2025 shortstops with at least 2,400 defensive outs (800 innings) at the position, ranked by OPS alongside their errors and fielding percentage there.
example_queries.sql: SELECT f.player_name, f.last_team_abbreviation, f.outs, f.errors, f.fielding_percentage, b.plate_appearances, b.ops FROM mlb.main.fielding_stats(season := 2025) f JOIN mlb.main.batting_stats(season := 2025) b USING (player_id) WHERE f.position_abbreviation = 'SS' AND f.outs >= 2400 ORDER BY b.ops DESC, f.player_id LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Shohei Ohtani's 2025 batting split by whether the opponent finished at .500 or better, joining his batting_game_log() to the final standings() on opponent_id.
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.winning_percentage >= 0.500 AS opponent_500_or_better, count(*) AS games, sum(g.at_bats) AS at_bats, sum(g.hits) AS hits, sum(g.home_runs) AS home_runs, round(sum(g.hits) / sum(g.at_bats), 3) AS batting_average FROM mlb.main.batting_game_log(660271, season := 2025) g JOIN mlb.main.standings(season := 2025) s ON s.team_id = g.opponent_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY opponent_500_or_better

example_queries.description: Current shortstops with substantial defensive playing time.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, last_team_abbreviation, outs, errors, fielding_percentage FROM mlb.main.current_fielding WHERE position_abbreviation = 'SS' AND outs >= 600 ORDER BY fielding_percentage DESC

example_queries.description: Current MLB home-run leaders.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, last_team_abbreviation, home_runs, ops FROM mlb.main.current_batting ORDER BY home_runs DESC LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: Current ERA leaders among pitchers with at least 300 outs.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, last_team_abbreviation, innings_pitched, strikeouts, era FROM mlb.main.current_pitching WHERE outs >= 300 ORDER BY era LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: Josh Naylor's 2025 batting totals separated by team.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, games_played, hits, home_runs, ops FROM mlb.main.batting_team_splits(647304, 2025) ORDER BY team_name

example_queries.description: Shohei Ohtani's regular-season career batting totals.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, games_played, hits, home_runs, batting_average, ops FROM mlb.main.batting_career(660271)

example_queries.description: Read the table's backing scan directly.
example_queries.sql: SELECT division_name, team_name, wins, losses FROM mlb.main.all_current_standings() WHERE division_rank = 1 ORDER BY division_name

example_queries.description: Qualified 2025 MLB OPS leaders.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, last_team_abbreviation, home_runs, ops FROM mlb.main.batting_stats(season := 2025, qualified_only := true) ORDER BY ops DESC LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: Current shortstop fielding lines from the backing scan.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, outs, errors FROM mlb.main.all_current_fielding() WHERE position_abbreviation = 'SS' ORDER BY outs DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: The 2025 final division standings.
example_queries.sql: SELECT division_name, division_rank, team_name, wins, losses FROM mlb.main.standings(season := 2025) ORDER BY division_name, division_rank

example_queries.description: The current American League wild-card race.
example_queries.sql: SELECT wild_card_rank, team_name, wild_card_games_back FROM mlb.main.standings(league := 'AL', standings_type := 'wildCard') ORDER BY wild_card_rank

example_queries.description: Shohei Ohtani's 2025 pitching game log.
example_queries.sql: SELECT game_date, opponent_abbreviation, innings_pitched, strikeouts, summary FROM mlb.main.pitching_game_log(660271, season := 2025) ORDER BY game_date

example_queries.description: Shohei Ohtani's regular-season career pitching totals.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, games_started, innings_pitched, strikeouts, era, whip FROM mlb.main.pitching_career(660271)

example_queries.description: Current strikeout leaders from the backing scan.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, strikeouts FROM mlb.main.all_current_pitching() ORDER BY strikeouts DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Qualified 2025 isolated-power leaders.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, plate_appearances, isolated_power, strikeouts_per_plate_appearance FROM mlb.main.advanced_batting_stats(season := 2025, qualified_only := true) ORDER BY isolated_power DESC LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: Current home-run leaders from the backing scan.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, home_runs FROM mlb.main.all_current_batting() ORDER BY home_runs DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: 2025 shortstops with at least 900 defensive outs.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, last_team_abbreviation, outs, errors, fielding_percentage FROM mlb.main.fielding_stats(season := 2025) WHERE position_abbreviation = 'SS' AND outs >= 900 ORDER BY fielding_percentage DESC

example_queries.description: Jhoan Duran's 2025 pitching totals separated by team.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, games_pitched, innings_pitched, strikeouts, era FROM mlb.main.pitching_team_splits(661395, 2025) ORDER BY team_name

example_queries.description: Shohei Ohtani's June 2025 batting game log.
example_queries.sql: SELECT game_date, opponent_abbreviation, summary FROM mlb.main.batting_game_log(660271, season := 2025, start_date := DATE '2025-06-01', end_date := DATE '2025-06-30') ORDER BY game_date

example_queries.description: Qualified 2025 pitchers by K-minus-BB percentage.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, strikeouts_minus_walks_percentage, whiff_percentage FROM mlb.main.advanced_pitching_stats(season := 2025, qualified_only := true) ORDER BY strikeouts_minus_walks_percentage DESC LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: Qualified 2025 pitchers ordered by ERA.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, last_team_abbreviation, innings_pitched, strikeouts, era FROM mlb.main.pitching_stats(season := 2025, qualified_only := true) ORDER BY era LIMIT 20

functions.name: standings
functions.comment: MLB standings by season, league, and standings view

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per MLB team with rankings, wins and losses, games back, run differential, streak, home/away and last-ten records, and clinching state. Use season for historical standings, league => 'AL' or 'NL' to narrow, and standings_type => 'wildCard' for the wild-card race. With no arguments it returns the current regular-season standings for both leagues.
tags.vgi.doc_md: MLB standings flattened to one row per team. All arguments are named and optional. `games_back` is numeric for sorting and arithmetic; the original MLB marker remains in `games_back_display`. The same applies to wild-card games back. Percentages use exact `DECIMAL` values rather than binary floats.

vgi.example_queries.description: The 2025 final division standings.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT division_name, division_rank, team_name, wins, losses FROM mlb.main.standings(season := 2025) ORDER BY division_name, division_rank

vgi.example_queries.description: The current American League wild-card race.

vgi.example_queries.description: Each 2025 division winner's lowest-ERA qualified pitcher, joining standings() to pitching_stats() on team_id (pitchers traded mid-season have no team_id and are excluded).

functions.name: fielding_stats
functions.comment: MLB player fielding statistics by season, league, and game type

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Season fielding lines at player-position grain, including defensive innings, putouts, assists, errors, chances, double plays, fielding percentage and range factors. A player can have several rows when he appeared at several positions.
tags.vgi.doc_md: One row per player and position. `innings` preserves baseball notation; use the derived integer `outs` for exact defensive-inning arithmetic.

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 shortstops with at least 900 defensive outs.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, last_team_abbreviation, outs, errors, fielding_percentage FROM mlb.main.fielding_stats(season := 2025) WHERE position_abbreviation = 'SS' AND outs >= 900 ORDER BY fielding_percentage DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 shortstops with at least 2,400 defensive outs (800 innings) at the position, ranked by OPS alongside their errors and fielding percentage there.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT f.player_name, f.last_team_abbreviation, f.outs, f.errors, f.fielding_percentage, b.plate_appearances, b.ops FROM mlb.main.fielding_stats(season := 2025) f JOIN mlb.main.batting_stats(season := 2025) b USING (player_id) WHERE f.position_abbreviation = 'SS' AND f.outs >= 2400 ORDER BY b.ops DESC, f.player_id LIMIT 10

functions.name: batting_game_log
functions.comment: Per-game batting lines for one MLB player

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One batting line per game for a player, optionally bounded to an inclusive date range.
tags.vgi.doc_md: One batting line per game for a player, optionally bounded to an inclusive date range.

vgi.example_queries.description: Shohei Ohtani's June 2025 batting game log.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT game_date, opponent_abbreviation, summary FROM mlb.main.batting_game_log(660271, season := 2025, start_date := DATE '2025-06-01', end_date := DATE '2025-06-30') ORDER BY game_date

vgi.example_queries.description: Shohei Ohtani's 2025 batting split by whether the opponent finished at .500 or better, joining his batting_game_log() to the final standings() on opponent_id.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT s.winning_percentage >= 0.500 AS opponent_500_or_better, count(*) AS games, sum(g.at_bats) AS at_bats, sum(g.hits) AS hits, sum(g.home_runs) AS home_runs, round(sum(g.hits) / sum(g.at_bats), 3) AS batting_average FROM mlb.main.batting_game_log(660271, season := 2025) g JOIN mlb.main.standings(season := 2025) s ON s.team_id = g.opponent_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY opponent_500_or_better

functions.comment: MLB player pitching statistics by season and league

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Season pitching lines at player grain: appearances, starts, wins, saves, innings, outs, strikeouts, walks, ERA, WHIP, opponent slash line, K/BB and per-nine rates. Defaults to all players in MLB's current season. Set qualified_only => true for qualified leaders, or pass a season and AL/NL league. Use outs—not the display innings_pitched string—for exact innings arithmetic.
tags.vgi.doc_md: One aggregate season pitching line per player. `innings_pitched` preserves baseball notation, where .1 and .2 mean one and two outs; divide `outs` by three for arithmetic. Rate statistics are exact `DECIMAL` columns.

workers.title: Mapbox Vector Tile Reader
workers.tagline: Read & write Mapbox Vector Tiles, PMTiles & MBTiles as tables with geometry in DuckDB (Python)
workers.subtitle: Decode PMTiles, MBTiles, XYZ and .mvt vector tiles into DuckDB rows with GEOMETRY columns.
workers.summary: Decodes Mapbox Vector Tiles from PMTiles and MBTiles files, XYZ tile servers, single tiles and tile blobs into DuckDB rows with GEOMETRY and attribute columns, and writes query results back out as PMTiles vector tilesets.
workers.doc_md:
# Read Mapbox Vector Tiles in DuckDB

**Turn vector tiles back into data.** Decode Mapbox Vector Tiles into rows with a DuckDB `GEOMETRY` column and the features' attributes, from PMTiles (file or URL), MBTiles, `{z}/{x}/{y}` tile servers, single `.mvt` / `.pbf` tiles or tile blobs in a query.

Coordinates come back as WGS84 longitude/latitude by default; Web Mercator metres and raw tile pixels are available too. Vector tiles are a lossy, display-oriented format: coordinates snap to a grid of usually 4096 per tile, and features are clipped at tile edges and simplified at low zoom, so read the highest zoom for the most faithful geometry.

## Sources and references

- [Mapbox Vector Tile specification](https://github.com/mapbox/vector-tile-spec): the protobuf tile encoding every decoder here reads.
- [PMTiles v3 specification](https://github.com/protomaps/PMTiles/blob/main/spec/v3/spec.md) ([Protomaps docs](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/)): the single-file archive format read over HTTP range requests and written by COPY TO.
- [MBTiles specification](https://github.com/mapbox/mbtiles-spec): the SQLite tileset container, including its TMS row order.

attach_options.name: tileset
attach_options.description: PMTiles file or http(s) URL, or local MBTiles file, to expose as tables (one per layer). Empty attaches only the reader functions.

attach_options.name: zoom
attach_options.description: Zoom level the layer tables read; -1 (default) uses the tileset's maxzoom.

attach_options.name: bbox
attach_options.description: Limit every layer table to the tiles covering 'west,south,east,north' (degrees); empty reads all.

attach_options.name: coordinates
attach_options.description: Geometry coordinates of the layer tables: 'wgs84' (default), 'web_mercator' or 'tile'.

attach_options.name: max_tiles
attach_options.description: A layer table scan fails rather than read more than this many tiles.

attach_options.name: tile_edges
attach_options.description: Features reaching a tile edge: 'merge' (default, one row per feature), 'clip' (one non-overlapping piece per tile) or 'raw' (as stored, tile buffers included).

example_queries.description: Features per layer of the fixture tileset: one row each, joined across tile edges
example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, geometry_type, count(*) AS features, round(sum(ST_Area(geometry)), 1) AS area FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/edges.pmtiles', zoom := 3) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: Tag each city with the region polygon that contains it (NULL when none): a spatial join of two layers
example_queries.sql: SELECT c.name AS city, r.label AS region FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'cities') AS c LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'regions') AS r ON ST_Within(c.geometry, r.geometry) ORDER BY city

example_queries.description: A spatial filter on the geometry also chooses which tiles are read
example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, count(*) AS features FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, ST_MakeEnvelope(8, 44, 18, 54)) GROUP BY layer ORDER BY layer

example_queries.description: Road kinds in the Protomaps Florence sample, read over HTTP range requests
example_queries.sql: SELECT properties->>'pmap:kind' AS kind, count(*) AS n FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protomaps/PMTiles/main/spec/v3/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles', zoom := 14) WHERE layer = 'roads' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

example_queries.description: US ZIP code areas touching a Manhattan bbox, from a remote PMTiles archive
example_queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT ZCTA5CE10 AS zip FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://r2-public.protomaps.com/protomaps-sample-datasets/cb_2018_us_zcta510_500k.pmtiles', zoom := 7, layer := 'zcta', west := -74.02, south := 40.70, east := -73.93, north := 40.80) WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, ST_MakeEnvelope(-74.02, 40.70, -73.93, 40.80)) ORDER BY zip

example_queries.description: Cities from one tile with their attributes as typed columns
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, geometry FROM mvt.main.read_mvt('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/0-0-0.mvt', 0, 0, 0, layer := 'cities') ORDER BY population DESC

example_queries.description: Feature counts per layer of a Mapbox Streets sample tile
example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, count(*) AS features FROM mvt.main.read_mvt('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mapbox/vector-tile-js/main/test/fixtures/14-8801-5371.vector.pbf', 14, 8801, 5371) GROUP BY layer ORDER BY features DESC

example_queries.description: Decode XYZ tile files fetched with read_blob, taking each tile's z/x/y from its URL path
example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, z, count(*) AS n FROM mvt.main.mvt_decode((SELECT content AS tile, p[-3]::INTEGER AS z, p[-2]::INTEGER AS x, split_part(p[-1], '.', 1)::INTEGER AS y FROM (SELECT content, string_split(filename, '/') AS p FROM read_blob(['https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/xyz/0/0/0.mvt', 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/xyz/1/0/0.mvt', 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/xyz/1/1/0.mvt'])))) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: Attribute names of each layer of the fixture PMTiles archive
example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, list(field ORDER BY field) AS attributes FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') GROUP BY layer ORDER BY layer

example_queries.description: Check each declared attribute against the decoded features: how many of its layer's features carry it
example_queries.sql: SELECT l.layer, l.field, count(*) AS features, count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.properties ->> l.field IS NOT NULL) AS with_field FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') AS l JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') AS t USING (layer) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: How many attributes each layer of a remote PMTiles basemap declares
example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, count(field) AS attributes FROM mvt.main.tileset_layers('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protomaps/PMTiles/main/spec/v3/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles') GROUP BY layer ORDER BY layer

example_queries.description: Name and bounds of the fixture PMTiles archive
example_queries.sql: SELECT key, value FROM mvt.main.tileset_metadata('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE key IN ('name', 'bounds') ORDER BY key

example_queries.description: Compare each layer's feature count in the tilestats metadata with the features read_tiles decodes at max zoom
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.layer, s.count AS declared, count(t.layer) AS decoded FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json(value -> 'layers', '[{"layer": "VARCHAR", "count": "BIGINT"}]'), recursive := true) FROM mvt.main.tileset_metadata('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE key = 'tilestats') AS s LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') AS t USING (layer) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: Max zoom of a remote PMTiles archive (reads only its header)
example_queries.sql: SELECT value FROM mvt.main.tileset_metadata('https://r2-public.protomaps.com/protomaps-sample-datasets/cb_2018_us_zcta510_500k.pmtiles') WHERE key = 'maxzoom'

example_queries.description: Write two cities as a one-layer tileset (zoom 0 to 8)
example_queries.sql: COPY (SELECT 'cities' AS layer, name, population, ST_Point(lon, lat) AS geometry FROM (VALUES ('Rome', 2800000, 12.5, 41.9), ('Paris', 2100000, 2.35, 48.86)) t(name, population, lon, lat)) TO 'cities.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 8)

example_queries.description: Re-tile every layer of an existing tileset into a new archive
example_queries.sql: COPY (SELECT layer, feature_id, properties, geometry FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles')) TO 'sample-copy.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 4, name 'sample copy')

example_queries.description: Format and zoom range of the fixture PMTiles archive
example_queries.sql: SELECT key, value FROM mvt.main.tileset_metadata('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE key IN ('format', 'minzoom', 'maxzoom') ORDER BY key;

example_queries.description: Decode a hand-made tile holding one point at the centre of tile 0/0/0

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Vector tile readers. Every feature-reading function returns the same leading columns: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry (`GEOMETRY`), properties (`JSON`). Tile addresses use the XYZ scheme (row 0 at the north); MBTiles stores TMS rows and is flipped for you. Whole tilesets are read one zoom at a time, limited by an optional WGS84 bbox (west, south, east, north) that selects tiles, not features: filter features afterwards with `ST_Intersects`. A `max_tiles` guard (default 10000) stops accidental planet-sized reads. Use DuckDB spatial (ST_*) on the geometry column; old (MVT v1) tilesets can contain self-intersecting polygons, which `ST_MakeValid` repairs.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Read vector tiles as tables: whole tilesets at one zoom, single tiles, or tile blobs already in DuckDB, plus the layer and metadata catalogues that describe a tileset.

Feature rows always carry `layer`, `z`, `x`, `y`, `feature_id`, `geometry_type`, `geometry` and `properties`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Features per layer of the fixture tileset: one row each, joined across tile edges
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, geometry_type, count(*) AS features, round(sum(ST_Area(geometry)), 1) AS area FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/edges.pmtiles', zoom := 3) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

vgi.example_queries.description: Tag each city with the region polygon that contains it (NULL when none): a spatial join of two layers
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT c.name AS city, r.label AS region FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'cities') AS c LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'regions') AS r ON ST_Within(c.geometry, r.geometry) ORDER BY city

vgi.example_queries.description: A spatial filter on the geometry also chooses which tiles are read
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT layer, count(*) AS features FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, ST_MakeEnvelope(8, 44, 18, 54)) GROUP BY layer ORDER BY layer

vgi.example_queries.description: Road kinds in the Protomaps Florence sample, read over HTTP range requests
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT properties->>'pmap:kind' AS kind, count(*) AS n FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/protomaps/PMTiles/main/spec/v3/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles', zoom := 14) WHERE layer = 'roads' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: US ZIP code areas touching a Manhattan bbox, from a remote PMTiles archive

vgi.example_queries.description: Cities from one tile with their attributes as typed columns
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, geometry FROM mvt.main.read_mvt('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/0-0-0.mvt', 0, 0, 0, layer := 'cities') ORDER BY population DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Feature counts per layer of a Mapbox Streets sample tile

vgi.example_queries.description: Decode XYZ tile files fetched with read_blob, taking each tile's z/x/y from its URL path

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT s.layer, s.count AS declared, count(t.layer) AS decoded FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json(value -> 'layers', '[{"layer": "VARCHAR", "count": "BIGINT"}]'), recursive := true) FROM mvt.main.tileset_metadata('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') WHERE key = 'tilestats') AS s LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles') AS t USING (layer) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY ALL

vgi.example_queries.sql: COPY (SELECT 'cities' AS layer, name, population, ST_Point(lon, lat) AS geometry FROM (VALUES ('Rome', 2800000, 12.5, 41.9), ('Paris', 2100000, 2.35, 48.86)) t(name, population, lon, lat)) TO 'cities.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 8)

functions.comment: Decode vector tile BLOBs from a query (tile, z, x, y) into one row per feature

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Table in-out function: pass a subquery whose rows hold vector tiles and get one row per feature back. The input needs a `BLOB` column `tile` (or `tile_data`; gzip is detected) and whole-number columns `z`, `x`, `y` in the XYZ scheme (row 0 at the north). MBTiles rows are TMS: convert with `(1 << zoom_level) - 1 - tile_row AS y`. Named arguments `layer` and `coordinates` work as in `read_tiles`. Output columns: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry (GEOMETRY), properties (JSON). Use `read_tiles` instead when the tileset is a file or URL.

functions.name: read_tiles
functions.comment: Read the features of a PMTiles, MBTiles or XYZ vector tileset as rows with a GEOMETRY column

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a Mapbox Vector Tile tileset back into rows, one per feature. `source` is a PMTiles archive (local path or http(s) URL, read with range requests), a local MBTiles file, or a tile URL template with `{z}/{x}/{y}`. Named arguments: `zoom` (defaults to the tileset maxzoom), `layer` (read one layer and add a typed column per attribute), `west`/`south`/`east`/`north` (WGS84 bbox; all four or none; required for URL templates), `coordinates` ('wgs84' default, 'web_mercator' or 'tile') and `max_tiles` (default 10000; the call fails rather than read more). A constant `WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, <geometry>)` (or ST_Within/ST_Contains/...) also narrows the tiles read, so it can replace the bbox arguments. Columns: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry (GEOMETRY), properties (JSON) and, with `layer`, one typed column per layer attribute. `tile_edges` ('merge' default, 'clip', 'raw') controls features that cross tile edges: 'merge' returns one row per feature, joining the per-tile pieces that share a feature_id (features without an id may come back as several non-overlapping pieces); 'raw' returns each tile's copy, buffer included. A feature extending past the tiles read is cut at their edge. Use `tileset_layers` first to discover layer and attribute names.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## read_tiles(source, zoom := maxzoom, layer := NULL, west/south/east/north := NULL, coordinates := 'wgs84', max_tiles := 10000, tile_edges := 'merge')

One row per vector-tile feature, with a `GEOMETRY` column and a JSON `properties` column. Sources: PMTiles (file or URL), MBTiles (file) or an `{z}/{x}/{y}` URL template.

Pass `layer` to also get each attribute of that layer as its own typed column. Features crossing tile edges come back once (`tile_edges := 'merge'`); use `'raw'` for each tile's stored copy.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT c.name AS city, r.label AS region FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'cities') AS c LEFT JOIN mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles', layer := 'regions') AS r ON ST_Within(c.geometry, r.geometry) ORDER BY city

functions.name: read_mvt
functions.comment: Read the features of one Mapbox Vector Tile (.mvt/.pbf) at a given z/x/y

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a single Mapbox Vector Tile file or URL into rows, one per feature. A tile stores coordinates relative to its own corner, so you must pass its zoom `z`, column `x` and row `y` (XYZ scheme, row 0 at the north) to get real coordinates back. Named arguments: `layer` (one layer, plus a typed column per attribute inferred from the tile) and `coordinates` ('wgs84', 'web_mercator' or 'tile'). Columns match `read_tiles`: layer, z, x, y, feature_id, geometry_type, geometry, properties.

functions.name: write_pmtiles
functions.comment: COPY ... TO format that encodes rows with a GEOMETRY column as a PMTiles vector tileset

tags.vgi.doc_llm: A COPY TO format, not a table function: use it as FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles' in a COPY ... TO statement whose destination is a local .pmtiles path. Each row is a feature. The `GEOMETRY` column must be WGS84 lon/lat (or EPSG:3857). A `VARCHAR` column named `layer` (or `layer_column`) names each row's layer, so one COPY can write several layers via UNION ALL; without it every row goes to `layer` (default: the file name). A column named `feature_id` (or `id_column`) becomes the feature id, and a column named `properties` holding JSON objects is expanded into attributes, so read_tiles output can be written back. Every other column becomes an attribute (`VARCHAR`, numbers, `BOOLEAN`; dates as ISO text; lists and structs as JSON text); NULLs are omitted. Options: minzoom/maxzoom (default 0/14); minzoom_column/maxzoom_column for per-feature zoom ranges; simplify and buffer (pixels of a 256-pixel tile); extent (4096); max_tile_bytes (500000: fails rather than dropping features); max_tiles; name, description, attribution. ORDER BY sets drawing order. COPY reports the number of rows written.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## COPY ... TO (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles')

Encode a query's rows as Mapbox Vector Tiles in a PMTiles archive. One row is one feature; a `layer` column puts rows in different layers of the same tiles, so a single COPY of a `UNION ALL` writes a whole multi-layer basemap.

vgi.example_queries.description: Write two cities as a one-layer tileset (zoom 0 to 8)
vgi.example_queries.sql: COPY (SELECT 'cities' AS layer, name, population, ST_Point(lon, lat) AS geometry FROM (VALUES ('Rome', 2800000, 12.5, 41.9), ('Paris', 2100000, 2.35, 48.86)) t(name, population, lon, lat)) TO 'cities.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 8)

vgi.example_queries.description: Re-tile every layer of an existing tileset into a new archive
vgi.example_queries.sql: COPY (SELECT layer, feature_id, properties, geometry FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Query-farm/vgi-mvt/v0.3.1/test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles')) TO 'sample-copy.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 4, name 'sample copy')

workers.doc_md:
# Nango

Query a [Nango](https://nango.dev) environment from DuckDB, read-only: the provider catalog, integrations, connections (credential type and expiry, never tokens), syncs, actions, sync status, synced records, and any of the 400+ APIs Nango brokers through its proxy.

Create a `nango` secret with your environment `SECRET_KEY` (and `HOST` for a self-hosted Nango). Filters push down into Nango's own parameters (`modified_after`, `filter`, `ids`, connection tags), pagination cursors travel with the scan, and HTTP 429 is retried after `Retry-After`.

### Sources and references

- [Nango API reference](https://nango.dev/docs/reference/backend/http-api/authentication) and its [OpenAPI spec](https://github.com/NangoHQ/nango/blob/master/docs/spec.yaml)
- [Records API](https://nango.dev/docs/reference/api/records/get) — cursor paging, `modified_after`, `filter`
- [Proxy](https://nango.dev/docs/guides/proxy-requests) and its pagination config
- [Self-hosting Nango](https://nango.dev/docs/guides/self-hosting/free-self-hosting/overview)

example_queries.title: connections_columns
example_queries.description: The connections() result columns (binds only; create a nango secret and drop LIMIT 0 for rows)
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, provider_config_key, has_auth_error, credential_expires_at FROM nango.main.connections() LIMIT 0;

example_queries.title: proxy_columns
example_queries.description: The proxy() result columns (binds only; create a nango secret and drop LIMIT 0 for rows)
example_queries.sql: SELECT page, item_index, http_status, item FROM nango.main.proxy('conn-1', 'github', '/user') LIMIT 0;

example_queries.description: Connections and broken (auth-error) connections per integration
example_queries.sql: SELECT provider_config_key, count(*) AS connections, count(*) FILTER (WHERE has_auth_error) AS broken FROM nango.main.connections() GROUP BY provider_config_key ORDER BY connections DESC

example_queries.description: One organization's connections and when their tokens expire
example_queries.sql: SELECT connection_id, provider, credential_type, credential_expires_at FROM nango.main.connections() WHERE organization_id = 'org_acme' ORDER BY credential_expires_at

example_queries.description: Open GitHub issues a Nango sync stored (typed model columns such as state are also available)
example_queries.sql: SELECT _record->>'title' AS title, _nango_last_modified_at FROM nango.main.records('github-prod', 'conn-ada-github', 'GithubIssue') WHERE _nango_deleted_at IS NULL AND _record->>'state' = 'open' ORDER BY title

example_queries.description: Incremental read: records changed since a timestamp (pushed down as modified_after)
example_queries.sql: SELECT id, _nango_last_action FROM nango.main.records('github-prod', 'conn-ada-github', 'GithubIssue') WHERE _nango_last_modified_at > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00' ORDER BY id

example_queries.description: Every GitHub repository the connection can see, following Link-header pages
example_queries.sql: SELECT item->>'full_name' AS repo FROM nango.main.proxy('conn-ada-github', 'github-prod', '/user/repos', paginate := 'provider', params := '{"per_page": 50}') ORDER BY repo

example_queries.description: HubSpot contacts through the proxy with the provider's cursor pagination
example_queries.sql: SELECT item->>'id' AS id, item->'properties'->>'email' AS email FROM nango.main.proxy('conn-acme-hubspot', 'hubspot', '/crm/v3/objects/contacts', paginate := 'provider') ORDER BY id

example_queries.description: How many catalog providers use each auth mode
example_queries.sql: SELECT auth_mode, count(*) AS providers FROM nango.main.providers GROUP BY auth_mode ORDER BY providers DESC

example_queries.description: CRM providers Nango supports
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, display_name, auth_mode FROM nango.main.providers WHERE list_contains(categories, 'crm') ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Integrations whose developer-app credentials are incomplete
example_queries.sql: SELECT unique_key, provider, missing_fields FROM nango.main.integrations WHERE NOT is_configured ORDER BY unique_key

example_queries.description: Each integration with its provider's auth mode
example_queries.sql: SELECT i.unique_key, p.auth_mode FROM nango.main.integrations i JOIN nango.main.providers p ON p.name = i.provider ORDER BY i.unique_key

example_queries.description: Enabled syncs and the models they produce
example_queries.sql: SELECT provider_config_key, name, models, runs FROM nango.main.syncs WHERE enabled ORDER BY provider_config_key, name

example_queries.description: Every (integration, model) pair records() can read
example_queries.sql: SELECT provider_config_key, unnest(models) AS model FROM nango.main.syncs ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: The account's environments
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, is_production FROM nango.main.environments ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Environment variables defined without a value
example_queries.sql: SELECT name FROM nango.main.environment_variables WHERE NOT is_set ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Failing syncs
example_queries.sql: SELECT provider_config_key, connection_id, sync_name, finished_at FROM nango.main.connection_syncs WHERE status = 'ERROR' ORDER BY ALL

example_queries.description: Records stored per sync for one integration
example_queries.sql: SELECT sync_name, sum(total_records) AS records FROM nango.main.connection_syncs WHERE provider_config_key = 'github-prod' GROUP BY sync_name ORDER BY records DESC

example_queries.description: Deployed actions per integration
example_queries.sql: SELECT provider_config_key, name, description FROM nango.main.actions ORDER BY provider_config_key, name

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Nango objects as SQL. Parameterless listings of the environment's setup are plain tables; anything that needs arguments is a table function: connections filtered by tags, the records a sync stored (by integration, connection id and model, typed from the model's JSON Schema), and proxy(connection_id, provider_config_key, path, …), which calls the upstream API through Nango with GET/HEAD only. The integration key is the same value everywhere (integration = provider_config_key = the integration's unique_key), so tables join on it. All objects need a `nango` secret.

functions.name: proxy
functions.comment: Read any API Nango brokers through the Nango proxy (GET/HEAD only) with Nango-managed credentials

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Call any of the 400+ APIs Nango supports with the connection's Nango-managed, auto-refreshed credential: proxy(connection_id, provider_config_key, path, method := 'GET', params := NULL, headers := NULL, response_path := NULL, paginate := NULL, max_pages := 100). `path` is relative to the provider's API base URL (see providers.proxy_base_url), e.g. '/user/repos' for GitHub. Each row is one element of the JSON array at response_path (e.g. 'results' or 'data.items'; JSON pointer '/data/items' also works), or the whole body when it is an object, as `item` JSON — extract fields with item->>'name'. params/headers are JSON objects. paginate: NULL reads one page; 'provider' uses the provider's default (providers.proxy_paginate); or pass Nango's config, e.g. '{"type":"cursor","cursor_path_in_response":"paging.next.after","cursor_name_in_request":"after","limit_name_in_request":"limit","limit":100,"response_path":"results"}', '{"type":"link"}' (Link header rel=next) or '{"type":"offset","offset_name_in_request":"start","limit":100,"limit_name_in_request":"limit"}'. Only GET and HEAD are allowed (read-only). HTTP 429 from Nango or the upstream API is retried after Retry-After.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## proxy(connection_id, provider_config_key, path, method := 'GET', params := NULL, headers := NULL, response_path := NULL, paginate := NULL, max_pages := 100)

Read-only calls through the Nango proxy. Columns: `page`, `item_index`, `http_status`, `item` (JSON).

- **Read-only:** `method` accepts GET and HEAD only; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE are rejected.
- **Pagination** mirrors Nango's proxy paginate config: `cursor` (cursor_path_in_response → cursor_name_in_request), `link` (Link header rel or link_path_in_response_body; absolute links must stay on the provider's base URL), `offset` (offset_name_in_request, per-page or by-response-size). `paginate := 'provider'` uses the catalog default.
- **Credentials:** Nango adds and refreshes them; the worker only holds your Nango secret key.

vgi.example_queries.description: Every GitHub repository the connection can see, following Link-header pages
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT item->>'full_name' AS repo FROM nango.main.proxy('conn-ada-github', 'github-prod', '/user/repos', paginate := 'provider', params := '{"per_page": 50}') ORDER BY repo

vgi.example_queries.description: HubSpot contacts through the proxy with the provider's cursor pagination
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT item->>'id' AS id, item->'properties'->>'email' AS email FROM nango.main.proxy('conn-acme-hubspot', 'hubspot', '/crm/v3/objects/contacts', paginate := 'provider') ORDER BY id

functions.comment: Records a Nango sync stored for one connection and model, typed from the model's JSON Schema

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Read the records a Nango sync stored (GET /records) for one connection: records(integration, connection_id, model, modified_after := NULL, filter := NULL, variant := NULL, page_size := 100). Find integration/model pairs in nango.main.syncs (models column) and connection ids in nango.main.connections(). When the deployed sync has a JSON Schema for the model, each model field is its own typed column (date-time strings are `TIMESTAMPTZ`, integers `BIGINT`); otherwise you get `id` and the payload as `_record` JSON (use _record->>'field'). Every row has _nango_last_action (ADDED/UPDATED/DELETED), _nango_last_modified_at, _nango_first_seen_at, _nango_deleted_at, _nango_pruned_at, _nango_cursor and _record. Deleted records are included (filter _nango_deleted_at IS NULL for live ones). For incremental reads filter _nango_last_modified_at > <ts>: it becomes Nango's modified_after.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## records(integration, connection_id, model, modified_after := NULL, filter := NULL, variant := NULL, page_size := 100)

Synced records for one connection and model. Columns come from the model's JSON Schema when the sync has one; otherwise `id` + `_record` JSON.

**Pushdown:** `_nango_last_modified_at` > / >= → `modified_after`; `_nango_last_action` = / IN → `filter`; `id` = / IN (≤ 100) → `ids`. Paging follows `next_cursor`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Open GitHub issues a Nango sync stored (typed model columns such as state are also available)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT _record->>'title' AS title, _nango_last_modified_at FROM nango.main.records('github-prod', 'conn-ada-github', 'GithubIssue') WHERE _nango_deleted_at IS NULL AND _record->>'state' = 'open' ORDER BY title

vgi.example_queries.description: Incremental read: records changed since a timestamp (pushed down as modified_after)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, _nango_last_action FROM nango.main.records('github-prod', 'conn-ada-github', 'GithubIssue') WHERE _nango_last_modified_at > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-01 00:00:00+00' ORDER BY id

workers.title: NASCAR Racing Data
workers.tagline: NASCAR Cup, Xfinity & Truck schedules, results, standings & lap data in DuckDB (Python)
workers.subtitle: Cup, O'Reilly Auto Parts and Truck Series schedules, results, standings and laps.
workers.summary: Read-only NASCAR schedules, results, standings, lap times and pit stops from NASCAR's feeds
workers.doc_md:
# NASCAR schedules, results and lap data

Query NASCAR's three national series directly from SQL: schedules and race summaries since 2015, official results, stage and session results, cautions, lead changes, lap-by-lap times (2020 onwards), pit stops, commentary, loop-data driver ratings and current points standings.

## Data model

Races are identified by `race_id`; drivers by `driver_id`. Find a race in `current_schedule` or `schedule()`, then pass its `race_id` (and `season` to skip the lookup) to the per-race functions. Missing upstream files yield empty results, not errors.

Data is fetched on demand and cached in-process; nothing is rehosted. Not affiliated with NASCAR.

## Sources and references

* [NASCAR.com](https://www.nascar.com/): the official site whose public `cf.nascar.com` JSON feeds this worker reads, for example the [driver directory feed](https://cf.nascar.com/cacher/drivers.json).

example_queries.title: current_schedule_is_populated
example_queries.description: The current season's schedule covers all three national series.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT series_id) = 3 AS populated FROM nascar.main.current_schedule;

example_queries.title: current_standings_have_drivers
example_queries.description: Every current standings row has a driver and a non-negative points total.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) > 0 AND bool_and(points >= 0) AND count(driver_id) = count(*) AS valid FROM nascar.main.current_standings;

example_queries.title: championship_race_2026_winner
example_queries.description: Ryan Blaney won the 2026 Cup Series Championship Race (race 5601).
example_queries.sql: SELECT driver_name FROM nascar.main.race_results(5601, season := 2026) WHERE finishing_position = 1;

example_queries.title: lead_stints_match_laps_led
example_queries.description: Lead stints in race 5601 add up to the 267 laps run.
example_queries.sql: SELECT sum(laps_led)::INTEGER AS laps FROM nascar.main.race_leaders(5601, season := 2026);

example_queries.description: Current Cup Series top ten.
example_queries.sql: SELECT position, driver_name, points, points_behind_leader, wins, top_5 FROM nascar.main.current_standings WHERE series_id = 1 ORDER BY position LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Points leader of each series.
example_queries.sql: SELECT series_name, driver_name, points FROM nascar.main.current_standings WHERE position = 1 ORDER BY series_id

example_queries.description: Top five of each series' latest race with each driver's championship position, season points and wins from the current standings.
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.series_name, r.finishing_position, r.driver_name, s.position AS championship_position, s.points, s.wins FROM nascar.main.last_race_results r JOIN nascar.main.current_standings s USING (series_id, driver_id) WHERE r.finishing_position <= 5 ORDER BY r.series_id, r.finishing_position

example_queries.description: Top ten of the 2026 Cup Series Championship Race with the green- and yellow-flag pit stops each made and their total time on pit road.
example_queries.sql: SELECT r.finishing_position, r.driver_name, count(*) AS stops, sum(p.pit_road_seconds) AS pit_road_seconds FROM nascar.main.race_results(5601, season := 2026) r JOIN nascar.main.pit_stops(5601, season := 2026) p USING (driver_id) WHERE r.finishing_position <= 10 AND p.pit_in_flag_state IN (1, 2) GROUP BY r.finishing_position, r.driver_name ORDER BY r.finishing_position

example_queries.description: Where each stage winner of the 2026 Cup Series Championship Race finished, and the laps they led.

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## NASCAR analytical data

Rows are race-, car-in-race-, stage-, caution-, lap- or pit-stop-grain, keyed by `race_id` and `driver_id`. Times and speeds are exact decimals.

Start with the current tables. For history, find a `race_id` with `schedule()` and pass it to the per-race functions; aggregate `season_results()` for season, team and manufacturer statistics.

functions.name: season_results
functions.comment: Official results of every completed race in one NASCAR series season

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per car per completed race of a season (points races and exhibitions; join schedule() on race_id and filter is_points_race when that matters). Aggregate it for season driver, team, owner or manufacturer statistics: wins, top 5s, laps led, average finish, DNFs (finishing_status <> 'Running'). Defaults to the current Cup season.
tags.vgi.doc_md: The per-race official results for a whole season, fetched with bounded concurrency and cached. This is the source for season and career aggregates in SQL; NASCAR's points feeds are only reliable for the current season.

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 Cup Series wins and top-fives by driver, points races only.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT r.driver_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.finishing_position = 1) AS wins, count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.finishing_position <= 5) AS top_5 FROM nascar.main.season_results(season := 2025) r JOIN nascar.main.schedule(season := 2025, series := 'cup') USING (race_id) WHERE is_points_race GROUP BY r.driver_name ORDER BY wins DESC, top_5 DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Laps led by team in the 2025 Truck Series.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, sum(laps_led) AS laps_led FROM nascar.main.season_results(season := 2025, series := 'truck') GROUP BY team_name ORDER BY laps_led DESC

functions.name: pit_stops
functions.comment: Timed pit-road visits with tire service for one NASCAR race

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per pit-road visit: lap, flag at entry, total pit-road time, stationary stop time, travel in and out, tires changed and positions gained or lost. stop_type FOUR_WHEEL_CHANGE / TWO_WHEEL_CHANGE_* / OTHER. Available from 2020.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Pit timing from NASCAR's live pit data feed; durations are exact seconds.

vgi.example_queries.description: Fastest four-tire green-flag stops in the 2026 Cup Series Championship Race.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT driver_name, lap, stop_seconds, pit_road_seconds FROM nascar.main.pit_stops(5601, season := 2026) WHERE stop_type = 'FOUR_WHEEL_CHANGE' AND pit_in_flag_state = 1 ORDER BY stop_seconds LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Top ten of the 2026 Cup Series Championship Race with the green- and yellow-flag pit stops each made and their total time on pit road.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT r.finishing_position, r.driver_name, count(*) AS stops, sum(p.pit_road_seconds) AS pit_road_seconds FROM nascar.main.race_results(5601, season := 2026) r JOIN nascar.main.pit_stops(5601, season := 2026) p USING (driver_id) WHERE r.finishing_position <= 10 AND p.pit_in_flag_state IN (1, 2) GROUP BY r.finishing_position, r.driver_name ORDER BY r.finishing_position

workers.title: VGI NATS Worker
workers.tagline: NATS monitoring, JetStream streams, consumers, KV and messages as SQL in DuckDB (Go)
workers.subtitle: NATS server monitoring and read-only JetStream streams, consumers, messages, KV and object stores.
workers.summary: NATS and JetStream as SQL tables in DuckDB: server, connection, account and JetStream monitoring, plus read-only streams, consumers with lag, stream messages, KV buckets and object stores.
workers.doc_md:
# NATS in DuckDB

Read a NATS deployment from SQL without changing it.

- **Monitoring**: servers, client connections, cluster routes, gateways, leaf nodes, subscriptions, accounts and JetStream usage, from the HTTP monitoring port or the `$SYS` request API, one row per server.
- **JetStream**: stream configuration and state, per-subject counts, consumers with their lag, and a non-destructive read of a stream's messages with subject, sequence and time filters pushed into the read.
- **KV and object stores**: buckets, current values or full revision history, objects and (on request) their content.

Credentials come from a `nats` DuckDB secret: token, user/password, NKey seed or `.creds` contents, with optional TLS.

example_queries.description: Version, JetStream status and load of every server
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, version, jetstream_enabled, connections, round(uptime_seconds / 3600, 1) AS uptime_hours FROM nats.main.server_info() ORDER BY server_name

example_queries.description: The 20 connections that published the most messages
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, account, ip, in_msgs, out_msgs FROM nats.main.connections(sort := 'msgs_from', max_rows := 20) ORDER BY in_msgs DESC

example_queries.description: Cluster routes by round-trip time
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, remote_name, rtt_seconds * 1000 AS rtt_ms, pending_bytes FROM nats.main.routes() ORDER BY rtt_ms DESC

example_queries.description: Super-cluster gateway connections of every server
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, direction, remote_gateway, rtt_seconds FROM nats.main.gateways() ORDER BY server_name, direction, remote_gateway

example_queries.description: Leaf-node connections and their accounts
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, name, account, rtt_seconds FROM nats.main.leafnodes() ORDER BY server_name, name

example_queries.description: Who receives a message published on orders.eu.created
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, subject, queue_group, msgs FROM nats.main.subscriptions(test_subject := 'orders.eu.created') ORDER BY account, subject

example_queries.description: Interest-graph size and match-cache efficiency per server
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, num_subscriptions, round(cache_hit_rate, 3) AS hit_rate, max_fanout FROM nats.main.subscription_stats() ORDER BY server_name

example_queries.description: Every account, which one is the system account and where JetStream is on
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, is_system, jetstream_enabled, client_connections FROM nats.main.accounts() ORDER BY account

example_queries.description: Messages published and delivered per account across the cluster
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, sum(received_msgs) AS published, sum(sent_msgs) AS delivered FROM nats.main.account_stats() GROUP BY account ORDER BY published DESC

example_queries.description: JetStream file-storage use per server
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, storage_bytes, max_storage_bytes, round(100.0 * storage_bytes / nullif(max_storage_bytes, 0), 1) AS pct_used FROM nats.main.jetstream_servers() ORDER BY pct_used DESC

example_queries.description: The ten largest streams across all accounts
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, stream, messages, bytes FROM nats.main.jsz_streams() ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Lagging consumers across every account
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, stream, consumer, lag, num_ack_pending FROM nats.main.jsz_consumers() WHERE lag > 0 ORDER BY lag DESC

example_queries.description: Health check of every server
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, status, error FROM nats.main.health() ORDER BY server_name

example_queries.description: JetStream usage and limits of the account
example_queries.sql: SELECT streams, consumers, storage_bytes, max_storage_bytes FROM nats.main.account_info()

example_queries.description: Streams by size, without the KV and object-store backing streams
example_queries.sql: SELECT stream, subjects, messages, bytes, consumer_count FROM nats.main.streams() WHERE kind = 'stream' ORDER BY bytes DESC

example_queries.description: Message count per subject in the ORDERS stream
example_queries.sql: SELECT subject, messages FROM nats.main.stream_subjects('ORDERS') ORDER BY messages DESC, subject

example_queries.description: Lagging consumers, worst first
example_queries.sql: SELECT stream, consumer, lag, num_ack_pending, num_redelivered FROM nats.main.consumers() WHERE lag > 0 ORDER BY lag DESC

example_queries.description: European order events, oldest first
example_queries.sql: SELECT sequence, subject, timestamp, payload_text FROM nats.main.messages('ORDERS', subject := 'orders.eu.*') ORDER BY sequence

example_queries.description: Every KV bucket with its size and history depth
example_queries.sql: SELECT bucket, keys, values, history, bytes FROM nats.main.kv_buckets() ORDER BY bucket

example_queries.description: Current value of every key in the config bucket
example_queries.sql: SELECT key, value_text, revision FROM nats.main.kv_entries('config') ORDER BY key

example_queries.description: Object stores by size
example_queries.sql: SELECT bucket, objects, size_bytes FROM nats.main.object_stores() ORDER BY size_bytes DESC

example_queries.description: Objects in the files store by size
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, size, chunks, modified FROM nats.main.objects('files') ORDER BY size DESC

example_queries.description: Subjects of a stream that a wildcard subscription would receive
example_queries.sql: SELECT subject, messages FROM nats.main.stream_subjects('ORDERS') WHERE nats.main.subject_matches('orders.*.created', subject) ORDER BY subject

example_queries.description: Total subscriptions across the cluster
example_queries.sql: SELECT sum(num_subscriptions) AS subs FROM nats.main.subscription_stats()

example_queries.description: Streams that have gone longest without a new message
example_queries.sql: SELECT stream, last_ts, now() - last_ts AS idle FROM nats.main.streams() ORDER BY idle DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: How many routes each server has (a full mesh has n-1 or more)
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, count(*) AS routes FROM nats.main.routes() GROUP BY server_name ORDER BY server_name

example_queries.description: Read small text objects
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, content_text FROM nats.main.objects('files', include_content := true, max_content_bytes := 1024) WHERE content_text IS NOT NULL ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Accounts with at least one connection
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, connections FROM nats.main.account_stats(include_unused := false) ORDER BY connections DESC

example_queries.description: Stream count and storage per account
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, count(*) AS streams, sum(bytes) AS bytes FROM nats.main.jsz_streams() GROUP BY account ORDER BY bytes DESC

example_queries.description: Leaf-node connections per account
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, count(*) AS leafs FROM nats.main.leafnodes() GROUP BY account ORDER BY leafs DESC

example_queries.description: Bytes sent to each remote cluster
example_queries.sql: SELECT remote_gateway, sum(out_bytes) AS bytes_sent FROM nats.main.gateways() WHERE direction = 'outbound' GROUP BY remote_gateway ORDER BY bytes_sent DESC

example_queries.description: Buckets whose entries expire
example_queries.sql: SELECT bucket, ttl_seconds FROM nats.main.kv_buckets() WHERE ttl_seconds IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ttl_seconds

example_queries.description: How many object stores and objects the account has
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS stores, sum(objects) AS objects FROM nats.main.object_stores()

example_queries.description: Change history of one key
example_queries.sql: SELECT revision, operation, value_text, created FROM nats.main.kv_entries('config', key := 'app.color', include_history := true) ORDER BY revision

example_queries.description: Total consumer lag per account
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, sum(lag) AS total_lag FROM nats.main.jsz_consumers() GROUP BY account ORDER BY total_lag DESC

example_queries.description: Streams, consumers and API errors on every JetStream server
example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, streams, consumers, api_errors FROM nats.main.jetstream_servers() WHERE enabled ORDER BY server_name

example_queries.description: Delivery position and lag of the ORDERS consumers
example_queries.sql: SELECT consumer, delivered_stream_seq, ack_floor_stream_seq, lag FROM nats.main.consumers(stream := 'ORDERS') ORDER BY consumer

example_queries.description: Open connections and pending bytes per account
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, count(*) AS conns, sum(pending_bytes) AS pending FROM nats.main.connections() GROUP BY account ORDER BY conns DESC

example_queries.description: Subscriptions per account
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, count(*) AS subs FROM nats.main.subscriptions() GROUP BY account ORDER BY subs DESC

example_queries.description: Cluster-wide message totals and slow-consumer events
example_queries.sql: SELECT sum(in_msgs) AS msgs_in, sum(out_msgs) AS msgs_out, sum(slow_consumers) AS slow FROM nats.main.server_info()

example_queries.description: Message count and bytes per subject after sequence 5 (the sequence filter is pushed down)
example_queries.sql: SELECT subject, count(*) AS msgs, sum(payload_bytes) AS bytes FROM nats.main.messages('ORDERS') WHERE sequence > 5 GROUP BY subject ORDER BY subject

example_queries.description: Decode JSON payloads and count created orders per region
example_queries.sql: SELECT json_extract_string(payload_text, '$.region') AS region, count(*) AS orders FROM nats.main.messages('ORDERS', subject := 'orders.*.created', max_msgs := 1000) GROUP BY region ORDER BY region

example_queries.description: How many servers fail the JetStream server health check
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT healthy) AS unhealthy FROM nats.main.health(js_server_only := true)

example_queries.description: Accounts that import or export streams or services
example_queries.sql: SELECT account, imports, exports FROM nats.main.accounts() WHERE imports > 0 OR exports > 0 ORDER BY account

example_queries.description: Created orders per region, counted by the server
example_queries.sql: SELECT split_part(subject, '.', 2) AS region, sum(messages) AS msgs FROM nats.main.stream_subjects('ORDERS', filter := 'orders.*.created') GROUP BY region ORDER BY region

example_queries.description: Share of the account's storage limit in use
example_queries.sql: SELECT round(100.0 * storage_bytes / max_storage_bytes, 1) AS pct_storage_used FROM nats.main.account_info() WHERE max_storage_bytes IS NOT NULL

example_queries.description: Single-token and trailing wildcards
example_queries.sql: SELECT p, nats.main.subject_matches(p, 'orders.eu.created') AS matches FROM (VALUES ('orders.*.created'), ('orders.>'), ('orders.*'), ('orders.us.created')) t(p) ORDER BY p;

example_queries.description: '>' needs at least one more token
example_queries.sql: SELECT nats.main.subject_matches('orders.>', 'orders') AS matches;

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The main schema holds every function; the table functions take an optional secret_name named argument. Monitoring rows start with server_id and server_name. Times are `TIMESTAMPTZ`, durations are *_seconds `DOUBLE` columns, limits are NULL when unlimited, and open-ended documents (varz, config, detail) are JSON text. messages reads stored messages oldest first: filter with WHERE on subject, sequence and timestamp (pushed down) and decode JSON payloads with the json_extract function over payload_text. kv_entries reads KV values (include_history for every revision); objects lists object-store objects (include_content to download). Streams named KV_<bucket> and OBJ_<bucket> back KV buckets and object stores (the kind column of streams). subject_matches applies NATS wildcard rules locally.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

A read-only window onto one NATS deployment. Monitoring data comes from the HTTP monitoring endpoints when the `nats` secret sets `MONITORING_URL`, and otherwise from the `$SYS` request API (system-account credentials, one answer per server). JetStream, KV and object-store data comes from the account the secret authenticates as; pass `secret_name` to pick between several secrets.

Conventions: times are `TIMESTAMPTZ`, durations are `*_seconds` doubles, unlimited limits are NULL, and open-ended server documents are JSON text. Message reads use short-lived ephemeral consumers without acknowledgements, so querying never consumes, acknowledges or deletes anything, and subject, sequence and time filters in `WHERE` are pushed into the read instead of scanning the whole stream.

Streams named `KV_<bucket>` and `OBJ_<bucket>` are the storage behind KV buckets and object stores.

vgi.example_queries.description: Version, JetStream status and load of every server
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, version, jetstream_enabled, connections, round(uptime_seconds / 3600, 1) AS uptime_hours FROM nats.main.server_info() ORDER BY server_name

vgi.example_queries.description: The 20 connections that published the most messages
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, account, ip, in_msgs, out_msgs FROM nats.main.connections(sort := 'msgs_from', max_rows := 20) ORDER BY in_msgs DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Cluster routes by round-trip time
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, remote_name, rtt_seconds * 1000 AS rtt_ms, pending_bytes FROM nats.main.routes() ORDER BY rtt_ms DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Super-cluster gateway connections of every server
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, direction, remote_gateway, rtt_seconds FROM nats.main.gateways() ORDER BY server_name, direction, remote_gateway

vgi.example_queries.description: Leaf-node connections and their accounts
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, name, account, rtt_seconds FROM nats.main.leafnodes() ORDER BY server_name, name

vgi.example_queries.description: Who receives a message published on orders.eu.created
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account, subject, queue_group, msgs FROM nats.main.subscriptions(test_subject := 'orders.eu.created') ORDER BY account, subject

vgi.example_queries.description: Interest-graph size and match-cache efficiency per server
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, num_subscriptions, round(cache_hit_rate, 3) AS hit_rate, max_fanout FROM nats.main.subscription_stats() ORDER BY server_name

vgi.example_queries.description: Every account, which one is the system account and where JetStream is on
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account, is_system, jetstream_enabled, client_connections FROM nats.main.accounts() ORDER BY account

vgi.example_queries.description: Messages published and delivered per account across the cluster
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account, sum(received_msgs) AS published, sum(sent_msgs) AS delivered FROM nats.main.account_stats() GROUP BY account ORDER BY published DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: JetStream file-storage use per server
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, storage_bytes, max_storage_bytes, round(100.0 * storage_bytes / nullif(max_storage_bytes, 0), 1) AS pct_used FROM nats.main.jetstream_servers() ORDER BY pct_used DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: The ten largest streams across all accounts
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account, stream, messages, bytes FROM nats.main.jsz_streams() ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Lagging consumers across every account
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT account, stream, consumer, lag, num_ack_pending FROM nats.main.jsz_consumers() WHERE lag > 0 ORDER BY lag DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Health check of every server
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT server_name, status, error FROM nats.main.health() ORDER BY server_name

vgi.example_queries.description: JetStream usage and limits of the account
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT streams, consumers, storage_bytes, max_storage_bytes FROM nats.main.account_info()

vgi.example_queries.description: Streams by size, without the KV and object-store backing streams
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT stream, subjects, messages, bytes, consumer_count FROM nats.main.streams() WHERE kind = 'stream' ORDER BY bytes DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Message count per subject in the ORDERS stream
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT subject, messages FROM nats.main.stream_subjects('ORDERS') ORDER BY messages DESC, subject

vgi.example_queries.description: Lagging consumers, worst first
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT stream, consumer, lag, num_ack_pending, num_redelivered FROM nats.main.consumers() WHERE lag > 0 ORDER BY lag DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: European order events, oldest first
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT sequence, subject, timestamp, payload_text FROM nats.main.messages('ORDERS', subject := 'orders.eu.*') ORDER BY sequence

vgi.example_queries.description: Every KV bucket with its size and history depth
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT bucket, keys, values, history, bytes FROM nats.main.kv_buckets() ORDER BY bucket

vgi.example_queries.description: Current value of every key in the config bucket
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT key, value_text, revision FROM nats.main.kv_entries('config') ORDER BY key

vgi.example_queries.description: Object stores by size
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT bucket, objects, size_bytes FROM nats.main.object_stores() ORDER BY size_bytes DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Objects in the files store by size
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, size, chunks, modified FROM nats.main.objects('files') ORDER BY size DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Subjects of a stream that a wildcard subscription would receive
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT subject, messages FROM nats.main.stream_subjects('ORDERS') WHERE nats.main.subject_matches('orders.*.created', subject) ORDER BY subject

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per object in an object store (the store's metadata subjects, read with a short-lived ordered consumer): name, description, size, chunks, digest, modified, nuid, deleted, link, headers and metadata maps (`MAP`). tags.vgi.doc_llm: Read a KV bucket: by default the latest revision of every live key; with include_history true, every stored revision (up to the bucket's history depth); include_deleted true adds DEL/PURGE markers. functions.name: messages
functions.comment: Read a stream's messages without consuming them; subject, sequence and time filters pushed down

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Read a JetStream stream's stored messages without consuming them: one row per message with stream, subject, sequence, timestamp `TIMESTAMPTZ`, key (the subject), payload `BLOB`, payload_text (`VARCHAR` when valid UTF-8, else NULL), payload_bytes, headers `MAP` (several values become a JSON array) and redelivered (always NULL), the shared Query.Farm messaging vocabulary. Args: stream (positional), subject (wildcards allowed), start_seq, start_time, max_msgs, secret_name. Pushed down: equality and IN-list filters on subject (or key), plus the subject argument, become the consumer's filter subjects; comparisons and ranges on sequence choose the start and stop sequence; a lower bound on timestamp chooses the start time. Every pushed filter is re-checked exactly on each row. Reads use a short-lived ephemeral AckNone consumer per batch (deleted afterwards), so durable consumers, acknowledgements and work-queue/interest retention are unaffected. The scan stops at the stream's last sequence when it started. Decode JSON payloads with the json_extract function over payload_text. Reads the JetStream API of the secret's own account; JETSTREAM_DOMAIN selects a domain. Read-only.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## messages(stream, subject := NULL, start_seq := NULL, start_time := NULL, max_msgs := NULL)

Browse a stream's messages without acknowledging or removing anything. `WHERE subject = ...`, `sequence` ranges and `timestamp >= ...` are pushed down into the read.

vgi.example_queries.description: European order events, oldest first
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT sequence, subject, timestamp, payload_text FROM nats.main.messages('ORDERS', subject := 'orders.eu.*') ORDER BY sequence

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT subject, count(*) AS msgs, sum(payload_bytes) AS bytes FROM nats.main.messages('ORDERS') WHERE sequence > 5 GROUP BY subject ORDER BY subject

vgi.example_queries.description: Decode JSON payloads and count created orders per region
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT json_extract_string(payload_text, '$.region') AS region, count(*) AS orders FROM nats.main.messages('ORDERS', subject := 'orders.*.created', max_msgs := 1000) GROUP BY region ORDER BY region

functions.name: subject_matches
functions.comment: True when a NATS subscription pattern (with * and > wildcards) receives a subject

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Return true when a subscription subject pattern receives messages published on subject, using NATS wildcard rules: '*' matches exactly one token, '>' matches one or more trailing tokens, tokens are separated by '.'. Both arguments are `VARCHAR` columns or constants; NULL in, NULL out. Runs locally, needs no secret or server. Use it to filter subjects from messages, stream_subjects or subscriptions with NATS semantics (SQL LIKE does not know that '*' stops at a dot).
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## subject_matches(pattern, subject)

NATS wildcard matching: `*` is one token, `>` the rest.

```sql
SELECT nats.main.subject_matches('orders.*.created', 'orders.eu.created');  -- true
```

vgi.example_queries.description: Subjects of a stream that a wildcard subscription would receive
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT subject, messages FROM nats.main.stream_subjects('ORDERS') WHERE nats.main.subject_matches('orders.*.created', subject) ORDER BY subject

vgi.executable_examples.description: Single-token and trailing wildcards
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT p, nats.main.subject_matches(p, 'orders.eu.created') AS matches FROM (VALUES ('orders.*.created'), ('orders.>'), ('orders.*'), ('orders.us.created')) t(p) ORDER BY p

vgi.executable_examples.description: '>' needs at least one more token
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT nats.main.subject_matches('orders.>', 'orders') AS matches

tags.vgi.title: Subject Wildcard Match

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.description: Subscription subject, possibly with * (one token) and > (one or more trailing tokens) wildcards; NULL in, NULL out.

arguments.name: subject
arguments.description: Subject to test, e.g. a message's subject; NULL in, NULL out.

examples: SELECT subject, messages FROM nats.main.stream_subjects('ORDERS') WHERE nats.main.subject_matches('orders.*.created', subject) ORDER BY subject
SELECT p, nats.main.subject_matches(p, 'orders.eu.created') AS matches FROM (VALUES ('orders.*.created'), ('orders.>'), ('orders.*'), ('orders.us.created')) t(p) ORDER BY p;
SELECT nats.main.subject_matches('orders.>', 'orders') AS matches;
