tags.vgi.doc_llm:
# similar_items

Item-to-item collaborative-filtering neighbour finder. Fits implicit-feedback ALS over the supplied `(user, item, value)` interaction relation, then for **every item** returns its top-N most similar items ranked by the cosine similarity of their ALS latent factors.

## When to use
Use this to power 'customers who liked X also liked Y', 'related products', or 'more like this' surfaces -- recommendations that depend on an item, not a user. For per-user recommendations use `recommend_all` or `recommend_for`.

## Inputs
- `Arg(0)`: a `(SELECT user, item, value)` subquery -- the interaction relation.
- `user`, `item`, `value`: names of the columns playing each role.
- `n`: similar items per item (default 10).
- `factors`: ALS latent-factor count (default 50, clamped on tiny matrices).

## Output
Rows of `(item, similar_item, similarity, rank)`; `similarity` is cosine of the ALS item factors (1.0 = identical) and `rank` is 1-based per item.

## Behavior & edge cases
An item is never listed as its own neighbour (the self-match at similarity 1.0 is dropped). `value` is interaction confidence and defaults to 1.0 when absent. Items co-interacted by the same users score as nearest neighbours. Deterministic (pinned random_state, single-threaded BLAS).
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## similar_items

Top-N most **similar items** for every item, by cosine similarity of implicit-feedback ALS item factors over the supplied interaction relation.

### Usage

Pass the interaction relation as the positional `(user, item, value)` subquery and name the role columns plus `n` (neighbours per item). Each output row is `(item, similar_item, similarity, rank)`; order by `item` then `rank` for a stable neighbour list. A ready-to-run demonstration lives in this function's example queries.

### Notes

- The query item itself is excluded from its own neighbour list.
- One ALS model is fit over the whole matrix, so the relation is fully buffered before any rows are emitted.
- `value` (confidence) defaults to 1.0 if the column is missing; `factors` is auto-clamped on small matrices.

workers.title: Windows Registry Hives
workers.tagline: Parse Windows registry hives in DuckDB with SQL — keys/values, transaction-log replay and deleted-cell recovery. A VGI worker.
workers.subtitle: Parse offline Windows Registry hive files into SQL rows for forensics, with transaction-log replay and deleted-key recovery.
workers.summary: Parse Windows Registry hive files (regf) into typed key/value rows for DFIR — transaction-log replay and deleted-cell recovery.
workers.doc_md:
# Reghive — Windows Registry Hive Parsing for DFIR in SQL

**Parse Windows Registry hive files (the on-disk `regf` format) directly in DuckDB SQL** — `SYSTEM`, `SOFTWARE`, `NTUSER.DAT`, `SAM`, `SECURITY`, `UsrClass.dat`, and `AmCache.hve` — into typed key/value rows for digital forensics and incident response. ATTACH a directory of thousands of collected hives and run **one query** that joins registry evidence (Run-key persistence, Services, installed software, AmCache program-execution) to the rest of your detection surface — IOC feeds, CVE data, YARA, Sigma — with no per-host RegRipper invocation and no result-wrangling.

The differentiators over export-only tools are **transaction-log (`.LOG1`/`.LOG2`) replay** of dirty hives captured mid-write and **deleted-cell recovery** of keys/values from unallocated space (flagged `is_deleted`), both powered by the Apache-2.0 [`notatin`](https://github.com/strozfriedberg/notatin) parser. Every value is surfaced both as a coerced `value_data` string and the lossless `value_raw` bytes; per-key last-write timestamps are a first-class column.

**Sensitivity note.** `SAM`/`SECURITY` hives contain password-hash material. This worker exposes hive structure faithfully (so those bytes appear in `value_raw`) but **never decodes credentials** — pair it with `vgi-mask`/`vgi-pii` to redact before results leave the analyst's session.

**How you work with it.** Point it at a directory glob of collected hives for bulk triage, or hand it a single in-memory hive to drill into one subtree, key, or value; header and validity probes tell you up front whether a hive is dirty and needs transaction-log recovery. The worker opens no socket and makes no outbound calls — zero egress, safe for air-gapped evidence stores.

Format references: the [msuhanov regf specification](https://github.com/msuhanov/regf/blob/master/Windows%20registry%20file%20format%20specification.md) and Google Project Zero's "Windows Registry Adventure #5: regf".

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Registry-hive parsing for DFIR

The single schema of the `reghive` worker. It turns offline Windows Registry hive files (`NTUSER.DAT`, `SYSTEM`, `SOFTWARE`, `SAM`, …) into typed key/value rows so a hive on disk can be queried as SQL.

Every read is offline and best-effort: dirty hives still parse, deleted cells can be recovered and labelled, and sensitive bytes are preserved raw and never decoded. The functions group into a few kinds of work:

- **Bulk parsing** — scan a whole hive (a directory glob, or a single blob) into rows for triage.
- **Targeted lookup** — pull one key or value, or a key's metadata, without walking the whole tree.
- **Header & validation** — read the base-block header and confirm the bytes are a well-formed regf hive.
- **Transaction logs** — report on `.LOG1`/`.LOG2` replay of a dirty hive.

Use it whenever you have a registry hive on disk and need its contents as rows, from fleet-wide triage down to a single key or value.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Scan Windows Registry hive files (regf: SYSTEM, SOFTWARE, NTUSER.DAT, SAM, SECURITY, UsrClass.dat, AmCache.hve) into typed key/value rows for DFIR. The first argument is either a local file glob (`VARCHAR`, e.g. '/cases/*/NTUSER.DAT') or a single in-memory hive (`BLOB`, e.g. from read_blob('s3://...')). By default it replays sibling .LOG1/.LOG2 transaction logs to recover a dirty hive (apply_logs) and reconstructs keys/values from unallocated cells (recover_deleted, flagged is_deleted). The named `mode` argument is 'values' (one row per value, default), 'keys' (one row per key), or 'all' (both). Emits full key paths, value name/type/data, the lossless value_raw bytes, per-key last-write timestamps, and recovery/diagnostics tags. Join it to IOC, CVE, YARA, and Sigma workers for fleet-scale registry triage.

workers.title: Cross-Encoder Reranking
workers.tagline: Local cross-encoder RAG reranking for DuckDB (Python, fastembed/ONNX)
workers.subtitle: Score and reorder retrieved passages against a query with local cross-encoder models, for sharper RAG results.
workers.summary: Local cross-encoder reranking (fastembed/ONNX) for second-stage RAG precision.
workers.doc_md:
# Cross-Encoder Reranking in SQL

![fastembed (Qdrant) logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qdrant/fastembed/main/docs/assets/favicon.png)

**Rerank retrieval results directly in DuckDB with a local cross-encoder reranker (fastembed / ONNX Runtime, no torch) -- the precision second stage that turns a good recall set into a great answer for RAG and semantic search.**

Retrieval-augmented generation and semantic search almost always run in two stages. A fast *recall* stage (DuckDB [VSS](https://duckdb.org) approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings, or BM25 full-text search) cheaply pulls a top-K candidate set out of a large corpus, but it ranks each document in isolation, so the truly best passage is often buried at rank 7 instead of rank 1. This worker adds the *precision* second stage: a **cross-encoder** that reads the query and a candidate document *together* in a single transformer forward pass and emits a relevance score that is far more accurate than bi-encoder cosine similarity. It is for anyone building local RAG pipelines, document search, or recommendation ranking who wants higher answer quality without standing up a separate model-serving service -- the reranking happens inside your SQL query.

Scores are computed entirely locally by [fastembed](https://github.com/qdrant/fastembed) (from Qdrant, Apache-2.0), which runs quantized cross-encoder models on [ONNX Runtime](https://onnxruntime.ai/) -- there is **no PyTorch dependency** and no network call at query time. The default model, [`Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`](https://huggingface.co/Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) (~80 MB, Apache-2.0), is fetched once on first use and cached, and the ONNX session is built a single time per worker process and amortized across every row. Because a cross-encoder scores each (query, document) pair at query time and cannot be precomputed or cached the way an embedding can, you should only ever run it over a recall-produced top-K candidate set -- never over a whole corpus.

The catalog exposes a small, focused surface. `rerank_score(query, document)` returns a `DOUBLE` relevance logit (higher = more relevant, meaningful only relative to other documents for the *same* query), so it drops straight into `ORDER BY rerank.rerank_score(:q, chunk) DESC LIMIT k`; a three-argument overload `rerank_score(query, document, model)` lets you pick a specific reranker such as `BAAI/bge-reranker-base`. The `supported_models()` table function (also available as the `supported_models` table) lists every reranker the worker can run together with the license of its weights. A NULL or empty query or document always yields a NULL score, so odd input never crashes a query.

## Getting started

Install and load the `vgi` community extension, then `ATTACH` this worker as a catalog (for example named `rerank`) pointed at `uv run rerank_worker.py`. Once attached, order any recall-produced candidate set by `rerank.main.rerank_score(:query, document) DESC` and keep the top *k* rows. Ready-to-run SQL for every function lives in each object's own examples and in the schema's example queries.

## Learn more

- fastembed source: <https://github.com/qdrant/fastembed>
- fastembed documentation: <https://qdrant.github.io/fastembed/>
- ONNX Runtime: <https://onnxruntime.ai/>

## main

The single schema of the `rerank` catalog: local cross-encoder relevance scoring exposed as SQL over Apache Arrow. Everything runs on-device via fastembed / ONNX Runtime (no torch, no network at query time once a model is cached), so second-stage RAG reranking becomes ordinary SQL.

**What you can do here**

- Score a `(query, document)` pair to a relevance logit and reorder a candidate set with `ORDER BY rerank_score(:q, doc) DESC LIMIT k`.
- Pick a specific reranker via the three-argument overload `rerank_score(query, document, model)`.
- Discover the available reranker models and their licenses.

**When to use it**

Apply reranking as the precision second stage over a recall-produced top-K candidate set (from DuckDB VSS ANN or BM25) -- never over a whole corpus, since a cross-encoder scores every pair at query time and cannot be precomputed. See each object's own documentation for arguments, worked examples, and output columns.

Query it to learn which model names are valid as the optional third argument to rerank_score(query, document, model) and to confirm licensing before adopting a model. The `model` column is the name to pass to rerank_score; the `license` column is the weights' license (every advertised model is permissive / commercially usable). # supported_models

A discovery table of every cross-encoder reranker the worker can run -- one row per model. Backed by the `supported_models()` table function, it is queried without parentheses -- project the `model` and `license` columns and order by `model`; see the examples below for ready-to-run SQL.

## Columns

| column | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | VARCHAR | Name to pass as the optional third argument to `rerank_score(query, document, model)` (primary key). |
| `license` | VARCHAR | SPDX-style license of the model weights. |

## Notes

Every advertised model is permissive / commercially usable. Reading this table loads no model, so it is always cheap.

functions.comment: Cross-encoder relevance score (DOUBLE) for a (query, document) pair using the default model (Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2). Higher = more relevant; the value is a raw logit, meaningful only RELATIVE to other documents for the SAME query. Intended for ORDER BY rerank_score(:q, doc) DESC LIMIT k over a top-K candidate set. # rerank_score(query, document, model)

Score a `(query, document)` pair with an **explicit** cross-encoder model (the three-argument arity overload of `rerank_score`).

## Arguments

- `query`, `document` -- the pair to score.
- `model` -- a model name from `supported_models()` (e.g. `Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`, `BAAI/bge-reranker-base`). Heavier models trade speed for quality and download on first use.

## Returns

`DOUBLE` -- the same relevance logit as the two-argument form.

## Notes

- Scalars are positional; this is an arity overload, not a named arg.
- NULL/empty query or document -> NULL score.

workers.doc_md:
# Rugby union data

Analyse rugby union from SQL: official world rankings and a match feed covering every sanctioned competition, plus league tables, fixtures, results and box scores for the major club and international competitions (Six Nations, Rugby Championship, Gallagher Prem, URC, Top 14, the European cups, Super Rugby and the Rugby World Cup).

## Two sources, two id spaces

- **World Rugby** (the governing body) supplies rankings, the cross-competition match feed and per-match team statistics, team sheets and timelines, keyed by World Rugby's 36-character `match_id`.
- **ESPN** supplies league tables with bonus points, season fixtures and results, and team and player box scores, keyed by a league key (such as `six_nations`) and ESPN's integer `event_id`.

Join the two sources on team names and dates, never on ids. Split seasons are labelled by their end year, so the 2026-27 Premiership is season 2027.

Access is read-only and keyless. The worker is not affiliated with World Rugby, ESPN or any league; data is fetched on demand and never rehosted.

## Sources and references

- [World Rugby](https://www.world.rugby/), the sport's governing body, and its [official world rankings](https://www.world.rugby/tournaments/rankings).
- [ESPN rugby](https://www.espn.com/rugby/) and its [league tables](https://www.espn.com/rugby/table); ESPN's endpoints are undocumented and subject to the [Disney terms of use](https://disneytermsofuse.com/).

example_queries.title: both_rankings_are_populated
example_queries.description: The current rankings table carries both the men's and women's tables.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT gender) = 2 AND count(*) > 100 AS populated FROM rugby.main.current_world_rankings;

example_queries.title: six_nations_2026_champion
example_queries.description: France won the 2026 Six Nations with 21 table points.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, table_points FROM rugby.main.standings(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) WHERE rank = 1;

example_queries.title: six_nations_2026_has_fifteen_results
example_queries.description: A Six Nations championship is fifteen matches.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS matches FROM rugby.main.results(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026);

example_queries.title: rankings_after_2023_world_cup
example_queries.description: South Africa led the men's rankings after winning the 2023 Rugby World Cup.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name FROM rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2023-10-30') WHERE position = 1;

example_queries.description: The current Gallagher Prem table.
example_queries.sql: SELECT rank, team_name, games_played, table_points FROM rugby.main.current_standings WHERE league = 'premiership' ORDER BY rank

example_queries.description: Champions Cup pool leaders.
example_queries.sql: SELECT group_name, team_name, table_points FROM rugby.main.current_standings WHERE league = 'champions_cup' AND rank = 1 ORDER BY group_name

example_queries.description: 2026 Six Nations upsets: results won by the side ranked lower in the World Rugby rankings in force before the championship (ESPN results joined to World Rugby rankings on team name).
example_queries.sql: WITH start_ranks AS (SELECT team_name, position FROM rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-02-01')) SELECT r.kickoff::DATE AS day, r.home_team_name, r.home_score, r.away_score, r.away_team_name, h.position AS home_rank, a.position AS away_rank FROM rugby.main.results(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) AS r JOIN start_ranks AS h ON h.team_name = r.home_team_name JOIN start_ranks AS a ON a.team_name = r.away_team_name WHERE (r.home_score > r.away_score AND h.position > a.position) OR (r.away_score > r.home_score AND a.position > h.position) ORDER BY r.kickoff

example_queries.description: Final 2026 Six Nations table beside each team's World Rugby ranking before (1 February) and after (16 March) the championship, with the ranking points gained or lost.
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.rank AS table_rank, s.team_name, s.table_points, b.position AS rank_before, a.position AS rank_after, round(a.points - b.points, 2) AS ranking_points_change FROM rugby.main.standings(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) AS s JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-02-01') AS b USING (team_name) JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-03-16') AS a USING (team_name) ORDER BY s.rank

example_queries.description: Nations Championship results from 1-10 November 2026 with each side's world ranking going in, joined on World Rugby team ids.
example_queries.sql: SELECT m.local_date, m.home_team_name, m.home_score, m.away_score, m.away_team_name, h.position AS home_rank, a.position AS away_rank FROM rugby.main.matches(start_date := DATE '2026-11-01', end_date := DATE '2026-11-10') AS m JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-11-01') AS h ON h.wr_team_id = m.home_wr_team_id JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-11-01') AS a ON a.wr_team_id = m.away_wr_team_id WHERE m.competition = 'Nations Championship 2026' ORDER BY m.kickoff

example_queries.description: Every score in England v Australia, 8 November 2026, with the scorer's team-sheet position (Replacement for the bench) and whether he started (timeline joined to the team sheets on wr_player_id).
example_queries.sql: SELECT t.clock_label, t.team_name, t.event_type, t.player_name, sq.position, sq.is_starter FROM rugby.main.match_timeline('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') AS t LEFT JOIN rugby.main.match_squads('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') AS sq USING (wr_player_id) WHERE t.points > 0 ORDER BY t.sequence

example_queries.description: International competitions and their current season.
example_queries.sql: SELECT league, name, current_season FROM rugby.main.competitions WHERE level = 'international' ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Recent results in men's international rugby.
example_queries.sql: SELECT local_date, competition, home_team_name, home_score, away_score, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.current_matches WHERE is_complete AND gender = 'men' AND (competition ILIKE '%Nations%' OR competition ILIKE '%International%') ORDER BY kickoff

example_queries.description: Upcoming matches in the next week.
example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff, competition, home_team_name, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.current_matches WHERE NOT is_complete AND kickoff > now() ORDER BY kickoff LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: Current men's top ten.
example_queries.sql: SELECT position, team_name, points, points_change FROM rugby.main.current_world_rankings WHERE gender = 'men' AND position <= 10 ORDER BY position

example_queries.description: Biggest risers in the latest women's update.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, previous_position, position FROM rugby.main.current_world_rankings WHERE gender = 'women' ORDER BY previous_position - position DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: The final 2026 Six Nations table.
example_queries.sql: SELECT rank, team_name, wins, losses, points_difference, bonus_points, table_points FROM rugby.main.standings(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) ORDER BY rank

example_queries.description: The 2025-26 Gallagher Prem table.
example_queries.sql: SELECT rank, team_name, table_points FROM rugby.main.standings(league := 'premiership', season := 2026) ORDER BY rank

example_queries.description: Super Saturday, 14 March 2026.
example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff, home_team_name, home_score, away_score, away_team_name, status_detail FROM rugby.main.scoreboard(league := 'six_nations', dates := '20260314') ORDER BY kickoff

example_queries.description: Side-by-side key statistics for England v Australia, 8 November 2026.
example_queries.sql: SELECT stat, max(value) FILTER (WHERE team_index = 0) AS home, max(value) FILTER (WHERE team_index = 1) AS away FROM rugby.main.match_stats('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') WHERE stat IN ('carries_metres', 'clean_breaks', 'tackles', 'possession') GROUP BY stat

example_queries.description: Metres carried by each side in England v Australia, 8 November 2026
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, value AS metres FROM rugby.main.match_stats('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') WHERE stat = 'carries_metres' ORDER BY team_index

example_queries.description: Scoring sequence of England v Australia, 8 November 2026.
example_queries.sql: SELECT clock_label, team_name, event_type, player_name, home_score, away_score FROM rugby.main.match_timeline('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') WHERE points > 0 ORDER BY sequence

example_queries.description: Top tacklers in England v Australia, 8 November 2026.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, player_name, tackles, missed_tackles FROM rugby.main.match_squads('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') ORDER BY tackles DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Starting fifteens for England v Australia, 8 November 2026
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, jersey_number, player_name, position FROM rugby.main.match_squads('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') WHERE is_starter ORDER BY team_index, jersey_number

example_queries.description: Every 2026 Six Nations result.
example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff::DATE AS day, home_team_name, home_score, away_score, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.results(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) ORDER BY kickoff

example_queries.description: Leading tacklers in Ireland v Scotland, 14 March 2026.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, player_name, tackles, missed_tackles FROM rugby.main.match_player_stats('six_nations', 602514) ORDER BY tackles DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Point scorers in Ireland v Scotland, 14 March 2026
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, player_name, points, tries FROM rugby.main.match_player_stats('six_nations', 602514) WHERE points > 0 ORDER BY points DESC

example_queries.description: Current leaders of every headline competition.
example_queries.sql: SELECT league_name, group_name, team_name, table_points FROM rugby.main.all_current_standings() WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY league_name, group_name

example_queries.description: Test results from the 2026 autumn window.
example_queries.sql: SELECT local_date, home_team_name, home_score, away_score, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.matches(start_date := DATE '2026-11-01', end_date := DATE '2026-11-10') WHERE competition ILIKE 'Nations Championship%' ORDER BY kickoff

example_queries.description: Upcoming 2026-27 Gallagher Prem fixtures.
example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff, home_team_name, away_team_name, venue_name FROM rugby.main.fixtures(league := 'premiership', season := 2027) ORDER BY kickoff LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Opening fixtures of the 2027 Rugby World Cup
example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff, home_team_name, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.fixtures(league := 'rugby_world_cup', season := 2027) ORDER BY kickoff LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Read both current number-one teams from the backing scan.
example_queries.sql: SELECT gender, team_name, points FROM rugby.main.all_current_world_rankings() WHERE position = 1 ORDER BY gender

example_queries.description: Ireland v Scotland, 14 March 2026: tackles and metres.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, stat, value FROM rugby.main.match_team_stats('six_nations', 602514) WHERE stat IN ('tackles', 'metres') ORDER BY stat, home_away

example_queries.description: Teams in the United Rugby Championship.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_id, team_name, abbreviation FROM rugby.main.teams(league := 'urc') ORDER BY team_name

example_queries.description: The six Six Nations teams

example_queries.description: Active club competitions.
example_queries.sql: SELECT league, name, region FROM rugby.main.all_competitions() WHERE level = 'club' AND is_active ORDER BY name

example_queries.description: Ireland's starting fifteen against Scotland, 14 March 2026.
example_queries.sql: SELECT jersey_number, player_name, position FROM rugby.main.match_lineups('six_nations', 602514) WHERE home_away = 'home' AND is_starter ORDER BY jersey_number

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Rugby union analytical data

Rows are explicitly team-, match-, team-statistic-, player- or event-grain. Current tables give today's view; parameterized functions select dates, seasons, leagues and individual matches.

World Rugby identifiers (`match_id`, `wr_team_id`, `wr_player_id`) and ESPN identifiers (`event_id`, `team_id`, `player_id`) are separate id spaces; join across the two sources on team names, not ids.

vgi.example_queries.description: The current Gallagher Prem table.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT rank, team_name, games_played, table_points FROM rugby.main.current_standings WHERE league = 'premiership' ORDER BY rank

vgi.example_queries.description: Champions Cup pool leaders.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT group_name, team_name, table_points FROM rugby.main.current_standings WHERE league = 'champions_cup' AND rank = 1 ORDER BY group_name

vgi.example_queries.description: 2026 Six Nations upsets: results won by the side ranked lower in the World Rugby rankings in force before the championship (ESPN results joined to World Rugby rankings on team name).
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH start_ranks AS (SELECT team_name, position FROM rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-02-01')) SELECT r.kickoff::DATE AS day, r.home_team_name, r.home_score, r.away_score, r.away_team_name, h.position AS home_rank, a.position AS away_rank FROM rugby.main.results(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) AS r JOIN start_ranks AS h ON h.team_name = r.home_team_name JOIN start_ranks AS a ON a.team_name = r.away_team_name WHERE (r.home_score > r.away_score AND h.position > a.position) OR (r.away_score > r.home_score AND a.position > h.position) ORDER BY r.kickoff

vgi.example_queries.description: Final 2026 Six Nations table beside each team's World Rugby ranking before (1 February) and after (16 March) the championship, with the ranking points gained or lost.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT s.rank AS table_rank, s.team_name, s.table_points, b.position AS rank_before, a.position AS rank_after, round(a.points - b.points, 2) AS ranking_points_change FROM rugby.main.standings(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) AS s JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-02-01') AS b USING (team_name) JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-03-16') AS a USING (team_name) ORDER BY s.rank

vgi.example_queries.description: Nations Championship results from 1-10 November 2026 with each side's world ranking going in, joined on World Rugby team ids.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT m.local_date, m.home_team_name, m.home_score, m.away_score, m.away_team_name, h.position AS home_rank, a.position AS away_rank FROM rugby.main.matches(start_date := DATE '2026-11-01', end_date := DATE '2026-11-10') AS m JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-11-01') AS h ON h.wr_team_id = m.home_wr_team_id JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-11-01') AS a ON a.wr_team_id = m.away_wr_team_id WHERE m.competition = 'Nations Championship 2026' ORDER BY m.kickoff

vgi.example_queries.description: Every score in England v Australia, 8 November 2026, with the scorer's team-sheet position (Replacement for the bench) and whether he started (timeline joined to the team sheets on wr_player_id).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.clock_label, t.team_name, t.event_type, t.player_name, sq.position, sq.is_starter FROM rugby.main.match_timeline('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') AS t LEFT JOIN rugby.main.match_squads('d21f7bed-f2f9-45bd-be33-3a0fc9beec42') AS sq USING (wr_player_id) WHERE t.points > 0 ORDER BY t.sequence

tables.name: current_matches
tables.comment: World Rugby matches from seven days ago to seven days ahead, one row per match

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Every match World Rugby records across all sanctioned competitions from seven days ago to seven days ahead: kick-off, competition, teams, score, outcome and venue. Start here for 'this weekend's results' or 'upcoming tests'. Use matches(start_date, end_date) for other windows and match_id with match_stats(), match_squads() and match_timeline().
tags.vgi.doc_md: A rolling two-week window of World Rugby's match feed. `is_complete` separates results from fixtures; filter `competition` with ILIKE.

vgi.example_queries.description: Recent results in men's international rugby.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT local_date, competition, home_team_name, home_score, away_score, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.current_matches WHERE is_complete AND gender = 'men' AND (competition ILIKE '%Nations%' OR competition ILIKE '%International%') ORDER BY kickoff

vgi.example_queries.description: Upcoming matches in the next week.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff, competition, home_team_name, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.current_matches WHERE NOT is_complete AND kickoff > now() ORDER BY kickoff LIMIT 20

tags.vgi.subtitle: Every World Rugby-recorded match from a week ago to a week ahead.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Current official World Rugby rankings for both men (gender = 'men') and women (gender = 'women'), one row per national team with position, points and movement since the previous update. Use world_rankings(as_of := ...) for a past day.

vgi.example_queries.description: Current men's top ten.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, previous_position, position FROM rugby.main.current_world_rankings WHERE gender = 'women' ORDER BY previous_position - position DESC LIMIT 5

functions.name: standings
functions.comment: Rugby league table for one competition and season

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Rugby league table for one competition and season, one row per team with rank, played, won, drawn, lost, points for/against/difference, tries for/against, try and losing bonus points and table points. Pool competitions (Champions Cup, Rugby World Cup) return one row per team per pool in group_name. season NULL returns the season in progress or, before it starts, the last completed one.
tags.vgi.doc_md: League tables with rugby bonus points. Split seasons such as the Premiership are labelled by their end year: the 2025-26 season is `season := 2026`.

functions.name: match_stats

functions.name: results
functions.comment: Finished matches and scores for one rugby competition season

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Finished matches in one competition season with full-time and half-time scores and the winner (home, away or draw). season NULL means the latest season with results. Aggregate home_score/away_score for points totals; event_id feeds the box-score functions.
tags.vgi.doc_md: One row per match. `event_id` feeds `match_team_stats`, `match_player_stats` and `match_lineups` with the same league. Split seasons span two calendar years.

vgi.example_queries.description: Every 2026 Six Nations result.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff::DATE AS day, home_team_name, home_score, away_score, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.results(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) ORDER BY kickoff

vgi.example_queries.description: 2026 Six Nations upsets: results won by the side ranked lower in the World Rugby rankings in force before the championship (ESPN results joined to World Rugby rankings on team name).
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH start_ranks AS (SELECT team_name, position FROM rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-02-01')) SELECT r.kickoff::DATE AS day, r.home_team_name, r.home_score, r.away_score, r.away_team_name, h.position AS home_rank, a.position AS away_rank FROM rugby.main.results(league := 'six_nations', season := 2026) AS r JOIN start_ranks AS h ON h.team_name = r.home_team_name JOIN start_ranks AS a ON a.team_name = r.away_team_name WHERE (r.home_score > r.away_score AND h.position > a.position) OR (r.away_score > r.home_score AND a.position > h.position) ORDER BY r.kickoff

functions.name: matches
functions.comment: World Rugby's cross-competition match feed for a date range

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Every match World Rugby records across all sanctioned competitions (tests, Six Nations, Premiership, Top 14, URC, Super Rugby, Sevens, women's rugby and dozens of second-tier competitions), one row per match with kick-off, competition, teams, score, outcome and venue. Filter by competition name with ILIKE, for example competition ILIKE 'Six Nations%'. match_id feeds match_stats(), match_squads() and match_timeline(). Ranges are limited to 366 days per query.
tags.vgi.doc_md: World Rugby's match feed flattened to one row per match. `home_*` is the first-listed team and `away_*` the second, which World Rugby uses for the home side. Scores of matches that are not `is_complete` may be provisional or zero.

vgi.example_queries.description: Test results from the 2026 autumn window.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT local_date, home_team_name, home_score, away_score, away_team_name FROM rugby.main.matches(start_date := DATE '2026-11-01', end_date := DATE '2026-11-10') WHERE competition ILIKE 'Nations Championship%' ORDER BY kickoff

vgi.example_queries.description: Nations Championship results from 1-10 November 2026 with each side's world ranking going in, joined on World Rugby team ids.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT m.local_date, m.home_team_name, m.home_score, m.away_score, m.away_team_name, h.position AS home_rank, a.position AS away_rank FROM rugby.main.matches(start_date := DATE '2026-11-01', end_date := DATE '2026-11-10') AS m JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-11-01') AS h ON h.wr_team_id = m.home_wr_team_id JOIN rugby.main.world_rankings(as_of := DATE '2026-11-01') AS a ON a.wr_team_id = m.away_wr_team_id WHERE m.competition = 'Nations Championship 2026' ORDER BY m.kickoff

workers.title: Salesforce CRM
workers.tagline: Salesforce objects via SOQL pushdown and Bulk API 2.0 as SQL in DuckDB (TypeScript)
workers.subtitle: Salesforce CRM as SQL: SOQL pushdown, Bulk API 2.0, describe-typed objects and a free ID toolkit.
workers.summary: Salesforce CRM as SQL: SOQL and Bulk API 2.0 scans with DuckDB filters pushed into SOQL, describe-typed object views, delete-aware incremental helpers, org metadata and limits, plus a credential-free Salesforce ID toolkit.
workers.doc_md:
# Salesforce CRM in DuckDB

Query a Salesforce org from SQL and join it to everything Salesforce reports cannot reach: product usage, billing, support data in local files. DuckDB predicates and projections become SOQL, so a six-column query against a 900-field object fetches six fields; large scans run as Bulk API 2.0 jobs whose `Sforce-Locator` is a resumable cursor; and column types come from the org's own describe metadata.

The ID toolkit needs no org at all: it fixes the 15- versus 18-character id join in any exported CSV.

**Reference notes.** Scans stop at `quota_guard_pct` (ATTACH option, default 80) of the org's daily API allowance, which is shared with its production integrations. Delete-aware incremental helpers refuse windows older than the recycle-bin retention rather than return an incomplete delete set. Everything is read-only.

Setup (connected app, certificate, JWT bearer): https://github.com/Query-farm/vgi-salesforce#connect-an-org

Upstream references: the [Salesforce REST API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/), [SOQL and SOSL reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.soql_sosl.meta/soql_sosl/), [Bulk API 2.0](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_asynch.meta/api_asynch/), and [OAuth authorization flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.remoteaccess_oauth_flows.htm&type=5) for connected apps.

attach_options.name: objects
attach_options.description: Comma-separated object API names to expose as sobjects.<Object> views, e.g. 'Account,Contact,Opportunity,Invoice__c'. Empty (the default) gives the functions and meta tables only; browse meta.objects, then re-attach.

attach_options.name: quota_guard_pct
attach_options.description: Fail a scan before an API call once the org's daily API usage (Sforce-Limit-Info) reaches this percentage (1-100).

attach_options.description: Directory for the Bulk/REST scan journal used by resume := true and meta.jobs (default $XDG_STATE_HOME/vgi-salesforce).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Schema main holds the worker's functions. The ID toolkit is scalar and needs no secret: it normalises, validates and classifies Salesforce ids in exported files, and is the join fix for 15- versus 18-character ids. Everything else needs a salesforce secret. The scans take SOQL or an object name and return describe-typed rows; filters on their columns, the projected columns and Top-N limits become SOQL, and above bulk_threshold rows the read switches to a Bulk API 2.0 job. The per-id functions are LATERAL-friendly and batch 200 ids per API call. The incremental helpers return changed and deleted ids for a time window and refuse windows older than Salesforce's retention.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Start here with a downloaded report: the ID toolkit works on any id column with no secret and no network, and fixes the classic join where one system exports 15-character ids and another 18.

With a `salesforce` secret, the scans read records with columns typed from the org's describe metadata and push DuckDB filters, projections and Top-N limits into SOQL, so a six-column query against a 900-field object fetches six fields; above `bulk_threshold` rows they switch to Bulk API 2.0. The per-row lookups are LATERAL-friendly and batch 200 ids per API call. The incremental helpers make loads delete-aware within Salesforce's retention windows.

functions.name: soql
functions.comment: Run a SOQL query; the result is typed at bind time from the select list and the org's describe metadata

tags.vgi.doc_llm: soql(query, api := 'auto', include_deleted := false, bulk_threshold := 10000, bulk_page_size := 50000, resume := false) sends a SOQL query to Salesforce as written and returns typed columns derived at bind time from its field list and describe metadata. Column names: fields are mangled to snake case (Account.Owner.Name becomes account_owner_name); aggregates take their alias, or expr0, expr1 … when unaliased; a bare COUNT() gives one row with a count column. Supported items: fields, parent paths up to 5 levels, COUNT, COUNT_DISTINCT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, the CALENDAR_/FISCAL_/DAY_ date functions, GROUPING and FIELDS(STANDARD). Subqueries, TYPEOF, toLabel, convertCurrency and FIELDS(ALL) are rejected at bind. Prefer query_object or the sobjects views when DuckDB filters should be pushed down. Needs a salesforce secret.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## soql(query, …)

Runs a SOQL query with a typed result. The select list is parsed against a closed grammar (fields, parent paths, aggregates, date functions, `FIELDS(STANDARD)`); anything else is a bind error naming the item.

tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
### Object scan (query_object, sobjects views, lookup)

One column per field of the object, typed from describe and named by the mangling rule (see meta.columns). For Opportunity, for example:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | VARCHAR | The record id (18 characters). |
| stage_name | VARCHAR | StageName (picklist). |
| amount | DECIMAL(16,2) | Amount (currency, precision and scale from describe). |
| close_date | DATE | CloseDate. |
| is_won | BOOLEAN | IsWon. |
| system_modstamp | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Last system change, the incremental watermark. |

### SOQL query (soql)

One column per select item. For SOQL selecting StageName, Account.Owner.Name, COUNT(Id) and SUM(Amount) total:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| stage_name | VARCHAR | A plain field, typed from describe. |
| account_owner_name | VARCHAR | A parent relationship path, flattened with underscores. |
| expr0 | BIGINT | An unaliased aggregate, numbered as the API numbers it. |
| total | DOUBLE | An aliased SUM/AVG (MIN/MAX keep the field's type). |
tags.vgi.title: Run a SOQL Query

arguments.name: query
arguments.description: A SOQL query. Select items: fields, parent paths (Account.Owner.Name), COUNT(), COUNT/COUNT_DISTINCT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX(f), date functions (CALENDAR_YEAR(f) …), GROUPING(f), FIELDS(STANDARD). Anything else is a bind error.

arguments.name: api
arguments.description: 'auto' (REST, switching to Bulk API 2.0 above bulk_threshold rows), 'rest' or 'bulk'. Aggregates are REST-only.

arguments.name: bulk_page_size
arguments.description: Records per Bulk API 2.0 results page (maxRecords); each page is one Sforce-Locator step.

arguments.name: bulk_threshold
arguments.description: In api 'auto', the totalSize above which the scan moves to a Bulk API 2.0 job.

arguments.name: include_deleted
arguments.description: Include soft-deleted and archived rows (queryAll).

arguments.name: resume
arguments.description: Continue an unfinished journalled scan of the same query from its saved Bulk job + locator.

examples: SELECT stage_name, deals, total FROM salesforce.main.soql('SELECT StageName, COUNT(Id) deals, SUM(Amount) total FROM Opportunity GROUP BY StageName') WHERE deals > 1 ORDER BY total DESC
SELECT name, account_name, account_owner_name FROM salesforce.main.soql('SELECT Name, Account.Name, Account.Owner.Name FROM Contact WHERE Email != null') ORDER BY name

functions.name: query_object
functions.comment: Rows of one Salesforce object, typed from its describe, with SQL filters, projection and LIMIT pushed into SOQL

tags.vgi.doc_llm: query_object(object_name, fields := NULL, where_clause := NULL, modified_after := NULL, modified_before := NULL, order_by := NULL, max_rows := NULL, api := 'auto', include_deleted := false, bulk_threshold := 10000, resume := false) returns the rows of one Salesforce object (Account, Opportunity, Invoice__c …) with one typed column per field, named lower snake case (StageName → stage_name, Acme__Score__c → acme_score, Account.Name → account_name). Types come from describe: ids/strings `VARCHAR`, currency/percent/double `DECIMAL(p,s)`, date `DATE`, datetime `TIMESTAMPTZ`, boolean `BOOLEAN`, multipicklist `VARCHAR[]`, address/geolocation `STRUCT`. WHERE filters on columns become SOQL WHERE (=, IN, IS NULL, numeric/date/datetime ranges, LIKE prefixes/contains); only the selected columns are fetched; modified_after/modified_before bound SystemModstamp for incremental loads. Use the sobjects.<Object> views for the same thing as a table. Needs a salesforce secret.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## query_object(object_name, …)

One Salesforce object as typed rows. See the README for the full pushdown table.

**Pushdown:** projection → SOQL SELECT list; `=`/`IN`/`IS [NOT] NULL` on any filterable field, numeric/date/datetime ranges, `LIKE 'x%'`/`starts_with`/`contains` → SOQL WHERE (string `!=`/ranges are re-applied locally because SOQL compares strings case-insensitively); `ORDER BY … LIMIT n` → SOQL when every filter translated exactly.

**Resume:** scans are ordered by SystemModstamp, Id, so an expired Bulk job or REST cursor is recovered with `SystemModstamp >= last` plus Id de-duplication.

vgi.example_queries.description: Open pipeline by stage (only StageName and Amount are fetched)
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT stage_name, count(*) AS deals, sum(amount) AS pipeline FROM salesforce.main.query_object('Opportunity', fields := ['StageName', 'Amount']) WHERE NOT is_closed GROUP BY stage_name ORDER BY pipeline DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Incremental extract: accounts changed since a watermark
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT id, name, system_modstamp FROM salesforce.main.query_object('Account', fields := ['Id', 'Name', 'SystemModstamp'], modified_after := TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-01 00:00:00+00') ORDER BY system_modstamp

tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:

One column per field of the object, typed from describe and named by the mangling rule (see meta.columns). For Opportunity, for example:

| Name | Type | Description |

| id | VARCHAR | The record id (18 characters). |
| stage_name | VARCHAR | StageName (picklist). |
| amount | DECIMAL(16,2) | Amount (currency, precision and scale from describe). |
| close_date | DATE | CloseDate. |
| is_won | BOOLEAN | IsWon. |
| system_modstamp | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | Last system change, the incremental watermark. |

One column per select item. For SOQL selecting StageName, Account.Owner.Name, COUNT(Id) and SUM(Amount) total:

| Name | Type | Description |

| account_owner_name | VARCHAR | A parent relationship path, flattened with underscores. |

functions.comment: Ids of records of an object deleted in a time window (REST getDeleted); errors outside recycle-bin retention

tags.vgi.doc_llm: deleted_ids(object_name, start_date, end_date) returns sf_id and deleted_date for every record of the object deleted in the window, via /sobjects/<o>/deleted. vgi.categories.name: metadata
vgi.categories.title: Metadata
vgi.categories.description: Describe metadata, org limits, Bulk jobs, users and access.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Schema meta exposes a Salesforce org's metadata as tables, all behind the salesforce secret. Use it to discover which objects exist before re-attaching with OBJECTS, to map Salesforce field names to the worker's snake_case column names, to audit who has which access, and to check the remaining daily API allowance before a large extract. Describe-based tables cover the objects in the ATTACH OBJECTS list. The Bulk job table merges the org's Bulk API 2.0 query jobs with this worker's resume journal.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## meta

Org metadata as tables, all behind the `salesforce` secret: what the org contains, how its fields map to column names, and who can see what.

Operational tables sit alongside: check the daily API request allowance before a large extract (scans also stop on their own at `quota_guard_pct`), and inspect Bulk API 2.0 jobs together with this worker's resume journal.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: sobjects has one view per object named in the ATTACH OBJECTS option (e.g. OBJECTS 'Account,Opportunity,Invoice__c'). Filtering a view, for example on stage_name = 'Closed Won', pushes the filter and the selected columns into SOQL. tags.vgi.doc_md:
## sobjects

One view per object in the ATTACH `OBJECTS` list, e.g. `OBJECTS 'Account,Opportunity,Invoice__c'`. Each view is `query_object('<Object>')`, so filters, projections and Top-N limits are pushed into SOQL.

Views cost nothing at ATTACH: an object's describe is fetched the first time a query binds it and cached for an hour. Without `OBJECTS` the schema is empty — browse `meta.objects`, then re-attach with the objects you want.

workers.title: SAML Forensics
workers.tagline: Parse and verify SAML in DuckDB with SQL — XML-DSig / C14N signature validation and golden-SAML / XML-signature-wrapping detection. A VGI worker.
workers.subtitle: Decode SAML 2.0 messages, verify their XML signatures, and flag XSW and Golden-SAML attacks in bulk.
workers.summary: SAML 2.0 decode + XML-DSig / exclusive-C14N signature verification + XSW / Golden-SAML detection, in SQL.
workers.doc_md:
# SAML — Decode, Signature Verification & Attack Detection in SQL

**Shred and security-check SAML 2.0 single-sign-on messages directly in DuckDB.** The `saml` worker base64-decodes (and, for the HTTP-Redirect binding, raw-DEFLATE inflates) a column of `SAMLResponse` blobs, decodes them into typed rows — subject, issuer, audience, the `Conditions` validity window, `AuthnContext`, and attribute statements — and, more importantly, runs the **XML-DSig** structural check the one-off tools only do one message at a time: exclusive XML canonicalization (`xml-exc-c14n#`), per-`Reference` digest verification, and signature math (RSA / ECDSA / EdDSA) against the **embedded** certificate.

The defensible value is **bulk security compute**: running **XML Signature Wrapping (XSW)** and **Golden-SAML** detection across millions of historical SAML messages in a forensic lake — in SQL, joinable against your IdP cert inventory and login telemetry. The worker flags the structural invariants every XSW1-XSW8 attack violates (multiple assertions, a signature that covers a different element than the consumer reads, duplicate/dangling reference IDs, an unsigned assertion inside a signed response, comment-splitting NameIDs, digest mismatches), and surfaces the signer certificate SHA-256 fingerprint so a left join against your known-good IdP certs surfaces the Golden-SAML smoking gun (a cryptographically perfect signature from a key you do not trust).

**Trust stays with you.** `sig_valid = true` means the embedded cert signed these bytes — never that the cert is authorized. The worker holds no private keys, no trust store, makes no network calls, and decrypts nothing; an `EncryptedAssertion` is counted and flagged, not opened. All decode and canonicalization is local CPU on bytes you already hold, so it is safe for air-gapped / regulated forensic data.

**Hardened against hostile input.** Every blob is attacker-controlled, so the XML loader rejects DTDs and entities unparsed (defeating XXE and billion-laughs/exponential-entity-expansion), bounds document size and inflate ratio (DEFLATE-bomb guard), and never panics — a hostile message returns an error verdict, it does not crash the scan. A well-formedness triage verdict reports the reason, and its dtd-present / entity-blocked kinds double as XXE and billion-laughs signals.

**When to reach for it.** Use it whenever you already hold a column of raw or encoded SAML messages and need to shred, verify, or threat-hunt over them at warehouse scale rather than one message at a time in a browser plugin. The signer certificate SHA-256 fingerprint left-joins against your IdP cert inventory, and decoded NameIDs can be scrubbed before sharing extracts when the source data is sensitive.

## Sources and references

- [OASIS SAML V2.0 standard](https://docs.oasis-open.org/security/saml/v2.0/) — the core assertion/protocol schemas and the HTTP-Redirect / HTTP-POST bindings the decoder follows.
- [W3C XML Signature Syntax and Processing 1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmldsig-core1/) — the XML-DSig `Signature` / `SignedInfo` / `Reference` model that is verified.
- [W3C Exclusive XML Canonicalization 1.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-exc-c14n/) — the `xml-exc-c14n#` transform applied before digesting and signature checks.

example_queries.description: Identify a SAML message by its root element.
example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.message_type('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"/>') AS kind

example_queries.description: Triage why a blob is not a usable SAML message.
example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.well_formed('not a saml message')).kind AS kind

example_queries.description: Decode an assertion and read its issuer.
example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.decode('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion>')).issuer AS issuer

example_queries.description: Base64-decode a SAMLResponse POST field to text.
example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.b64decode('PHNhbWw+')::VARCHAR AS decoded

example_queries.description: Count the structural anomaly flags on a message.
example_queries.sql: SELECT len(saml.main.anomalies('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"/>')) AS n

example_queries.description: XSW coverage check: list every assertion in a Response next to the signature (if any) whose Reference points at it; the wrapped evil assertion _evil shows no covering signature.
example_queries.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#" ID="_r"><saml:Assertion ID="_evil"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>admin@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><ds:Signature><ds:SignedInfo><ds:Reference URI="#_a1"/></ds:SignedInfo></ds:Signature><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion></samlp:Response>' AS msg), asr AS (SELECT a.* FROM m, UNNEST(saml.main.assertions(m.msg)) AS _(a)), sig AS (SELECT s.* FROM m, UNNEST(saml.main.signatures(m.msg)) AS _(s)) SELECT asr.idx, asr.id, asr.subject, sig.idx AS covering_signature FROM asr LEFT JOIN sig ON sig.references_id = asr.id ORDER BY asr.idx

example_queries.description: Triage a batch of blobs before decoding: well_formed classifies each one, and only the usable messages are passed on to message_type and decode for their issuer.
example_queries.sql: SELECT t.blob_id, (saml.main.well_formed(t.blob)).kind AS triage, CASE WHEN (saml.main.well_formed(t.blob)).ok THEN saml.main.message_type(t.blob) END AS msg_type, CASE WHEN (saml.main.well_formed(t.blob)).ok THEN (saml.main.decode(t.blob)).issuer END AS issuer FROM (VALUES (1, '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion>'), (2, 'not a saml message'), (3, '<!DOCTYPE x [<!ENTITY e SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"/>')) AS t(blob_id, blob) ORDER BY t.blob_id

example_queries.description: Per-login security verdict: who each message claims to be (decode), whether it carries a signature (signature), and which structural flags fire (anomalies); login-1 is signed but its digest does not match (digest-mismatch), login-2 is unsigned and carries two assertions (multiple-assertions).
example_queries.sql: WITH logins AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('login-1', '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><ds:Signature><ds:SignedInfo><ds:Reference URI="#_a"/></ds:SignedInfo></ds:Signature><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion>'), ('login-2', '<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_r"><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>bob@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion><saml:Assertion ID="_a2"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>admin@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion></samlp:Response>')) AS v(login_id, msg)) SELECT login_id, (saml.main.decode(msg)).subject AS subject, (saml.main.signature(msg)).signed AS signed, saml.main.anomalies(msg) AS flags FROM logins ORDER BY login_id

example_queries.description: Roll a multi-valued role attribute up per subject: decode supplies the NameID and the attributes fan-out supplies each role value.
example_queries.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject><saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute><saml:Attribute Name="dept"><saml:AttributeValue>finance</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement></saml:Assertion>' AS msg) SELECT (saml.main.decode(m.msg)).subject AS subject, list_sort(list(a.value)) AS roles FROM m, UNNEST(saml.main.attributes(m.msg)) AS _(a) WHERE a.name = 'role' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY subject

example_queries.description: Classify why a blob is not a usable SAML message (kind = 'bad-base64' here: text that is not XML is sniffed as a base64 transport wrapper).
example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.well_formed('not a saml message')).kind;

example_queries.description: Surface signature-wrapping / structural red flags (here, multiple-assertions) for a message.
example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.anomalies('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"/><saml:Assertion ID="_a2"/></samlp:Response>');

example_queries.description: Explode a multi-valued attribute to long form (one row per value).
example_queries.sql: SELECT a.name, a.value FROM UNNEST(saml.main.attributes('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement></saml:Assertion>')) AS _(a) ORDER BY a.value;

example_queries.description: Flag the multiple-assertions XSW indicator on a two-assertion Response.
example_queries.sql: SELECT list_contains(saml.main.anomalies('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_r"><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"/><saml:Assertion ID="_a2"/></samlp:Response>'), 'multiple-assertions') AS has_multi;

example_queries.description: Explode a multi-valued attribute into one row per value.
example_queries.sql: SELECT a.value AS value FROM UNNEST(saml.main.attributes('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement></saml:Assertion>')) AS _(a) ORDER BY a.value;

example_queries.description: Read the AuthnContext class (e.g. detect MFA downgrade).
example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.authn('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:AuthnStatement><saml:AuthnContext><saml:AuthnContextClassRef>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport</saml:AuthnContextClassRef></saml:AuthnContext></saml:AuthnStatement></saml:Assertion>')).class_ref;

example_queries.description: Decode a base64 SAMLResponse form field to raw bytes.
example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.b64decode('PHNhbWw+');

example_queries.description: Enumerate assertions and their parents to reveal wrapping.
example_queries.sql: SELECT a.idx, a.id, a.parent FROM UNNEST(saml.main.assertions('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"/></samlp:Response>')) AS _(a) ORDER BY a.idx;

example_queries.description: Base64-decode then raw-DEFLATE-inflate a redirect-binding SAMLRequest to its XML text.
example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.inflate(saml.main.b64decode('sylOzM0psHIsLcnIC0otLE0tLlGoyM3JK7YCS9gqlRblWeUnFmcWW+Ul5qYWW5UkWwU7+vpYGekZWBUU5ZfkJ+fnKCl4utgqxRcZKunbAQA='));

example_queries.description: Read the assertion validity window for an own-skew expiry check.
example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.conditions('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:Conditions NotBefore="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2026-01-01T01:00:00Z"/></saml:Assertion>')).not_on_or_after;

example_queries.description: Check whether a SAML message's embedded signature is internally valid (false here — the assertion is unsigned).
example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.signature('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion>')).sig_valid;

example_queries.description: Identify the kind of a SAML message from its root element.
example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.message_type('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"/>');

example_queries.description: Decode a SAML assertion to its subject + core fields.
example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.decode('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion>')).subject;

example_queries.description: Enumerate every signature and its scope to spot wrapping.
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.idx, s.scope, s.sig_valid FROM UNNEST(saml.main.signatures('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"><ds:Signature><ds:SignedInfo><ds:Reference URI="#_a1"/></ds:SignedInfo></ds:Signature><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"/></samlp:Response>')) AS _(s) ORDER BY s.idx;

example_queries.description: Recover the XML from a URL-encoded, base64-wrapped transport parameter.
example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.unwrap('PHNhbWxwOlJlc3BvbnNlIHhtbG5zOnNhbWxwPSJ1cm46b2FzaXM6bmFtZXM6dGM6U0FNTDoyLjA6cHJvdG9jb2wiLz4%3D');

XML: '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:AuthnStatement AuthnInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"><saml:AuthnContext><saml:AuthnContextClassRef>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport</saml:AuthnContextClassRef></saml:AuthnContext></saml:AuthnStatement></saml:Assertion>'.
Base64-decode the string 'PHNhbWw+' and return its UTF-8 text as one column named decoded.

Does this assertion's Conditions validity window stay open past the start of 2030? Return one boolean column named expires_after_2030. XML: '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Conditions NotBefore="2020-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2035-06-01T00:00:00Z"><saml:AudienceRestriction><saml:Audience>https://sp.example.com</saml:Audience></saml:AudienceRestriction></saml:Conditions></saml:Assertion>'.

Is the embedded XML-DSig signature on this assertion internally valid? Return one boolean column named sig_valid. XML: '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion>'.

Recover the SAML XML from this URL-encoded, base64-wrapped transport parameter and return it as one column named xml. Value: 'PHNhbWxwOlJlc3BvbnNlIHhtbG5zOnNhbWxwPSJ1cm46b2FzaXM6bmFtZXM6dGM6U0FNTDoyLjA6cHJvdG9jb2wiLz4%3D'.

Return one VARCHAR column named assertion_id holding its ID. XML: '<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#" ID="_r"><ds:Signature><ds:SignedInfo><ds:Reference URI="#_a1"/></ds:SignedInfo></ds:Signature><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion><saml:Assertion ID="_a2"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion><saml:Assertion ID="_a3"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><ds:Signature><ds:SignedInfo><ds:Reference URI="#_a3"/></ds:SignedInfo></ds:Signature></saml:Assertion></samlp:Response>'.

For this assertion, return its subject NameID and how many values its 'role' attribute has, as two columns: subject (VARCHAR) and n_roles (BIGINT). XML: '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>carol@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject><saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="dept"><saml:AttributeValue>it</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>auditor</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>helpdesk</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement></saml:Assertion>'.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: SAML decode and XML-DSig verification functions: decode a message to a struct, explode attribute statements, read the Conditions window and AuthnContext, verify the signature (exclusive C14N + embedded-cert math), enumerate signatures and assertions, flag XSW / Golden-SAML anomalies, triage well-formedness, and decode the base64/DEFLATE/URL transport.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
SAML 2.0 forensic decoding and XML-DSig verification, in-database.

## What it does

Turns an opaque SAML message — a base64 / DEFLATE / URL-encoded blob or raw XML — into typed, queryable rows, and independently re-verifies its cryptographic signature so you can trust (or distrust) what an identity provider asserted, without leaving SQL. Each capability is a separate function that takes one content-sniffed message argument (raw XML, base64, base64+DEFLATE, or a URL-encoded wrapper).

## Key concepts

- **Signature verification is real, not implied.** The outermost XML-DSig signature is re-checked here — SignedInfo is re-canonicalized with exclusive C14N, per-Reference digests are recomputed, and SignatureValue is verified (RSA / ECDSA / EdDSA) against the certificate embedded in the message itself. A validity result reports whether that embedded key signed these exact bytes; it never asserts the key is trusted, so Golden-SAML detection is a downstream JOIN of the signer certificate SHA-256 fingerprint against your own IdP cert inventory. No key store, no network egress.
- **Attack detection.** Structural red flags for XML Signature Wrapping (XSW) and Golden-SAML — multiple assertions, a signature that covers a different element than the consumer reads, duplicate/dangling reference IDs, digest mismatches, comment-splitting NameIDs — surface tampering a naive parser misses.
- **Hostile-input safety.** Every entry point is total and panic-free, with DTD / entity expansion disabled (defeating XXE and billion-laughs) and decompression bomb-bounded.

## When to use

Reach for this schema to audit or bulk-scan SAML responses and assertions offline: confirming who signed a message, reading its subject / issuer / audience / validity window / AuthnContext / attribute statements, checking whether its signature holds, and flagging attack fingerprints — over millions of historical messages, joinable against your cert inventory and login telemetry.

vgi.example_queries.description: Identify a SAML message by its root element.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.message_type('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"/>') AS kind

vgi.example_queries.description: Triage why a blob is not a usable SAML message.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.well_formed('not a saml message')).kind AS kind

vgi.example_queries.description: Decode an assertion and read its issuer.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT (saml.main.decode('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion>')).issuer AS issuer

vgi.example_queries.description: Base64-decode a SAMLResponse POST field to text.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.b64decode('PHNhbWw+')::VARCHAR AS decoded

vgi.example_queries.description: Count the structural anomaly flags on a message.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT len(saml.main.anomalies('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"/>')) AS n

vgi.example_queries.description: XSW coverage check: list every assertion in a Response next to the signature (if any) whose Reference points at it; the wrapped evil assertion _evil shows no covering signature.
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#" ID="_r"><saml:Assertion ID="_evil"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>admin@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><ds:Signature><ds:SignedInfo><ds:Reference URI="#_a1"/></ds:SignedInfo></ds:Signature><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion></samlp:Response>' AS msg), asr AS (SELECT a.* FROM m, UNNEST(saml.main.assertions(m.msg)) AS _(a)), sig AS (SELECT s.* FROM m, UNNEST(saml.main.signatures(m.msg)) AS _(s)) SELECT asr.idx, asr.id, asr.subject, sig.idx AS covering_signature FROM asr LEFT JOIN sig ON sig.references_id = asr.id ORDER BY asr.idx

vgi.example_queries.description: Triage a batch of blobs before decoding: well_formed classifies each one, and only the usable messages are passed on to message_type and decode for their issuer.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT t.blob_id, (saml.main.well_formed(t.blob)).kind AS triage, CASE WHEN (saml.main.well_formed(t.blob)).ok THEN saml.main.message_type(t.blob) END AS msg_type, CASE WHEN (saml.main.well_formed(t.blob)).ok THEN (saml.main.decode(t.blob)).issuer END AS issuer FROM (VALUES (1, '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer></saml:Assertion>'), (2, 'not a saml message'), (3, '<!DOCTYPE x [<!ENTITY e SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"/>')) AS t(blob_id, blob) ORDER BY t.blob_id

vgi.example_queries.description: Per-login security verdict: who each message claims to be (decode), whether it carries a signature (signature), and which structural flags fire (anomalies); login-1 is signed but its digest does not match (digest-mismatch), login-2 is unsigned and carries two assertions (multiple-assertions).
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH logins AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('login-1', '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#" ID="_a"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><ds:Signature><ds:SignedInfo><ds:Reference URI="#_a"/></ds:SignedInfo></ds:Signature><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion>'), ('login-2', '<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_r"><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>bob@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion><saml:Assertion ID="_a2"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>admin@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject></saml:Assertion></samlp:Response>')) AS v(login_id, msg)) SELECT login_id, (saml.main.decode(msg)).subject AS subject, (saml.main.signature(msg)).signed AS signed, saml.main.anomalies(msg) AS flags FROM logins ORDER BY login_id

vgi.example_queries.description: Roll a multi-valued role attribute up per subject: decode supplies the NameID and the attributes fan-out supplies each role value.
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject><saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute><saml:Attribute Name="dept"><saml:AttributeValue>finance</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement></saml:Assertion>' AS msg) SELECT (saml.main.decode(m.msg)).subject AS subject, list_sort(list(a.value)) AS roles FROM m, UNNEST(saml.main.attributes(m.msg)) AS _(a) WHERE a.name = 'role' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY subject

functions.name: well_formed
functions.comment: Triage a SAML blob into STRUCT(ok BOOL, kind VARCHAR, detail VARCHAR); kind is one of ok / not-xml / not-saml / bad-base64 / bad-deflate / dtd-present / entity-blocked / truncated / encoding-error. Never panics.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Classify an attacker-controlled blob into a (ok, kind, detail) triage verdict without ever panicking. `kind` is one of ok, not-xml, not-saml, bad-base64, bad-deflate, dtd-present, entity-blocked, truncated, or encoding-error. The dtd-present and entity-blocked kinds double as XXE / billion-laughs signals: the hardened loader rejects any DOCTYPE/entity before it can be expanded, so their presence is reported rather than processed.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Triage a SAML blob into `(ok, kind, detail)`; `dtd-present`/`entity-blocked` flag XXE / billion-laughs attempts.

functions.name: anomalies
functions.comment: Flag XSW (XML Signature Wrapping) / Golden-SAML / structural anomalies as a LIST<VARCHAR>; empty list = no structural red flag found (not a safety guarantee)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Return the structural anomaly flags for a SAML message as a `LIST(VARCHAR)`. These are the invariants every XML Signature Wrapping (XSW1-XSW8) attack violates plus the XXE-class text-extraction tells: multiple-assertions, signature-covers-other-element, reference-uri-id-mismatch, unsigned-assertion-in-signed-response, signature-placement-anomaly, detached-signature, nameid-comment-splitting, digest-mismatch, c14n-inclusive-on-moved-assertion, and encrypted-assertion-present. An EMPTY list is not a safety guarantee — Golden SAML (a forgery with a stolen but valid IdP key) leaves no structural trace, so combine this with a trust-table JOIN on signer_cert_sha256.
tags.vgi.doc_md: List XSW / structural red flags for a SAML message (e.g. `multiple-assertions`, `signature-covers-other-element`, `digest-mismatch`); empty != safe.

vgi.example_queries.description: Surface signature-wrapping / structural red flags (here, multiple-assertions) for a message.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT saml.main.anomalies('<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:Assertion ID="_a1"/><saml:Assertion ID="_a2"/></samlp:Response>');

functions.name: attributes
functions.comment: Explode SAML attribute statements to a LIST<STRUCT> (statement_idx, name, name_format, friendly_name, value, value_type); UNNEST to long form

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Return a SAML assertion's AttributeStatement(s) as a `LIST(STRUCT(statement_idx, name, name_format, friendly_name, value, value_type))`, one struct per AttributeValue. UNNEST it over a column to explode attributes to long form, so multi-valued attributes (roles, groups) fan out into one row each and can be pivoted or joined downstream. Returns an empty list for a message with no attributes and NULL for a NULL input.
tags.vgi.doc_md: Return SAML attribute values as a `LIST<STRUCT(statement_idx, name, name_format, friendly_name, value, value_type)>`; UNNEST to explode to long form.

vgi.example_queries.description: Explode a multi-valued attribute to long form (one row per value).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT a.name, a.value FROM UNNEST(saml.main.attributes('<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"><saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement></saml:Assertion>')) AS _(a) ORDER BY a.value;

vgi.example_queries.description: Roll a multi-valued role attribute up per subject: decode supplies the NameID and the attributes fan-out supplies each role value.
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_a"><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject><saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute><saml:Attribute Name="dept"><saml:AttributeValue>finance</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement></saml:Assertion>' AS msg) SELECT (saml.main.decode(m.msg)).subject AS subject, list_sort(list(a.value)) AS roles FROM m, UNNEST(saml.main.attributes(m.msg)) AS _(a) WHERE a.name = 'role' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY subject

functions.comment: Extract the AuthnStatement + AuthnContext: STRUCT(authn_instant TIMESTAMPTZ, session_index VARCHAR, session_not_on_or_after TIMESTAMPTZ, class_ref VARCHAR, decl_ref VARCHAR, authenticating_authority VARCHAR)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Extract a SAML assertion's AuthnStatement and AuthnContext as a struct: the AuthnInstant and SessionNotOnOrAfter (`TIMESTAMPTZ`, UTC), the SessionIndex, the AuthnContextClassRef / DeclRef (the authentication method, e.g. PasswordProtectedTransport vs an MFA class — useful for spotting downgrades), and any AuthenticatingAuthority. Returns NULL when there is no AuthnStatement.

functions.name: b64decode
functions.comment: Base64-decode a string to bytes (accepts standard and URL-safe alphabets, padded or not); NULL on failure

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a base64 string to a `BLOB`, accepting both the standard (`+/`) and URL-safe (`-_`) alphabets, padded or unpadded. This is the HTTP-POST-binding step: a SAMLResponse form field is base64 of the XML (or of DEFLATE-compressed XML for the redirect binding). Returns NULL when the input is not valid base64.
