tables.name: members
tables.comment: Every member of Congress since 1789, one row per person, keyed by bioguide_id, with cross-walk IDs.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per person who has served in the US House or Senate since 1789 (about 12,800 rows), keyed by bioguide_id. Columns: names, birthday, gender, is_current (serving now), first_term_start, last_term_end, term counts per chamber, the latest term's chamber/state/party, and cross-walk IDs (thomas_id, lis_id for Senate votes, govtrack_id, icpsr_id for Voteview, opensecrets_id, votesmart_id, fec_ids list, cspan_id, wikidata_id, ...). For who served when, which state, district or party at a date, use member_terms instead. No API key needed.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## members

One row per member of Congress since 1789, keyed by `bioguide_id`, with the identifiers other datasets use (ICPSR, GovTrack, FEC, OpenSecrets, Wikidata). Source: [unitedstates/congress-legislators](https://github.com/unitedstates/congress-legislators) (CC0 public domain), downloaded on first scan and cached; refreshed after the cache TTL.

functions.name: rollcalls

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Roll-call votes from Voteview, one row per vote, House and Senate, from the 1st Congress (1789) to today. rollcalls(congress) reads one Congress; rollcalls() with no argument reads every Congress (a 30 MB download). chamber := 'house' or 'senate' limits to one chamber. Key: (congress, chamber, rollnumber); rollnumber is Voteview's sequential number, clerk_rollnumber the clerk's per-session number (matches senate_votes.vote_number). Columns include date, session, majority_requirement, yea_count, nay_count, bill_number ('HR2882', 'S5', nominations 'PN...'), vote_result, vote_desc, vote_question and DW-NOMINATE cutting-line parameters. Join member_votes on (congress, chamber, rollnumber) for individual positions. No API key needed.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## rollcalls(congress, chamber := NULL) / rollcalls(chamber := NULL)

Every House and Senate roll call since 1789 with tallies, the question and the result. Source: [Voteview](https://voteview.com/data), updated as votes are taken; files are cached per user. functions.name: bills
functions.comment: List bills and resolutions from Congress.gov, newest update first, with filters pushed into the API

tags.vgi.doc_llm: List bills and resolutions from Congress.gov, most recently updated first. Narrow it with congress := N and bill_type := 'hr' | 's' | 'hjres' | 'sjres' | 'hconres' | 'sconres' | 'hres' | 'sres', or with WHERE congress = N AND bill_type = '...' (pushed into the request path) and WHERE update_date >= / <= `TIMESTAMPTZ` (pushed as fromDateTime/toDateTime). Without a congress filter it pages through every bill since 1973, 250 per request, so always filter or LIMIT. Columns: congress, bill_type, bill_number, bill_id ('hr2882-118'), title, origin_chamber, introduced_date, latest_action_date, latest_action_text, update_date. For sponsor, policy area and status use bill(congress, bill_type, bill_number). tags.vgi.doc_md:
## member_ideology(congress, chamber := NULL) / member_ideology(chamber := NULL)

DW-NOMINATE and Nokken-Poole ideology scores for every member of every Congress. Source: [Voteview](https://voteview.com/data), updated as votes are taken; files are cached per user. vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT congress, round(median(nominate_dim1) FILTER (WHERE party_code = 200) - median(nominate_dim1) FILTER (WHERE party_code = 100), 3) AS gap FROM us_congress.main.member_ideology(chamber := 'senate') WHERE congress >= 100 GROUP BY congress ORDER BY congress

functions.name: member_votes
functions.comment: How every member voted on every roll call of one Congress, from Voteview, with bioguide IDs

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per member per roll call for one Congress (required positional argument; the House alone has about 300,000 rows per Congress). chamber := 'house' or 'senate' limits to one chamber and one download. Columns: congress, chamber, rollnumber (join rollcalls on congress, chamber, rollnumber), icpsr, bioguide_id (join members/member_terms), cast_code (0-9), vote (simplified: 'Yea', 'Nay', 'Present', 'Not Voting', 'Not a member'), vote_detail ('Paired Yea', 'Announced Nay', ...) and prob. Count vote = 'Yea' per member for voting records; compare with the party majority for party-unity scores. No API key needed.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## member_votes(congress, chamber := NULL)

Each member's position on each roll call, with cast codes decoded and bioguide IDs attached. Source: [Voteview](https://voteview.com/data), updated as votes are taken; files are cached per user. Please cite: Lewis, Jeffrey B., Keith Poole, Howard Rosenthal, Adam Boche, Aaron Rudkin, and Luke Sonnet. Voteview: Congressional Roll-Call Votes Database. https://voteview.com/

vgi.example_queries.description: Senators who missed the most roll calls in the 118th Congress
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT bioguide_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE vote = 'Not Voting') AS missed, count(*) AS votes FROM us_congress.main.member_votes(118, chamber := 'senate') GROUP BY bioguide_id ORDER BY missed DESC LIMIT 5

vgi.example_queries.description: How the Senate split on the first roll call of the 119th Congress
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT v.vote, count(*) AS members FROM us_congress.main.member_votes(119, chamber := 'senate') v WHERE v.rollnumber = 1 GROUP BY v.vote ORDER BY members DESC

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Return Voteview's label for a cast code: 0 'Not a member', 1 'Yea', 2 'Paired Yea', 3 'Announced Yea', 4 'Announced Nay', 5 'Paired Nay', 6 'Nay', 7 and 8 'Present (some Congresses)', 9 'Not Voting'. workers.doc_md:
# US Elections

**Certified US federal election results, House apportionment, congressional district maps and FEC campaign finance as DuckDB tables.**

- Results: [MIT Election Data + Science Lab](https://electionlab.mit.edu/data) on Harvard Dataverse (CC0): House, Senate and President 1976-2024, county-level President 2000-2024.
- Apportionment: [Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/data/tables/time-series/dec/apportionment-data-text.html) 1910-2020 (public domain).
- Districts: [Lewis et al., UCLA](https://cdmaps.polisci.ucla.edu/) (MIT licence) for the 1st-119th Congress and [Census cartographic boundaries](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for the 119th.
- Campaign finance: the [FEC OpenFEC API](https://api.open.fec.gov/developers/) (api.data.gov key).

Districts are two-digit text, `'00'` at-large; states carry both USPS and FIPS codes.
workers.readme_sql:
-- Who won each Senate race in 2024, and by how much?
SELECT state_po, candidate, party_simplified, round(100 * vote_share, 1) AS pct
FROM us_elections.main.senate_results
WHERE year = 2024 AND stage = 'gen' AND NOT special
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY state_po ORDER BY candidatevotes DESC) = 1
ORDER BY pct;

example_queries.description: Winners of Delaware's at-large House general elections since 2016
example_queries.sql: SELECT year, candidate, party_simplified, round(100 * vote_share, 1) AS pct FROM us_elections.main.house_results WHERE state_po = 'DE' AND stage = 'gen' AND year >= 2016 QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY candidatevotes DESC) = 1 ORDER BY year

example_queries.description: Winner and vote share of every 2024 regular general Senate race

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The `main` schema holds US federal election data. Result tables are read like ordinary tables and accept WHERE filters on year and state, which are applied before rows leave the worker. Boundary functions take a Congress number and an optional state and return polygons as GEOMETRY for spatial joins with the spatial extension. FEC functions page through the OpenFEC API and need a `us_elections_fec` secret holding an api.data.gov key. Use state_po or state_fips plus a two-digit district ('00' at-large) to join results, districts and finance; convert other spellings with the district normalizer. Vote shares are derived (candidatevotes / totalvotes); MEDSL rows include write-ins and, for some states, separate vote modes, so filter writein and mode as needed.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

US federal election results, seats, district maps and campaign finance.

- **Results** are tables; filter on `year` and `state_po` and they are narrowed in the worker.
- **Districts** are table functions returning `GEOMETRY('OGC:CRS84')`.
- **FEC** functions need an api.data.gov key in a secret:

```sql
CREATE SECRET fec (TYPE us_elections_fec, API_KEY 'your-key');
```

tables.name: apportionment
tables.comment: US House seats, population and seats change per state after each census, 1910-2020 (Census Bureau).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: US House seats per state after each decennial census 1910-2020, from the Census Bureau's historical apportionment file (public domain, bundled, no download). One row per (census_year, state) for states that had seats: census_year, state, state_po, state_fips, seats, seat_change (vs the previous census), resident_population, population_change_pct, population_density, avg_population_per_seat. Seats from census year Y apply to Congresses elected from Y+2 (2020 census -> 2022 elections -> 118th Congress). Electoral votes = seats + 2. 1920 had no reapportionment. Earlier censuses (1790-1900) are only published as PDF and are not included.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## apportionment

House seats per state after each census, 1910-2020, from the [Census Bureau](https://www.census.gov/data/tables/time-series/dec/apportionment-data-text.html) (public domain).

vgi.example_queries.description: States that gained House seats in the 2020 apportionment
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT state_po, seats, seat_change FROM us_elections.main.apportionment WHERE census_year = 2020 AND seat_change > 0 ORDER BY seat_change DESC, state_po

vgi.example_queries.description: California's House seats after each census since 1950
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT census_year, seats FROM us_elections.main.apportionment WHERE state_po = 'CA' AND census_year >= 1950 ORDER BY census_year

vgi.example_queries.description: Total House seats: 433 after 1910 (Arizona and New Mexico added 2 on admission), then 435
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT census_year, sum(seats) AS house_seats FROM us_elections.main.apportionment WHERE census_year IN (1910, 1960, 2020) GROUP BY census_year ORDER BY census_year

vgi.executable_examples.description: States that gained House seats in the 2020 apportionment
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT state_po, seats, seat_change FROM us_elections.main.apportionment WHERE census_year = 2020 AND seat_change > 0 ORDER BY seat_change DESC, state_po

vgi.executable_examples.description: California's House seats after each census since 1950
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT census_year, seats FROM us_elections.main.apportionment WHERE state_po = 'CA' AND census_year >= 1950 ORDER BY census_year

vgi.executable_examples.description: Total House seats: 433 after 1910 (Arizona and New Mexico added 2 on admission), then 435
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT census_year, sum(seats) AS house_seats FROM us_elections.main.apportionment WHERE census_year IN (1910, 1960, 2020) GROUP BY census_year ORDER BY census_year

tables.name: senate_results
tables.comment: US Senate returns by state, 1976-2024: one row per candidate per contest (MEDSL, CC0).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: State-level US Senate election returns 1976-2024 from the MIT Election Data + Science Lab (CC0). One row per candidate per contest: year, congress (derived), state, state_po, state_fips, stage ('gen', 'pre', 'runoff'), special, candidate, party_detailed, party_simplified, writein, mode, candidatevotes, totalvotes, vote_share (derived), unofficial, version. A state can hold a regular and a special Senate election in the same year: partition by (year, state_po, special). WHERE filters on year, state_po, state_fips and congress are applied inside the worker before rows are sent; other filters are applied exactly too, just after a full read of the cached file.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## senate_results

US Senate returns by state, 1976-2024, from the [MIT Election Lab](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/PEJ5QU) (CC0). Regular and special contests in the same year are separate (`special`).

vgi.example_queries.description: Winner and vote share of every 2024 regular general Senate race
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT state_po, candidate, party_simplified, round(100 * vote_share, 1) AS pct FROM us_elections.main.senate_results WHERE year = 2024 AND stage = 'gen' AND NOT special QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY state_po ORDER BY candidatevotes DESC) = 1 ORDER BY state_po

vgi.example_queries.description: Delaware Senate general-election results in 2024
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT candidate, party_detailed, candidatevotes, round(100 * vote_share, 2) AS pct FROM us_elections.main.senate_results WHERE year = 2024 AND state_po = 'DE' AND stage = 'gen' ORDER BY candidatevotes DESC

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: congress

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Two-digit FIPS state code as VARCHAR with the leading zero ('06').

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Election stage, lower case: 'gen' (general), 'pre' (primary) or 'runoff'.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: special

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Party label exactly as on the ballot or in the official return ('DEMOCRATIC-FARMER-LABOR').

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Simplified party: DEMOCRAT, REPUBLICAN, LIBERTARIAN or OTHER.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: writein
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: TRUE for write-in candidates (including aggregated 'scattering' rows).

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: mode
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Vote mode, lower case: 'total' for most rows; some states report election-day/absentee/early separately.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: candidatevotes
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Votes for this candidate in this contest (and mode).

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: totalvotes
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Total votes cast in the contest (all candidates); the denominator of vote_share.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: vote_share
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: Derived fraction (0 to 1) of the contest's votes: candidatevotes / totalvotes; NULL when totalvotes is 0.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: unofficial
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: TRUE when MEDSL marked the count unofficial (not yet certified when compiled).

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: version
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: MEDSL's version stamp for the row's source vintage (e.g. '20250203').

tables.name: county_president_results
tables.comment: US presidential returns by county, 2000-2024, with five-digit county FIPS codes (MEDSL, CC0).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: County-level US presidential returns 2000-2024 from the MIT Election Data + Science Lab (CC0). One row per candidate per county per vote mode: year, state, state_po, state_fips, county_name, county_fips (five-digit `VARCHAR`, joins to Census county data), candidate, party (DEMOCRAT, REPUBLICAN, LIBERTARIAN, GREEN, OTHER), mode, candidatevotes, totalvotes, vote_share (derived), version. Most counties report mode = 'total'; some states (e.g. 2020 GA, NC) report only per-mode rows, so sum over modes when no 'total' row exists and never add 'total' to the others. WHERE filters on year, state_po, state_fips and county_fips are applied inside the worker before rows are sent; other filters are applied exactly too, just after a full read of the cached file. Harvard Dataverse requires a guestbook response (name, email, institution, position) to download this file: ATTACH with GUESTBOOK_NAME, GUESTBOOK_EMAIL, GUESTBOOK_INSTITUTION and GUESTBOOK_POSITION, or save a browser download into the cache (see cache_info()).

## house_results

US House returns by district, 1976-2024, from the [MIT Election Lab](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/IG0UN2) (CC0).

- `district` is two-digit text; `'00'` means at-large.
- Fusion candidates have one row per party line.
- The Dataverse file needs a guestbook response to download; see the README.

vgi.example_queries.description: Winners of Delaware's at-large House general elections since 2016
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT year, candidate, party_simplified, round(100 * vote_share, 1) AS pct FROM us_elections.main.house_results WHERE state_po = 'DE' AND stage = 'gen' AND year >= 2016 QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY candidatevotes DESC) = 1 ORDER BY year

vgi.example_queries.description: Two-party House popular vote by year
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT year, sum(candidatevotes) FILTER (WHERE party_simplified = 'DEMOCRAT') AS dem, sum(candidatevotes) FILTER (WHERE party_simplified = 'REPUBLICAN') AS rep FROM us_elections.main.house_results WHERE stage = 'gen' AND year >= 2016 GROUP BY year ORDER BY year

functions.name: districts
functions.comment: Congressional district boundaries for any Congress from 1789 to today, as GEOMETRY

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Boundaries of every US congressional district in force in one Congress, 1st (1789) through 119th (2025-2027), from Lewis, DeVine, Pritcher and Martis's UCLA district boundary files (MIT licence). Positional argument: congress (`INTEGER` 1-119). Named: state := 'DE' (USPS code, FIPS code or name); strongly recommended, because each state is a separate download of up to 14 MB the first time. Columns: congress, state, state_po, state_fips, district (two-digit `VARCHAR`, '00' at-large), start_congress, end_congress, district_id, law, note, geometry (GEOMETRY('OGC:CRS84') polygons). States that elected all members at large in a Congress return a single '00' row or, where no map exists, no rows. Join to house_results on (congress, state_po, district) and to Congress member data the same way. Use the spatial extension for ST_Area, ST_Contains and friends.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## districts(congress, state := NULL)

District polygons for any Congress, 1st-119th, from [Lewis et al., UCLA](https://cdmaps.polisci.ucla.edu/) (MIT licence).

- Pass `state :=`; each state's file is downloaded once and cached.
- `district` is two-digit text, `'00'` at-large.

vgi.example_queries.description: Delaware's at-large district in the 118th Congress
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT congress, state_po, district, start_congress, end_congress FROM us_elections.main.districts(118, state := 'DE') ORDER BY district

vgi.example_queries.description: Wyoming's district count in the 100th and 119th Congress
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT congress, count(*) AS districts FROM (SELECT * FROM us_elections.main.districts(100, state := 'WY') UNION ALL SELECT * FROM us_elections.main.districts(119, state := 'WY')) GROUP BY congress ORDER BY congress

workers.title: US Plant Hardiness Zones
workers.tagline: USDA plant hardiness zones by ZIP or point and USDA PLANTS data in DuckDB (Python)
workers.subtitle: USDA 2023 hardiness zones by ZIP, point or temperature, and USDA PLANTS data with derived zones.
workers.summary: USDA 2023 plant hardiness zones by ZIP code, coordinates or temperature, and USDA PLANTS data with derived plant zones. Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: derived from the PRISM/Oregon State GIS datasets.
workers.doc_md:
# US plant hardiness zones and plants

**What hardiness zone is a ZIP code or a point in, and which plants tolerate its winters?** This [VGI](https://query.farm/vgi) worker answers both in DuckDB SQL from public data: the 2023 USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map GIS datasets from the [PRISM Group, Oregon State University](https://prism.oregonstate.edu/phzm/) and the [USDA NRCS PLANTS Database](https://plants.usda.gov).

ZIP-code zones and the plant checklist are bundled, so they work offline. Point lookups read the 1991-2020 mean annual extreme minimum temperature grid, downloaded once into a local cache the first time a point in that region is looked up.

> **Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.**

> plant_min_zone_derived is DERIVED by this worker from the USDA PLANTS 'Temperature, Minimum (°F)' characteristic; neither USDA PLANTS nor the USDA hardiness map publishes a zone for a plant.

attach_options.name: cache_dir
attach_options.description: Directory for downloaded PRISM temperature grids; empty (default) uses the per-user cache directory (e.g. ~/.cache/vgi-us-hardiness).

attach_options.name: grid_url
attach_options.description: Where zone_for_point fetches phzm_<region>_grid_2023.zip: an http(s) base URL or a local directory; empty (default) uses the PRISM site.

example_queries.description: Half zones of ZIPs in New York, Portland, Anchorage and Honolulu
example_queries.sql: SELECT z AS zip, us_hardiness.main.zone_for_zip(z).half_zone AS half_zone FROM (VALUES ('10001'), ('97201'), ('99501'), ('96813')) v(z) ORDER BY z

example_queries.description: Zone and winter low at Honolulu (downloads the small Hawaii grid on first use)
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.half_zone, p.min_temp_f FROM (SELECT us_hardiness.main.zone_for_point(21.3069, -157.8583) AS p)

example_queries.description: Half zones for a few winter low temperatures in °F
example_queries.sql: SELECT t AS temp_f, us_hardiness.main.zone_for_temperature(t) AS half_zone FROM (VALUES (-25.0), (0.0), (5.0), (42.5)) v(t) ORDER BY t

example_queries.description: Half zones for winter lows given in Celsius
example_queries.sql: SELECT c AS temp_c, us_hardiness.main.zone_for_temperature(c, 'C') AS half_zone FROM (VALUES (-40.0), (-20.0), (-5.0)) v(c) ORDER BY c

example_queries.description: Native shrubs for a Minneapolis ZIP code's zone
example_queries.sql: SELECT scientific_name, common_name, mature_height_ft_high FROM us_hardiness.main.plants_for_zone(us_hardiness.main.zone_for_zip('55401').half_zone, state := 'MN', native_only := true) WHERE list_contains(growth_habit, 'Shrub') ORDER BY scientific_name LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Plants hardy in zone 7b, grouped by their derived minimum zone
example_queries.sql: SELECT plant_min_zone_derived, count(*) AS plants FROM us_hardiness.main.plants_for_zone('7b') GROUP BY plant_min_zone_derived ORDER BY plants DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Celsius bands of zones 5 and 6
example_queries.sql: SELECT half_zone, min_temp_c_low, min_temp_c_high FROM us_hardiness.main.zones WHERE zone BETWEEN 5 AND 6 ORDER BY zone_index

example_queries.description: The five most common half zones among contiguous-US ZIP codes
example_queries.sql: SELECT half_zone, count(*) AS zips FROM us_hardiness.main.zip_zones WHERE region = 'conus' GROUP BY half_zone ORDER BY zips DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: The five plant families with the most accepted taxa
example_queries.sql: SELECT family, count(*) AS accepted_taxa FROM us_hardiness.main.plants WHERE is_accepted GROUP BY family ORDER BY accepted_taxa DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: How many documented trees have each derived minimum zone
example_queries.sql: SELECT plant_min_zone_derived, count(*) AS trees FROM us_hardiness.main.plants WHERE list_contains(growth_habit, 'Tree') AND plant_min_zone_derived IS NOT NULL GROUP BY plant_min_zone_derived ORDER BY trees DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: How many documented taxa have each flower color
example_queries.sql: SELECT value AS flower_color, count(*) AS taxa FROM us_hardiness.main.plant_characteristics WHERE characteristic = 'Flower Color' GROUP BY value ORDER BY taxa DESC

example_queries.description: Which grids are already downloaded
example_queries.sql: SELECT region, cached, size_bytes FROM us_hardiness.main.grids ORDER BY region

example_queries.description: The four grid regions
example_queries.sql: SELECT region FROM us_hardiness.main.grids ORDER BY region;

example_queries.description: Red maple's PLANTS minimum temperature and derived zone
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, common_name, min_temp_f_low, min_temp_f_high, plant_min_zone_derived FROM us_hardiness.main.plants WHERE symbol = 'ACRU';

example_queries.description: Red maple's flower color and shade tolerance
example_queries.sql: SELECT characteristic, value FROM us_hardiness.main.plant_characteristics WHERE symbol = 'ACRU' AND characteristic IN ('Flower Color', 'Shade Tolerance') ORDER BY characteristic;

example_queries.description: Puerto Rico ZIPs per whole zone
example_queries.sql: SELECT zone, count(*) AS zips FROM us_hardiness.main.zip_zones WHERE region = 'puerto_rico' GROUP BY zone ORDER BY zone;

example_queries.description: The two halves of zone 7
example_queries.sql: SELECT half_zone, min_temp_f_low, min_temp_f_high FROM us_hardiness.main.zones WHERE zone = 7 ORDER BY zone_index;

example_queries.description: How many native trees in Minnesota tolerate zone 4a
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS trees FROM us_hardiness.main.plants_for_zone('4a', state := 'MN', native_only := true) WHERE list_contains(growth_habit, 'Tree');

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Everything lives in `main`. To find the zone of a place, use a ZIP code (bundled official listing, fastest, offline) or a latitude/longitude (reads the PRISM temperature grid, downloaded to a cache on first use per region: about 41 MB for the contiguous US, 15 MB for Alaska, under 1 MB for Hawaii or Puerto Rico). Zone results carry the half zone (e.g. '7a'), the whole zone number and the temperature band. To relate plants to zones, use the PLANTS checklist keyed by PLANTS symbol; only plants with PLANTS characteristics have a minimum temperature and therefore a derived minimum zone. A plant is suited to a zone when its derived minimum zone is the same or colder. Set the ATTACH options `cache_dir` (where grids are stored) and `grid_url` (an alternate location of the grid zips, http(s) or a local directory) when needed. Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

- **Zones:** look up a hardiness zone by ZIP code, by coordinates, or by temperature.
- **Plants:** the USDA PLANTS checklist and characteristics, with a minimum zone derived from each plant's minimum temperature.

> Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per PLANTS symbol from the USDA NRCS PLANTS complete checklist: accepted names (`is_accepted`) and synonyms (`accepted_symbol` points to the accepted name), with `scientific_name` (with author), `common_name` and `family`. For the ~2,200 accepted taxa where PLANTS publishes characteristics (`has_characteristics`), the row also has `plant_group`, `growth_habit` and `duration` (lists), `native_status` (list of `STRUCT`(region, status), e.g. region 'L48' = lower 48 states), `states` (USPS codes), the PLANTS minimum-temperature range `min_temp_f_low`..`min_temp_f_high`, `plant_min_zone_derived`, shade/drought tolerance, mature height range, bloom period and growth rate; for all other rows these are NULL (PLANTS does not publish them in bulk). Filter with `list_contains(growth_habit, 'Tree')`, `list_contains(states, 'MN')`. plant_min_zone_derived is DERIVED by this worker from the USDA PLANTS 'Temperature, Minimum (°F)' characteristic; neither USDA PLANTS nor the USDA hardiness map publishes a zone for a plant. Source: USDA NRCS PLANTS Database (https://plants.usda.gov), public domain; checklist plus the characteristics search service, bundled.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Long-format USDA PLANTS characteristics: `symbol`, `category` (Growth Requirements, Morphology, Reproduction, Suitability Use), `characteristic` (e.g. 'Flower Color', 'pH, Minimum', 'Temperature, Minimum (°F)', 'Toxicity') and `value` exactly as PLANTS publishes it: categories like 'High' / 'Yes' or range labels like '5.1-5.2' and '-47 - -43'; a not-applicable marker means PLANTS recorded no value. A characteristic can have several values for a plant (e.g. several flower colors). Join to `plants` on `symbol`. The most used characteristics are also typed columns of `plants`. Source: USDA NRCS PLANTS Database (https://plants.usda.gov), public domain; checklist plus the characteristics search service, bundled.

functions.name: plants_for_zone
functions.comment: Accepted PLANTS taxa whose DERIVED minimum zone is the given zone or colder, optionally limited to a state and to native plants

tags.vgi.doc_llm: List the accepted USDA PLANTS taxa that tolerate the winters of a hardiness zone: those whose `plant_min_zone_derived` is the same as or colder than `zone` (so zone '6a' includes plants rated 1a..6a). `zone` is positional ('6a', '6b' or '6', which means 6a). Named arguments: `state := 'MN'` keeps plants PLANTS records in that state; `native_only := true` keeps plants Native or Probably Native to the state's PLANTS region (lower 48 = 'L48', or AK, HI, PR, VI, Pacific Basin), or to any US region when no state is given. Only the ~2,100 taxa with a PLANTS minimum temperature can appear. Minimum temperature is the only climate test: PLANTS has no heat or maximum zone, so warm-zone results include cold-climate plants. Get the zone for a place first with `zone_for_zip(...).half_zone`. plant_min_zone_derived is DERIVED by this worker from the USDA PLANTS 'Temperature, Minimum (°F)' characteristic; neither USDA PLANTS nor the USDA hardiness map publishes a zone for a plant.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## plants_for_zone(zone, state := NULL, native_only := false)

Plants documented to survive a zone's winter lows, by the minimum temperature in USDA PLANTS.

> plant_min_zone_derived is DERIVED by this worker from the USDA PLANTS 'Temperature, Minimum (°F)' characteristic; neither USDA PLANTS nor the USDA hardiness map publishes a zone for a plant.

vgi.example_queries.description: Plants hardy in zone 7b, grouped by their derived minimum zone

vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT count(*) AS trees FROM us_hardiness.main.plants_for_zone('4a', state := 'MN', native_only := true) WHERE list_contains(growth_habit, 'Tree')

arguments.description: When true, only plants Native or Probably Native to the PLANTS region of `state` (L48, AK, HI, PR, VI, Pacific Basin); without a state, native to any US region.

arguments.name: state
arguments.description: USPS code of a US state or territory (e.g. 'MN'); only plants PLANTS records there. NULL (default) means anywhere.

examples: SELECT scientific_name, common_name, mature_height_ft_high FROM us_hardiness.main.plants_for_zone(us_hardiness.main.zone_for_zip('55401').half_zone, state := 'MN', native_only := true) WHERE list_contains(growth_habit, 'Shrub') ORDER BY scientific_name LIMIT 10
SELECT plant_min_zone_derived, count(*) AS plants FROM us_hardiness.main.plants_for_zone('7b') GROUP BY plant_min_zone_derived ORDER BY plants DESC LIMIT 5
SELECT count(*) AS trees FROM us_hardiness.main.plants_for_zone('4a', state := 'MN', native_only := true) WHERE list_contains(growth_habit, 'Tree');

result_columns.name: symbol
result_columns.description: USDA PLANTS symbol, the join key (e.g. 'ACRU' for red maple).

result_columns.name: scientific_name
result_columns.description: Scientific name with author, as in the PLANTS checklist.

result_columns.name: common_name
result_columns.description: PLANTS common name; NULL when none is recorded.

result_columns.name: family
result_columns.description: Plant family (synonyms inherit their accepted name's family).

result_columns.name: growth_habit
result_columns.description: Growth habits, e.g. ['Tree'] or ['Shrub', 'Subshrub'] (Forb/herb, Graminoid, Shrub, Subshrub, Tree, Vine).

result_columns.name: duration
result_columns.description: Life durations: Annual, Biennial and/or Perennial.

result_columns.name: plant_min_zone_derived
result_columns.description: DERIVED, not USDA-published: zone_for_temperature(min_temp_f_high), clamped to '1a' for plants hardier than -60 °F. The coldest half zone the plant is documented to tolerate.

result_columns.name: min_temp_f_low
result_columns.description: Low end of the PLANTS 'Temperature, Minimum (°F)' range (PLANTS publishes ranges, e.g. -47 to -43).

result_columns.name: min_temp_f_high
result_columns.description: High end of the PLANTS 'Temperature, Minimum (°F)' range: the plant tolerates at least this cold.

result_columns.name: native_status
result_columns.description: Nativity per PLANTS region: `STRUCT`(region, status) with region L48 (lower 48), AK, HI, PR, VI, CAN, GL, PB, NAV, SPM and status Native, Introduced, Probably Native, Probably Introduced or Waif.

result_columns.name: shade_tolerance
result_columns.description: PLANTS shade tolerance: Intolerant, Intermediate or Tolerant.

result_columns.name: drought_tolerance
result_columns.description: PLANTS drought tolerance: None, Low, Medium or High.

result_columns.name: mature_height_ft_low
result_columns.description: Low end of the PLANTS 'Height at Maturity (feet)' range.

result_columns.name: mature_height_ft_high
result_columns.description: High end of the PLANTS 'Height at Maturity (feet)' range.

result_columns.name: bloom_period
result_columns.description: PLANTS bloom period, e.g. 'Early Spring', 'Late Summer'.

functions.name: zone_for_point
functions.comment: Hardiness zone and 1991-2020 mean annual extreme minimum temperature at a latitude/longitude, from the PRISM 2023 PHZM grid (downloaded to a cache on first use). Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Look up the 2023 USDA Plant Hardiness Zone at a point (`lat`, `lon` in decimal degrees, NAD83/WGS84) by reading the PRISM 1991-2020 mean annual extreme minimum temperature grid (800 m cells for the contiguous US and Alaska, 400 m for Hawaii and Puerto Rico). Returns `STRUCT`(`half_zone` e.g. '6b', `zone` `INTEGER`, `min_temp_f` `DOUBLE`, `min_temp_c` `DOUBLE`, `region` 'conus'/'alaska'/'hawaii'/'puerto_rico'). NULL for NULL input, points outside the four grids (e.g. Canada, open ocean) or no-data cells such as water. The first lookup in a region downloads that region's grid once into the cache (about 41 MB contiguous US, 15 MB Alaska, under 1 MB Hawaii/Puerto Rico); later lookups are local. Prefer `zone_for_zip` when you have a ZIP code. Grid cells give sub-zonal detail, so a point may differ from its ZIP code's listed zone. Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.
tags.vgi.doc_md:

> Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.

functions.name: zone_for_zip
functions.comment: 2023 USDA hardiness zone of a US ZIP code as `STRUCT`(zone, half_zone, min_temp_f_low, min_temp_f_high, region); NULL for unknown ZIPs. Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Look up the 2023 USDA Plant Hardiness Zone of a US ZIP code in the bundled PRISM/Oregon State ZIP-code listing (about 40,500 ZIPs across the contiguous US, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico; offline). Returns a `STRUCT`: `zone` (whole zone, `INTEGER` 1-13), `half_zone` (e.g. '7a'), `min_temp_f_low` / `min_temp_f_high` (the half zone's °F band of mean annual extreme minimum temperature, low inclusive) and `region` ('conus', 'alaska', 'hawaii', 'puerto_rico'). Pass the ZIP as `VARCHAR`; '97201-1234' (ZIP+4) and 3-4 digit values (leading zeros lost, e.g. '501') are normalized. Unknown or malformed ZIPs return NULL. Read a field with `zone_for_zip('10001').half_zone`. Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## zone_for_zip(zip)

`zone_for_zip('10001')` returns `{zone: 7, half_zone: 7b, min_temp_f_low: 5, min_temp_f_high: 10, region: conus}`. Offline, from the official 2023 ZIP-code listing.

> Not the official USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map: values are derived from the 2023 USDA PHZM GIS datasets (PRISM Group, Oregon State University); see planthardiness.ars.usda.gov for the official map.

workers.title: US Professional Soccer Data
workers.tagline: MLS & NWSL standings, matches, player stats & xG in DuckDB (Python)
workers.subtitle: MLS, NWSL, NEXT Pro, and USL standings, schedules, stats, and xG as SQL tables.
workers.summary: Read-only MLS, NWSL, and American Soccer Analysis data for US professional soccer
workers.doc_md:
# US professional soccer

Query MLS, NWSL, and the wider US soccer pyramid directly from SQL.

## Schemas

- `mls` uses the official MLS Stats API behind [mlssoccer.com/stats](https://www.mlssoccer.com/stats/). It covers MLS, NEXT Pro, and the cups.
- `nwsl` uses the official NWSL Sports Data Platform behind [nwslsoccer.com](https://www.nwslsoccer.com/).
- `asa` uses [American Soccer Analysis](https://www.americansocceranalysis.com/) for expected goals, goals added, and salaries, through its public [API](https://app.americansocceranalysis.com/api/v1/__docs__/).

Every call fetches on demand and nothing is rehosted. Seasons are passed as plain years. ASA data is CC BY-SA 4.0 and must be attributed to American Soccer Analysis. This worker is not affiliated with MLS, the NWSL, or ASA.

example_queries.title: mls_current_standings_are_populated
example_queries.description: The current MLS table contains club rows with stable identifiers.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) > 0 AND count(club_id) = count(*) AS populated FROM us_soccer.mls.current_standings;

example_queries.title: mls_historical_match_result
example_queries.description: FC Cincinnati lost 0-2 at home to Columbus Crew on 18 October 2026.
example_queries.sql: SELECT home_club_abbreviation, home_goals, away_goals, away_club_abbreviation FROM us_soccer.mls.match('MLS-MAT-0009NL');

example_queries.title: mls_2025_has_thirty_clubs
example_queries.description: The final 2025 MLS regular-season table has 30 clubs.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS clubs FROM us_soccer.mls.standings(season := 2025);

example_queries.title: nwsl_2025_has_fourteen_teams
example_queries.description: The final 2025 NWSL table has 14 teams.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS teams FROM us_soccer.nwsl.standings(season := 2025);

example_queries.title: asa_2025_mls_team_xg
example_queries.description: ASA publishes 2025 team xG for all 30 MLS clubs.
example_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS teams FROM us_soccer.asa.xg_teams(season := 2025);

example_queries.description: 2025 MLS teams by expected goal difference.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, round(xgoal_difference, 1) AS xgd FROM us_soccer.asa.xg_teams(season := 2025) ORDER BY xgd DESC

example_queries.description: 2025 MLS players with 1,500+ minutes ranked by goals added above average per US$1M of guaranteed compensation, joining goals_added_players to each player's latest salaries() release.
example_queries.sql: WITH pay AS (SELECT player_id, team_id, guaranteed_compensation FROM us_soccer.asa.salaries(season := 2025) QUALIFY release_date = max(release_date) OVER (PARTITION BY player_id, team_id)) SELECT g.player_name, g.team_abbreviation, round(g.goals_added_above_avg, 2) AS gplus, p.guaranteed_compensation, round(g.goals_added_above_avg / (p.guaranteed_compensation / 1e6), 2) AS gplus_per_million FROM us_soccer.asa.goals_added_players(season := 2025, minimum_minutes := 1500) AS g JOIN pay AS p USING (player_id, team_id) ORDER BY gplus_per_million DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Top 2025 NWSL players by goals added above average.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, team_abbreviation, general_position, round(goals_added_above_avg, 2) AS gplus FROM us_soccer.asa.goals_added_players(league := 'nwsl', season := 2025, minimum_minutes := 1000) ORDER BY goals_added_above_avg DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: USL Championship teams.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_abbreviation, team_name FROM us_soccer.asa.teams(league := 'uslc') ORDER BY 2

example_queries.description: The 2025 MLS matches with the highest combined xG.
example_queries.sql: SELECT kickoff, home_team_name, away_team_name, home_goals, away_goals, round(home_xgoals + away_xgoals, 2) AS total_xg FROM us_soccer.asa.xg_games(season := 2025) ORDER BY total_xg DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: 2025 MLS players who most outperformed their xG.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, team_abbreviation, goals, round(xgoals, 1) AS xg, round(goals_minus_xgoals, 1) AS diff FROM us_soccer.asa.xg_players(season := 2025, minimum_minutes := 1500) ORDER BY goals_minus_xgoals DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Highest guaranteed compensation in the latest 2025 release.
example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, team_abbreviation, guaranteed_compensation FROM us_soccer.asa.salaries(season := 2025) QUALIFY release_date = max(release_date) OVER () ORDER BY guaranteed_compensation DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: 2025 MLS teams by expected goal difference.
example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, points, round(xpoints, 1) AS xpts, round(xgoal_difference, 1) AS xgd FROM us_soccer.asa.xg_teams(season := 2025) ORDER BY xgoal_difference DESC

example_queries.description: The current Supporters' Shield table.
example_queries.sql: SELECT position, club_name, games_played, points, goal_difference FROM us_soccer.mls.current_standings ORDER BY position

example_queries.description: Clubs with the best goal difference per game.
example_queries.sql: SELECT club_name, goal_difference, games_played FROM us_soccer.mls.current_standings ORDER BY goal_difference DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: 2025 MLS players who scored the largest share of their club's regular-season goals, joining player_stats to the final standings.
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.player_name, p.club_abbreviation, p.goals, s.goals_for AS club_goals, round(100.0 * p.goals / s.goals_for, 1) AS pct_of_club_goals FROM us_soccer.mls.player_stats(season := 2025) AS p JOIN us_soccer.mls.standings(season := 2025) AS s USING (club_id) ORDER BY pct_of_club_goals DESC, p.player_name LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Minutes, shots, xG, and goals for every starter in MLS-MAT-0009NL, joining match_lineups to match_player_stats.
example_queries.sql: SELECT l.club_abbreviation, l.shirt_number, l.player_name, s.minutes_played, s.shots, round(s.xg, 2) AS xg, s.goals FROM us_soccer.mls.match_lineups('MLS-MAT-0009NL') AS l JOIN us_soccer.mls.match_player_stats('MLS-MAT-0009NL') AS s USING (player_id) WHERE l.starter ORDER BY l.club_abbreviation, l.shirt_number

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## American Soccer Analysis

Expected goals, expected assists, goals added (g+), and MLS salaries. Licensed [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/); attribute American Soccer Analysis.

Every function takes `league` (`mls`, `mlsnp`, `nwsl`, `uslc`, `usl1`, `usls`, `nasl`) and `season`. Player metrics are at player-team grain and accept `minimum_minutes`; `stage` selects regular season, playoffs, or all games.

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 MLS teams by expected goal difference.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT team_name, round(xgoal_difference, 1) AS xgd FROM us_soccer.asa.xg_teams(season := 2025) ORDER BY xgd DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 MLS players with 1,500+ minutes ranked by goals added above average per US$1M of guaranteed compensation, joining goals_added_players to each player's latest salaries() release.
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH pay AS (SELECT player_id, team_id, guaranteed_compensation FROM us_soccer.asa.salaries(season := 2025) QUALIFY release_date = max(release_date) OVER (PARTITION BY player_id, team_id)) SELECT g.player_name, g.team_abbreviation, round(g.goals_added_above_avg, 2) AS gplus, p.guaranteed_compensation, round(g.goals_added_above_avg / (p.guaranteed_compensation / 1e6), 2) AS gplus_per_million FROM us_soccer.asa.goals_added_players(season := 2025, minimum_minutes := 1500) AS g JOIN pay AS p USING (player_id, team_id) ORDER BY gplus_per_million DESC LIMIT 10

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Use current_standings, current_player_stats, current_club_stats, and current_schedule for the live MLS season. Parameterized functions take season (a year) and competition (alias such as next_pro or leagues_cup). Match-level functions take MLS-MAT- ids from schedule(); player_match_log takes MLS-OBJ- ids from player_stats().
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## MLS Stats API

Standings since 1996, schedules, season club and player statistics, and per-match lineups, events, commentary, and box scores for MLS-family competitions.

Pass `season` as a year and `competition` as an alias from the `competitions` table, such as `next_pro` or `leagues_cup`. Match functions take `MLS-MAT-` ids from `schedule()`; `player_match_log()` takes `MLS-OBJ-` ids from `player_stats()`.

vgi.example_queries.description: The current Supporters' Shield table.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT position, club_name, games_played, points, goal_difference FROM us_soccer.mls.current_standings ORDER BY position

vgi.example_queries.description: Clubs with the best goal difference per game.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT club_name, goal_difference, games_played FROM us_soccer.mls.current_standings ORDER BY goal_difference DESC LIMIT 5

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 MLS players who scored the largest share of their club's regular-season goals, joining player_stats to the final standings.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.player_name, p.club_abbreviation, p.goals, s.goals_for AS club_goals, round(100.0 * p.goals / s.goals_for, 1) AS pct_of_club_goals FROM us_soccer.mls.player_stats(season := 2025) AS p JOIN us_soccer.mls.standings(season := 2025) AS s USING (club_id) ORDER BY pct_of_club_goals DESC, p.player_name LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: Minutes, shots, xG, and goals for every starter in MLS-MAT-0009NL, joining match_lineups to match_player_stats.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT l.club_abbreviation, l.shirt_number, l.player_name, s.minutes_played, s.shots, round(s.xg, 2) AS xg, s.goals FROM us_soccer.mls.match_lineups('MLS-MAT-0009NL') AS l JOIN us_soccer.mls.match_player_stats('MLS-MAT-0009NL') AS s USING (player_id) WHERE l.starter ORDER BY l.club_abbreviation, l.shirt_number

functions.name: player_stats
functions.comment: Season player statistics for an MLS-family competition, per player and club

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Season player statistics, one row per player and club (a player traded mid-season has one row per club). Includes minutes, goals, assists, tracking-model xG, shots, passing, discipline, aerial duels, distance covered, top speed, and goalkeeper saves, goals conceded, clean sheets, and expected saves.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Season player statistics, one row per player and club (a player traded mid-season has one row per club). Includes minutes, goals, assists, tracking-model xG, shots, passing, discipline, aerial duels, distance covered, top speed, and goalkeeper saves, goals conceded, clean sheets, and expected saves.

Typical use: 2025 MLS Golden Boot race.

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 MLS Golden Boot race.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT player_name, club_abbreviation, goals, assists, round(xg, 1) AS xg FROM us_soccer.mls.player_stats(season := 2025) ORDER BY goals DESC LIMIT 10

vgi.example_queries.description: 2025 MLS players who scored the largest share of their club's regular-season goals, joining player_stats to the final standings.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.player_name, p.club_abbreviation, p.goals, s.goals_for AS club_goals, round(100.0 * p.goals / s.goals_for, 1) AS pct_of_club_goals FROM us_soccer.mls.player_stats(season := 2025) AS p JOIN us_soccer.mls.standings(season := 2025) AS s USING (club_id) ORDER BY pct_of_club_goals DESC, p.player_name LIMIT 10

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Use current_standings, current_player_stats, and current_matches for the live NWSL season. Functions take season as a year; the platform's opaque ids are resolved automatically. roster() accepts a team acronym such as GFC.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## NWSL

Standings, teams, rosters, Opta-derived team and player statistics, matches, and match event feeds from the official NWSL Sports Data Platform.

Pass `season` as a year; opaque platform ids are resolved automatically. `roster()` accepts a team acronym such as `GFC`.

vgi.example_queries.description: The current NWSL table.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT position, team_name, points FROM us_soccer.nwsl.current_standings ORDER BY position

vgi.example_queries.description: The final 2025 NWSL table with each team's leading scorer (ties broken by name) and her share of the team's goals, joining standings to player_stats.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT s.position, s.team_name, s.goals_for, p.player_name, p.goals, round(100.0 * p.goals / s.goals_for, 1) AS pct_of_team_goals FROM us_soccer.nwsl.standings(season := 2025) AS s JOIN us_soccer.nwsl.player_stats(season := 2025) AS p USING (team_id) QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.team_id ORDER BY p.goals DESC, p.player_name) = 1 ORDER BY s.position

workers.title: US State Legislatures
workers.tagline: US state legislators, committees, elections, ideology, bills and votes in DuckDB (Python, Open States)
workers.subtitle: State legislators, committees, election returns, ideology scores, bills and roll-call votes.
workers.summary: US state legislatures in SQL: current and former state legislators, their terms and committee rosters from the Open States people data, state legislative election returns since 1967, Shor-McCarty legislator ideology scores, and live bills, votes and events from the Open States API.
workers.doc_md:
# US State Legislatures

**Legislators, committees, elections, ideology, bills and votes for the 50 US states, DC and Puerto Rico, queryable from DuckDB.**

Most of the catalog works without any account: the [Open States people data](https://github.com/openstates/people) (CC0), Carl Klarner's [State Legislative Election Returns](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/3WZFK9) (CC0) and the [Shor-McCarty ideology data](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/SGOQ7G) (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) are downloaded on first use into a per-user cache and reused. Live bills, roll-call votes and events come from the [Open States API v3](https://docs.openstates.org/api-v3/) and need a free API key stored as a DuckDB secret:

```sql
CREATE SECRET (TYPE openstates, API_KEY 'your-key');
```

Identifiers follow Open States (`ocd-person/...`, `ocd-jurisdiction/...`), states are USPS codes with two-digit FIPS codes, and `chamber` is `upper`, `lower` or `legislature` (Nebraska's unicameral Legislature and the DC Council).
workers.readme_sql:
-- How each sitting Nebraska senator voted on a bill, with their district (needs an API key).
SELECT l.district, l.name, v.option
FROM us_statelegs.main.os_votes(state := 'NE', session := '109') o, unnest(o.votes) AS u(v)
JOIN us_statelegs.main.legislators(state := 'NE', current := true) l ON l.person_id = v.person_id
WHERE o.bill_identifier = 'LB 1'
ORDER BY l.district::INTEGER;

attach_options.name: cache_dir
attach_options.description: Directory for downloaded datasets (people ~5 MB, Klarner ~110 MB + Parquet, Shor-McCarty ~7 MB). Default: the per-user cache directory, e.g. ~/Library/Caches/vgi-us-state-legislatures.

attach_options.name: max_age_days
attach_options.description: Re-check the Open States people archive once the cached copy is this many days old.

attach_options.name: offline
attach_options.description: Never download; use cached datasets only (a missing one fails).

attach_options.name: openstates_api_url
attach_options.description: Base URL of the Open States API v3; override for a mirror or a test server.

attach_options.name: openstates_min_interval
attach_options.description: Minimum seconds between Open States API requests (free-tier rate limits).

attach_options.name: people_archive_url
attach_options.description: URL of the openstates/people repository tar.gz.

attach_options.name: klarner_url
attach_options.description: URL of the Klarner election returns tab file (Harvard Dataverse).

attach_options.name: shor_mccarty_url
attach_options.description: URL of the Shor-McCarty individual legislator tab file (Harvard Dataverse).

example_queries.description: Identifiers for Nebraska and North Carolina
example_queries.sql: SELECT state, state_fips, jurisdiction_id FROM us_statelegs.main.states WHERE state IN ('NE', 'NC') ORDER BY state

example_queries.description: Party balance of the sitting North Carolina General Assembly by chamber
example_queries.sql: SELECT chamber, party, count(*) AS members FROM us_statelegs.main.legislators(state := 'NC', current := true) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY chamber, members DESC

example_queries.description: Ohio legislators who served in both chambers
example_queries.sql: SELECT person_id, name, count(DISTINCT chamber) AS chambers FROM us_statelegs.main.legislator_roles(state := 'OH') GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(DISTINCT chamber) > 1 ORDER BY name LIMIT 20

example_queries.description: The largest Nebraska Legislature committees and their chairs
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, chair, members FROM us_statelegs.main.committees(state := 'NE') WHERE classification = 'committee' ORDER BY members DESC, name LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Nebraska senators with the most committee assignments
example_queries.sql: SELECT m.member_name, count(*) AS committees FROM us_statelegs.main.committee_members(state := 'NE') m GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY committees DESC, m.member_name LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: How often Wisconsin Assembly incumbents won their general elections, by year
example_queries.sql: SELECT year, round(avg(won::INT) FILTER (WHERE incumbent), 3) AS incumbent_win_rate FROM us_statelegs.main.election_returns(state := 'WI', chamber := 'lower') WHERE election_type = 'g' GROUP BY year ORDER BY year

example_queries.description: Texas House party medians by year: how far apart the parties are
example_queries.sql: SELECT year, party, round(median(np_score), 3) AS median_np FROM us_statelegs.main.legislator_ideology(state := 'TX') WHERE chamber = 'lower' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY year, party

example_queries.description: The ten most polarized state legislative chambers in 2020
example_queries.sql: SELECT state, chamber, party_gap FROM us_statelegs.main.chamber_ideology(first_year := 2020, last_year := 2020) ORDER BY party_gap DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Which datasets are cached, and under what licence
example_queries.sql: SELECT dataset, licence, cached, downloaded_at FROM us_statelegs.main.cache_info() ORDER BY dataset

example_queries.description: Pull the latest Open States people data now
example_queries.sql: SELECT dataset, status, bytes FROM us_statelegs.main.refresh_cache('people')

example_queries.description: The five states whose bill data were updated least recently
example_queries.sql: SELECT state, latest_bill_update FROM us_statelegs.main.os_jurisdictions() ORDER BY latest_bill_update LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: North Carolina's five most recent sessions
example_queries.sql: SELECT session, name, start_date FROM us_statelegs.main.os_sessions(state := 'NC') ORDER BY start_date DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: North Carolina's current state senators by district
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, party, district FROM us_statelegs.main.os_people(state := 'NC', chamber := 'upper') ORDER BY district::INTEGER

example_queries.description: Ten recently passed Nebraska bills
example_queries.sql: SELECT identifier, title, latest_action_date FROM us_statelegs.main.os_bills(state := 'NE', session := '109') WHERE latest_passage_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY latest_action_date DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Recent final-passage votes in the Nebraska Legislature
example_queries.sql: SELECT bill_identifier, motion_text, yes, no, result FROM us_statelegs.main.os_votes(state := 'NE', session := '109') WHERE 'passage' = ANY(motion_classification) ORDER BY vote_date DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: The five largest North Carolina House committees
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, len(members) AS size FROM us_statelegs.main.os_committees(state := 'NC', chamber := 'lower') ORDER BY size DESC LIMIT 5

example_queries.description: Upcoming North Carolina committee meetings
example_queries.sql: SELECT start_time, name, location_name FROM us_statelegs.main.os_events(state := 'NC', after_date := '2026-01-01') WHERE status <> 'cancelled' ORDER BY start_time LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: How many legislatures use each name for their lower chamber
example_queries.sql: SELECT lower_chamber_name, count(*) AS states FROM us_statelegs.main.states WHERE NOT unicameral GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY states DESC

example_queries.description: The unicameral legislatures
example_queries.sql: SELECT state, legislature_name FROM us_statelegs.main.states WHERE unicameral ORDER BY state;

example_queries.description: How the lower chambers are named
example_queries.sql: SELECT lower_chamber_name, count(*) AS n FROM us_statelegs.main.states WHERE NOT unicameral GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC, lower_chamber_name;

example_queries.description: How many committees each chamber has
example_queries.sql: SELECT state, chamber, count(*) AS committees FROM us_statelegs.main.committees() GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY state, chamber

example_queries.description: Committee chairs in North Carolina by party
example_queries.sql: SELECT l.party, count(*) AS chairs FROM us_statelegs.main.committee_members(state := 'NC') m JOIN us_statelegs.main.legislators(state := 'NC') l USING (person_id) WHERE m.role = 'chair' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY chairs DESC

example_queries.description: Seats won by party in Minnesota general elections since 2000
example_queries.sql: SELECT year, party, count(*) AS seats_won FROM us_statelegs.main.election_returns(state := 'MN', first_year := 2000) WHERE general AND won GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY year, party

example_queries.description: Nebraska's unicameral Legislature drifting over time
example_queries.sql: SELECT year, median, party_gap FROM us_statelegs.main.chamber_ideology(state := 'NE') ORDER BY year

example_queries.description: Who cast the most no votes on recently updated North Carolina bills
example_queries.sql: SELECT v.voter_name, count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.option = 'no') AS no_votes FROM us_statelegs.main.os_votes(state := 'NC', updated_since := '2025-06-01'), unnest(votes) AS u(v) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY no_votes DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: How many Nebraska seats turned over each year
example_queries.sql: SELECT year(end_date) AS year, count(*) AS roles_ended FROM us_statelegs.main.legislator_roles() WHERE state = 'NE' AND end_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY year

example_queries.description: North Carolina's most prolific primary sponsors among recently updated bills
example_queries.sql: SELECT s.name, count(*) AS bills FROM us_statelegs.main.os_bills(state := 'NC', updated_since := '2025-06-01'), unnest(sponsors) AS u(s) WHERE s.is_primary GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY bills DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: The first ten districts of the unicameral Nebraska Legislature
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, district, email FROM us_statelegs.main.legislators(current := true) WHERE state = 'NE' ORDER BY district::INTEGER LIMIT 10

example_queries.description: Average ideology of legislators serving since 2020, by state
example_queries.sql: SELECT state, count(DISTINCT legislator_id) AS legislators, round(avg(np_score), 3) AS mean_np FROM us_statelegs.main.legislator_ideology(first_year := 2020) GROUP BY state ORDER BY mean_np

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The `main` schema of the US state legislatures catalog. Keyless functions read cached open datasets and accept an optional `state` (USPS code) argument that limits what is parsed; a `WHERE state = 'XX'` filter is pushed down the same way. Functions prefixed `os_` call the Open States API v3 live and need a `openstates` secret holding an API key; their filters (state, session, chamber, classification, updated_since) are sent to the API. `chamber` is 'upper' (state senate), 'lower' (house, assembly or house of delegates) or 'legislature' for the unicameral Nebraska Legislature and the Council of the District of Columbia.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Everything about the 52 legislatures lives in this one schema. Keyless functions read cached open datasets; `os_*` functions call the Open States API and need an `openstates` secret.

- **Reference**: the legislatures and their identifiers.
- **Legislators and committees** from the Open States people data (keyless, CC0).
- **Elections and ideology**: Klarner election returns 1967-2016 and Shor-McCarty scores.
- **Open States API** (`os_*`): live bills, votes, people, committees, events; needs a key.
- **Cache**: what has been downloaded, and a refresh.

vgi.example_queries.description: Identifiers for Nebraska and North Carolina

vgi.example_queries.description: Ohio legislators who served in both chambers
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT person_id, name, count(DISTINCT chamber) AS chambers FROM us_statelegs.main.legislator_roles(state := 'OH') GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(DISTINCT chamber) > 1 ORDER BY name LIMIT 20

functions.name: election_returns
functions.comment: State legislative election returns 1967-2016, one row per candidate (Klarner, CC0)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Carl Klarner's State Legislative Election Returns (1967-2016): one row per candidate per election per party line, for general elections everywhere and many primaries/specials. Key columns: state, year, election_date, chamber, district (ballot designation, `VARCHAR`), election_type ('g' = general; filter `general` for all general-type contests), candidate, candidate_id, party (d/r/nonmaj/nonpart/writein/b/partymiss), incumbent, votes, outcome, won, seats_up, district_type. Some 2013-2016 returns are split by county (county_name non-NULL) and fusion candidates can have several party lines, so SUM(votes) per candidate_id and contest before computing shares. Arguments: state, first_year, last_year, chamber; WHERE state/year filters are pushed down. The ~110 MB source is downloaded once. `chamber` is 'upper' (state senate), 'lower' (house, assembly or house of delegates) or 'legislature' for the unicameral Nebraska Legislature and the Council of the District of Columbia.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## election_returns(state := NULL, first_year := NULL, last_year := NULL, chamber := NULL)

Candidate-level returns for state legislative elections 1967-2016. Sum `votes` over county and party-line rows before computing vote shares.

Source: [Klarner, State Legislative Election Returns, 1967-2016](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/3WZFK9) (Harvard Dataverse V3, CC0 1.0), downloaded on first use (about 110 MB).

functions.name: os_votes
functions.comment: Roll-call votes on state bills from the live Open States API, with individual legislators' votes

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per vote event on the bills that match the filters (same arguments as os_bills; the API is queried for bills with votes included): vote_id, bill_id, bill_identifier, state, session, chamber, vote_date, motion_text, motion_classification, result ('pass'/'fail'), yes, no, other, counts, votes (`LIST` of `STRUCT`(option, voter_name, person_id)); unnest(votes) for how each legislator voted. Arguments (all sent to the API): state, session (from os_sessions), chamber, classification, subject, updated_since 'YYYY-MM-DD', q (full text), sponsor. WHERE state/session/chamber = and updated_at >= are pushed down too. A state or q is required. Pages hold 20 bills; always filter or LIMIT on the free tier. Needs an Open States API key stored in a DuckDB secret of type `openstates` (field `API_KEY`); keys are free at https://open.pluralpolicy.com/accounts/signup/. Without the secret the call fails naming the secret type.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## os_votes(state, session, chamber, classification, subject, updated_since, q, sponsor)

Live roll-call votes with individual votes. Arguments (all sent to the API): state, session (from os_sessions), chamber, classification, subject, updated_since 'YYYY-MM-DD', q (full text), sponsor. WHERE state/session/chamber = and updated_at >= are pushed down too. A state or q is required. Pages hold 20 bills; always filter or LIMIT on the free tier. 

Source: [Open States API v3](https://docs.openstates.org/api-v3/).

Needs a free Open States API key ([register](https://open.pluralpolicy.com/accounts/signup/)) stored as a DuckDB secret:

```sql
CREATE SECRET (TYPE openstates, API_KEY 'your-key');
```

functions.name: legislators
functions.comment: Current and former state legislators from the Open States people data (keyless, CC0)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: One row per person who has held a seat in a state legislature (50 states, DC, PR) according to the Open States people repository: person_id (ocd-person id), name, state, current (sitting member), chamber and district of the most recent seat, party, first/last role dates, contact details, social handles, party history and other identifiers (including legacy Open States ids). Arguments: `state := 'NE'` and `current := true`. Former members are mostly those tracked since about 2010. No API key needed. `chamber` is 'upper' (state senate), 'lower' (house, assembly or house of delegates) or 'legislature' for the unicameral Nebraska Legislature and the Council of the District of Columbia.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## legislators(state := NULL, current := NULL)

Current and former state legislators, one row per person. `state` (argument or `WHERE state = ...`/`IN (...)`) limits which state files are parsed.

Source: [Open States people repository](https://github.com/openstates/people) (CC0 1.0), downloaded on first use (about 5 MB) and re-checked weekly.

workers.title: US Occupational Wages
workers.tagline: US occupational employment and wages by metro, state and occupation in DuckDB (Python, BLS OEWS)
workers.subtitle: Occupational employment and wages for the US, states and metro areas, plus SOC occupations.
workers.summary: US employment and wages by occupation for the nation, states, metro and nonmetro areas from the BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) survey, with the SOC 2018 occupation classification, occupation search and a ZIP-to-metro lookup. No API key needed.
workers.doc_md:
# US Wages

Employment and pay for about 830 occupations across the US, every state, about 390 metropolitan areas and 140 nonmetropolitan areas, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics [Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/oes/) (OEWS) survey. Each May reference period is a *release*; the worker reads BLS's [all-data files](https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm), converts them once into a local Parquet cache and filters them locally.

Occupations follow the [2018 Standard Occupational Classification](https://www.bls.gov/soc/2018/); occupation search also covers the alternate job titles of the [O*NET 31.0 database](https://www.onetcenter.org/database.html) (CC BY 4.0, by the U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration). The ZIP lookup uses the Census Bureau's [2020 ZCTA relationship files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/geo/relationship-files.html) and gives *metro-level* figures, never ZIP-level ones.

BLS suppression and top-code markers become NULL plus a flag, never 0.

attach_options.name: cache_dir
attach_options.description: Directory for downloaded BLS files and their Parquet conversions (about 25 MB per release). Default: the per-user cache directory, e.g. ~/.cache/vgi-us-wages or ~/Library/Caches/vgi-us-wages.

attach_options.name: base_url
attach_options.description: Where BLS files are fetched from: https://www.bls.gov (default), a mirror URL, or a local directory laid out like bls.gov (oes/tables.htm, oes/special-requests/oesmYYall.zip, oes/area_definitions_mYYYY.xlsx).

attach_options.name: user_agent
attach_options.description: User-Agent sent to bls.gov (default 'vgi-us-wages/0.1 (+https://query.farm)'). BLS asks automated clients to identify themselves, ideally with contact details; set your own if bls.gov answers 403.

attach_options.name: offline
attach_options.description: Never touch the network: use only what is cached (default false).

example_queries.description: The five best SOC matches for 'nurse'

example_queries.description: National median pay of the occupations matching 'truck driver'

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Everything lives in `main`. Wage estimates come from table functions with named arguments that filter locally (occupation, area, area_type, state, industry, release); WHERE clauses on the result columns are pushed down too. The default release is 'latest' (most recent May reference year); pass release := '2024' for another year. Cross-industry rows are the default; industry := 'all' adds the national industry (NAICS) breakdowns. SOC codes are `VARCHAR` 'XX-XXXX'; area codes are `VARCHAR` and keep leading zeros; join metro rows to other data on cbsa_code and states on state_fips.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## main

Wage estimates from the BLS [OEWS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/) survey, the areas they cover, and the SOC 2018 occupations they are classified by.

- **Wages**: estimates by occupation, area and industry; a ZIP-to-metro shortcut.
- **Geography**: the OEWS areas of a release and the counties that make them up.
- **Occupations**: the SOC 2018 hierarchy and a title search with O*NET alternate titles.
- **Cache**: what has been downloaded, and a way to refresh it.

The US, states, territories, metropolitan (CBSA) and nonmetropolitan areas in a release, with codes to pass to `wages(area := ...)`. See BLS [area definitions](https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/msa_def.htm).

vgi.example_queries.description: How many areas of each type the latest release covers
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT area_type_name, count(*) AS areas FROM us_wages.main.areas() GROUP BY area_type_name ORDER BY areas DESC

vgi.example_queries.description: Metro areas that include part of Connecticut
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT area_code, area_title, county_count FROM us_wages.main.areas() WHERE area_type_name = 'metro' AND list_contains(states, 'CT') ORDER BY area_code

functions.name: refresh
functions.comment: Download a release into the cache, or re-download it when BLS has republished it

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Prefetch or update cached data. refresh(release := 'latest', force := false) re-checks the BLS tables page for the newest May release (ignoring the 24-hour latest pointer), downloads it if absent, re-downloads it when BLS's ETag/Last-Modified changed or force := true, also fetches the county area definitions (May 2024+), and returns the resulting cache_info rows. Only the local cache is written; nothing upstream changes.
tags.vgi.doc_md:

functions.name: wages_for_zip
functions.comment: Metro-level OEWS wages for the metro or nonmetro area containing a ZIP code (not ZIP-level)

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Look up OEWS wages for the area around a ZIP code. OEWS publishes no ZIP-level data: this maps the ZIP to its 2020 Census ZCTA, the ZCTA to counties by land-area overlap, and the counties to the release's OEWS metro (CBSA) or nonmetro area, then returns that area's rows. Arguments: zip (5 digits, positional), occupation (positional: SOC code '29-1141', prefix '29-' or 'all'), all_areas := true to also get other areas a ZIP straddles, release := 'latest' or a year >= 2024. Columns say which area was used (area_code, area_title, cbsa_code), zcta_land_share, is_primary_area and estimate_geography (always 'metro-level ...' or 'nonmetropolitan-area ...'). Errors for ZIPs without a ZCTA (PO boxes).
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## wages_for_zip(zip, occupation, all_areas := false, release := 'latest')

The **metro (or nonmetro) area's** OEWS figures for a ZIP code, with the area used and the share of the ZIP's land in it. ZIP codes are matched to [2020 ZCTAs](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/guidance/geo-areas/zctas.html), which approximate but are not identical to USPS ZIP codes.

vgi.example_queries.description: Software developer pay in the metro area that contains ZIP 94103
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT area_title, cbsa_code, estimate_geography, a_median FROM us_wages.main.wages_for_zip('94103', '15-1252') ORDER BY area_code

vgi.example_queries.description: Best-paid healthcare occupations in the metro area around Hartford ZIP 06103
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT occ_title, a_median FROM us_wages.main.wages_for_zip('06103', '29-') WHERE o_group = 'detailed' ORDER BY a_median DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

functions.name: search_occupations
functions.comment: Find SOC 2018 codes for a job title, searching SOC titles and 54,000 O*NET alternate titles

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Turn a job title into SOC codes. search_occupations(text, max_results := 10) matches every word of text (word prefixes; plurals folded) against SOC 2018 titles, O*NET occupation titles and O*NET alternate job titles (e.g. 'barista' -> 35-3023 Fast Food and Counter Workers), keeps the best title per SOC code and ranks by score. Use the rank-1 soc_code with wages(occupation := ...). Bundled data; no network.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## search_occupations(text, max_results := 10)

Title search over SOC 2018 and [O*NET](https://www.onetcenter.org/database.html) alternate titles. O*NET data is CC BY 4.0, U.S. Department of Labor/ETA.

vgi.example_queries.description: The five best SOC matches for 'nurse'
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT rank, soc_code, soc_title, matched_title FROM us_wages.main.search_occupations('nurse', max_results := 5) ORDER BY rank

vgi.example_queries.description: National median pay of the occupations matching 'truck driver'
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT s.soc_code, s.soc_title, w.a_median FROM us_wages.main.search_occupations('truck driver', max_results := 3) s JOIN us_wages.main.wages(area := '99') w ON w.occ_code = s.soc_code ORDER BY s.rank

vgi.executable_examples.description: Best SOC code for 'software developer'
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT soc_code, soc_title FROM us_wages.main.search_occupations('software developer') WHERE rank = 1

vgi.executable_examples.description: An alternate title resolves to its SOC occupation
vgi.executable_examples.sql: SELECT soc_code, match_source FROM us_wages.main.search_occupations('barista', max_results := 1) ORDER BY rank

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: rank
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: 1 = best match.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: soc_code

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: soc_title

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: major, minor, broad or detailed.

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: The title that matched the search text.

vgi.result_columns_schema.description: soc_title, onet_title or onet_job_title (O*NET alternate title).

functions.name: wages
functions.comment: BLS OEWS employment and wages by occupation, area and industry for one May release

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Occupational employment and wage estimates from BLS OEWS, one row per area x industry x occupation. All arguments are named and optional and filter before rows leave the worker: occupation := SOC code '15-1252' or prefix '15-'; area := OEWS area code ('99' US, '06' California, '41860' San Francisco metro, '0600001' a nonmetro area); area_type := 'national'|'state'|'territory'|'metro'|'nonmetro'; state := 'CA' (the state's own row plus metros and nonmetro areas whose primary state it is); industry := 'cross-industry' (default), 'all', or a NAICS code (industry rows exist for the US only); release := 'latest' or a year such as '2024'. WHERE filters on area_code, occ_code, o_group, prim_state, cbsa_code, tot_emp, wages etc. are pushed down as well. Use o_group = 'detailed' to avoid double counting aggregates. Wages are US dollars; suppressed ('*', '**') and top-coded ('#') values are NULL and listed in suppressed_columns / topcoded_columns. The first call for a release downloads the BLS all-data file (~80 MB) into the local cache; later calls are local.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## wages(occupation := , area := , area_type := , state := , industry := , release := )

BLS [OEWS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/) estimates: employment, mean and percentile wages for every occupation in the US, each state, metro (CBSA) and nonmetro area.

- Filters are named arguments and pushed-down `WHERE` clauses, applied locally.
- `*`/`**`/`#` markers become `NULL` plus `suppressed_columns` / `topcoded_columns`.
- The first query for a release downloads the BLS file (~80 MB) into the cache.
