tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## xquery_rows

Run an **XQuery 3.1** query against one document and emit **one `(seq, value)` row per item** of the result sequence, in sequence order.

**When to use:** when the query yields a sequence (e.g. a FLWOR `for $x in //i return $x*2`) and you want each item as its own row to join, filter, or aggregate in SQL. Use the `xquery` scalar instead when you want the whole result serialized into one value.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document, bound as the context item) and `expr` (the XQuery 3.1 source). Both `VARCHAR`; named-argument syntax supported.

**Output columns:** `seq` (`BIGINT`, 1-based position) and `value` (`VARCHAR`, the item's string value).

**Behavior & edge cases:** an empty result sequence -> zero rows. Malformed XML or a malformed query raises a clean DuckDB error.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# xquery_rows

Table function: one `(seq, value)` row per item in an XQuery 3.1 result sequence.

## Usage

Call `xslt.main.xquery_rows(xml, expr)` in a `FROM` clause to expand each item of the result sequence into a numbered `(seq, value)` row.

functions.name: is_well_formed
functions.comment: True if the text is well-formed XML; false if malformed (never an error)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## is_well_formed

Test whether a string is **well-formed XML** — returns `true` if it parses, `false` if it is malformed. **Never raises** (unlike the other functions).

**When to use:** validate or filter a column of candidate XML before transforming or querying it, e.g. `WHERE xslt.main.is_well_formed(doc)`, so malformed rows do not abort the scan.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the candidate text). `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `BOOLEAN` — `true` for well-formed XML, `false` for malformed text; NULL input yields NULL.

**Behavior & edge cases:** this checks *well-formedness* (does it parse), not schema validity — SaxonC-HE is not schema-aware, so there is no XSD validation. Well-formedness is the strongest XML check the HE edition offers.
tags.vgi.doc_md: # is_well_formed Return `true` if the text is well-formed XML, `false` if malformed (never errors). ## Usage ```sql SELECT xslt.main.is_well_formed(''); -- true SELECT xslt.main.is_well_formed(''); -- false ``` ## Notes - Checks well-formedness only; there is no XSD/schema validation (HE limitation). - Safe to use in `WHERE` to filter out malformed rows. - NULL input -> NULL output.

vgi.example_queries.description: Check whether a string is well-formed XML.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT xslt.main.is_well_formed('')

vgi.example_queries.description: Skip malformed documents with is_well_formed, then read each remaining order's id attribute and customer with xpath_string and its total (sum of qty * price over its lines) with xpath_number; the malformed order C3 is dropped (A1/acme/21.5, B7/globex/38.0).
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH docs(id, doc) AS (VALUES (1, '<order id="A1"><customer>acme</customer><line sku="bolt" qty="2" price="9.5"/><line sku="nut" qty="10" price="0.25"/></order>'), (2, '<order id="B7"><customer>globex</customer><line sku="bolt" qty="4" price="9.5"/></order>'), (3, '<order id="C3"><customer>initech</order>')) SELECT id, xslt.main.xpath_string(doc, 'string(/order/@id)') AS order_id, xslt.main.xpath_string(doc, '/order/customer') AS customer, xslt.main.xpath_number(doc, 'sum(//line/(@qty * @price))') AS total FROM docs WHERE xslt.main.is_well_formed(doc) ORDER BY id

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_string

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return the **string value of the first match** (or NULL when nothing matches).

**When to use:** pull a single text value out of XML — an element's text, an attribute, or any atomic computed by XPath (`string(...)`, `concat(...)`, etc.).

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `VARCHAR` — the string value of the first node/atomic in document order, or NULL if the expression selects nothing.

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. A malformed document or a malformed XPath raises a clean DuckDB error. Namespaces follow the document's in-scope bindings; use `//*:name` or `local-name()` predicates for namespace-agnostic matching.
tags.vgi.doc_md: # xpath_string Return the string value of the first XPath 3.1 match in a document, or NULL. ## Usage ```sql SELECT xslt.main.xpath_string('x', '//a'); -- 'x' ``` ## Notes - Returns the FIRST match only; use `xpath_array` to collect all matches. - NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/XPath raises an error. - Namespace-agnostic matching: `//*:tag` or `local-name() = 'tag'`.

functions.name: xpath_array
functions.comment: String values of ALL matches of an XPath 3.1 expression, as a list -- UNNEST it to shred one document into rows

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_array

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return the string values of **all matches** as a `VARCHAR[]` list.

**When to use:** shred XML into rows. Apply this to a column of documents and `UNNEST(...)` the result to turn one document into many rows — the per-row counterpart to the `xpath_nodes` table function (which binds one constant document).

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression selecting many items). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `VARCHAR[]` — the string value of every match, in document order; an empty list when nothing matches.

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL (not an empty list). Malformed XML or XPath raises a clean DuckDB error.
tags.vgi.doc_md: # xpath_array Return the string values of ALL XPath 3.1 matches as a `VARCHAR[]` list. ## Usage ```sql SELECT UNNEST(xslt.main.xpath_array('ab', '//i')); ``` ## Notes - `UNNEST` the list to shred a column of documents into rows. - For a single constant document, the `xpath_nodes` table function is handier. - NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/XPath raises an error.

vgi.example_queries.description: Shred all matching nodes into rows with UNNEST.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT UNNEST(xslt.main.xpath_array('ab', '//i'))

vgi.example_queries.description: Shred the lines of a column of order documents with two position-aligned UNNEST(xpath_array(...)) calls, tag each line with its order's customer via xpath_string, and total the quantity per SKU (bolt 6 from acme,globex; nut 10 from acme).
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH docs(id, doc) AS (VALUES (1, '<order id="A1"><customer>acme</customer><line sku="bolt" qty="2"/><line sku="nut" qty="10"/></order>'), (2, '<order id="B7"><customer>globex</customer><line sku="bolt" qty="4"/></order>')), lines AS (SELECT xslt.main.xpath_string(doc, '/order/customer') AS customer, UNNEST(xslt.main.xpath_array(doc, '//line/@sku')) AS sku, CAST(UNNEST(xslt.main.xpath_array(doc, '//line/@qty')) AS INTEGER) AS qty FROM docs) SELECT sku, CAST(SUM(qty) AS BIGINT) AS total_qty, string_agg(customer, ',' ORDER BY customer) AS customers FROM lines GROUP BY sku ORDER BY sku

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_boolean

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return its **effective boolean value** (EBV).

**When to use:** test a condition over XML inside a SQL `WHERE`/`CASE` — does a node exist (`boolean(//x)`), does a count match (`count(//a) = 1`), or any predicate that XPath can express.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `BOOLEAN` — the EBV of the expression (a non-empty node-set is true, an empty one is false; numeric/string EBV rules apply for atomics).

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. Malformed XML or XPath raises a clean DuckDB error.

## xpath_number

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return its **numeric value** as a `DOUBLE`.

**When to use:** extract a number from XML and use it in SQL arithmetic — a measurement, a count (`count(//item)`), a sum (`sum(//price)`), or any numeric XPath computation.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `DOUBLE` — the numeric value of the first match, or NULL when the value is non-numeric (XPath NaN) or nothing matches.

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. Wrap a path in `number(...)` to coerce a text node. Malformed XML or XPath raises a clean DuckDB error.

# xpath_number

Return the numeric (`DOUBLE`) value of the first XPath 3.1 match, or NULL.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT xslt.main.xpath_number('<r><n>42</n></r>', 'number(//n)');  -- 42.0
```

- Non-numeric results (XPath NaN) come back as NULL.
- Use XPath aggregates like `count(...)` / `sum(...)` directly.
- NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/XPath raises an error.

## xquery

Run an **XQuery 3.1** query against an XML document (bound as the context item) and return the serialized result.

**When to use:** richer querying than a single XPath — FLWOR expressions (`for`/`let`/`where`/`order by`/`return`), constructed elements, joins across parts of the document, and string/sequence functions like `string-join(//i, ',')`.

**Output:** `VARCHAR` — the serialized query result (atomic text, or constructed XML, depending on the query).

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. Use `xquery_rows` instead when you want one row per item of the result sequence. Malformed XML or a malformed query raises a clean DuckDB error.

## xslt

Apply an **XSLT 3.0** stylesheet to an XML document and return the serialized transformation result as text.

**When to use:** reshape, rename, filter, or compute over XML — the full power of XSLT 3.0 (templates, `xsl:value-of`, `xsl:for-each`, modes, functions) — directly in SQL.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the source document) and `stylesheet` (the XSLT 3.0 source). Both are `VARCHAR`.

workers.title: YARA Malware Scanning
workers.tagline: Scan data/files against YARA rules in DuckDB (Rust, yara-x)
workers.subtitle: Scan blobs and text for malware with YARA rules, straight from SQL.
workers.summary: Defensive YARA-X malware scanning: compile YARA rules and scan blobs/text for matches, all in SQL over Apache Arrow.
workers.doc_md:
# YARA Malware Scanning in SQL

![YARA-X logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VirusTotal/yara-x/main/ls/editors/code/images/icon.png)

Scan blobs, files, and text columns for malware and indicators of compromise (IOCs) straight from DuckDB SQL by compiling and matching **YARA rules** — no external scanner, no native `libyara`, just functions you can call in a query.

This extension brings defensive YARA rule matching to the database, so security engineers, threat hunters, and data teams can triage suspicious files, hunt for signatures, and enforce detection rules over data they already have in DuckDB. Instead of exporting samples to a standalone tool, you write a YARA ruleset (or load one from a column) and let SQL fan it across millions of rows: filter a table of email attachments, label artifacts in an object store, or join scan verdicts back onto your metadata — all in one place.

Matching is powered by [YARA-X](https://github.com/VirusTotal/yara-x), VirusTotal's pure-Rust rewrite of the classic YARA engine, embedded directly in the worker so there is no C dependency to install or keep patched. Rules are compiled once per batch and reused, and scanning is *total*: untrusted, garbage, empty, or deliberately hostile data simply yields no matches rather than crashing the worker, so you can point it at live malware safely. The full YARA syntax — string, hex, and regex patterns, conditions, namespaces, tags, and the standard `pe`/`elf`/`hash`/`math` modules — is supported.

Two shapes of access are offered. Per-row scalar functions test a whole column of blobs or text against a ruleset, giving you a filter predicate, a match count, or the name of the rule that fired — ideal for triaging a table of samples or labelling artifacts in place. Table functions instead expand a single scan into detail rows, one per matching rule or per individual pattern hit (with byte offsets and the matched bytes), for forensics and drill-down. There is also a validation helper for checking that a ruleset compiles before you scan with it, and a `yara_modules` reference table listing the YARA-X modules (`pe`, `elf`, `hash`, `math`, …) a rule may import.

For rule-writing syntax and module reference see the official [YARA-X documentation](https://virustotal.github.io/yara-x/) and the [yara-x crate docs](https://docs.rs/yara-x).

tags.vgi.doc_md:
# YARA — `main` schema

The single schema holding this worker's YARA rule-compilation and malware-scanning functions over Apache Arrow. The functions fall into a few groups:

- **Scanning** — per-row scalars that test a column of blobs or text against a ruleset (match predicate, matching-rule count, first matching rule).
- **Match Details** — table functions that expand a single scan into detail rows: one per matching rule, or one per individual pattern hit with byte offsets.
- **Rule Validation** — check that a ruleset compiles before you scan with it.
- **Reference** — the `yara_modules` table lists the YARA-X modules (`pe`, `elf`, `hash`, `math`, …) compiled into this worker that a rule may import.

Scanning is *total*: untrusted or hostile data yields no matches rather than crashing the worker; only an invalid rule source raises an error.

workers.summary: Yahoo Finance market data as DuckDB tables: history (OHLCV), quote (snapshot), search (symbol lookup) — vgi-yfinance
workers.doc_md:
## Yahoo Finance

Market data from Yahoo Finance's public, keyless endpoints as DuckDB table functions: OHLCV price history over a named or explicit date range, current-price snapshots (price, change, day & 52-week range, volume) for a list of tickers, and name-to-ticker resolution.

No secret or API key is required. Prices are delayed and provided for informational use only; review Yahoo's terms before redistribution. Intraday candles are only available for recent ranges.

### Sources and references

- [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/), whose unofficial, undocumented chart and search endpoints this worker reads.
- [Exchanges and data providers on Yahoo Finance](https://help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN2310.html): per-exchange delays and data sources.
- [Yahoo terms of service](https://legal.yahoo.com/us/en/yahoo/terms/otos/index.html).

example_queries.title: search_symbol
example_queries.description: Resolve a company name to candidate tickers
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, short_name FROM yfinance.main.search('apple') ORDER BY score DESC, symbol LIMIT 3;

example_queries.title: recent_history
example_queries.description: Fetch the last few daily candles for a ticker
example_queries.sql: SELECT timestamp, close FROM yfinance.main.history('AAPL', range := '5d') ORDER BY timestamp;

example_queries.description: Last month of daily candles for Apple, oldest first
example_queries.sql: SELECT timestamp, open, high, low, close, volume FROM yfinance.main.history('AAPL') ORDER BY timestamp

example_queries.description: Current price for several megacaps at once
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, regular_market_price FROM yfinance.main.quote('AAPL,MSFT,GOOG') ORDER BY symbol

example_queries.description: Find a ticker by company name, best matches first
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, long_name FROM yfinance.main.search('vanguard') ORDER BY score DESC, symbol

example_queries.description: Rank companies by three-month total return starting from their names: search resolves each name to its top-scoring EQUITY ticker, then history supplies dividend-adjusted closes (adjclose) to compute the return
example_queries.sql: WITH pick AS (SELECT c.name, s.symbol FROM (VALUES ('apple'), ('costco'), ('walmart')) c(name), LATERAL yfinance.main.search(c.name, count := 5) s WHERE s.quote_type = 'EQUITY' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.name ORDER BY s.score DESC) = 1) SELECT p.name, p.symbol, round(100 * (arg_max(h.adjclose, h.timestamp) / arg_min(h.adjclose, h.timestamp) - 1), 2) AS total_return_3mo_pct FROM pick p, LATERAL yfinance.main.history(p.symbol, range := '3mo') h GROUP BY p.name, p.symbol ORDER BY total_return_3mo_pct DESC, p.name

example_queries.description: Look up the live price of companies you only know by name: search resolves each name to its top-scoring EQUITY ticker, then quote returns that listing's exchange, currency, price and change versus the previous close
example_queries.sql: WITH pick AS (SELECT c.name, s.symbol FROM (VALUES ('netflix'), ('tesla'), ('toyota')) c(name), LATERAL yfinance.main.search(c.name, count := 5) s WHERE s.quote_type = 'EQUITY' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.name ORDER BY s.score DESC) = 1) SELECT p.name, q.symbol, q.long_name, q.exchange, q.currency, q.regular_market_price, round(q.regular_market_change_percent, 2) AS change_pct FROM pick p, LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(p.symbol) q ORDER BY p.name

example_queries.description: Watchlist momentum check: compare each ticker's live quote price with the average of its daily closes over the past month from history, to see which names trade above or below their recent level
example_queries.sql: WITH q AS (SELECT symbol, regular_market_price FROM yfinance.main.quote('AAPL,MSFT,GOOG')), m AS (SELECT q.symbol, avg(h.close) AS avg_close_1mo FROM q, LATERAL yfinance.main.history(q.symbol, range := '1mo') h GROUP BY q.symbol) SELECT q.symbol, q.regular_market_price, round(m.avg_close_1mo, 2) AS avg_close_1mo, round(100 * (q.regular_market_price / m.avg_close_1mo - 1), 2) AS pct_vs_1mo_avg FROM q JOIN m USING (symbol) ORDER BY pct_vs_1mo_avg DESC, q.symbol

example_queries.description: Price foreign listings in US dollars: quote each listing, then quote the FX pair named by its own currency column (EUR=X is euros per dollar; JPY=X, which Yahoo echoes back as USDJPY=X, is yen per dollar) and divide. London listings quote in pence (currency GBp) and would also need dividing by 100, so none is included
example_queries.sql: SELECT l.symbol, l.currency, l.regular_market_price AS local_price, fx.symbol AS fx_pair, fx.regular_market_price AS units_per_usd, round(l.regular_market_price / fx.regular_market_price, 2) AS price_usd FROM yfinance.main.quote('ASML.AS,MC.PA,7203.T,NESN.SW') l, LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(l.currency || '=X') fx ORDER BY price_usd DESC, l.symbol

example_queries.description: Where does each asset class sit in its 52-week range? Quote every symbol_reference ticker (equity, ETF, index, crypto, FX) and show its position in the range (0 = at the low, 100 = at the high) and its percent distance from the 52-week high
example_queries.sql: SELECT r.asset_type, r.symbol, q.regular_market_price, round(100 * (q.regular_market_price - q.fifty_two_week_low) / nullif(q.fifty_two_week_high - q.fifty_two_week_low, 0), 1) AS pct_of_52w_range, round(100 * (q.regular_market_price / q.fifty_two_week_high - 1), 1) AS pct_from_52w_high FROM yfinance.main.symbol_reference r, LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(r.symbol) q ORDER BY r.asset_type, pct_of_52w_range DESC, r.symbol

example_queries.description: How closely does each registry equity and ETF track the S&P 500? Pull six months of daily history for the symbol_reference equities, ETFs and the ^GSPC index, turn dividend-adjusted closes into daily returns, and correlate each ticker's returns with the index's on matching trading days
example_queries.sql: WITH px AS (SELECT r.symbol, h.timestamp, h.adjclose / lag(h.adjclose) OVER (PARTITION BY r.symbol ORDER BY h.timestamp) - 1 AS ret FROM yfinance.main.symbol_reference r, LATERAL yfinance.main.history(r.symbol, range := '6mo') h WHERE r.asset_type IN ('EQUITY', 'ETF', 'INDEX')) SELECT a.symbol, round(corr(a.ret, b.ret), 3) AS corr_with_sp500 FROM px a JOIN px b ON a.timestamp = b.timestamp AND b.symbol = '^GSPC' WHERE a.symbol <> '^GSPC' GROUP BY a.symbol ORDER BY corr_with_sp500 DESC, a.symbol

example_queries.description: List the reference tickers for a given asset type
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, name, exchange FROM yfinance.main.symbol_reference WHERE asset_type = 'ETF' ORDER BY symbol

example_queries.description: Count the reference symbols grouped by asset type
example_queries.sql: SELECT asset_type, count(*) AS n FROM yfinance.main.symbol_reference GROUP BY asset_type ORDER BY n DESC, asset_type

example_queries.description: Snapshot quote for Apple
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, regular_market_price, regular_market_change_percent FROM yfinance.main.quote('AAPL')

example_queries.description: Latest price for every ticker in a table, via LATERAL
example_queries.sql: SELECT w.sym, q.regular_market_price FROM (VALUES ('AAPL'), ('MSFT')) w(sym), LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(w.sym) q ORDER BY w.sym

example_queries.description: Find symbols matching 'apple'
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, short_name, exchange FROM yfinance.main.search('apple') ORDER BY score DESC, symbol

example_queries.description: Up to 20 candidate symbols for a query
example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, long_name, exchange FROM yfinance.main.search('vanguard', count := 20) ORDER BY score DESC, symbol

example_queries.description: Best-matching ticker for every company name in a table, via LATERAL
example_queries.sql: SELECT c.name, s.symbol FROM (VALUES ('apple'), ('microsoft')) c(name), LATERAL yfinance.main.search(c.name, count := 1) s ORDER BY c.name

example_queries.description: The five most recent daily closes and volumes for Apple

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The functions that return Yahoo Finance data. `history` yields a time series of OHLCV candles for one symbol; `quote` returns a one-row-per-symbol snapshot of current pricing; `search` maps free text to ticker symbols. tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Market data

Time series of OHLCV candles, one-row-per-symbol pricing snapshots, and ticker lookup. Use the time series for charting, returns and backtests; the snapshots for dashboards and watchlists; and the lookup when you only know a company name.

Everything is keyless. `history` takes one ticker, `quote` one ticker or a comma-separated list, and `search` free text, each plus optional named arguments; any of them can read its input from a column with `LATERAL`, so one function's output can feed the next. Symbols follow Yahoo's convention (e.g. `AAPL`, `BRK-B`, `BTC-USD`, `^GSPC`).

vgi.example_queries.description: Last month of daily candles for Apple, oldest first
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT timestamp, open, high, low, close, volume FROM yfinance.main.history('AAPL') ORDER BY timestamp

vgi.example_queries.description: Current price for several megacaps at once
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, regular_market_price FROM yfinance.main.quote('AAPL,MSFT,GOOG') ORDER BY symbol

vgi.example_queries.description: Find a ticker by company name, best matches first
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT symbol, long_name FROM yfinance.main.search('vanguard') ORDER BY score DESC, symbol

vgi.example_queries.description: Rank companies by three-month total return starting from their names: search resolves each name to its top-scoring EQUITY ticker, then history supplies dividend-adjusted closes (adjclose) to compute the return
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH pick AS (SELECT c.name, s.symbol FROM (VALUES ('apple'), ('costco'), ('walmart')) c(name), LATERAL yfinance.main.search(c.name, count := 5) s WHERE s.quote_type = 'EQUITY' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.name ORDER BY s.score DESC) = 1) SELECT p.name, p.symbol, round(100 * (arg_max(h.adjclose, h.timestamp) / arg_min(h.adjclose, h.timestamp) - 1), 2) AS total_return_3mo_pct FROM pick p, LATERAL yfinance.main.history(p.symbol, range := '3mo') h GROUP BY p.name, p.symbol ORDER BY total_return_3mo_pct DESC, p.name

vgi.example_queries.description: Look up the live price of companies you only know by name: search resolves each name to its top-scoring EQUITY ticker, then quote returns that listing's exchange, currency, price and change versus the previous close
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH pick AS (SELECT c.name, s.symbol FROM (VALUES ('netflix'), ('tesla'), ('toyota')) c(name), LATERAL yfinance.main.search(c.name, count := 5) s WHERE s.quote_type = 'EQUITY' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.name ORDER BY s.score DESC) = 1) SELECT p.name, q.symbol, q.long_name, q.exchange, q.currency, q.regular_market_price, round(q.regular_market_change_percent, 2) AS change_pct FROM pick p, LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(p.symbol) q ORDER BY p.name

vgi.example_queries.description: Watchlist momentum check: compare each ticker's live quote price with the average of its daily closes over the past month from history, to see which names trade above or below their recent level
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH q AS (SELECT symbol, regular_market_price FROM yfinance.main.quote('AAPL,MSFT,GOOG')), m AS (SELECT q.symbol, avg(h.close) AS avg_close_1mo FROM q, LATERAL yfinance.main.history(q.symbol, range := '1mo') h GROUP BY q.symbol) SELECT q.symbol, q.regular_market_price, round(m.avg_close_1mo, 2) AS avg_close_1mo, round(100 * (q.regular_market_price / m.avg_close_1mo - 1), 2) AS pct_vs_1mo_avg FROM q JOIN m USING (symbol) ORDER BY pct_vs_1mo_avg DESC, q.symbol

vgi.example_queries.description: Price foreign listings in US dollars: quote each listing, then quote the FX pair named by its own currency column (EUR=X is euros per dollar; JPY=X, which Yahoo echoes back as USDJPY=X, is yen per dollar) and divide. London listings quote in pence (currency GBp) and would also need dividing by 100, so none is included
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT l.symbol, l.currency, l.regular_market_price AS local_price, fx.symbol AS fx_pair, fx.regular_market_price AS units_per_usd, round(l.regular_market_price / fx.regular_market_price, 2) AS price_usd FROM yfinance.main.quote('ASML.AS,MC.PA,7203.T,NESN.SW') l, LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(l.currency || '=X') fx ORDER BY price_usd DESC, l.symbol

vgi.example_queries.description: Where does each asset class sit in its 52-week range? Quote every symbol_reference ticker (equity, ETF, index, crypto, FX) and show its position in the range (0 = at the low, 100 = at the high) and its percent distance from the 52-week high
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT r.asset_type, r.symbol, q.regular_market_price, round(100 * (q.regular_market_price - q.fifty_two_week_low) / nullif(q.fifty_two_week_high - q.fifty_two_week_low, 0), 1) AS pct_of_52w_range, round(100 * (q.regular_market_price / q.fifty_two_week_high - 1), 1) AS pct_from_52w_high FROM yfinance.main.symbol_reference r, LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(r.symbol) q ORDER BY r.asset_type, pct_of_52w_range DESC, r.symbol

vgi.example_queries.description: How closely does each registry equity and ETF track the S&P 500? Pull six months of daily history for the symbol_reference equities, ETFs and the ^GSPC index, turn dividend-adjusted closes into daily returns, and correlate each ticker's returns with the index's on matching trading days
vgi.example_queries.sql: WITH px AS (SELECT r.symbol, h.timestamp, h.adjclose / lag(h.adjclose) OVER (PARTITION BY r.symbol ORDER BY h.timestamp) - 1 AS ret FROM yfinance.main.symbol_reference r, LATERAL yfinance.main.history(r.symbol, range := '6mo') h WHERE r.asset_type IN ('EQUITY', 'ETF', 'INDEX')) SELECT a.symbol, round(corr(a.ret, b.ret), 3) AS corr_with_sp500 FROM px a JOIN px b ON a.timestamp = b.timestamp AND b.symbol = '^GSPC' WHERE a.symbol <> '^GSPC' GROUP BY a.symbol ORDER BY corr_with_sp500 DESC, a.symbol

## symbol_reference

A browsable, credential-free registry of well-known tickers. One row per symbol, naming the instrument, its asset type, its listing exchange, and the Yahoo symbol-format convention it illustrates. tags.vgi.doc_md:
## quote

Current-price snapshot for a comma-separated list of tickers, one row per symbol. Backed by Yahoo's keyless chart-metadata plane, so `regular_market_change` and `regular_market_change_percent` are derived from the previous close, and market cap is not available. An unresolvable ticker is dropped rather than failing the batch, so the result may have fewer rows than symbols requested. Each symbol is fetched with its own lightweight request, in parallel, so a long watchlist stays responsive.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Resolve a company name or partial symbol to candidate ticker symbols, best matches first. Use it when you only know a name — take the resulting `symbol` and pass it to `history` or `quote`. Returns equities, ETFs, indices, and other instruments with their exchange and type.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## search

Ticker lookup over Yahoo's search endpoint. Returns up to `count` candidate symbols (news results are dropped), ranked by Yahoo's relevance score, best matches first. Take the resulting `symbol` and feed it into `history` or `quote`. The `count` argument caps how many candidates come back and is clamped to 1..50 (default 8).

vgi.example_queries.description: Up to 20 candidate symbols for a query

WITH pick AS (SELECT c.name, s.symbol FROM (VALUES ('apple'), ('costco'), ('walmart')) c(name), LATERAL yfinance.main.search(c.name, count := 5) s WHERE s.quote_type = 'EQUITY' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.name ORDER BY s.score DESC) = 1) SELECT p.name, p.symbol, round(100 * (arg_max(h.adjclose, h.timestamp) / arg_min(h.adjclose, h.timestamp) - 1), 2) AS total_return_3mo_pct FROM pick p, LATERAL yfinance.main.history(p.symbol, range := '3mo') h GROUP BY p.name, p.symbol ORDER BY total_return_3mo_pct DESC, p.name

WITH pick AS (SELECT c.name, s.symbol FROM (VALUES ('netflix'), ('tesla'), ('toyota')) c(name), LATERAL yfinance.main.search(c.name, count := 5) s WHERE s.quote_type = 'EQUITY' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY c.name ORDER BY s.score DESC) = 1) SELECT p.name, q.symbol, q.long_name, q.exchange, q.currency, q.regular_market_price, round(q.regular_market_change_percent, 2) AS change_pct FROM pick p, LATERAL yfinance.main.quote(p.symbol) q ORDER BY p.name

functions.name: history
functions.comment: Historical OHLCV candles for one symbol from Yahoo Finance (v8 chart API). Pick a named window (range := '1y') plus a candle width (bar := '1wk'), or an explicit start_date/end_date range. The symbol may be a column, so LATERAL history(t.sym) fetches candles for every row. Returns columns symbol, timestamp (UTC), open, high, low, close, adjclose, and volume.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Daily or intraday OHLCV candles for a single ticker over a chosen window. Use it for price history, charting, returns, and technical analysis. Pick a named range (range := '1y') with a candle width (bar := '1wk'), or an explicit start_date/end_date range. Thin or halted candles come back as NULL cells rather than failing the scan. The newest candle may still be forming: during a session its close is the latest live price.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## history

Historical OHLCV candles for one ticker from Yahoo's chart feed. Choose a named `range` (e.g. `'6mo'`, `'1y'`, `'max'`) plus a `bar` candle width (`'1d'`, `'1wk'`, `'1mo'`, or an intraday width like `'5m'` on recent ranges), or pass an explicit `start_date`/`end_date` pair to override `range`. Emits one row per candle, ordered oldest-first; thin or halted candles come back with NULL price cells rather than failing the scan. Intraday bars are only retained by Yahoo for recent windows, so an intraday `bar` on a long `range` yields fewer rows than the range implies. `adjclose` falls back to `close` when Yahoo omits it. When Yahoo has not yet filled the newest candle's close, it is taken from the latest market price.

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT timestamp, close, volume FROM yfinance.main.history('AAPL', range := '1mo') ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 5
vgi.example_queries.description: The five most recent daily closes and volumes for Apple

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT timestamp, close, volume FROM yfinance.main.history('MSFT', range := '1y', bar := '1wk') ORDER BY timestamp
vgi.example_queries.description: One year of weekly closes for Microsoft

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT max(high) AS high_52w, min(low) AS low_52w FROM yfinance.main.history('SPY', range := '1y')
vgi.example_queries.description: The 52-week high and low for SPY, aggregated from daily candles

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT w.sym, max(h.close) AS high_close FROM (VALUES ('AAPL'), ('MSFT')) w(sym), LATERAL yfinance.main.history(w.sym, range := '1mo') h GROUP BY w.sym ORDER BY w.sym
vgi.example_queries.description: Highest close over the last month for every ticker in a table, via LATERAL

arguments.name: symbol
arguments.description: The ticker to fetch, written the way Yahoo lists it — equities, class shares, crypto pairs, and caret-prefixed indices are all accepted. Passed as the first positional argument (not symbol := ...); a literal or a column (LATERAL history(t.sym)). A NULL or empty symbol yields no rows.

arguments.name: bar
arguments.description: Candle width — how much time each bar spans. Intraday widths only work on recent ranges. Default '1d'.

arguments.name: end_date
arguments.description: Exclusive end date 'YYYY-MM-DD', after start_date. Defaults to now when start_date is set; setting it without start_date fails the bind.

arguments.name: prepost
arguments.description: Include pre-market and post-market candles. Default false.

arguments.name: range
arguments.description: Named lookback window over which to fetch candles. Ignored when start_date is set. Default '1mo'.

arguments.name: start_date
arguments.description: Inclusive start date 'YYYY-MM-DD'. When set, [start_date, end_date) overrides range. Empty = use range. A malformed date fails the bind.

examples: SELECT timestamp, close, volume FROM yfinance.main.history('AAPL', range := '1mo') ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 5
SELECT timestamp, close, volume FROM yfinance.main.history('MSFT', range := '1y', bar := '1wk') ORDER BY timestamp
SELECT max(high) AS high_52w, min(low) AS low_52w FROM yfinance.main.history('SPY', range := '1y')
SELECT w.sym, max(h.close) AS high_close FROM (VALUES ('AAPL'), ('MSFT')) w(sym), LATERAL yfinance.main.history(w.sym, range := '1mo') h GROUP BY w.sym ORDER BY w.sym
